Learned, not designed: WP-1.3's three review rounds attacked pre-registration revision 1, the amendments they forced went in as revision 2 on the strength of those reviews plus operator rulings, and revision 2 — the document that actually governed every game and every profile — was never attacked by any fresh context (docs/experiments/wp13_results.md §6a). Nothing in that experiment is known to be wrong because of it, which is exactly why the rule lands now rather than after the run it would have saved: the gap is invisible until it is not. The cost is one more review round per amended pre-registration, bounded by the diff being small when the amendment is — flips never; a run too urgent for the review of its own governing document is a run this project does not make.

D-196: PROCESS LAW, added to CLAUDE.md's Process section: a named design decision with more than one viable option is settled by an OPTION MATRIX — options, costs, failure modes, recommendation — attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM subagent BEFORE selection, and the surviving option's ADR line records the strongest surviving attack. This was this session's standing instruction made permanent, and its first application is D-198..D-202 below, where the matrix round found two MAJOR gaps in the implementing session's own design before a line of it was written (a third script engine whose handshake the change would have broken, and a pre-registered test that could not fail against the defect it existed to pin). The recorded-attack clause is the part that earns the line: an ADR that records only the winner invites the next session to rediscover the losing options, while the strongest surviving attack is precisely the thing that flips the decision if it ever strengthens — flips never as process; individual matrices are as re-openable as any ADR.

D-197: OPERATOR RULING on strength calibration, recorded in docs/research/sealbot_notes.md: pistol is NOT at strong-human strength and will not be after these work packages; sealbot is strong but strong humans exploit its weaknesses decently well, so sealbot is a MILESTONE, not a human-strength proxy; the order is pistol below sealbot, sealbot below strong humans who exploit it; and NO human-strength claim is made without measurement — rule 6's discipline applied to a claim class where the temptation is strongest, because "beats sealbot" reads like "human-strength" to anyone who has not watched a strong human farm sealbot's colony blindness — flips only by measurement against the population the claim names, never by extrapolation from an engine-engine result.

D-198: ENGINE IDENTITY CLOSES OVER THE EVAL WEIGHTS. The engine digests `eval.weights_file` and emits `id weights_sha256 <hex>` in its handshake; the arena REQUIRES that field of every engine (missing or malformed = a named handshake refusal), captures it into `EngineIdentity`, folds it into `experiment_sha256` and records it on every report's `engine` line — closing the hole D-188 recorded, where two engines differing only in the weight table were byte-identical in every recorded digest while `nelo_pair` moved by 98 points. Settled by an option matrix under D-196's process, attacked by a fresh-context round: the ENGINE digests rather than the arena because the engine is the process that actually reads the file, resolved against its own working directory — an arena-side digest would attest bytes the engine may never have loaded, couple pistol-arena to the engine config schema it deliberately treats as opaque, and break every stub-instrument test whose config is not an engine document; requiring the field rather than recording-if-present is what actually closes the hole, and D-180 already confines the arena to pistol builds. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, recorded per D-196: the attestation is a second read of the file at handshake-build time, not the bytes the eval parsed, so a swap landing between the eval's read and the digest read is attested wrongly for that one process — every reachable divergence still fails loud (it surfaces as D-199's IdentityDrift at the next spawn, or re-baselines a run-start capture no game used), and digesting inside the loader is declined for now because pistol-eval sits below this workspace's one hashing implementation and a second SHA-256 for this residual is not worth owning — REPORT_SCHEMA moves to 2 — flips if the codebook-net work ever gives pistol-eval a content-addressed weights path of its own, which is where the loader-digest belongs.

D-199: THE ARENA RE-VERIFIES ENGINE IDENTITY AT EVERY SPAWN: before each game, each engine's config document is re-digested from disk and the fresh handshake's ENTIRE id-line vector is compared against the run-start capture; any drift is the named abort `IdentityDrift` — never a game result, never a silent continuation — turning D-188's operating rule ("no configs/ edit and no rebuild while a run is live") from a habit into code, pinned by `arena_aborts_on_mid_run_config_swap` with a stub that edits its own config mid-run and by a mutation run that disabled the check and watched the test fail. Comparing the whole id-line vector rather than only the weights field was the decision-red-team's improvement, adopted: the handshake is deterministic by construction, so on an honest run the comparison can never false-abort, and it additionally catches a swap landing inside the run-start window between the first engine's config read and the arena's digest of it. RESIDUALS, named rather than implied: the binary is NOT re-digested per spawn (a multi-megabyte digest per game buys a failure mode nobody has observed; the binary is re-executed, not re-read, so a swap changes behaviour the determinism gates see); and a swap landing between the LAST game's verification and that engine's own config read has no later spawn to catch it — the check narrows the window from a whole run to one spawn, it does not close it, and only an in-process attestation of every input could — flips if a run is ever observed to slip through either window, at which point per-spawn binary digests and an engine-side `id config_sha256` are the recorded next steps.

D-200: `--out` IS CLAIMED AT DISPATCH WITH `create_new` (O_EXCL) AND THE REPORT IS WRITTEN THROUGH THE CLAIMED HANDLE, killing wp13_results §6b's TOCTOU: the existence check and the creation are one syscall, so of two racing runs exactly one owns the path from its first instant and the other fails by name before spending anything. Settled by an option matrix under D-196: `create_new` only at the final write was rejected because a racing run would then discover the collision AFTER playing its whole sample — the report's content lost at the most expensive moment — while the dispatch-claim costs one visible empty file per live run. A refusal BEFORE any game still exits 2 with "no report at all", because the refusal path removes the claim it created — safe by construction, since `remove_file` there can only ever hit a file this process made via `create_new` (a pre-existing file fails the claim before anything is written, and a concurrent claimant fails its own `create_new`). STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, recorded per D-196: two loud residuals — a run dispatched in the window between another's claim and its refusal-removal is refused although the path frees milliseconds later, and a run that CRASHES leaves an empty claim that blocks a rerun at that path until an operator removes it; both are noisy-refusal shaped, never silent-overwrite shaped, which is the trade the matrix chose. Pinned by `out_path_collision_fails_by_name` on the claim itself, because the binary-level pre-existing-file test cannot distinguish the fix from the TOCTOU (the old code refused that case too — the decision-red-team's finding) — flips never; a future locked append-log for multi-run experiments would be a new mechanism, not a relaxation of this one.

D-201: `first_player_wins` IS COMPUTED OVER DECIDED NON-FORFEIT GAMES ONLY, with the forfeit count printed adjacent on the same line and the token `conditional` appended whenever that count is nonzero — paying wp13_results §6b's debt, where a win by forfeit counted as a first-player observation and the rate was therefore "only readable beside a zero forfeits count", a reading rule that lived in a document instead of in the number. A forfeit measures a protocol bug in the loser, not the game, so it leaves the numerator AND the denominator; it stays in the `counts` line's `decided` because the offender genuinely lost, and the report now carries two deliberately different words — `decided` (forfeit-inclusive, the game's outcome) and `decided_non_forfeit` (the rate's denominator) — so neither can be mistaken for the other. Every WP-1.3 rate (D-189's 61.8%, D-191's 57.1%) is unaffected: both runs had zero forfeits, which is exactly why the hole never bit. REPORT_SCHEMA moves to 3 — flips never; a report format that made a conditional rate look unconditional is the thing this line exists to forbid.

D-202: `run.openings_skip` JOINS `run.openings_take`, so two runs can draw DISJOINT windows of ONE book — the knob whose absence forced WP-1.3's confirmatory run onto the other book (D-190, wp13_results §6b). The window is contiguous, which keeps D-143's argument intact: the book is emitted in content-hash order, so any contiguous window is as much a sample as a prefix is, and skip t/take t is disjoint from skip 0/take t by construction. The whole file is still parsed, digest-verified and symmetry-deduped before the window is cut; `skip + take` past the book is a named refusal citing both keys, never a silent shortening; the skip is printed in the instrument block and folded into `experiment_sha256`, because it decides WHICH games are played. A named trap, recorded per the review: `game … opening <i>` stays WINDOW-relative, so two disjoint-window reports both label openings `0..take` and the absolute book position is `openings_skip + i` — the doc comments say so where the index is defined and where it is printed. `openings_skip` is REQUIRED (rule 1: no code-side default; a run that skips nothing writes 0), so ARENA_SCHEMA_VERSION moves to 2 and all five committed arena configs gain `openings_skip = 0` with `schema_version = 2` — settled by an option matrix under D-196 against staying at version 1 (a version that does not move when the schema moves is decorative; either way an old document fails loudly at load). THIS EDITS THE TWO HISTORICAL WP-1.3 DOCUMENTS, and the reconciliation with D-186's "flips only by a NEW pre-registration commit, never by an edit to the registered one" is written out rather than assumed: no run is live and none will re-run those documents (D-194 already made them self-matches); `schema_version` is document metadata OUTSIDE `experiment_sha256`, and every experiment value in them is untouched; they cannot stay at version 1 because `tools/config_check.sh` validates every `configs/arena_*.toml` against the current build on every CI run; and reproduction goes by the recorded revision and the reports' `config_sha256` lines, not by path (D-161, D-194's precedent). STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, recorded per D-196: relocating the two historical documents out of `configs/` would have frozen their bytes forever instead — declined because completed reports cite them at their committed paths and a document the config gate no longer validates is a document that rots invisibly; the attack stands as the recorded alternative if a future schema change would have to alter an experiment VALUE rather than metadata, which this one does not — REPORT_SCHEMA moves to 4 — flips if a published claim is ever made against a specific config revision, after which that document freezes and a versioned successor takes edits.

D-203: `tools/artifact_check.sh` RECOGNIZES A MATCH REPORT BY CONTENT — a tracked file whose first line is the report schema header (`arena_report <n>` / `arena_report_aborted <n>`) is a violation whatever it is named — closing wp13_results §6b's hole, where a report committed as `.txt` or `.report` passed both `.gitignore` and the gate's name patterns and the only mitigation was the habit of naming reports `.matchlog`. The check rides the gate's existing per-file loop with the bash builtin `read` (no process per file), trims a CR so a CRLF report cannot slip through, drops `read`'s stderr because it complains about NUL bytes in binary files it cannot match anyway, and tolerates empty and newline-less files under `set -e` by design. It is pinned by `artifact_check_catches_renamed_report` in a SCRATCH git repository with the script copied to `<scratch>/tools/` — one directory down, because the script roots itself at `dirname/..`, and a copy at the scratch's top level would silently check the scratch's parent (the review's finding) — with a clean-repo control run so the test cannot pass on a gate that refuses everything. The residual is inherent to a content signature: a report whose FIRST line is altered is no longer recognized — but such a file is no longer a report the schema reads either, and the name patterns still stand in front — flips if the report format ever stops carrying its kind on line one, which D-160 argues it never should.

D-204: THE TACTICAL FIXTURE'S THRESHOLDS BIND AT THE COMMITTED CONFIG HENCEFORTH, AND NO THRESHOLD VALUE CHANGES. The suite holds 20 of 20 at the now-committed candidate radius 2 — D-194 cited the gate at the switch, and this session's gate runs reproduce it (`selftest: 20 cases from crates/pistol-cli/tests/fixtures/tactical_v0.txt (required 20)`, tools/ci.sh gate 8) — but the thresholds were PRE-REGISTERED against radius 3 and were never re-derived for the new policy, which wp13_results §6d records as open debt. This line closes it as an operator ruling rather than leaving it half-open: the suite's `require 20` and its per-case expectations now bind at whatever `configs/instrument_v0.toml` commits, so a future config change that fails a case is a red gate to investigate, never a licence to re-read the threshold — that is CLAUDE.md's no-post-hoc-threshold rule applied to the one suite that predates the policy it now guards. What it deliberately does NOT claim: that 20/20 at radius 2 means the thresholds are as DISCRIMINATING at radius 2 as they were at radius 3 — nothing measured that, and a re-derivation would be its own pre-registered work package — flips by that pre-registered threshold re-derivation, or when WP-1.5's threat-first generation supersedes the radius policy entirely (D-194's own flip), never by a quiet re-read after a failure.

D-205: RECORDS THE SLACK SESSION'S REVIEW-impl AND RED-TEAM ROUNDS against revision 6475e48 (fresh contexts, both reports header-pinned to that revision), because two findings were ADR sentences the code did not honour — D-181's defect class, caught by the round that exists to catch it — and four were leniencies fixed here with reproducer tests that were run RED before the fix landed. **Fixed.** (1) REVIEW-impl MAJOR: the engine digested the weights BEFORE `Pistol::from_config` while D-198 and the function doc described the reverse; reordered to match the recorded design — the eval loads first, so a missing weights file keeps pistol-eval's named error, and the digest is genuinely the second read D-198 says it is. (2) RED-TEAM MINOR: two `weights_sha256` id lines naming different tables were accepted with the first silently winning — a self-contradictory identity in the one property D-198 exists to make unambiguous; now refused by name, pinned by `arena_refuses_a_self_contradictory_or_non_canonical_weights_identity`. (3) RED-TEAM + REVIEW-impl NOTE, tightened rather than accepted: uppercase hex was admitted, and two runs of the SAME weights differing only in case would have computed different `experiment_sha256` — the digest is now required to be 64 LOWERCASE hex digits, the canonical spelling every pistol build emits. (4) RED-TEAM MINOR: the artifact gate's content signature was exact-match, so `arena_report 4 extra` and a trailing-space header slipped it while a token-splitting consumer reads both as reports; the match is now on the header's tokens, pinned by the extended `artifact_check_catches_renamed_report`. **Doc-amended, not code-changed.** REVIEW-impl MINOR: the claim-removal path also fires on a report WRITE that failed partway after a played run — deleting a truncated non-report and exiting 2 is the right behaviour (a partial report nothing marks partial is worse than none), but D-200's "refusal BEFORE any game" wording and `outpath::abandon`'s doc described a narrower scope than the code executes; both docs now state the write-failure path, and this sentence amends D-200's scope. **Accepted residuals, named.** A tracked file the gate cannot READ skips the content check with a stray stderr line (unreachable from a fresh CI checkout); `shake`'s `id`-prefix parsing tolerates a missing space after `id` (pre-existing leniency, accepts sloppy handshakes and refuses nothing it should accept); and `abandon`'s unlink under a local symlink-swap race removes the link, not any target (outside the threat model, no victim file destroyable). **What RED-TEAM attacked that HELD**, so it is not re-attacked as unexplored: report-structure injection through crafted id lines (line-anchored `# timing` and newline-free channel framing make it impossible by construction), a weights-only drift evading the config digest (the id-vector comparison caught it naming the exact line), a real 40-process race on one `--out` (exactly one winner), `--out` at directories/symlinks/dangling links/missing parents (all refused, no symlink followed), openings_skip windows over files with defects OUTSIDE the window (whole-file validation held), overflow and typo-ceiling probes on skip/take, and six 4-worker mid-run-drift runs (always an aborted report, never a verdict-carrying or corrupted one) — flips never; this line is history, and the lines it describes are the record.

D-206: THE SEALBOT DEEP-DIVE REGISTER IS A LEAD SHEET, NOT A DESIGN SOURCE — docs/research/sealbot_deep_dive.md records 78 claims harvested from a full-history clone of ramora0/sealbot (master c94749c, nnue-eval 6892e5e, mixnet-repro ef40a22), every one carrying a checkable citation, a mapped WP/stage, STATUS: UNVERIFIED, and a proposed verification, with a fresh-context spot-check (seed 20260819, 12 random + 2 extra entries, all PASS, one evidence-line correction applied) appended to the document; nothing in that register may drive a pistol code change until its claim is verified by the entry's proposed method, and verification results amend the register entry by entry (UNVERIFIED -> VERIFIED/REFUTED with the measurement's citation) — reason: the operator's calibration (D-197) makes sealbot facts leads rather than truths, and importing another engine's unverified tuning numbers or design conclusions would bypass Hard Rule 6's judge exactly where the temptation is strongest (WP-1.5's thresholds, which the register feeds) — flips per entry by that entry's own verification, never wholesale; the binding rule itself flips only if the operator re-rules the calibration D-197 records.

D-207: MOVETIME IS A CEILING — SUPERSEDES D-95 AND AMENDS D-74, whose first-iteration-uninterruptible rule now binds REPRODUCIBLE stops only. The mechanism, chosen by option matrix and a fresh-context decision-red-team (verdict: O1+ stands; O2's best-so-far root loop was proved to carry ZERO information beyond passive salvage at root granularity because root beta is infinite, and O3's ladder rungs stay unbounded without O1's checks): under a Deadline stop the search secures a bounded fallback BEFORE deepening — an instant-win scan over the ascending candidate set, then the first candidates of that deterministic ordering, second-stone win included, all replayed through GameState so legality is the rules' own answer — then every iteration is abortable, the deadline is tested at EVERY abortable node (the 1024-node mask stays node-budget-only) and every 64 scored cells inside move ordering, and the answer under abort is the aborted iteration's completed root prefix (`Run::salvage`, sound because a ply-0 promotion only ever carries a completed child's exact score and a turn-whole line), else the last completed depth, else the fallback. `SearchOutcome.provenance` (CompletedDepth | PartialRoot | Fallback) makes the answer's kind machine-readable at the Engine seam; the WIRE grammar is unchanged on purpose — play-mode movetime output is never evidence for a claim (rule 6) and a play-only token would fork the grammar the API contract mirrors — which flips when the API spec needs provenance. `depth_turns` counts only completed depths, 0 included: the report understates, never overstates. Reproducible budgets are untouched end to end: no clock read exists on any instrument path (the ordering's deadline parameter is None there), salvage and fallback are Deadline-gated at both compute and read sites, and the proof is byte-identity — the full determinism-gate workload (20 tactical positions x {depth_turns 4, nodes 200000}, gate config, release) normalized to strip nps/time hashes e2154653998b06d913bca52a84217b44ba6a215e7d16100ef7a3f97f113f4caf at revision 3926110 and again after this change. MEASURED (Ryzen 7 3700X, release, play_v0 radius 3, epsilon 50 ms): movetime 500 went from 644 / 2334 / 14135 ms at 11 / 21 / 51 spread-8 stones to 499 ms at all of 11/21/51/99 stones; movetime 50 answers in 49 ms and movetime 1 in 1 / 0 / 1 / 3 ms; worst overshoot 2 ms. THE PROMISE'S DOMAIN, stated because the decision-red-team's strongest surviving attack is that it cannot be unconditional: epsilon covers the bounded uninterruptible sections — the fallback (two candidate generations plus two O(|C|) win scans, no eval), one node's candidate generation, at most 64 ordering scorings, the unwind and report I/O — and every one of them grows linearly with candidate count without limit, so the 50 ms value is measured on this machine up to the fixture's 99-stone envelope and re-measurement accompanies any driver on a materially bigger class; raising `play.movetime_epsilon_ms` to green a failing movetime gate is a post-hoc threshold move CLAUDE.md forbids — flips when WP-1.5's threat-first generation shrinks the first iteration to a rounding error, at which point the salvage path decays to a rarely-taken safety net and this line is re-measured.

D-208: ENGINE SCHEMA v2 — the required `[play]` section arrives with `movetime_epsilon_ms` (bounds 1..=MAX_MOVETIME_EPSILON_MS=1000; a rejection bound, not a value, per D-18) and SCHEMA_VERSION moves 1 -> 2 so a version-1 document fails by version rather than by missing key (D-16's equality reading). The section is stated in every document whatever its mode, mirroring D-93's `[instrument]`-in-a-play-document precedent, and is consumed where play mode speaks: the play handshake advertises `id movetime_epsilon_ms <n>` for a driver to size its clamp against, while the instrument handshake is unchanged byte-for-byte. Named consequence rather than surprise: all four committed engine configs were edited, so their sha256 digests moved and a re-run of a committed WP-1.3 arena config will record a different `config_sha256`/`experiment_sha256` than the completed reports — those reports cite the digests of the documents as they stood, which is what a digest is for — flips never; a second play key lands in the section that already exists.

D-211: THE STDIO-SHIM SPEC — pistol-api, when its implementation is licensed, is a THIN JSON-lines adapter over the `Engine` trait speaking hexo-bridge stdio-protocol v1 (../hexo-bridge/docs/stdio-protocol.md), and this line is the spec that implementation will be reviewed against; pistol-api stays EMPTY of code until then (CLAUDE.md rule 11). The mapping: `reset` -> `new_game`, replying `{"ok":true,"v":1}`; `setup` + the per-stone `place` stream -> ONE `set_position`, the stones grouped into turns by rule 3's structure with each stone's declared side checked against the side that structure implies and any mismatch a loud refusal; a `setup` of the standard single origin cross joins the move list directly (D-6 move-list form), while a general `free_setup` board — which no move list can express — maps to D-6's `position set` form, and a board even that form refuses (a completed line, an impossible count) is refused loudly, never repaired; `best_move time_ms` -> `go(MovetimeMs(time_ms))`, honorable now because D-207 made movetime a ceiling; the reply is 2 coordinate pairs for an ordinary turn and 1 for a turn the rules end after one stone — rule 4's first-stone win, and rule 3's turn 1 should a driver ever ask — with play order chosen by the adapter as any legal ordering of the pair (D-6: a pair is legal iff SOME ordering is); an EMPTY move list is never emitted, because the bridge reads it as a concession, so an engine-side error becomes a nonzero exit with the named error on stderr, which the bridge surfaces as SubprocessEngineError; the p1<->x mapping lives in the adapter alone (pistol-core knows no colors but its own). What the wire does NOT carry, named as a limit: stdio v1's `reset` reply admits no extra fields, so `movetime_epsilon_ms` is not readable off this wire — the operator states the clamp from the config on both sides — flips when the API layer is specified, which replaces this line with the spec it produces.

No BLOCKING findings; the mechanism, the byte-identity and every pinned digest were independently verified — REVIEW-impl rebuilt revision 3926110 in its own worktree, replayed all 40 golden cases through that binary with zero divergence, and reproduced the full-gate-budget pre/post transcript identity itself. **Fixed.** (1) REVIEW-impl MAJOR, D-181's defect class: D-209's sentence "the full set runs in release via the oracle gate's release cargo test" was FALSE — no gate ran the full golden set in release; it now runs in tools/movetime_check.sh's release layer (gate 11), and this sentence amends D-209 to say so. The check stays (one branch per 64 scorings, real milliseconds shaved in its band); a test added instead pins the ceiling at 299 stones (`deadline_holds_on_a_spread_past_the_fixture_envelope`), where a returning D-95-class uninterruptible stretch fails by minutes. **Wording amendments to D-207, substance unchanged:** "no clock read exists on any instrument path" means no clock read on a CHOICE path — `time_ms`/`nps` measurement reads predate this WP and are choice-neutral; "salvage Deadline-gated at both compute and read sites" — the cheap `root_score` write fires on every ply-0 promotion and is behavior-neutral, the binding gates being the Deadline matches at the fallback compute and the salvage read, plus the byte-identity evidence. **RED-TEAM numbers that extend D-207's domain statement:** the N+50 promise measured intact to 449 spread stones (42 ms worst at movetime 1), breaks at ~499 (52 ms) and 999 (183 ms, the bare fallback cost), movetime 500 still fine at 999 (455 ms); 2-D spreads are NOT worse than lines (radius-3 balls are disjoint at spacing >= 7 either way, 36 candidates/stone the geometric maximum); ~500 hostile runs produced zero illegal replies, zero panics, zero ceiling misses inside the domain, and depth_turns always equalled the completed-info-line count. **What RED-TEAM attacked that HELD**, not to be re-attacked as unexplored: deadline-landing hammers across iterations 1-4 (408 runs), mate-in-1 by first stone and by pair-second-stone at movetime 1 (the fallback's win scans, score mate 1 at 0 ms), TT reuse across repeated wall-clock searches, cross-process fallback determinism, `go movetime 0`/bare/`-1`/`1.5`/non-canonical-pair/occupied/distance-9 refusals all named with the engine alive, and instrument mode refusing movetime by name then answering a depth budget — flips never; this line is history.
D-214: `Eval::delta` LANDS — a fourth trait method, PROVIDED, receiver `&mut self`, default body = the D-76 apply/value/undo roundtrip, overridden in `HandcraftedV0` by a read-only fast path (no map surgery, nothing to undo) that `Position::static_score_after` now routes move ordering through — the work package D-192's H1 licensed at 76.27%, its shape pre-approved by D-110 and settled here by three option matrices under D-196, each attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM (no BLOCKING; one MAJOR, adopted into the matrix as the recorded strongest attack). TWO AMENDMENTS TO D-110'S LETTER, recorded rather than drifted: (1) the parenthetical "a method taking `&self`" is unsatisfiable beside the roundtrip default the same line mandates — `apply`/`undo` take `&mut self`; a panicking `&self` default is the correctness fork D-110 forbids, and a `&self` body cannot route through a `&mut` helper — so the receiver is `&mut self`, and object safety, the property the parenthetical was guarding, is equally unaffected; (2) D-110's prose "the score change of placing a stone" is overruled by its own oracle equation `delta(c,p) == apply(c,p); value(p); undo(c,p)`: the method returns the VALUE AFTER the hypothetical stone, to the prober, which is the number ordering sorts by, and the trait doc says so loudly because the name suggests a difference. The contract's "leaves the eval indistinguishable" means OBSERVATIONAL equivalence through apply/undo/value; whole-state `PartialEq` is HandcraftedV0's own pin of it, per-backend discipline exactly as D-110 made the oracle equation per-override. The fast path's equivalence proof carries two named premises — `windows_through` yields pairwise-distinct windows (pinned in eval_window_tests; apply reads a map its earlier iterations mutated, the fast path reads the unmutated map, and they agree only because no window repeats), and i64 associativity unconditional because the sum is bounded ~1.2e15 << i64::MAX even on the full lattice — and mirrors apply's full-window desync check, so an impossible stone panics with the same EVAL_DESYNC token instead of returning a number (the token is shared; the post-panic STATE deliberately not — the default panics mid-mutation, the fast path untouched, observable only under catch_unwind, where an eval is never reused). The oracle test runs TWO oracles because one is maskable: the literal equation inline on the same eval (unmaskable by any dispatch), plus a `DefaultDelta` wrapper whose `delta` IS the provided default running as real code — over 1200 seeded playout steps probing both players at every ply parity (a mid-turn probe is a census-listed READ under D-111, never a node answer; the invariant is untouched, and this line AMENDS the mechanism prose of D-76 and D-111 per rule 10: ordering no longer applies-and-takes-back, it calls `delta`, so `Eval::value` may vanish from ordering stacks) — plus the full clamp start-region x end-region matrix over {below, inside, above} both signs (the start-saturated cases kill a `clamp(p1_score) + diff` fast path), mixed-window transitions, the i16 lattice edge where a cell has fewer than 18 windows, indistinguishability by whole-state equality, and desync parity. SEARCH-IDENTITY GATE, the non-interference half (the oracle is the value half — the gate is blind to any monotone distortion of delta, since ordering consumes only relative order): the full determinism-gate workload (20 tactical positions x {depth_turns 4, nodes 200000}, gate config, release) normalized to strip nps/time hashes e2154653998b06d913bca52a84217b44ba6a215e7d16100ef7a3f97f113f4caf at revision f31cffe and BYTE-IDENTICAL again after this change (the same hash D-207 pinned at 3926110); the D-209 golden replays green in release, tools/determinism.sh green, 453 workspace tests green, clippy clean. Coverage caveat, stated: the gate runs at radius 1; the bench harness's per-position node-identity assertion over 24 midgame positions at instrument radius 2 is the identity evidence at deployment-shaped candidate sets. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACKS, recorded per D-196 — M1 (receiver): the omitted-then-listed O5 split, a provided `&self` `try_delta -> Option<i32>` probe plus a `&mut delta` wrapper, which satisfies D-110's letter at the override point and makes a mutating override structurally impossible instead of test-pinned; flips to it if a mutating or caching override (the Stage-2 codebook net warming a feature cache) ever appears. M2 (seam): `static_score_after` keeps its name while the mechanism it named is gone, and D-111 leaned on that mechanism in prose; flips toward a rename when a second caller class arrives (Stage-4 futility/razoring, D-111's named future readers). M3 (full-window check): 18 never-taken branches per probe on the single hottest path guard an input no legal caller can produce; flips only if a bench shows them costing a measurable share of the gain bracket — flips as each attack states, never silently.
D-215: THE DELTA BENCH HARNESS IS tools/bench_delta.sh AND THE OFFICIAL VERDICT IS THE OPERATOR'S — the pre-registration, fixed before implementation in the WP dispatch and restated in the script header: hotspot = the eval roundtrip (85.6% of stacks, 76.3% under ordering, D-192); expected gain 1.4x-2.5x nps AND time-to-depth >= 1.4x, both bands of bench_positions_v1, fixed-node instrument runs, IQR-gated, >= 5 reps; abort < 1.15x nps = revert and record. D-216: THE POST-DELTA RE-PROFILE IS PRE-REGISTERED in docs/experiments/delta_reprofile_prereg.md, committed before the run it governs, with H3 registered as its OWN hypothesis line per D-114 (a third hypothesis is a new line and a new profile, never an addition to D-192/D-193 after their numbers). D-217: RECORDS THE Eval::delta REVIEW ROUNDS — DECISION-RED-TEAM and REVIEW-design against revision f31cffe (the design, pre-code), REVIEW-impl and RED-TEAM against revision eaebbe0 (the landed work), all fresh contexts, all header-pinned, and the round closes with `git worktree list` showing only the main checkout. D-218: `corpus-extract` MEASURES PLACEMENT DISTANCE, AND THE MEASUREMENT CLOSES SB-65's RADIUS-6 CLAIM AS VERIFIED-FALSE — `LEGAL_RADIUS` STAYS 8 AND NOTHING IN pistol-core MOVES. The stats block now reports, for every stone after a game's first, the hex distance to the nearest stone already placed, in two columns: the raw count, and the count of ORDER-INDEPENDENT placements. Over the human corpus (SHA-256 `b2fe61eb…`, D-184's pin, verified before the run) 8698 games and 538553 stones give distance 1: 471674, 2: 44785, 3: 11811, 4: 2912, 5: 1542, 6: 805, 7: 845, 8: 4179, MAX 8 — and of those, 479 at distance 7 and 2333 at distance 8 are order-independent, so **2812 placements the platform accepted cannot be made legal at radius 6 by ANY ordering of their turn**, and the sealbot log note's "radius 6 of a stone" (docs/research/sealbot_deep_dive.md SB-65) is refuted. D-101's operator ruling stands. THE TWO-COLUMN SPLIT IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS A REVIEW FINDING, NOT A DESIGN: the measurement is order-sensitive where legality is not (a turn is legal iff SOME ordering of its stones is — D-6, D-51), and a stone is a sound witness only when it is the LAST STONE OF ITS OWN TURN as recorded, because then every turn-mate is already inside its minimum and reordering can only take stones off the board at the moment it is placed — making its measured distance a lower bound over every ordering. A stone that is NOT the last of its turn has a partner recorded AFTER it, which its minimum never saw, and that partner can bridge: the corpus really contains such placements, `dff648bcbc1833d0` index 1 sitting at distance 7 from the only stone before it while its partner is 6 from that stone and 1 from it, so the reversed ordering is legal at radius 6. Fifty of the 5024 raw far placements are demonstrably rescuable that way; the refuting count is 2812 for a stricter reason, namely that the shipped criterion counts ONLY the order-independent stones and discards the other 2212 as UNPROVEN rather than disproven — 5024 minus the 50 would be 4974, which is the reviewers' stronger figure and not this one (D-219). The reason this measurement had to exist at all is the one-sidedness of the evidence that preceded it, and that is the transferable lesson: D-149's zero legality violations over the same 8698 games NEVER DISTINGUISHED THE TWO HYPOTHESES, because radius-6-legal games are a strict subset of radius-8-legal games and a clean replay under 8 is what both predict — that is the necessary side, this is the sufficient side, and a confirmation that cannot come out the other way is not a test. It lives in a new `corpus/distance.rs` rather than in `stats.rs` (single responsibility, and stats.rs was already near rule 9's cap), it computes nothing itself — hex distance is `Coord::distance` and the turn structure is `stones_in_turn`, both pistol-core's, per CLAUDE.md rule 2 — and it counts EVERY game read rather than the eligible ones, because the question is what the platform accepted and a game pistol-core would refuse is still a game the platform recorded. Counted in `BTreeMap`s and rendered from the smallest observed distance to the largest with zero rows printed, so the order is the distance order on every machine (rule 4) and a gap in the distribution shows as a gap. Two facts bound what this cost: both committed fixtures re-emit BYTE-IDENTICAL (`5ccc3dc0…`, `931c50b1…` — the change is additive and no curation number moved), and the bridge re-read the entry also proposed found the radius stated NOWHERE — hexo-bridge at `4a96d13` deliberately does not vendor the htttx spec (`src/hexo_bridge/specs.py:7-8`, `README.md:126`), its ground-truth rule list (`core/__init__.py:6-27`) has no radius bullet, its wire models (`htttx_models.py:31-134`) have no radius field, and `docs/data-flow.md:51` assigns legality to the HeXO server without defining it; the likely origin of the "6" is the `six-in-a-row` FINISH REASON (`adapters/platforms/hexo_models.py:172`) or the `range(2, 6)` empty-cell search spiral at `core/move.py:145` whose siblings cap at 20, 20 and 50. Named residual: the htttx YAML itself was never on this disk and was not fetched, so the ruling rests on D-101 plus this corpus and not on the platform's own words — flips on a corpus, or a spec text, in which a placement the platform accepted sits beyond `LEGAL_RADIUS`, which is a rules-truth escalation to the operator and never a code change made in session; the radius-6 arm of SB-65 does not reopen without new platform evidence, and SB-65's colony-blocking arm stays UNVERIFIED under D-206.

D-219: RECORDS THE PLACEMENT-DISTANCE REVIEW ROUNDS — REVIEW-impl and RED-TEAM, both fresh contexts, both dispatched against revision `447803d`, both header-pinned to it, each having run its mutation and probe work in its own throwaway `git worktree` and removed it, and the round closes with `git worktree list` showing only the main checkout. BOTH REVIEWERS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME BLOCKING DEFECT, which is the strongest signal in this round and the reason the line above reads as it does: revision 447803d's D-218, its SB-65 amendment and both module docs asserted that a stone measured at distance `d >= 7` from every EARLIER stone is also `>= 7` from its own pair partner, and therefore that all 5024 far placements refuted radius 6. THE SECOND CONJUNCT IS FALSE FOR THE FIRST STONE OF A PAIR: the flat array is `[single, pair, pair, …]`, so a stone at an odd index has its partner at the NEXT index, outside the minimum entirely. Each reviewer produced its own corpus reproducer — `a7bf376041f893b0` turn 2, where `(7,-6)` measures 7 from the origin but `(2,-1)` is 2 from the origin and 5 from it, and `dff648bcbc1833d0` index 1 — and the implementing session reproduced both before any fix landed, per CLAUDE.md's minimal-reproducer rule. Blast radius, measured rather than estimated: 2812 of the 5024 are order-independent and sound, 2212 are not, and 50 of those are genuinely rescuable by reordering, so the claim overcounted its own evidence by 50 placements and 32 games. THE VERDICT NEVER MOVED — the RED-TEAM's independent turn-decomposed replay found 2991 of 8698 games (34.4%) admit NO ordering whatsoever under radius 6 against 0 of 8698 illegal under radius 8, a margin of roughly 93x over the error — which is exactly why this is recorded as an ADR line rather than a retraction: the conclusion was right, the stated proof was not, and in a rules-truth document those are not the same thing. The fix is the two-column split D-218 now describes, carried by a new sound criterion (last-stone-of-its-turn, read from `stones_in_turn` rather than from index parity, so rule 4's truncated turn falls out correctly — a stone with no turn-mate has nothing that could bridge it). REVIEW-impl's two MAJORs are also fixed and each now has a test that goes red without it: the ENTIRE `Display` impl was unbound (mutants skipping zero rows, collapsing the printed range and inflating the total all survived the whole suite, and that rendered block is the path D-218's numbers were transcribed from), now pinned by `the_rendered_block_lists_every_distance_in_range_including_the_zero_rows`; and "counts every game read rather than the eligible ones" was unbound workspace-wide (an eligibility filter left `cargo test --workspace` green, because this corpus happens to have zero exclusions), now pinned by `every_game_read_is_counted_including_the_ineligible_ones` over a fixture in which no game is eligible. Its MINOR m2 is taken too — the fixture is SHA-pinned like its sibling. WHAT THE REVIEWERS CONFIRMED CLEAN, worth recording because it bounds where the defect was: the histogram arithmetic itself reproduced exactly under two independent Python re-derivations (counts sum to 538553 = 547251 - 8698), both committed fixtures re-emit byte-identical, no file under pistol-core is touched at either revision, `Coord::distance` widens to i32 and survived all sixteen sign combinations at the i16 lattice edge, and `histogram_deterministic_across_runs` was checked NOT to be decorative — it goes red under a `HashMap` swap exactly as its comment predicts. Three RED-TEAM corroborations are folded into SB-65 rather than lost: stone ownership derived purely from the declared turn structure matches the corpus's independently exported `winner` field on all 8698 games, which kills the whole family of export-artefact hypotheses at once; the odd-r/even-r offset misreading of the coordinates produces MAX 12 with a smeared tail while the axial reading gives a hard cap, so the clean cap at 8 is evidence the reading is right; and measured against the PRE-TURN board only, the distribution spikes at 8, spikes again at exactly 16 and is absolutely zero at 17, which is the signature of "within 8 of the board, with the pair permitted to chain" and independently corroborates D-6/D-51's some-ordering rule from platform data — 866 stones in the corpus are legal ONLY because their partner rescues them. Accepted residuals, named: the shipped tool reports the conservative 2812 rather than the reviewers' stronger 4974, because the stronger number needs a per-turn counterfactual legality check at a radius the game does not have, and putting a second legality rule in pistol-cli is the rule-2 breach the convenience tempts; and `stats.rs` now sits exactly at rule 9's cap, so the next addition to it moves a responsibility out rather than growing the file. A THIRD ROUND, a fresh-context REVIEW-impl CONFIRMATION against revision `9ef2142`, closes the work: PASS, no BLOCKING and no MAJOR, both earlier MAJORs verified closed by mutants that now go red BY NAME, and 16 of 16 mutants killed — including the nine the confirming reviewer added of its own, of which the sharpest was `unrescuable_beyond` summing the RAW map, the exact overclaim this commit exists to prevent, killed by `only_order_independent_far_stones_refute_a_radius`. It re-derived every number independently in Python and confirmed all of them, and it proved the new criterion sound by the subset argument (only the WITHIN-turn order is free, so the board under any reordering is a subset of `moves[..i]` and a minimum over a subset is never smaller); its one attempted counterexample — a MID-GAME truncated turn, which would shift every later boundary and could mark a first-of-pair stone as last-of-turn — is recorded as REJECTED, unconstructible because `group_turns` emits a single only when the array runs out, corroborated by hexo-bridge's own ground-truth note at `core/__init__.py:22-24` and by the ownership-vs-`winner` parity holding on all 8698 games. Its three MINORs are all fixed here: D-218 had stated a reason that did not support its own number ("fifty rescuable, WHICH IS WHY the count is 2812" — 5024 minus 50 is 4974, not 2812; 2812 comes from the stricter order-independence criterion discarding 2212 stones as unproven rather than disproven), SB-65 still leaned on the raw 5024 in the bullet defending the verdict, and `unrescuable_beyond` had NO production call site at all, so the headline 2812 was a hand-sum off the rendered rows — the precise transcription path that carried the original false claim. The rendered block now prints `order-independent beyond 6` through that function against a named `CLAIMED_RADIUS`, which puts the refuting number under the rendered-block test — flips never; this line is history.

D-220: THE OFFICIAL Eval::delta BENCH VERDICT IS **PASS IN BOTH BANDS, INSIDE THE PRE-REGISTERED [1.4, 2.5] BRACKET** — D-215's successor, written from the operator-hardware run this number was reserved for, and the reservation is now spent. COMMAND ACTUALLY RUN: `tools/bench_delta.sh rev:f31cffe rev:bdfca3f 5`, which is NOT the literal this line reserved (`tools/bench_delta.sh f31cffe bdfca3f 5`) and could not be: the per-side revision mode landed between the reservation and the run (D-226), so a bare `f31cffe` is now refused by name as a binary that is not executable, and the reserved literal is recorded here as superseded rather than quietly rewritten. GOVERNING REVISION of the harness: the amended `tools/bench_delta.sh` whose measurement half is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reviewed original, verified line for line from `# Positions and their bands` onward — pinned config, NODES=50000, DEPTH=2, EARLY_MAX=17, SESSION_TIMEOUT=900, the >= 5 reps floor, the 10%-of-median IQR gate, the per-position node-identity assertion and the 1.15/1.4/2.5 thresholds with their verdict wording, none of which moved. MACHINE: AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core, 16 threads, single-thread instrument mode. INSTRUMENT: `configs/instrument_v0.toml` sha256 3579855e7cf23d07c54c431e42656818838230aded9d921215cad1cee8b9ec13 at radius 2 (D-194), `configs/eval_v0_weights.toml` sha256 41ef549666d787bf404b2922ce644b7797a49680f09366e6fef6239b3f91f2c3, `bench_positions_v1.txt` sha256 931c50b19411eef5aaf0385df46782bb2babbf3443e65a6e56fe7bd169906e47, 24 positions (12 early, 12 late), 5 reps, both budgets. BINARY DIGESTS, built by the harness from the two revisions in throwaway worktrees: baseline `f31cffe` -> 09068541ecaef3a59caf2230eaf444f9904b7f81bbd996e7bdbdf0c04734361f, candidate `bdfca3f` -> 681e1a244c4906feb0d0aba75c3c1b6bd49dbeaa888e6121a498cf4f1c6816d2 — BIT-FOR-BIT the digests D-215 recorded as advisory dev-machine numbers, on the same machine, so THIS IS A RE-MEASUREMENT WITH PINNED PROVENANCE AND NOT AN INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, and the line says so rather than letting the agreement below read as corroboration it is not. THE NUMBERS. Early band: nps 37988.1 -> 82844.2, RATIO 2.181; time-to-depth-2 7811.0 ms -> 3465.0 ms, ratio 2.254, |deviation| 0.073. Late band: nps 35155.2 -> 72552.6, RATIO 2.064; time-to-depth-2 41687.0 ms -> 18777.0 ms, ratio 2.220, |deviation| 0.156. THE IQR GATE PASSED WITH ROOM: the widest spread in the run is 1.07% of its median (late-band candidate nps), against a gate that withholds a verdict above 10% — early band 0.33/0.45/0.37/0.98%, late band 0.44/1.07/0.82/0.79% for baseline-nps, candidate-nps, baseline-ttd and candidate-ttd respectively. Per-position node identity held between the binaries under both budgets in every rep, which is also the radius-2 search-identity evidence D-214 cites. Time-to-depth is the declared cross-check and not independent evidence — nodes-to-depth are identical by search identity, so its ratio is the nps ratio over the depth-2 node mix — and it agrees with the fixed-node ratio to within 0.073 and 0.156, which is what a cross-check agreeing looks like. THE RADIUS CONFOUND NAMED IN D-215 DID NOT BITE: the bracket descends from a radius-3 profile (D-192) while this run is radius 2, and the result landed inside the bracket anyway, so no finding about the confound is owed and no threshold was touched in either direction. THE VERDICT IS THEREFORE PASS ON THE OPERATOR'S STANDING RULING, with neither of its two branches reached — nothing is above 2.5 so no calibration note is owed, and nothing is below 1.15 so no abort and no revert. `Eval::delta` (D-214) is accepted on this evidence. Flips never; this line is the measurement. A later engine measuring differently is a NEW line about a new engine, not an amendment to this one.

D-221: THE POST-DELTA RE-PROFILE PRE-REGISTRATION IS AT REVISION 2, WITH THE OPERATOR'S THRESHOLD RULINGS AND AN H3 SPLIT, AND IT GOVERNS NOTHING UNTIL ITS OWN REVIEW PASSES. Revision 1 (at `bdfca3f`, registered by D-216) was attacked by a fresh-context governing-revision review under D-195 and returned FAILS AS GOVERNING REVISION on one BLOCKING and two MAJOR findings, so no measurement it authorized was ever taken — which is the law working, not a setback. F1 BLOCKING: the H3 visibility precondition could FALSE-PASS, because btree symbols survive in the binary through the apply/undo SURGERY path while `delta`'s `get()` is inlined and leaves no frame, so H3 could read ~0% with the structure exonerated by symbol invisibility; the pre-registered command was doubly broken besides — `grep -c 'btree.*search'` matched the substring `pistol_search` (REPRODUCED: the one match in the dev binary is a `SpecFromIterNested` over `btree::set::IntoIter<Coord>` inside `pistol_search::candidates::within_radius`, nothing to do with map descent), and `> 0` was a shell REDIRECTION, not a comparison. F2 MAJOR: the 70% under-delivery bar was derived from D-192's radius-3 pooled share while the run is radius 2, where full success would read ~71–72% and falsely CONFIRM under-delivery. F3 MAJOR: the fallback probe's measured cost fed no rule. F4–F6 MINOR/NOTE: double-fire precedence, bench-verdict conditioning and binary digests, "pooled" cited rather than inherited. THE OPERATOR RULED NINE THRESHOLDS, all APPROVED as proposed and each restated at its point of use with its derivation: BAR_a = ceil_0.5(100 - (100 - P2) x 1.4 + 3.0) over the control run's MEASURED radius-2 P2, with 1.4 fixed as the bracket floor and NEVER the measured speedup — a bar built from the thing it judges is no bar; instrument margin M = 3.0 pp decomposed 0.9 sampling + 1.0 frame-pointer + 1.0 Amdahl idealisation; positive control V_ord >= 10.0% pooled at `f31cffe`, below which the METHOD failed and every H3 verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, never REFUTE; visibility check V_delta >= 1.0% pooled, whose conservatism is recorded rather than hidden (a genuinely cheap map read reading under 1% yields INCONCLUSIVE where REFUTE would have been right — the safe direction, costing one re-measurement instead of closing a real question on evidence that never existed); probe cost C <= 5% accepted / 5–15% accepted with a near-bar INCONCLUSIVE zone / > 15% the profile is not the workload and the probe run is INVALID; H1'-b >= 20% and H3 >= 15% unchanged. THE H3 SPLIT is an amendment taken inside D-216's pre-run window and it is the substantive change: H3-e (pistol-eval's `BTreeMap<Window, Counts>` share) adjudicates at >= 15% and licenses WP-1.5a's window-storage option matrix; H3-c (the candidate-set `BTreeSet` share) is MEASUREMENT ONLY with no licensed action, because that structure is scheduled for supersession by WP-1.5b's Staged policy, because full-set iteration and window-keyed lookup are different access patterns so one is not evidence about the other, and because splitting RAISES the effective bar for the expensive structural work package, which is the correct direction. A FACT THE SPLIT RULING DID NOT HAVE, found while writing the counting rule and recorded because it strengthens the same conclusion: the binary holds FOUR btree families, not two — of 94 demangled `alloc::collections::btree::` symbols, 7 are over `<pistol_eval::window::Window, pistol_eval::handcrafted::Counts>`, 6 over the `BTreeSet<Coord>` shape (shared by `pistol_search::candidates` AND `pistol_core::movegen`'s region set, indistinguishable by type arguments alone, hence attributed by CALLER frame — `within_radius` does not survive as a symbol, `candidate_cells` does), and SIXTEEN over `<pistol_core::coord::Coord, pistol_core::board::Player>`, which is `Board::stones` itself, touched by every place/undo on every node; the rest are `toml` and `gimli` off the hot path. D-193's 23.21% therefore spans at least four structures and its largest symbol family is one that neither registered hypothesis names, so the pre-registered classifier counts all four, names every unclassified symbol individually, and lets only H3-e adjudicate. The three counting commands were exercised on a synthetic six-sample `perf script` block before commit — one stack per family, each landing in its own bucket — a syntax-and-attribution check on invented input, never evidence about the engine. FOUR FLAGGED CALLS: an ABOVE-BRACKET bench is a PASS plus a recorded calibration note (our prediction machinery under-predicted; the perf claim stands); a BELOW-BRACKET bench KEEPS the change flagged under-bracket and the profile runs, with the expected H1'-a under-delivery flag recorded as ONE fact reported by two instruments rather than two findings; the control at `f31cffe` is a FULL-workload run because a method validated on a slice is not validated on the workload; H3 adjudicates before H1', both off that control run. AND experiment records under docs/experiments/ are EXEMPT from rule 9's soft cap BY CLASS — a governing document's single-artifact integrity outweighs the file-size discipline, and the mechanized gate's `.rs` scope is deliberate, not incidental. Flips by amendment BEFORE the first run it governs, which reopens its review however small the diff (D-195); after a sample is taken, never. The fresh-context review of THIS revision is outstanding at this commit and its verdict lands in its own successor line; until that line says PASS, no measurement this document authorizes may be taken.

D-222: THE TIME-MATCHED r2-vs-r3 PLAY-MODE EXPERIMENT IS DEFERRED, NOT CANCELLED, AND `configs/play_v0.toml` STAYS AT RADIUS 3 — amending D-212's "licensed and not run" to a dated deferral with a named trigger. The radius-3 setting is already justified by WP-1.3's 1.9x wall-clock finding, and WP-1.5b supersedes the candidate-radius policy outright with a Staged generator, so measuring the radius knob now is spend on code with weeks to live and would produce a number whose subject no longer exists when it lands. The deferral flips ONLY if platform play precedes WP-1.5b — at that point the radius in the shipping play config is a live question again, D-212's licensed paired experiment is the way to answer it, and this line is the record that it was deferred on schedule grounds rather than forgotten.

D-223: THE POST-DELTA RE-PROFILE'S ADJUDICATING HYPOTHESES ARE RETIRED AND docs/experiments/delta_reprofile_prereg.md BECOMES AN OBSERVATION RECORD — the profile registered by D-216 and amended by D-221 cannot adjudicate what it registers, and its licensing answer was already determined by the record, so spending an operator run on it would have bought ceremony. Six fresh-context rounds in one session established it — one governing-revision review and five red-teams, the seventh on this document counting the review that failed revision 1 — and each finding was reproduced at least twice. THE QUANTITY WAS NEVER THE COST: there are ZERO `get` and ZERO `entry` instantiations over `<pistol_eval::window::Window, pistol_eval::handcrafted::Counts>` in the release binary — the seven surviving eval-family symbols are `map::entry::Entry`, `OccupiedEntry` x2, `VacantEntry` and `node::BalancingContext` x3, i.e. insert/split/steal/merge/remove — because the search descent is inlined into `delta`'s `get()`, `apply`'s `entry()` and `undo`'s removal alike, so H3-e counted btree node RESTRUCTURING and never map ACCESS, and `V_delta ≡ 0` was provable from the symbol table before any run (the §4.5 precondition could not pass and the §4.6 probe was the certain path, not a fallback). THE PROPOSED REPAIR FAILED TWICE OVER: building with `debug = "line-tables-only"` and dropping `--no-inline` does surface the descent (inside `delta` the line tables resolve `search_tree`/`get`/`search_node`/`find_key_index`/`cmp`, 81 resolved frames carrying the literal `pistol_eval::window::Window`, and `delta`'s 291-instruction body is byte-identical so codegen is unperturbed) — but `perf script` renders DWARF frames with their short `DW_AT_name`, so `pistol_search::ordering::order` prints as `order (inlined)` and every caller-keyed literal in the document goes from 99.4% to 0.00% on the same `perf.data`; and on a calibrated synthetic the inline-expanded instrument reported 0.00% FOR A COMPONENT THAT WAS 76% OF RUNTIME (LLVM unrolled the loop, the inline record and the line numbers vanished, 479 of ~824 code bytes resolving to line 0, no diagnostic, `debug = 2` no cure), with a 4-8 pp systematic LOW bias where records do survive and 62 of 296 instructions inside pistol's own `delta` carrying no line information at all. THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY KNOWN: `delta` sits on ~56.5% of samples and its body is 18 `BTreeMap::get` calls against ~15-20 straight-line operations of other work per window, predicting a 34-48% eval-map share, so P(H3-e >= 15%) > 0.95 before the run and no bar registered at that point could fail — registering one would have been the contamination the pre-registration existed to prevent. H1'-a IS RETIRED RATHER THAN REPLICATED, redundant with the official bench in revision 2's own words ("one fact reported by two instruments, not two independent findings"), and `BAR_a`, `S_min` and the instrument margin M go with it; H1'-b survives as an observation at ~56.5% against its 20% line. AND ONE RUN PER BINARY WAS NEVER ENOUGH: eight replications give SD 0.457 pp over a 1.24 pp range with background load worth ~+1 pp, against a document that took one run and covered the gap with a theoretical 3.0 pp margin while D-215's own bench discipline demands >= 5 IQR-gated reps for a cheaper claim. WHAT SURVIVED IS WORTH RECORDING: the 15% bar was correct by measurement — standalone benches of the matrix's own options give k = 7.2-7.5 (open addressing) and 7.9-8.5 (dense array) on the lookup path, `1/(1 - p + p/k) >= 1.15` returns EXACTLY 15.00% at k = 7.67, and every defensible k lands inside [14.8%, 17.4%], narrower than the document's own margin; a proposal to re-derive the bar at `k_floor = 3` was rejected because 3 is outside the measured range and the rule would have REFUTED, at a true 18% share, work whose measured payoff is 1.184x. The observation profile that remains licenses nothing. Flips if an instrument appears that attributes an inlined callee's cycles without a codegen change and without DWARF short-name renaming — `perf annotate` over `delta`'s descent range is the nearest candidate and is not ruled out, only unregistered.

D-224: AMENDS D-221'S btree CENSUS AND ITS "LARGEST FAMILY" CLAIM, both falsified by this round and both in an append-only line, so the correction lands here rather than by edit. D-221 wrote that beyond the 7 eval, 6 `<Coord, SetValZST>` and 16 `<Coord, Player>` symbols "the rest are `toml` and `gimli` off the hot path": 7 + 6 + 16 + 20 (gimli) + 39 (toml) = 88 of 94, and the SIX unaccounted are four std `<usize, std::sys::pal::unix::stack_overflow::thread_info::ThreadInfo>` maps plus two `<alloc::vec::Vec<Coord> as SpecFromIterNested<Coord, Filter<alloc::collections::btree::set::IntoIter<Coord>, pistol_search::candidates::within_radius::{closure#0}>>>` symbols — which are on 4.21% of pooled samples, MORE than the eval family itself post-delta at 2.89%, and are therefore emphatically on the hot path and the single largest entry in the classifier's `other` bucket. Separately, `<Coord, Player>` at 16 is NOT "the largest symbol family in the binary" as the retired §4.2 stated and D-221 implied — `toml` has 39 and `gimli` 20 — it is the largest ENGINE-side family, which is what both places meant and neither said. One further correction for whoever reads the `other` bucket: folding that `SpecFromIterNested` frame into the candidate family would OVER-count, because 442 of its 642 samples have `Board::is_legal_placement` as the leaf — the legality filter, not btree descent — which is the inclusive-versus-self trap D-193 already recorded at a different site. Flips never; these are counts.

D-225: WP-1.5a IS LICENSED ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN ON A PROFILE THRESHOLD, AND ITS OPTION MATRIX GAINS AN OPTION AND LOSES A CONSTRAINT. Licensed because D-223's §0.4 prediction puts the eval map at 34-48% of samples and standalone benches put its replacements at k = 5.1-8.5, not because any bar was crossed — the WP opens its D-196 matrix on that basis. THE OPTION THE EARLIER LIST OMITTED: packing `Window` (`{ axis: Axis, start: Coord { q: i16, r: i16 } }`) into an order-preserving `u64` key, `axis << 32 | (q + 32768) << 16 | (r + 32768)`, which is EXACTLY the derived `(axis, q, r)` lexicographic order so `BTreeMap` iteration order and `PartialEq` are untouched — measured 1.54x-1.89x on the lookup path and 1.25-1.30x on surgery in a standalone bench, for roughly twenty lines and no structural change, and it lowers both p and k for every structural option beside it (open addressing against a PACKED btree measures k = 4.1, not 7.4), so the matrix must evaluate it FIRST and recompute the others against it. THE CONSTRAINT THAT DOES NOT APPLY: `self.windows` is used in exactly three operations — `entry()` in `apply`, `entry()` in `undo`, `get()` in `delta` — and is NEVER ITERATED, so its ordering is unobservable and an unordered or hashed store cannot influence move choice; D-32's no-hasher-near-a-played-value rule is about `Board` occupancy, which IS iterated, and does not reach the eval's window map. The WP still owes its own pre-registration under rule 5 — named hotspot, expected-gain bracket, abort threshold — reviewed in fresh context before implementation, and its bracket belongs in whole-engine nps against `tools/bench_delta.sh`, the instrument that moots every question the retired profile could not answer. Flips if `self.windows` ever gains an iterating caller, which would put the determinism law back in front of every unordered option.

D-226: `tools/bench_delta.sh` GAINS A PER-SIDE REVISION MODE AND THE MEASUREMENT IT WAS PRE-REGISTERED WITH DOES NOT MOVE — the successor D-215 said its official line would need, taken here rather than inside D-220, whose reservation forbids anything else taking that number. Each positional side is now either a path to an executable or `rev:<commit-ish>`, resolved independently. HOW A SIDE IS NAMED was settled by an option matrix under D-196's process and attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM: a whole-run `--revisions A B` flag is WITHDRAWN because it cannot express the case Stage 1 actually runs — an UNCOMMITTED candidate against a COMMITTED baseline — and forces it through `git stash create`, which silently omits untracked files, so the operator would measure a candidate missing its newest source file; auto-detection of executable-versus-revision was rejected outright as the silent misclassification rule 3 forbids. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK on the adopted per-side form: a file literally named `rev:x` is shadowed by the prefix — impossible in practice, and unlike auto-detection the prefix is EXPLICIT, so nothing is ever guessed. THE BUILD STRATEGY is `git worktree add --detach` per `rev:` side with cargo's in-worktree target directory, verified against a silent shared-target fallback by reading (`cargo metadata` reports the in-worktree path, no `.cargo/config.toml` at any level, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`); its strongest surviving attack is that `git archive` — option (d) — produced the design's own build-provenance evidence successfully, so (d)'s rejection rests SOLELY on the stash discriminator, which is not a safety property, and (d) is unadopted only because `worktree add --detach` is this project's own idiom (D-217, D-219) and a second extraction path would be a second thing to keep right. THE INSTRUMENT-CONSTANCY GUARD is a HANDSHAKE-IDENTITY comparison over the ENUMERATED set `config`, `eval`, `tt_bytes`, `candidate_policy`, `weights_sha256`, taken from each process's own `id` lines: digesting the two revisions' committed configs with `git show` was withdrawn because it attests bytes no engine read — D-198's hole reintroduced inside the guard built to close it — and on a dirty tree it compares COMMITTED bytes while the run reads WORKING-TREE bytes. What the guard is worth is stated in the header rather than implied: it catches two binaries PARSING THE SAME LIVE DOCUMENTS DIFFERENTLY, and it CANNOT catch the two revisions having shipped different instruments, because neither process ever reads its own revision's config. THE REVIEW ROUND FAILED THIS WORK and the failures are the reason this line reads as it does; each was reproduced in a throwaway clone before its fix landed. BLOCKING, found INDEPENDENTLY BY BOTH REVIEWERS: `BASE="$(resolve_side …)"` is a command substitution, so the subshell's `WORKTREES` never reached the parent and `fail`'s `exit 1` left only the subshell — and `cleanup` ran `git worktree prune` BEFORE `rm -rf "$WORK"`, so prune correctly declined an entry whose directory still existed and the directory was then deleted underneath it; a build failure LEAKED A PRUNABLE WORKTREE INTO THE LIVE REPOSITORY, breaking the exact invariant the code above it cited (REPRODUCED at a 2 s build timeout, `git worktree list` showing `wt.base … prunable`; the root cause isolated to `V=""; f(){ V="$V x"; }; R="$(f)"` printing `parent V=[]`). The resolver now sets a global, cleanup removes then deletes then prunes in that order, a removal that fails is reported instead of swallowed and its entry KEPT for the retry, and the round's closing invariant is PRINTED — `git worktree list` at exit — so a report cites the script's own output for it instead of a human's recollection. MAJOR, both reviewers: the script re-`mktemp -d`ed into `$WORK` and replaced the trap, leaking the first directory on every run and destroying the worktree backstop entirely at the same stroke, in a script whose own comment says /tmp is RAM here (REPRODUCED: five runs, five leaked directories); the second mktemp is gone. MAJOR: the guard diffed `grep '^id '` WHOLESALE rather than the five enumerated fields, so a workspace VERSION BUMP between baseline and candidate aborted the bench with a message blaming `configs/instrument_v0.toml` for a field that document does not contain (REPRODUCED) — a false-refusal path the design deliberately scoped away; the comparison is now the enumerated set, the refusal names the fields that actually differ, and an out-of-set difference prints as a NOTE because two revisions differ in `name`/`version` by construction. MAJOR: `[ -x "$side" ]` accepted a bare name, which bash PATH-resolves at exec time while `sha256sum` reads the cwd-relative file, so `binary_sha256` could attest a file that never ran and the same-digest refusal — the only defence against a silent false ABORT — was defeated by two spellings of one engine (REPRODUCED, two digests, one binary); each side is now `command -v`'d and `realpath`'d before it is digested, and `-f` refuses the directory and the FIFO that `[ -x ]` admits and that hung the script with no output at all. NAMED RESIDUAL, recorded rather than closed: a wrapper script that `exec`s another engine is a genuinely different file, so its digest is truthful and the same-digest refusal still cannot see through it — that case is caught by reading the two digests, not by the script. Flips if a bench ever needs each side to read ITS OWN revision's instrument documents, which is the config-treatment A/B option (f) was named for and which this pinned-config bench is not.

D-227: THE DRY-RUN RULE IS PROCESS LAW IN CLAUDE.md — a pre-registration's literal commands are exercised before its review passes, on an input of the SAME KIND as the registered workload and never on the registered workload itself. The rule exists because D-221's counting commands passed a synthetic six-sample dry run and still shipped broken: `grep -c 'btree.*search'` matched the substring `pistol_search` and `> 0` was a shell REDIRECTION rather than a comparison, and D-223 then had to retire the document those commands governed. A synthetic stand-in exercises SYNTAX; only a real instance of the kind exercises ATTRIBUTION, which is the half that failed. ONE SENTENCE DEVIATES from the text the governing design revision declared final and the deviation is recorded here rather than reverted, because REVIEW-impl was right that the rule needs it: "The dry run is not a governed sample and does not consume the pre-registration's first run." Without it the paragraph collides with the one immediately above, which says the governing revision must pass review BEFORE THE FIRST RUN IT GOVERNS — a reader could conclude the dry run is that first run and that the rule contradicts itself. The rule constrains the dry run's INPUT and constrains no reviewer, who may run anything including the registered workload, and it is not mechanized: no script checks it. Flips if a dry run is ever shown to have contaminated a pre-registration by consuming the very sample it was meant to protect, at which point the same-kind constraint tightens to same-kind-and-discarded.

D-228: THE PROPORTIONALITY RULE IS PROCESS LAW IN CLAUDE.md — a pre-registration states what its governed run COSTS in wall time, operator attention and machine hours, so the proportion between the document and the run is visible on the document's own face; and where the run is cheap, doubt about the instrument is answered by REPLICATION and by a SECOND INSTRUMENT whose agreement criterion is registered before either runs, never by a margin derived to defend a single sample. Its ground is D-223's arithmetic: the retired re-profile took ONE run per binary and covered the gap with a theoretical 3.0 pp margin decomposed sampling-plus-frame-pointer-plus-Amdahl, while eight replications of the same measurement gave SD 0.457 pp over a 1.24 pp range — a derived margin is the instrument of a measurement that cannot be taken again, and it was the wrong instrument for a workload measured in seconds, in a document whose sibling bench discipline (D-215) already demanded five IQR-gated reps for a cheaper claim. THE "WHAT THIS DOES NOT CATCH" CLAUSE LANDED IN CLAUDE.md RATHER THAN HERE, contrary to the governing design's assignment of it to these ADR lines, and it stays there: a rule whose limits are stated only in a decision log is a rule the next reader applies without them, and the limit is sharp enough to belong beside the rule — neither this rule nor D-227's is mechanized, and neither would have caught D-223's actual killing finding, that the answer was already known before the run was taken. That defect is judged, not checked, and no paragraph added here legislates it. Flips if a mechanized check for either rule is ever found — a pre-registration's cost statement is machine-readable in principle — at which point the unmechanized disclaimer is what needs amending.

D-229: THE SETUP-COST QUESTION IS REGISTERED AND ITS GOVERNED RUN WAS NOT TAKEN, so this line records the design, the one number the project actually has, and the future work package — not a finding. The question: how large is the fixed, node-count-independent component of an instrument-mode search's wall time, split into a per-PROCESS part and a per-`newgame` part, with the transposition table the prime suspect, since `tt_bytes = 268435456` is a REQUEST and `previous_power_of_two(268435456/96) * 96` allocates 192 MiB that `Table::new` writes once per process and `Table::clear` writes on every `newgame`. THE THRESHOLD IS DELETED, and its deletion is the most important thing this line carries: revision 2's bar was computable before the run and its two candidate denominators STRADDLED it — `C + P_fixed/24` gives 0.021 NOT MATERIAL, `P_fixed + C` gives 0.069 MATERIAL — with the choice between them made after the exploratory numbers were already in hand, which is a post-hoc threshold move in effect and is D-223's retirement ground with the sign reversed. The design therefore registers a PREDICTION, not a bar: the SESSION exposure is about 2 % of a 50 000-node search's per-position wall, not material, and the TT is why. ANSWERED BY READING, WITH NO RUN ATTACHED: `tools/bench_delta.sh`'s reported nps and time-to-depth have ZERO exposure to this cost, because `search()` takes its `Instant::now()` at search.rs:163, AFTER `check_root`, `reset_to` and `new_generation` at 154-157, so the engine's own `time` excludes every component in question; the real exposures are exactly two, an operator's total wall time for a run and an external driver timing from its own send, which is the `movetime` ceiling contract's stated blind spot. THE ONE MEASUREMENT THE PROJECT HAS is not from this pre-registration at all: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` measures `setup_fraction_pct` on every run from its own wall clock against the sum of the engine's reported times, and over the registered 24-position session at `0f6c495` on a Ryzen 7 3700X it reads 1.66-1.71 % across three runs whose invariant blocks were byte-identical — the session-level exposure the prediction names, at the prediction's own size, taken by an instrument that is not the registered one. An exploratory three-rep budget sweep beside it (entries 3, 16 and the disqualified 17, one config) put the per-PROCESS residual at 33-44 ms and FLAT in the budget from 5 000 to 500 000 nodes, which is the signature of a fixed cost and is why the prediction was written the way it was; those numbers are exploratory, not the registered run, and no line here rests on them. THE FUTURE WORK PACKAGE is named on that measured size and on no bar: a session-level setup cost under ~2 % buys nothing worth a code change today, so the WP is DEFERRED with the trigger written down — it opens when a harness runs ONE PROCESS PER SEARCH, where the per-process 33-44 ms is paid 24 times over instead of once and the exposure is an order of magnitude larger. Flips when that pre-registration passes its own fresh-context review and its run is taken, which is what turns this line's prediction into a finding; and separately if `tt_bytes` moves, since the whole suspicion rests on the size of the table being cleared.

D-230: THE BASELINE SNAPSHOT IS MEASUREMENT INFRASTRUCTURE, NOT A BENCHMARK, AND ITS RECORD CLAIMS INVARIANCE ONLY OVER WHAT IS ACTUALLY INVARIANT. `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` is a STANDING before/after instrument every Stage-1 strength WP's report cites beside its SPRT verdict, so a change that wins on strength while losing a third of its node rate cannot land without that being visible. IT LICENSES NOTHING: it pre-registers no hypothesis, sets no threshold and accepts no change — rule 6's judge is SPRT over paired balanced openings and `tools/bench_delta.sh` remains the harness that carries a hotspot, a bracket and an abort threshold. That distinction is what keeps it clear of D-14 and rule 5, which say a benchmark ships with the first perf-sensitive change and its pre-registered numbers, not before: this is the same class as pistol-arena, an instrument with no hypothesis of its own that per-change pre-registrations then cite, and it does not implement `bench`. THE RECORD FORMAT is the arena report's idiom (D-139, D-147, D-160, D-161) rather than JSON or TOML, both rejected as growing a serializer D-139 already ruled against, and rather than a flat `key value` file with a per-line `measured` marker, which was WITHDRAWN on a reproduced attack: a marker cannot mark the ABSENCE of a line, and a wall-clock cap decides whether a ladder depth's line exists at all, so a partial run is a DIFFERENT KIND TOKEN (`baseline_snapshot_incomplete`) and not a flag — no consumer can diff a partial record against a complete one. Key is the leading tokens and value is the rest of the line, because the engine's own handshake carries multi-token values and a rule that refused a space would refuse the engine. THE REVIEW ROUND FAILED THIS WORK, and every finding below was reproduced in a throwaway clone before its fix landed. BLOCKING: the record's central claim was FALSE, because `revision <sha> dirty|clean` sat ABOVE the `# timing` marker while the token is a function of the WORKING TREE AT RUN TIME, not of the revision — and the loop was self-inflicted, since the record is an artifact the gate was extended to recognize BECAUSE records land in the repository, and a record landing in the repository dirties the tree for the next run (REPRODUCED in a clean clone at one revision, machine, binary, corpus and budget: `-revision 11b60417… clean` / `+revision 11b60417… dirty`, the two invariant blocks differing in that token and nothing else); the token moved below the marker as `timing tree`, and the shipped test could STRUCTURALLY never have caught it because it took both snapshots back to back under one tree state, the only arrangement in which the defect is invisible. BLOCKING: the ladder's terminal reasons were ASSERTED and never checked — any nonzero exit was recorded as the wall-clock `cap`, so a crashed or refusing engine yielded exit 0 and a record stating the cap had fired (REPRODUCED with an engine exiting 3), and anything short of the requested depth was recorded as `mate`, so a run stopping at depth 1 with `score cp 308` produced `ladder_terminal … mate` one line below the score contradicting it, and an engine emitting NOTHING produced a COMPLETE record asserting a mate at depth 0 (both REPRODUCED through the shipped `--binary` flag, patching nothing); `timeout` reports exactly 124 or 137 and everything else now fails by name, and `mate` is now read from the engine's own validated score. BLOCKING: a corpus entry with no stones count was silently accepted where the sibling `tools/bench_delta.sh` guards the IDENTICAL expression three lines from where this script used the correct idiom — exit 0, a COMPLETE token, a raw `[: integer expected` on stderr, the band silently `late` and the WHOLE ENTRY LINE as the record's `stones` value; and a CRLF corpus is the same gap with a different payload, since `[ 15$'\r' -le 17 ]` is ACCEPTED by bash, putting a bare CR mid-line in the invariant block where two records differing only in a corpus's line endings look identical in any diff viewer (both REPRODUCED).
