MAJOR, from mutation testing in a separate worktree: five of ten mutants SURVIVED both named tests, which bound the record's SHAPE and none of its SEMANTICS — dropping the `newgame` that D-7 requires (not a no-op: on the real 24-position corpus the invariant block diverges in 46 lines as `hashfull` carries across positions, 0/1 becoming 2,3,4,5,7,7,8,10,11,12,13,14 — REPRODUCED), nailing the kind token to `complete`, deleting the `ladder_terminal` line, having the SCRIPT re-derive the weights digest D-198 says the ENGINE must print, and nailing the setup flag to `ok`. All five now die: the session script is asserted to carry one `newgame` per position, and the suite gained a STUB ENGINE driven through the shipped `--binary` flag, because the semantic claims are all claims about what the script does with an answer it did not expect and the real engine cannot be made to give one. ACCEPTED MINORS, each with its own reason: the `late_mid` ladder rung is now chosen BY BAND rather than by the magic index `sed -n 13p`, which on a short corpus named an EARLY position `late_mid` three lines below the record labelling the same entry `early` — on the registered corpus the first late entry IS entry 13, so the registered record is unchanged; `setup_fraction_pct` gained SETUP-NEGATIVE and SETUP-UNMEASURED, because a negative fraction was flagged `ok` and an unmeasurable wall clock printed `0.00`, a PERFECT setup score for a run that measured nothing; the corpus session and the handshake gained loud timeouts, since `[ -x ]` admits a FIFO and a read that never returns is indistinguishable from a slow machine without one; the `--binary` name is `command -v`'d and `realpath`'d before it is digested for the same reason D-226 gives; the score parser rejects what it cannot read rather than leaking a bare `pv` token into the score field; and `tools/artifact_check.sh`'s content recognizer now trims a leading BOM and leading whitespace, a bypass PRE-EXISTING on the `arena_report` branch and copied verbatim into the snapshot's, where a leading-space line splits to exactly the tokens the recognizer's own comment says a consumer reads. TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS from the enumerated design, recorded rather than taken silently: the record carries `hashfull`, one field beyond the enumerated schema, and it earns its place — it is the field that exposed the `newgame` carryover above; and `--binary` is a flag the workload-versus-budget split does not name, workload-affecting and not budget-affecting, so a DEBUG-build record is indistinguishable from a release one except by `binary_sha256`, which is why that line is in the record. Flips if a Stage-1 WP ever needs the snapshot to adjudicate rather than to inform, at which point it stops being infrastructure and owes rule 5 a pre-registered bracket of its own.

D-231: `tools/bench_delta.sh` IS DRIVEN BY A TEST, AND THE BYTE-IDENTICAL CERTIFICATION NOW CARRIES ONE NAMED EXCEPTION. The round-three BLOCKING was a SILENT ABORT in the branch F7 added to stop a false refusal: the NOTE for a handshake difference outside the guarded set ran `diff -u … | grep … | sed …` as the last command in a `then` BODY, `diff` exits 1 whenever it has anything to say, `pipefail` propagated it and `set -e` killed the script — exit 1 with no `FAIL:` line, no identity block, no rep and no verdict, on the difference D-226 itself calls INEVITABLE between two revisions (REPRODUCED twice independently, once with two stub engines differing only in `id version` and once as a three-line shell reduction). It did NOT touch D-220's numbers: `f31cffe` and `bdfca3f` emit identical `id` lines and the run log carries the identity block, so the branch was never taken. The NOTE now uses the idiom written two lines above it — the diff redirected into `$WORK` inside the `if !` CONDITION, the file read afterwards. THE CLASS WAS SWEPT and found exactly one more instance, `grep -v '^#' "$FIXTURE" | grep .`, where an empty fixture aborted one line before the `COUNT -gt 0` refusal written for it; that line is inside the region D-220 and D-226 certify as BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reviewed original, so it is FIXED and the certification is corrected here rather than in either line: D-220's sentence describes the harness revision that GOVERNED ITS RUN, preserved at stash object `1edbb61`, and remains true of it; from this line on the measurement half carries one named exception, `|| true` on that one pipeline, which writes the same bytes as before on every fixture with an entry and differs only where the old code died without a diagnostic. Everything the certification is about — the pinned config, NODES, DEPTH, EARLY_MAX, SESSION_TIMEOUT, the reps floor, the IQR gate, the node-identity assertion and the 1.15/1.4/2.5 thresholds with their verdict wording — is untouched. AND THE REAL FINDING BEHIND BOTH DEFECTS: NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY DROVE THIS SCRIPT AT ALL, which is why two rounds of defects in the harness that produced the official perf verdict were each found by a reviewer running it by hand. `crates/pistol-cli/tests/bench_delta_tests.rs` drives the shipped script in a THROWAWAY GIT REPOSITORY holding copies of the four paths it reads — never the live checkout, whose worktree admin the script's own cleanup writes to — with two stub engines differing only in `id version`, and asserts the run reaches the NOTE, the identity block, the reps, the node-identity line, both band verdicts and the closing line; a second test pins the empty-fixture refusal by name. Also fixed there: `WORKTREES` is an ARRAY, since `for wt in $WORKTREES` word-split on the spaces a TMPDIR may contain, so the removal loop iterated path fragments and its rule-3 WARNING was unreachable — no leak followed, because `rm -rf "$WORK"` precedes `git worktree prune`, but the safety came from the ORDERING and not from the loop meant to provide it. Flips if the measurement half ever needs a second exception, at which point "byte-identical with named exceptions" has stopped being a claim worth making and the honest move is to re-review the measurement in full.

D-232: THE SNAPSHOT'S THIRD ROUND — the record now states only what it read, and its test suite is no longer VACUOUS. Every finding below was reproduced before its fix landed. (1) The determinism test was vacuous IN THE TREE IT IS RUN IN: `snapshot_deterministic_across_a_clean_and_a_dirty_working_tree` needed its first snapshot to see a CLEAN tree, and the work under review is uncommitted, so `git status --porcelain` was already non-empty and both runs saw `dirty` — a mutant emitting the tree token BOTH above and below the marker survived it, and a mutant putting `checkout $TREE` above the marker survived every one of the suite's ten tests, because mutating any tracked file dirties the "clean" run too. The suite's fix for that had also written an untracked, NON-IGNORED file into the repository ROOT, against its own scaffolding's stated invariant and against this project's review procedure, whose first step is `git add -A`: a concurrent one would have staged the dirt into the reviewed revision, and a SIGKILL would have left it. Both are settled by one change: the test builds a THROWAWAY GIT REPOSITORY holding copies of the four paths the script reads, commits it, snapshots it CLEAN, dirties it, snapshots it again, and asserts the two tree tokens actually DIFFERED — and additionally that NO LINE above the marker carries `clean` or `dirty` as a token, which kills the whole class rather than the one mutant. (2) F5's mechanism was REBORN on the line F4's fix wrote: `[ "$last" -lt "$LADDER_DEPTH" ]` with a non-numeric `last` writes `[: x: integer expected` to stderr, evaluates FALSE, and falls through to `reason=complete` — exit 0, a COMPLETE kind token and a terminal reason nothing verified (REPRODUCED through the shipped `--binary` flag). Every engine-reported field the script records or computes with is now refused unless it is a count, by the idiom the corpus loop already used, and the ladder additionally refuses a depth that is not GREATER than the last, since iterative deepening only deepens and a terminal depth below one the record already states contradicts it. (3) AN OOM-KILLED ENGINE WAS RECORDED AS THE WALL-CLOCK CAP. `timeout` passes the CHILD'S OWN status through unchanged, so 124 is also what an engine exiting 124 yields and 137 is exactly what an OOM kill yields; both were recorded as `cap` in MILLISECONDS against a 30 s bound (REPRODUCED with stubs exiting 124 and 137 at once), and the shipped `capped` stub exited 124 immediately, so THE SUITE INSTITUTIONALISED THE ASSUMPTION. The status is now necessary and not sufficient: each rung is timed and 124/137 is the cap only if the run lasted the cap. That made the cap path untestable at 30 s per rung, so `--ladder-cap-s` joins the flags — recorded as a deviation from the enumerated set for the same reason `--binary` was, and NOT given a second provenance token on its record line, because the cap's own VALUE is already in the invariant block and a record taken under a different cap therefore cannot be mistaken for a registered one. (4) The corpus BASENAME is a caller-controlled path component inside the invariant block, and a name containing a NEWLINE injected attacker-chosen LINES into it — a forged `ladder_terminal` and a forged `position`, exit 0, COMPLETE token (REPRODUCED). A control character in either recorded basename is now refused by name. NAMED RESIDUAL, not closed: two byte-identical corpora under two names still give differing blocks, which is D-147's "by SHA-256 AND BY NOTHING ELSE — no path" objection exactly. It stands because the format is pinned by a three-run byte-identical invariance result that two reviews verified, and dropping the basename would restate that result rather than reproduce it; the header now enumerates all FOUR paths above the marker instead of the two it claimed. (5) The engine's `time` token reached bash ARITHMETIC unvalidated, and `$(( ))` performs command substitution on its operand: `time PIPESTATUS[$(>PWNED)]` RAN that command with the record still written and exit 0, `time 0` fabricated `setup_fraction_pct 100.00 SETUP-HEAVY`, and an unset name gave a raw `unbound variable` with no named error (all three REPRODUCED). (6) ACCEPTED MINORS: `--out ''` fell back to stdout in silence and every flag now refuses an empty value; `--nodes 010` passed `[ … -ge 1 ]` as OCTAL while the engine read decimal 10, and `+50000` and ` 50000` landed above the marker un-normalized, the last putting a DOUBLE SPACE inside an invariant line, so a count must now be spelled with no sign, space or leading zero; the engine-resolution refusal told an operator who had named a directory to go and build the engine, and each reason now has its own refusal; the handshake refusal names its bound as the corpus and ladder refusals already did; an EMPTY openings fixture passed `[ -f ]` and made the opening rung `position` with no argument; `score_checked` accepted `mate 0`, a distance the ladder would have read as a verified terminal reason; the header said the slowest registered ladder position measured 9.30 s where the governing design says 9.38 s, and the design's figure is restored; and `LC_ALL=C` is exported, because `$EPOCHREALTIME` writes the LOCALE'S decimal separator and the cap comparison is a wall-clock comparison that may not depend on who is logged in. (7) THE COVERAGE GAP behind most of this: eight repaired failure paths and two record fields had no test at all — the CRLF guard, the both-bands refusal, the binary resolution, the bestmove count, the regular-file check, the score parse, the corpus exit status, the band label and the `reached` depth — and the suite now binds every one of them. NOT BOUND, deliberately: the corpus session's 900 s timeout, which no flag shortens and no test can afford to wait out; binding it would mean a second override flag for a guard whose failure mode is a hang, and the hang is what the timeout already turns into a named refusal. Flips if a third round finds a semantic claim in this record that a stub could have falsified, at which point the stub grew too small rather than the suite too large.

D-233: `tools/artifact_check.sh` READS THE TRACKED BYTES AND NOT THE WORKING TREE — a CI gate that could be WALKED PAST, closed. `git ls-files` names a path and `<"$path"` then opened a DIFFERENT FILE, the worktree's copy, which a committer controls independently of what reaches HEAD: staging a record and overwriting the worktree copy with something harmless passed the gate GREEN and `git show HEAD:record.txt` still yielded the record, and a committed record whose worktree copy was merely deleted was skipped outright by `[ -f "$path" ] || continue` — which skipped the rule-7 size ceiling for the same paths (BOTH REPRODUCED in a scratch repository with the script at `<scratch>/tools/` per D-203). D-203's contract is "a TRACKED file whose first line is the schema header", so the bytes read are now the INDEX'S: `git ls-files -s -z` names each path's blob, `git cat-file --batch-check` sizes them all in one process, and the first line comes from `git cat-file blob`. The skip is GONE with the worktree read that needed it, so tracked-but-absent is no longer a case the gate has. PRE-EXISTING on the `arena_report` branch and inherited verbatim by the snapshot recognizer, which is why it is recorded here and not left as a note. Cost, stated rather than hidden: the recognizer's "no process per file" boast is spent — one `git cat-file` per tracked file, measured at well under a second over this repository's tracked set, against a gate that runs after `cargo test`. `LC_ALL=C` is also exported, because the leading-whitespace trim was only as wide as the AMBIENT locale and `tools/ci.sh` pins none, so `LC_ALL=C` and `LC_ALL=en_US.utf8` gave two answers about a first line led by U+2028 — the gate is now DETERMINISTIC and states its width exactly, ASCII whitespace and no more, with the non-ASCII case a named residual of the same class as D-203's content-signature residual and standing behind the name patterns. `artifact_check_reads_the_index_and_not_the_working_tree` pins both reproducers with a clean-repository control. Flips if the gate is ever asked about the WORKTREE — a pre-commit hook wanting to refuse a record before it is staged — which is a different question and takes a different entry point, not an amendment to this one.

D-234: THE RECORD GAPS D-230 LEFT, AND THE MECHANIZATION RULE 9 DID NOT HAVE. Four corrections, appended rather than edited in. (1) D-230 RECORDS NO STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK on the record format it adopted and does not say the matrix was attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM, which the Process paragraph requires and which D-226 does twice. It was attacked, and the withdrawal it forced is already in D-230's own text — the flat `key value` file with a per-line `measured` marker fell to a reproduced attack, that a marker cannot mark the ABSENCE of a line while a wall-clock cap decides whether a ladder depth's line exists at all. THE STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK on the adopted arena-report idiom, recorded here because D-230 does not state it: the invariant/timing split is enforced by NOTHING BUT THE PRODUCER — a consumer that reads the whole file cannot tell which half a line came from except by finding the marker, and every defect this record has had was a line on the wrong side of it. What answers the attack is not the format but the test that diffs the block across two arranged tree states, which is why D-232's first finding was the one that mattered. (2) A REQUIRED TEST NAME WAS DROPPED WITH NO RECORD: the dispatch named `snapshot_deterministic_given_revision_and_budget` and the suite ships `snapshot_deterministic_across_a_clean_and_a_dirty_working_tree`. The replacement is BETTER — it names the transition the defect lived in rather than the two inputs held fixed — but the criterion was "recorded AND better" and only half was met; this is the record. (3) RULE 9'S MECHANIZATION COULD NOT REACH THE ONLY FILES OVER THE CAP. `tools/file_justification_check.sh` iterated `git ls-files '*.rs'` and matched `^[[:space:]]*//.*RULE9-JUSTIFICATION:`, while the two files that actually crossed the soft cap are shell scripts carrying the marker in a `#` comment: rule 9 was satisfied as PROSE and unmechanized in fact. The file set is now `*.rs` and `*.sh`, the marker regex accepts either comment spelling, and the gate's own seeded self-test gained a shell case that must pass and a shell case that must fail — because a checker nobody has watched fail is not a checker. (4) THE TEST HARNESS LEAKED SCRATCH DIRECTORIES FOREVER: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/common/mod.rs` never cleaned them, and the machine this was found on held thousands, on a `/tmp` that is RAM — the hazard `tools/bench_delta.sh`'s own comment names. A `Drop` guard is the wrong shape, since a failing test's output is the first thing anybody reads, and a test binary has no reliable teardown hook, so the sweep is once per process at the front of the only function that creates one, over entries older than any live run can own, with every error ignored: a sweep that failed a test would be worse than the litter. NOT THIS WORK PACKAGE'S DEFECT and recorded rather than blamed. Flips for (3) if a tracked file over the cap is ever written in a language whose comments are neither `//` nor `#`, which takes a third spelling and not a third gate.

D-235: TWO CORRECTIONS TO D-220'S RECORD, AND FIVE PROCESS FINDINGS RECORDED OPEN RATHER THAN ADOPTED. D-220 is a measurement line whose in-place reservation is SPENT, so both corrections are here. (1) ITS "THIS IS A RE-MEASUREMENT WITH PINNED PROVENANCE AND NOT AN INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION" DISCLOSURE IS NOW MOOT, and the disclosure was right to be there when it was written. A fresh-context REVIEW-impl re-ran `tools/bench_delta.sh rev:f31cffe rev:bdfca3f 5` in a fresh clone at a DIFFERENT PATH and got early nps ratio 2.197 against D-220's 2.181 and late 2.076 against 2.064, both bands PASS inside [1.4, 2.5], node identity holding, widest IQR 1.37 % against a 10 % gate, and both revisions rebuilding to the digests D-220 records — which is REPRODUCIBILITY of a deterministic build and not a copied number. D-220's verdict therefore now has an independent replication behind it; the numbers in that line are unchanged and this line is the corroboration it declined to claim for itself. (2) ITS WORDING QUIETLY RELAXED A RESERVATION: D-215 reserved the number for "the operator's own run" and D-220 says "operator-hardware run". The run was taken on the operator's machine by a session the operator dispatched, which is what the reserved number was for — but the relaxation was taken silently where the same line dispositioned the superseded COMMAND LITERAL explicitly, and the asymmetry is the defect. Recorded, not re-argued: a reservation's terms are dispositioned in the line that spends it or in a line like this one, never absorbed. THE FIVE PROCESS FINDINGS, against the two paragraphs D-227 and D-228 put in CLAUDE.md, are recorded OPEN and are NOT adopted, because those paragraphs are law and the operator has not ruled: (T1) the added dry-run sentence resolves the collision for the PRE-REGISTRATION and not for the HARNESS, and this very work package is the instance — D-220's bench was taken on a `bench_delta.sh` revision whose review had failed and whose successor was still under review, so the run is licensed by ARGUMENT and not by the text; (T2) "the same sort of artefact, differing only in identity" constrains KIND and not REPRESENTATIVENESS, and "records the dry-run input and its output" requires RECORDING and not CHECKING, so D-221's own `grep -c 'btree.*search'` defect would pass a compliant dry run on any real profile whose symbol table lacks the confusable substring; (T3) there is no exception for a workload with ONE INSTANCE of its kind, where "never on the registered workload itself" is unsatisfiable and rule 3 leaves a session no sanctioned way to proceed; (T4) "where the run is cheap" is a SELF-JUDGING trigger with no threshold, decided by the same document that states the cost, against rule 5's numeric reps floor; (T5) the second-instrument clause requires an agreement criterion registered in advance and states NO CONSEQUENCE FOR DISAGREEMENT, which leaves exactly the after-the-numbers decision it exists to forbid. All five are judged SOUND as readings; none is amended here. A-3 and D-229 are untouched by this round and nothing above rests on them. Flips when the operator rules on any of T1-T5, at which point the ruling amends CLAUDE.md and takes its own line.

D-236: THE SETUP COST IS MEASURED, THE CIRCLE IS BROKEN, AND THE PREDICTION D-229 REGISTERED IS CONFIRMED — D-229's successor, written from the run that line records as not taken. GOVERNING REVISION: DESIGN_r3 §A-3 (the BL-1 threshold deletion, adopted by a fresh-context REVIEW-design and RATIFIED by the operator); the run card restates §A-3.PR of revision 2 as r3 amends it and makes no new law, so nothing here rests on a document that has not passed its own review. WHAT WAS RUN, and what `a3/run_registered.sh` was not: that script names `bench_positions_v1` entries 1/13/17 and predates r2's PR.7 — its entries are two A-4 ladder positions and the one DISQUALIFIED by the mate-freeness precondition — and it carries no K-sweep at all, so it cannot answer the question, which is registered as a SPLIT between a per-PROCESS and a per-`newgame` component. The registered positions are entries 3, 16 and 18, and the precondition was re-checked and printed before the run at HEAD ccba146, binary 62c102cc: entries 3, 16 and 18 return `cp` at 500 000 nodes with N = 500736, entry 17 returns `score mate 1` at N = 5541 and is disqualified, replicating r2's B1 reproducer exactly. INSTRUMENT: `configs/instrument_v0.toml` (`tt_bytes` 268435456) and a scratchpad copy differing in that one key (1048576), release binary 62c102cc, AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, single-thread instrument mode, 5 reps, K ∈ {1,4,16} at B = 50 000 for the primary estimator and B ∈ {5 000, 50 000, 500 000} one process per cell for the secondary. THE NUMBERS, medians over the three registered positions: per-PROCESS `P_fixed` = 19.6 ms and per-`newgame` `C` = 8.65 ms at 268435456; `P_fixed` = 1.5 ms and `C` = 0.67 ms at 1048576. SESSION EXPOSURE `E = C + P_fixed/24` = 9.46 ms, which is 2.02 % of a 50 000-node search's per-position wall — the registered prediction said "about 2 %, not material" and this is that number. The per-PROCESS exposure `P_fixed + C` = 28.2 ms is reported beside it and is PROTOCOL-DEPENDENT: it is what a harness running one process per search pays 24 times over, and it is never compared against anything. THE TT IS CONFIRMED AS THE CAUSE on the criterion registered before the run — `C(256MiB) − C(1MiB) ≥ 5 ms` AND `C(256MiB) ≥ 5·C(1MiB)` — by 7.97 ms and 12.88x, and by 7.57 ms and 10.01x in the WORST CASE over all 15 independent per-rep fits (minimum C at 268435456 against MAXIMUM C at 1048576), so the criterion is met by an order of magnitude and not by a median's luck. PR.4's secondary estimator behaved exactly as r3 re-registered it: the OLS intercept is +99.8, +163.5 and −244.6 ms on the three positions, uninterpretable SIGN INCLUDED, and it is not quoted as the fixed component. THE IQR GATE, honestly: one cell of 18 in the 268435456 arm is NOISY (p3 at K=1, IQR 13.2 % of its median) and refitting that position without it moves `E` from 9.45 to 9.47 ms; the 1048576 arm is noisy in 7 cells of 9, because its overheads are 2-13 ms while the engine reports `time` in whole milliseconds — at that magnitude a 10 %-of-median gate measures QUANTIZATION and not instability, which is a finding about the gate's applicability, not a reason to move it. REPLICATION (D-228's own rule, and the reason the run is cheap enough to have one): two complete independent executions of the registered command at the same revision gave E = 9.46 ms both times, E/(S+E) 2.02 % and 2.00 %, C 8.65 and 8.63 ms, P_fixed 19.6 and 19.9 ms. COST, stated on the pre-registration's face before it ran and confirmed after: 7-9 minutes of one core, no operator attention; measured 433.3 s and 433.9 s. THE DELIVERABLE — A-4'S SNAPSHOT BUDGET IS VERIFIED AND THE CIRCULAR CALIBRATION IS BROKEN: D-229 borrowed its one number from `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh`, the instrument whose own budget that number was supposed to justify. A-3's `P_fixed` and `C` come from a different protocol (a K-sweep timed by the shell over sessions of 1, 4 and 16 searches) on different positions, so they are an INDEPENDENT estimate: at the registered 50 000 nodes they predict a session setup fraction of 2.02 %, against the script's own <5 % criterion, and the criterion needs only that a position average more than 179.8 ms of search — measured median 458 ms, minimum 185 ms over the three. THE BUDGET PASSES and NOTHING CHANGES; the snapshot instrument's own reading of 1.66-1.71 % over its 24 positions is now a cross-instrument corroboration rather than the source of the claim. Flips if `tt_bytes` moves, since every number here is the size of the table being cleared; and a harness that runs ONE PROCESS PER SEARCH re-opens the question at 28.2 ms per search rather than 9.46 ms per position, which is the trigger D-229 wrote down and this line leaves standing.

D-237: THE TWO SHELL INSTRUMENTS REFUSE WHAT THEY CANNOT READ, AND A HOUSEKEEPING LISTING NO LONGER DECIDES A VERDICT'S EXIT STATUS — three defects of one class, EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER, each REPRODUCED at ccba146 before its fix and re-run after, each now carrying a named test. (1) THE DISCARDED DIGEST. `echo "binary_sha256 $(sha256sum "$BINARY" | cut -d' ' -f1)"` cannot fail: the substitution's status is an ARGUMENT, so an engine that is executable and not readable (mode 0111) wrote the line with NOTHING after it, exited 0 and carried the COMPLETE kind token — and since `binary_sha256` is the only line that separates a debug-build record from a release one (D-230's `--binary` argument), two records from two engines whose digests differ were BYTE-IDENTICAL in their whole invariant block, which is what the reproducer showed. Both reviewers found this independently. `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` now takes every digest through a `digest` helper that refuses by name and checks the answer is 64 hex digits, BEFORE the engine is launched and before a line of the record is written; `tools/bench_delta.sh` had the sibling spelling as an ASSIGNMENT, where `set -e` killed the run with no `bench_delta: FAIL:` line at all — rule 3's other failure, a death that names nothing — and it matters there because two unreadable sides would both have digested to the empty string and been refused as "the same binary", a WRONG DIAGNOSIS. Pinned by `an_engine_this_script_cannot_read_is_refused_rather_than_digested_as_nothing` and `a_side_this_harness_cannot_read_is_refused_by_name`. (2) THE CONTROL-CHARACTER GUARD WAS ASCII-ONLY. `LC_ALL=C` is exported for determinism — `$EPOCHREALTIME` writes the locale's decimal separator — and under C the class `[[:cntrl:]]` is ASCII, so the guard on the two basenames that reach the invariant block refused LF and ADMITTED U+2028 and U+0085, both of which wrote a `corpus` line and exited 0 with the COMPLETE kind token. The operator's two named options were to drop the `LC_ALL` narrowing or scope it to the sort; NEITHER IS TAKEN AND THE DEVIATION IS RECORDED HERE: this script has no sort, and dropping the pin would trade a narrow guard for a nondeterministic record. The class is INVERTED to an allow-list (`*[![:print:]]*`) instead, which makes the pin widen the refusal rather than narrow it — under C only printable ASCII is admitted, and a locale calling fewer characters printable can only refuse more. Named cost: a corpus whose file name is not printable ASCII is now refused, which is what an ASCII record's provenance line can honestly carry. Pinned by `a_corpus_name_carrying_a_unicode_separator_is_refused_like_an_ascii_newline`, and the existing newline test's assertion moves to the new wording. (3) THE EXIT TRAP'S LAST COMMAND. `cleanup`'s `git worktree list | sed` is a pipeline under `pipefail` and bash exits with the status of the last command run in an EXIT trap, so a COMPLETED bench that had already printed `bench_delta: done —` exited 128 outside a git directory. The trap now takes `local rc=$?` first and `return "$rc"` last, and a listing it cannot take is a named WARNING rather than a death — the measurement above is unaffected either way, and a verdict printed and a run failed are the two things this exit status exists to tell apart. Pinned by `a_bench_that_printed_its_verdict_exits_0_even_when_the_worktree_listing_cannot_be_taken`. TWO ASSERTIONS THE EARLIER ROUND'S MUTANTS WALKED PAST are added with them: `ladder_cap_s` is stated in the invariant block at a NON-DEFAULT value, so both the deleting mutant and a nailed constant die and D-232's argument for omitting a provenance token keeps the line it depends on; and a ladder rung reported SHALLOWER than one already recorded is refused, through a new `backward` stub mode, because a record that contradicts itself one line after stating a depth is the failure that refusal exists for. Flips never for the fail-loud direction; the allow-list's width flips if a fixture path this project ships ever needs a character outside printable ASCII, which would be a finding about the record's encoding and not a reason to widen the guard quietly.

D-238: `tools/file_justification_check.sh` READS THE TRACKED BYTES AND NOT THE WORKING TREE — D-233's fix, applied to the sibling gate the same change set left it out of. `git ls-files` names a PATH and `wc -l`/`grep` then opened the WORKTREE file of that name, which is a different file: staging an over-cap unjustified source file and overwriting its worktree copy with two lines made the gate print `0 over the cap, all justified` and exit 0 while the real bytes went to HEAD. REPRODUCED at ccba146 in a scratch repository with one `.rs` and one `.sh` staged and both decoyed, and re-run after the fix, where both are named. What commits is the INDEX, so the index is what is read: `git ls-files -s -z` names each path's blob, `git cat-file blob` unpacks it into a scratch file inside the `$SEED` directory the existing trap already removes (a second `trap … EXIT` REPLACES the first — D-231's leak), and an extraction git refuses is a named refusal rather than a skip. The `[ -f "$file" ] || …` case survives for the seeded self-test and is named as unreachable from the tracked loop rather than deleted, on D-232's precedent for a branch nothing can reach at this revision. THE SUMMARY LINE IS COUNTED BY THE LOOP ITSELF and no longer by a second `git ls-files` with its own pathspec: the two could disagree, and did — a mutant dropping `*.sh` from the enumeration left the line still saying `.rs/.sh` while counting only `.rs`, so every over-cap shell script went unseen by the gate that had just been widened to see them (D-234). Pinned by two tests in a scratch git repository, each with a clean-repo control so a pass cannot come from a gate that refuses everything: `the_justification_gate_reads_the_index_and_not_the_working_tree` and `the_justification_gate_counts_the_shell_scripts_its_summary_says_it_counts`, the second asserting the summary's count over one tracked `.rs`, one tracked `.sh` and one tracked `.txt`. THE GATE HAD NO TEST AT ALL before this — it self-tests its `verdict` function over seeded files, and nothing ever drove the half that decides WHICH files that function is asked about, which is exactly where both defects lived. Flips never; the index read is what rule 9 has always meant.

D-239: THE TEST SUITES' SCRATCH DIRECTORIES CARRY A PREFIX THE WORKSPACE DOES NOT — `pistol-testscratch-`, replacing the bare `pistol-` the sweep matched and the `pistol-arena-` the arena spelled. D-234's sweep is the only code in this workspace that DELETES directories it did not create, and it matched this project's OWN NAMING SCHEME: every crate directory is `pistol-something`. REPRODUCED at ccba146 — a `TMPDIR` holding `pistol-core`, `pistol-cli`, `pistol-eval`, `pistol-search` and `pistol-arena` with old timestamps, one `cargo test -p pistol-cli --test bench_delta_tests`, and the test PASSED having removed all five; after the fix the same run leaves all five and its own two scratch directories carry the new prefix. A sweep by prefix must own the prefix. THE TWO CRATES' SCAFFOLDING AGREES BY TEST AND NOT BY COMMENT: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/common/mod.rs` names the constant and `crates/pistol-arena/tests/common/mod.rs` extends it (`pistol-testscratch-arena-`), because the cli suite's sweep is what removes what the arena's `Drop` guard cannot — a test binary that aborts or is killed runs no destructor — and an agreement stated only in a comment breaks silently. The destructive half is now a function over a NAMED directory (`sweep_scratch_in`), so a test can watch it work: `the_scratch_sweep_spares_every_directory_it_did_not_make` seeds all eight crate directory names plus an unrelated one and both suites' scratch spellings and asserts exactly which survive; `the_sweep_leaves_a_scratch_directory_that_is_not_stale_alone` binds the age half, so the name test cannot pass a sweep that deletes everything named right regardless of when it was written — which would remove a CONCURRENT test process's directories; `every_scratch_directory_this_suite_makes_carries_the_prefix_the_sweep_matches` closes the loop from the other side, since a scratch directory the sweep cannot recognize is one nothing ever removes; and the arena's `every_arena_scratch_directory_is_one_the_cli_suites_sweep_will_recognize` restates the prefix rather than importing it, because the two crates are what must agree and importing would make them agree by construction. Flips if a third suite ever makes scratch directories, which joins the prefix rather than inventing one.

D-240: `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` IS THE STANDING REVIEW INSTRUMENT FOR `tools/`, AND CLAUDE.md SAYS SO — adopted because the fix-seeds-defect pattern ran through all three prior rounds and was ONE MATERIAL CLASS, not three coincidences: shell under `set -euo pipefail` parsing unvalidated output and failing as EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER. A refusal that exits 1 is a working gate having a bad day; a pass that should have been a refusal is a gate that does not exist, and nothing downstream can tell. Ten items, each written from a defect this project actually shipped: a command substitution whose status is discarded in an ARGUMENT (D-237); a pipeline in a `then` body versus one in a condition (D-231); grep-under-pipefail, including `grep -c` printing `0` and still exiting 1, and the substring that matched `pistol_search` and retired the document its count governed (D-221, D-223); `LC_ALL` scoping and the question every character class must answer — does the pin make this refuse MORE or LESS (D-237); index-versus-working-tree reads and the count that must come from the same enumeration (D-233, D-238); scratch namespacing (D-239); traps, their last command's status and the second `trap … EXIT` that replaces the first (D-231, D-237); one spelling per number and one refusal per reason (D-232); and what reaches a record being caller-controlled (D-232). THE COVERAGE RULE IS THE BINDING ONE: any `tools/` script that produces a recorded number carries at least one test driving the SHIPPED script, in a scratch directory or scratch repository, with a control run — `tools/bench_delta.sh` produced this project's official perf verdict (D-220) with ZERO tests until D-231, which is precisely why two rounds of defects in it went unbound and were found by reviewers running it by hand. A REVIEW PROMPT FOR A `tools/` CHANGE CITES THE FILE and the reviewer answers its items by name; the rule is in CLAUDE.md rather than only here, for D-228's reason — a rule whose limits are stated only in a decision log is one the next reader applies without them. NOT MECHANIZED, and the checklist says so: no script checks it, and a fourth round is what it exists to be cheaper than. Flips if a mechanized check for any of its items is found, which would move that item out of the judged list and into `tools/ci.sh`.

D-241: A CERTIFICATION REVISION IS ANCHORED BY A `cert/<decision>` TAG, AND THAT IS THE STANDING PATTERN — the forward-pointing half of D-231, which preserved the harness revision D-220's run was taken on as stash object `1edbb61` and then depended on that object staying alive. A `git stash create` commit is on no branch and in no reflog once the stash entry is gone: it is UNREACHABLE, `git gc` is entitled to collect it, and the certification would then cite a revision nobody can check out — the whole point of naming a revision. `cert/d220` now points at `1edbb61`; the object is reachable (`git rev-list --all` finds it, `git fsck --unreachable` no longer reports it) and a lightweight tag is enough, because what is wanted is a ref that keeps the object, not a second signature on a certification the ADR line already carries. THE PATTERN, so the next certification does not rediscover it: any line that certifies a revision it does not otherwise commit — a stash object, a throwaway worktree's build, a revision that was reviewed and then amended — takes a `cert/<decision-number>` tag at the moment the line is written, and the line quotes both the tag and the object. A revision cited without one is cited on the assumption that nobody runs `git gc --prune`, which is not a property this project may assume of an operator's machine. Flips if these tags ever accumulate faster than they are read, at which point the pattern narrows to certifications whose revision is not an ancestor of `main` — which is already the only case that needs it.

D-242: THE T-BUCKET IS DISPOSITIONED AT BITE TIME, NOT PRE-LITIGATED — the operator's rule for the eight process-text ambiguities against CLAUDE.md's dry-run and proportionality paragraphs, of which T1-T5 are on the record in D-235 and T6-T8 came from the closing round on the same two paragraphs. THE RULE: they stay OPEN, and the FIRST SESSION THAT ACTUALLY HITS ONE resolves it then, with a one-line amendment citing the T-number and describing the instance that forced it. Rules sharpen by contact. Writing eight amendments now would be eight rulings made without an instance, by the same reasoning D-228 applies to a margin derived to defend a single sample — and it is the proportionality rule turned on its own siblings, which is the argument for it and also its weakest point: a rule left ambiguous is a rule the next session may apply wrongly before anyone notices. THE BUCKET'S BOUNDARY IS WHAT MAKES THAT ACCEPTABLE HERE, and it is stated rather than assumed: NONE of the eight was graded blocking, and every one of them is an AMBIGUITY — a reading the text does not settle — rather than an exploit. A finding that is exploitable against RESULT INTEGRITY, where following the text as written produces a wrong number or licenses a run that should have been refused, does NOT belong in this bucket and is not deferred by this line; it is a defect in process law and takes an amendment immediately. Flips the moment one is hit, which is what the rule is for; and flips wholesale if the count grows — eight open readings of two paragraphs is a bucket, and a materially larger one is evidence the paragraphs need rewriting rather than annotating.

D-243: THE HOT-WINDOW THEOREM — A HOT WINDOW IS AN UNCONDITIONAL WIN IN ONE TURN FOR ITS OWNER AT THE START OF THAT TURN, AND FOUR THINGS FOLLOW FROM IT. Written down once here because WP-1.5a and WP-1.5b both cite it as their design source, and a theorem restated in two work packages is a theorem that drifts in one of them. DEFINITIONS, exact, and only one of the four is the eval crate's own: WINDOW is `crates/pistol-eval/src/window.rs`'s (`Window`, `WINDOW_LEN`, `WINDOWS_PER_CELL`, `windows_through` — three axes, six offsets, eighteen windows), one of the length-`WINDOW_LEN` = `WIN_LEN` = 6 axial segments through a cell; LIVE has an indirect basis there and no name — `HandcraftedV0::contribution` in `crates/pistol-eval/src/handcrafted.rs` scores nothing for a window holding both players, which is the DEAD case — and is defined here as: a window is LIVE for side S iff it holds at least one S-stone and no opponent stone; HOT and WIN-IN-ONE-PLY exist nowhere in `pistol-eval`, are introduced by this line, and are `pistol-solver`'s to implement — WIN-IN-ONE-PLY for S is a live-S window with five S-stones, HOT for S is a live-S window with at least four. A WP implementer who greps the eval crate for `is_hot` finds nothing, and that is the crate's correct state rather than a gap in it. THE THEOREM: a hot window has at most `WIN_LEN` − 4 = 2 empties and a turn places `TURN_STONES` = 2 stones, so its owner, on their move with both stones unspent, fills every empty in it and wins by rule 2 — a counting identity between the window's slack and the turn's budget, not a heuristic, and it is why the hot threshold is 4 and not a tuned number. THE THEOREM IS STONES-REMAINING CONDITIONED, and this line says so rather than reading as unconditional in phase: "on their move" means at `Phase::First` with two stones left. At `Phase::Second` one stone is left and only a hot window with EXACTLY ONE empty — the win-in-one-ply case — is a win now; a two-empty hot window is not, and a generator that reads the count without the phase claims a mate it cannot play. Turn 1 is not an exception: it places `FIRST_TURN_STONES` = 1 stone, but the board before it is empty, so no window holds four of anything and no hot window can exist to be conditioned. LEGALITY IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH, which is the premise the word "unconditional" rests on and is therefore checked rather than assumed: `Coord::distance` is `(|dq| + |dr| + |dq+dr|)/2`, and each of the three axis directions — `(0,1)`, `(1,0)`, `(1,−1)` — gives exactly `k` for `k` steps, so any two cells of a window are within `WIN_LEN` − 1 = 5 of each other. That 5 is the bound for ARBITRARY cells of a window, and it is not the bound the theorem needs. THE BINDING QUANTITY IS THE DISTANCE FROM A HOT WINDOW'S EMPTY TO ITS NEAREST OWN STONE, and a hot window holds at least four own stones among six cells, which caps that at 2: exhaustively over all three axes and all 4-of-6 and 5-of-6 placements the maximum gap is 2, witness `ConstQ` with own stones at window indices 0, 1, 2 and 3 and the empty at index 5. Every empty of a hot window is therefore within 2 of a stone already on the board and sits inside rule 5's radius-`LEGAL_RADIUS` = 8 region with six to spare. No hot window is ever uncompletable for legality reasons, and no legality argument can rescue a side that has left one standing. THE FOUR CONSEQUENCES, which are what the work packages cite: (1) THE ONLY ANSWER TO AN OPPONENT HOT WINDOW OTHER THAN HITTING IT IS WINNING THIS TURN — creating a new hot window of one's own, or a new win-in-one-ply, loses the race by move order, since either pays off one turn later than the threat it answers. This is a NECESSARY condition and never a sufficient one: it does not say that hitting a hot window saves the game, because against two disjoint hot windows one hit is not enough, and the multi-window case is carried by (4). (1) AND (4) ARE ONE REQUIREMENT AND MAY NOT BE QUOTED APART — (1) alone, lifted into a work package, licenses the one-stone-and-done defensive generator that (4) exists to forbid; (2) STAGE F MUST GENERATE TWO-STONE COMPLETIONS of own hot windows as FORCED moves — mate-in-1-by-pair — rather than trusting a delta ranking to surface both halves of a pair whose first stone is worth little alone; (3) `unblockable_double_threat` IS ONLY A WIN IF THE SIDE TO MOVE CANNOT ITSELF WIN THIS TURN, because by (1) the side to move's own hot window outruns it — without that guard the check returns a mate score for the side that is losing; (4) DEFENSIVE GENERATION NEEDS THE UNION OF CELLS OVER ALL INCLUSION-MINIMAL COVERS OF SIZE ≤ STONES-LEFT, and the contrast that matters is against MINIMUM-CARDINALITY covers, not against covers at large. A COVER of the opponent's hot windows is a set of empty cells that meets every one of them, hitting at least one empty of each; under that reading any superset of a cover is also a cover, so "all covers of size ≤ stones-left" restricts nothing whenever a size-1 cover exists and two stones are left. With S on `(0,0) (1,0) (2,0) (3,0) (5,0)` and the opponent on `(-1,0)` and `(6,0)`, the `ConstR` window `(0,0)…(5,0)` is the only hot window on the board — every other `ConstR` window holding an S stone also holds `(-1,0)` or `(6,0)` and is dead, and no off-axis window through an S stone holds more than one S stone, since the five S stones have pairwise distinct `q` and pairwise distinct `q+r` — so its single empty `(4,0)` is the unique inclusion-minimal cover, while the covers of size ≤ 2 are `{(4,0)}` together with `{(4,0), x}` for every legal empty `x`, whose union of cells is the entire legal region. INCLUSION-MINIMAL is the notion that restricts, and it still delivers the case this consequence exists for: two disjoint hot windows needing different cells have minimal covers `{a, b}`, so the defender's two-stone split stays reachable at ply 1. THE UNION OF CELLS IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT — a generator that forms both stones of a pair from within a single window offers every cell of the union and still never offers the cross-window pair `(a, b)`, so the PAIRING obligation is part of this requirement rather than a detail of implementing it. Flips only on a rules change, never on anything in search, eval or the candidate policy: to `WIN_LEN`, since a longer window admits a hot count with three empties and the slack-versus-budget arithmetic fails; to `TURN_STONES`, since fewer stones per turn stops the two-empty case being a win now; or to `LEGAL_RADIUS`, which breaks the legality premise only BELOW 2 — not below 5: the 5 is the arbitrary-cell bound and the 2 is the empty-to-nearest-own-stone bound derived above, so the theorem survives `LEGAL_RADIUS` ∈ {2, 3, 4} as well as 8, and a trigger written at 5 would fire on three radii where nothing is wrong.

D-244: THE TACTICAL-V0 FIXTURE'S HEADER NAMED THE WRONG CONFIG AND THE WRONG RADIUS, AND THE CORRECTION TAKES ITS OWN COMMIT — prose only, in the file whose whole argument is that "a threshold means nothing without the search that has to meet it". The stanza naming the configs each case is a claim about said `configs/instrument_v0.toml` is "the DEPLOYMENT config, candidate radius 3 … at the radius that ships". BOTH FACTS WERE WRONG at this revision and both were checked against the tree rather than against memory: `configs/instrument_v0.toml` is `radius = 2` and has been since D-190/D-194 fired WP-1.3 Run 1's pre-registered H1, and the deployment config is `configs/play_v0.toml`, which is `radius = 3` and describes itself as "the deployment counterpart of configs/instrument_v0.toml". The header therefore misdescribed the search that FIFTEEN of the twenty cases — every mate-in-one and every must-block case — are a claim about, in the one document whose stated reason for naming a config at all is that the claim is meaningless without it. The stanza's "every … runs here" clause was its only accurate part and is kept. THE THRESHOLD, THE BUDGETS, THE POSITIONS AND THE EXPECTATIONS ARE UNTOUCHED, verified rather than asserted: the diff is ONE hunk, three comment lines out and four in, and the file's 141 non-comment lines are BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after, checked by stripping comments from both revisions and diffing. `TACTICAL_V0_SHA256` moves from `2d0b7653…` to `7acb3ea3…` in this same commit; `tactical_v0_fixture_is_pinned_and_every_position_is_legal` was run RED first and the digest it computed matched an independent `sha256sum` of the file, which is the pin doing its job rather than an obstacle to be routed around. WHY A DOCUMENTATION ERROR INSIDE A SHA-PINNED FIXTURE EARNS ITS OWN COMMIT, twice over: WP-1.5b's plan creates `tactical_staged_v0.txt` as a sibling of this file, so an uncorrected header is one copy-paste away from being propagated into a SECOND pinned fixture, after which it costs two corrections and two digest moves instead of one; and folding a digest change into a strength work package puts an unrelated sha in that package's diff, where a reviewer reading the package cannot tell the documentation fix from the thing under test — the same separation D-215's one-change-one-commit-one-bench rule buys for perf. Flips when either config's radius moves again: `configs/play_v0.toml` carries a pre-registered movetime-matched run that is licensed and has not been taken, and whichever way that lands, this header is a claim about a config VALUE and is re-read whenever the value changes.

D-245: A REGISTERED AGREEMENT CRITERION CARRIES A REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE — the proportionality rule's second-instrument clause is amended to say that a pre-registration naming a second instrument states, before either instrument runs, what DISAGREEMENT does to the verdict; without it the clause requires a criterion and then leaves the after-the-numbers decision it exists to forbid (T5, D-235). First contact: WP-1.5b's SPRT pre-registration, whose second instrument is the baseline snapshot's completed-depth change and whose registered consequence is that on disagreement the work package does not land on the SPRT alone. This is D-242's bite-time rule firing for the FIRST time, and it takes the shape that rule prescribes — a one-line amendment citing the T-number and describing the instance that forced it — and because the ruling is law it amends CLAUDE.md's proportionality paragraph in the same commit rather than living only here, for D-228's own reason: a rule whose limits are stated only in a decision log is one the next reader applies without them. THE REST OF THE BUCKET AT THIS SAME CONTACT, recorded because D-242's rule WORKING is worth as much on the record as its rulings, and because a T-item touched and deliberately left alone is otherwise indistinguishable from one never reached. T4 — "where the run is cheap" is a SELF-JUDGING trigger with no threshold — was TOUCHED AND NEEDED NO AMENDMENT: the work package judged its own run cheap (≈35 minutes expected, ≈1 h 40 m worst case, one workstation) and therefore APPLIED the replication clause rather than arguing out of it, and resolving a self-judging trigger in the direction that BINDS MORE is safe under either reading of it. No ruling is owed for that direction; a package that judged itself EXPENSIVE in order to escape the clause would be a different instance entirely, and it is the one T4 is still waiting for. T1, T2 and T3 were CHECKED AND ARE NOT HIT: T1 (a harness reviewed after the run it governs) is avoided by the ordering the pre-registration registers in its opening section; T2 (recording versus checking the dry-run output) is OVER-satisfied, because the pre-registration states in advance what each dry run must SHOW, which is stricter than the statute and legislates nothing for anyone else; T3 (a kind with only one instance, where "never on the registered workload itself" is unsatisfiable) does not arise, because each of the three registered commands has a constructible second instance and the spread position is CONSTRUCTED from rule 5 rather than borrowed from the fixture. Flips if a package is ever found for which no consequence can be stated in advance, which would mean the instrument was not a second instrument.

D-246: THE SNAPSHOT'S SETUP CRITERION IS SESSION-LEVEL, AND THE THREE POSITIONS THAT FAIL IT PER-POSITION ARE RECORDED CONTEXT AND NOT A FAILING GATE — MAJOR-2's operative reading, written down because the criterion has two arithmetically identical spellings and a reader who picks the wrong SCOPE for it reaches the opposite verdict. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY COMPUTES, read off the script rather than remembered: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` forms `setup_fraction_pct = 100*(corpus_wall_ms − engine_sum_ms)/corpus_wall_ms` over the WHOLE CORPUS and raises `SETUP-HEAVY` above 5.0. At 050961d the baseline snapshot reads `timing corpus_wall_ms 14413 engine_sum_ms 14178` and `timing setup_fraction_pct 1.63 ok`, so THE GATE PASSES, with a factor of 3.07 of headroom against its own bar. THE SOURCE RECORD IS SHA-INDEXED RATHER THAN COMMITTED, which is what rule 8 allows and what D-236 already does for its own inputs: the snapshot is `baseline_050961d.txt`, 5764 bytes, sha256 `9feb8212885676a5215e3a0e29d301ede160da74854d67b9b63a017777fcdc89`, written to the WP session's scratchpad under `…/7f24c595-3326-49da-b96a-5afaabf52572/scratchpad/workbench/`. It is an artifact and is never committed; the digest is here so the table below can be re-checked against the record it was read from instead of being taken on this line's word. AND THE RECORD'S OWN MARKING IS STATED RATHER THAN PASSED OVER: its line 57 heads the timing block `# timing — machine-, schedule- and worktree-dependent; excluded from every comparison`, and EVERY number quoted here — the corpus wall, the engine sum, the fraction and all 24 per-position `time_ms` — comes from inside that block. The ruling below is CONSISTENT with that marking and is strengthened by saying so: a block excluded from every comparison can still carry a flag about the run that produced it, which is what the corpus-level fraction is, but it cannot license a per-position reading to be set against anything else, which is precisely why those readings are diagnostic here and not a gate. THE PER-POSITION READING, computed here rather than quoted: at D-236's measured session exposure E = 9.46 ms the same formula applied to a single position is `E/(t + E)`, which clears 5 % iff `t > 19E` = 179.7 ms of search — D-236's number restated, not a second one: 19 × 9.46 = 179.74, which that line rounds to 179.8 and this one to 179.7, and a reader meeting both is reading one quantity — equivalently iff that position's TOTAL wall exceeds `E/0.05` = 189.2 ms. THE TWO NUMBERS ARE THE SAME CRITERION ON DIFFERENT DENOMINATORS, differing by exactly E, and that is the trap this line exists to disarm: comparing an engine-reported `time_ms` against 189.2 fails a fourth position that in fact passes, which is a real derivation this session made and had to correct. Over the 24 positions THREE FAIL: position 15 at `time_ms 170` (5.27 %), position 17 at `time_ms 18` (34.45 %, and it is the corpus minimum), position 20 at `time_ms 165` (5.42 %). Position 18 at `time_ms 187` is NEAR THE LINE at 4.82 % and PASSES. THE RULING: THE SESSION-LEVEL FLAG IS THE OPERATIVE CRITERION; the three per-position failures are RECORDED CONTEXT and no gate fired. The snapshot is a CORPUS instrument — it emits one record over 24 positions and every comparison it licenses is corpus-to-corpus — so the fraction that governs is the one taken over the corpus, and a per-position fraction is a diagnostic naming which positions carry the least search per unit of setup, which is a fact about corpus COMPOSITION and not about the budget. A later session reading those three numbers must not conclude the budget failed: it did not, and nothing here reopens the verdict D-236 recorded. ONE APPARENT DISAGREEMENT WITH D-236 IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND: this line reads `setup_fraction_pct 1.63` where D-236 records the snapshot instrument at 1.66-1.71 % over its 24 positions, which is OUTSIDE that stated range. It is neither a contradiction nor a correction of D-236 — it is a different run at a different revision, and the timing block both readings come from is marked excluded from every comparison, so the two were never comparable and neither number moves the other. What WOULD be a defect is quoting 1.63 while claiming to restate nothing of D-236's, so the claim is narrowed to what is true: this line restates D-236's E and its 179.7/179.8 threshold, and reports its own run's fraction as a fresh reading of an explicitly non-comparable quantity rather than as corroboration. ONE QUANTITY THIS LINE ADDS: the session's own implied per-position setup, (14413 − 14178)/24 = 9.79 ms, sits 0.33 ms from the K-sweep's independently fitted E = 9.46 ms — a second and weaker corroboration of the same number out of the snapshot's own arithmetic, offered as that and not as a re-measurement. Flips on D-236's trigger and no other: if `tt_bytes` moves then E moves and every threshold above is recomputed from it; and a harness running ONE PROCESS PER SEARCH pays 28.2 ms rather than 9.46, at which point NINE positions rather than three sit under the per-position line and the question of which scope governs is worth re-asking rather than being answered by this line.

D-247: T6, T7 AND T8 HAVE NO CONTENT ON THE RECORD, AND THE GAP IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FILLED — D-242 counts EIGHT open process readings against CLAUDE.md's dry-run and proportionality paragraphs, and only FIVE of them exist anywhere. THE FINDING, run rather than quoted, and SPELLED SO THAT A LATER READER CAN RE-RUN IT — the naive form of this check falsifies itself the moment this line lands, because a line about T-numbers necessarily contains T-numbers and a raw count then counts them: `grep -o "T[1-9])" docs/decisions.md | sort -u` returns exactly `T1)` through `T5)`, five DISTINCT numbers, with no sixth, seventh or eighth among them — and this line is careful never to write a T-number of its own in that parenthesised form, because doing so would break the command in the sentence that states it — where the un-deduplicated form returns a LARGER count that this line deliberately does not pin, because it re-quotes `T1)` and `T5)` in the act of explaining itself and any future line discussing the bucket will do the same: a raw count is unstable by construction, and fixing a number to it would re-create the exact defect this sentence exists to remove. The ENUMERATED occurrences — the ones that introduce a reading rather than mention one — are all inside D-235. And `grep -rn "T[6-8]" --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=target .` returns exactly TWO lines in the whole tree, both in this log — D-242's own sentence saying they "came from the closing round on the same two paragraphs", and this line — and nothing outside `docs/decisions.md` at all. Neither command finds CONTENT for the three; both find only mentions of a missing thing, which is the finding. A reproducer in an append-only law log has to survive the line that states it, or it certifies nothing to the only reader who needs it. The session scratchpads were searched as well, since a closing round's brief is where such text would live: the round-three brief's process-findings section — the one headed "judge, propose, do NOT unilaterally amend" — enumerates T1 through T5 and stops, and no fourth-round or closing brief exists on disk. THE CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is a line and not a shrug: D-242's rule is that "the FIRST SESSION THAT ACTUALLY HITS ONE resolves it then, with a one-line amendment citing the T-number", and that rule is UNEXECUTABLE for these three, because a session cannot recognize — let alone resolve — a reading it cannot read. D-242's count of eight is therefore five on the record and three unrecorded, and a later reader counting T-numbers in this log will find five and must not conclude the missing three were resolved somewhere. WHY THAT IS TOLERABLE MEANWHILE, stated here rather than assumed: D-242's own boundary clause holds that NONE of the eight was graded blocking and that every one of them is an AMBIGUITY — a reading the text does not settle — rather than an exploit; and the same clause excludes from the bucket any finding exploitable against RESULT INTEGRITY, where following the text as written produces a wrong number or licenses a run that should have been refused, which takes an amendment immediately and is deferred by nothing. So whatever the three say, the boundary that admitted them to the bucket is also the guarantee that they are not hiding such a finding. THE GAP COSTS RECOGNITION, NOT INTEGRITY: what is lost is a session's ability to notice it has hit one of the three, which is exactly what D-245 was able to do for T5. RECORDING A GAP IS NOT INVENTING ITS CONTENTS — no reconstruction of T6, T7 or T8 is offered here and none may be, because this log is append-only law and a plausible invention in it is worse than an absent line, which is the same standard D-227 applies to a dry run that exercises syntax and calls it attribution. Flips when the operator supplies the three sentences, at which point they take their T-numbers and the bucket is whole again; and D-242's other trigger stands beside it — if the count GROWS rather than closes, eight open readings of two paragraphs stop being a bucket and become evidence that the paragraphs need rewriting rather than annotating.

D-248: THE "DEPLOYMENT CONFIG = `instrument_v0.toml`, RADIUS 3" CLAIM WAS A CLASS AND D-244 CLOSED ONE INSTANCE OF IT; THIS CLOSES THE CLASS, AT SEVEN SITES. Found by the fresh-context REVIEW-impl of `050961d..1c27974` and NOT by the check that produced D-244, which is the finding worth recording: D-244's flip clause reads "this header is a claim about a config VALUE and is re-read whenever the value changes", scoped to the one file it was fixing, so nothing in it scheduled the SIBLING copies of the same sentence for re-reading — an instance-scoped correction that leaves the class alive, which is silent drift under rule 10 wearing the costume of a correction. THE FACTS, taken from `tools/config_check.sh`'s own output rather than from memory: `configs/gate_v0.toml` is `radius = 1`, `configs/instrument_v0.toml` is `radius = 2` (D-190/D-194), and the config that SHIPS is `configs/play_v0.toml`, `radius = 3`, `mode=Play`. THE SEVEN SITES: `configs/gate_v0.toml`'s opening stanza ("NOT a deployment config. That is configs/instrument_v0.toml, whose candidate radius of 3…") and its "the shallow tactical cases … run at the radius that ships" clause; `crates/pistol-cli/tests/tactical_v0_tests.rs`'s module doc, its `configs()` assertion message, its depth-one comment, and its `#[ignore]` reason; and `tools/tactical_check.sh`'s header — the seventh, which the review's own list did not name and which the class sweep for the word "deployment" across `crates/`, `configs/` and `tools/` found. That seventh site is the argument for sweeping a class by its words instead of by its report: a list of instances is itself an instance-scoped artefact. `tools/determinism.sh`'s neighbouring comment was swept and LEFT ALONE, because it is true — it says the gate is not the deployment config and that depth 4 at radius 3 costs hours, and names no config as the deployment one. THE COST FIGURE IS ALSO CORRECTED, and it was measured here rather than copied: the `#[ignore]` reason said "at the deployment radius a completed depth 3 costs ~100 s", but NO case in `tactical_v0.txt` runs at radius 3 — five depth-3 cases run at `gate_v0`'s radius 1 and the other fifteen at the instrument radius 2 — and the whole twenty-case suite, each case searched twice, costs 4823/4810/4816 ms over three replications through `./target/release/pistol selftest --fixtures crates/pistol-cli/tests/fixtures/tactical_v0.txt`, against 63.13 s for the same suite as the ignored test under `cargo test --locked -p pistol-cli --test tactical_v0_tests -- --ignored`. THE `#[ignore]` THEREFORE STAYS AND ITS REASON CHANGES: the marker was defensible for the wrong reason, and the right one is the ~13x debug penalty, not a radius the suite never runs at. The 84-100 s figure stays in `gate_v0.toml`'s measurement table, where it is the true cost of radius 3 and this config's whole reason for existing. WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE EDITING, because a prose-only edit can still break a pin: `configs/gate_v0.toml` has NO digest pinned anywhere — its sha256 `8c053f35…` appears nowhere in the tree, and D-220 pins `instrument_v0.toml` (`3579855e…`), the weight table and the bench corpus, not this file — so nothing needed re-pinning; `tools/config_check.sh` re-validated all four engine documents `ok` after the edit; `tactical_v0.txt` is BYTE-UNTOUCHED and still hashes to D-244's `7acb3ea3…`, so `TACTICAL_V0_SHA256` does not move in this commit; and the `tools/tactical_check.sh` edit is comment-only, verified by diffing both revisions with comment lines stripped, so none of `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md`'s ten items is reachable by it — no command substitution, pipeline, `grep` status, locale, index, prefix sweep, trap, number spelling or recorded value changes. TWO SENTENCES THAT FOLLOWED HERE ARE CORRECTED IN PLACE UNDER A `tools/`-SCOPED REVIEW FINDING (D-250), on the operator's in-place licence for lines landed in this session's sequence — unmerged on `dev`, cited by nothing. THE FIRST READ «and its coverage rule is untouched because the script's recorded number still comes from the shipped binary the gate already drives», AND IT IS REBUTTED. The produce-versus-forward distinction is not one D-240 draws — its rationale is «A number nothing tests is a number nothing defends» — and `tools/tactical_check.sh` is CI GATE 8 OF 13 (`tools/ci.sh:63`), its stdout carries `selftest: 20 of 20 cases solved (required 20), 0 failed to reproduce`, and its exit status IS the gate verdict. The clause's premise failed outright besides: the review REPRODUCED the script printing that very line and exiting 0 for a binary that was never built, so its verdict was not a statement about the shipped binary at all, and NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY EXECUTED THIS SCRIPT until D-250 added `crates/pistol-cli/tests/tactical_check_gate_tests.rs`. THE SECOND READ «A tools/-scoped review is nevertheless owed on that header under CLAUDE.md's tools/ clause and this session could not dispatch it», AND THAT REVIEW HAS NOW BEEN TAKEN — fresh context, against `d2a09b0`, answering `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` by name — AND IT FOUND A MAJOR: the gate ran a hardcoded `./target/release/pistol` that cargo need not have built, which is EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER, fixed with its reproduction at D-250. An owed review that was discharged and found a MAJOR is a materially different record from one still outstanding, which is why this is corrected rather than left to read as an open item. The comment-only reasoning above was sound ABOUT THE EDIT and simply did not reach the FILE the edit was in — which is the whole lesson of this line, arriving one paragraph late. Flips ON THE CLASS AND NOT ON A FILE: whenever ANY committed config's candidate radius moves, or a config joins or leaves `configs/`, every site naming a config's radius in prose is re-read together — the sweep is `grep -rn "deployment\|radius that ships\|instrument_v0" crates/ configs/ tools/ docs/ROADMAP.md` — and a correction that names one file without running that sweep is this same defect recurring.

D-249: AMENDS D-225 — WP-1.5a IS THE `pistol-solver` THREAT GENERATOR, AND THE EVAL WINDOW-MAP STORAGE CHANGE D-225 CALLED BY THAT NAME IS RENUMBERED **WP-1.9**, LICENSED AND NOT SCHEDULED. Operator ruling, on a conflict the WP-1.5a DESIGN session found and reported in its own draft-F line. D-225 IS NOT EDITED; this is the successor-line form the log uses for an amendment (D-235 amending D-220), and only the three lines the operator ruled on in the REVIEW-impl fix set were touched in place. THE CONFLICT: D-225 opens WP-1.5a as the `pistol-eval` map-storage change on D-223's profile and says "its bracket belongs in whole-engine nps against `tools/bench_delta.sh`", while WP-1.5a's dispatch scopes it to the `pistol-solver` threat generator and makes any `pistol-eval` refactor an explicit NON-GOAL. Two work packages under one designation is silent drift under rule 10 whichever of them is right, and D-216 shows how it happened: the storage WP was scheduled BEFORE WP-1.5's threat tables and the two later took one name. THE HARD CONSEQUENCE THAT DECIDES IT: **p = 0 for `pistol-solver`**, so D-225's whole-engine bracket is not merely inconvenient for the dispatch's scope, it is UNSATISFIABLE there. Measured, not asserted, and re-verified independently at this revision: `grep -rn "pistol-solver" Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml` returns ONE line, the crate's own `name =`; `cargo tree -p <crate> --locked` shows no `pistol-solver` edge from ANY of the seven workspace crates, `pistol-cli` included; and `crates/pistol-solver/src/lib.rs` is a doc-only stub whose own text says it "carries no code until the threat generation work package opens". Amdahl is then `1/(1 − 0 + 0/k) = 1.000` for EVERY k. SO WP-1.5a's PRE-REGISTRATION REGISTERS H1 AS EXACTLY `1.000x`, A NO-CHANGE HYPOTHESIS, adjudicated by the baseline snapshot's INVARIANT block being byte-identical excluding the `revision` line, `binary_sha256` included. That is falsifiable and it is not a placeholder: what a 1.000x bracket catches is an ACCIDENTAL DEPENDENCY EDGE — a solver crate that quietly enters the shipped binary changes the digest and fails the hypothesis — and it is written down here because a reader meeting "1.000x" in a rule-5 bracket will otherwise read it as a number someone forgot to fill in. WP-1.9's LICENSING EVIDENCE, carried over so the renumbering costs nothing: D-223's §0.4 prediction putting the eval map at 34-48 % of samples (D-225's own ground, unchanged), plus the eval-side stake the DESIGN session measured — k = 4.4-4.9 for its storage winner over the incumbent `BTreeMap<Window, Counts>` shape, over the real corpus at the real occupancy of 120-386 windows, three replications — from which `1/(1 − p + p/k)` PREDICTS a whole-engine 1.36x-1.62x. That figure is a prediction off a micro-instrument and an earlier profile, never a whole-engine measurement, and WP-1.9's own `bench_delta.sh` run is what replaces it. `docs/ROADMAP.md` is amended in this same commit to carry WP-1.9 and to name the WP-1.5a/WP-1.5b cut, so the roadmap and this log cannot disagree about what the designations mean. TWO CORRECTIONS TO D-225'S NUMBERS, which is what a later reader most needs from this line. Its headline "measured 1.54x-1.89x on the lookup path and 1.25-1.30x on surgery in a standalone bench" DOES NOT REPRODUCE on this machine: the DESIGN session re-derived rather than inherited it and measures the packed-`u64` key at 1.289/1.360/1.343 on lookup across three replications of nine reps, FLAT at 1.34-1.37 across occupancies from 547 to 11 457 entries — the prior's lower bound above the new upper bound at every occupancy reachable — while surgery comes in at 1.377/1.439/1.407, which is ABOVE D-225's 1.25-1.30. The two halves miss in OPPOSITE directions, which argues the difference is in what was timed rather than in the machine. But D-225's RELATIVE figure — "open addressing against a PACKED btree measures k = 4.1" — DOES reproduce, at a floor-subtracted 4.07/4.20/4.17, which points at the incumbent-side measurement as the discrepancy and leaves the STRUCTURAL conclusion of D-225 standing while its headline does not. THIS IS RECORDED AS AN OPEN DISCREPANCY BETWEEN TWO INSTRUMENTS AND NEITHER IS DECLARED WRONG: the earlier number came from a standalone bench whose shape cannot now be re-inspected, nothing currently rests on it — the packed key is adopted as a COMPONENT of the recommended option, where its cost is inside that option's own measured k — and declaring a winner between two instruments on the evidence of one of them is the move D-245's agreement-criterion clause exists to forbid. LOGGED, NOT DISPATCHED: the threat core stays on the critical path and WP-1.9 opens when the operator schedules it. Flips two ways: an edge from any binary to `pistol-solver` makes p non-zero and reopens the whole-engine question for the threat generator, at which point WP-1.5a's H1 stops being 1.000x and needs a real bracket; and WP-1.9 opening its own pre-registration replaces the 1.36x-1.62x stake recorded here with a measurement, which supersedes this line's numbers and the discrepancy above with it.

D-250: EVERY GATE THAT BUILDS A BINARY RESOLVES ITS PATH FROM CARGO'S OWN ARTIFACT STREAM, WHICH IS THE BINARY THE GATE RUNS AT THREE OF THE FOUR AND WAS NOT AT GATE 12 UNTIL D-252 — THIS HEADLINE READ «EVERY GATE THAT BUILDS A BINARY NOW RUNS THE BINARY CARGO BUILT» AND IS CORRECTED IN PLACE UNDER A `tools/`-SCOPED REVIEW FINDING, ON THE OPERATOR'S IN-PLACE LICENCE FOR LINES LANDED IN THIS SESSION'S SEQUENCE — AND `tools/tactical_check.sh` IS DRIVEN BY A TEST. Found by the fresh-context `tools/`-scoped review D-248 said was owed, dispatched against `d2a09b0`, and it is the class `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` opens with: EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER. THE DEFECT: the gate ran `cargo build --release --locked --quiet --bin pistol` and then executed the literal `./target/release/pistol` with no guard of any kind, and cargo's target directory is redirectable — by `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, by `[build] target-dir` in any `.cargo/config.toml`, and by `[build] target`, which moves the artifact into a per-triple subdirectory. REPRODUCED BEFORE ANY FIX LANDED, in a scratch tree holding the shipped script over a zero-dependency stub crate whose `--bin pistol` is the engine: with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` redirected and the previous build left at the hardcoded path, the gate printed `selftest: 20 of 20 cases solved (required 20), 0 failed to reproduce` and exited 0 while the binary cargo had just built printed `19 of 20` and exited 1; with nothing at that path, bash's 127 flowed into the `||` and the gate answered `the tactical suite did not meet its pre-registered threshold`, blaming the ENGINE for a tactical regression that never happened — a worse wrong diagnosis than the one `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh:281-285` was already fixed for. LATENT ON THIS MACHINE, checked rather than assumed — `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` unset, no `~/.cargo/config.toml`, no repository `.cargo/` — so no gate claim already made is in doubt. THE REMEDY WAS CHOSEN AGAINST THREE ALTERNATIVES AND MEASUREMENTS DECIDED IT, not the sibling pattern's familiarity. (i) The reviewer's minimum — `ENGINE="$ROOT/target/release/pistol"` plus `[ -x ]`, as `tools/determinism.sh` and `tools/arena_smoke.sh` already spelled it — closes the missing-binary case and LEAVES THE STALE-BINARY REPRODUCER OPEN, which is the half that exits 0. (ii) `cargo metadata`'s `target_directory` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and `[build] target-dir`, but was MEASURED here reporting `<root>/target` while `[build] target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"` puts the artifact at `<root>/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/pistol` — the same stale-binary hole, one directory deeper. (iii) An explicit `--target-dir` overrides both redirects but was MEASURED landing at `<dir>/<triple>/release/pistol` under that same config key, so it leaves the hole too, and it would countermand a deliberate operator redirect — a shared build cache, a small disk — which a gate has no business doing. (iv) ADOPTED: `cargo build … --message-format=json-render-diagnostics`, reading the `executable` field off the artifact record. The path is then A FACT REPORTED BY THE BUILDER rather than an inference by the script, which is the only one of the four that cannot be wrong; rustc diagnostics still render to stderr, and the extra cost is 0.034 s on an already-fresh build. THE FIX IS CLASS-SCOPED AND NOT FILE-SCOPED, which is D-248's own flip clause applied to the correction that answers it: all four gates that run a binary they just built take the same block — `tools/tactical_check.sh` (CI gate 8), `tools/determinism.sh` (gate 9), `tools/movetime_check.sh` (gate 11), `tools/arena_smoke.sh` (gate 12). D-253: THE `WIN_LEN` WINDOW ENUMERATION MOVES FROM `pistol-eval` INTO `pistol-core` AS `pistol_core::window`, AND `pistol_eval::window` BECOMES A RE-EXPORT SO NO CALL SITE CHANGES — D-67's OWN FLIP CLAUSE FIRING AS WRITTEN, RECORDED AS THE FLIP AND NOT AS AN AMENDMENT TO D-67. D-67 says it in the sentence that decides the case: “flips if Stage 1's threat generator needs the same enumeration, which moves this module into core rather than copying it”. Stage 1's threat generator (WP-1.5a) needs exactly that enumeration, so the clause fires. OPERATOR RULING, against a design revision that recommended the solver define its own window and quoted D-67's PREMISE (“a window length is a property of an eval backend and not a rule”) while omitting the flip clause that disposes of the question — citing an ADR's premise without the clause that decides it is the drift rule 10 exists to prevent, and worse than a wrong recommendation because it makes the log look like it agreed. RULE 2 IS THE INDEPENDENT GROUND: the solver's window length is `WIN_LEN` BECAUSE of rule 2, and rules truth lives in `pistol-core` only. WHAT MOVES: `WINDOW_LEN`, `WINDOWS_PER_CELL`, `Window` (`new`, `cells`) and `windows_through`, composing the geometry core already owns (`Axis::direction` through `Coord::checked_step`) and restating no rule. WHAT IS NEW SURFACE, added by the same commit because the threat state needs it: `Window::cell(index)`, which PANICS by name on an index off the end rather than wrapping or clamping (rule 3), and `windows_through_indexed`, which yields the index each window holds the cell at — the enumeration's own loop variable, free, and what lets a consumer carry per-window occupancy MASKS instead of bare counts, so that WHICH cells of a window are empty is answerable without a second reading of the board. `windows_through` is now that enumeration with the index dropped, so the eval and the threat state cannot walk two different sequences. MEASURED, TWICE AND INDEPENDENTLY: both the design session's migration and a reviewer's textually-different one produce a `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` invariant block BYTE-IDENTICAL to stock on all 24 positions, differing only in `binary_sha256`; this implementation reproduces that a third time, and ITS PAIR DIFFERS IN TWO INVARIANT LINES AND NOT ONE — `revision` (72316a7 against cdbcbf0) as well as `binary_sha256` — because that third comparison SPANS A COMMIT while the first two were taken at the same working revision and so shared a `revision` line. Corrected in place under a REVIEW-impl finding, and the correction is to the ACCOUNT ONLY: no reading moves, every position still matches. D-249's wording for the same instrument — byte-identical excluding the `revision` line — is the one that generalises, and a blanket "two lines" would be as wrong about the first two comparisons as "one line" was about the third. Workspace tests, clippy `-D clippy::all`, `tools/file_justification_check.sh` and `tools/determinism.sh` all pass. THE COST CLAIM IS BOUNDED, NOT ZERO: `windows_through` is 13.51 % of pooled eval self time (D-192) and this workspace sets no LTO (D-14), so a lost cross-crate inline was the risk; the measured effect is NOT RESOLVABLE BELOW ABOUT 2 %, which suffices to decide, because a lost inline on 13.51 % of self time would show far above that. It does NOT establish that `#[inline]` is unnecessary, and this line does not claim it: `#[inline]` is applied to `Window::new`, `Window::cells`, `Window::cell`, `windows_through` AND `windows_through_indexed` as INSURANCE whose necessity is UNMEASURED, never as a fix for a cost anyone observed. THE FIFTH WAS MISSING WHEN THIS LINE FIRST SHIPPED AND IS ADDED UNDER A REVIEW-impl FINDING, because the insurance could not reach the code it was taken out for: the enumeration BODY moved into `windows_through_indexed`, which carried no attribute, so `windows_through`'s `#[inline]` inlined a ONE-LINE WRAPPER over a non-inlinable cross-crate call and the loop stayed behind it.
