MEASURED ONLY AS CODEGEN AND CLAIMED NO FURTHER: adding the attribute changes the release `pistol` digest `ff018398a886…` to `a9ea9d145777…`, and that pair was reproduced at a later revision by a session other than the one that found it, so the compiler genuinely does something different. WHETHER IT COSTS OR SAVES ANYTHING IS UNMEASURED and sits below the ~2 % this instrument resolves; a single-sample nps reading offered in its defence would be precisely the sin this line's own strongest surviving attack names, and none is offered. RULE 5's DISPOSITION FOR THE `#[inline]` IS WRITTEN DOWN HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO INFERENCE, under a REVIEW-impl finding that the rule is prima facie ENGAGED — an inline attribute is a purely performance-directed change and nothing in this line said why it does not owe a pre-registered hotspot, a gain bracket, an abort threshold and one IQR-gated bench. IT DOES NOT, FOR ONE REASON: rule 5's apparatus exists to ADJUDICATE A CLAIM, and this line makes none. The necessity is recorded as UNMEASURED, an nps reading is explicitly refused, and there is no hypothesis for a bracket to bracket or a threshold to abort. AND THE ARGUMENT THAT WOULD BE WRONG HERE IS NAMED SO NOBODY REACHES FOR IT: this is NOT excused by D-249's `p = 0`. That figure is about `pistol-solver`, which nothing links; the attribute is in `pistol-core`, which the shipped binary DOES link, and the moving digest is the proof of it. What disposes of rule 5 is the absence of a claim, not the absence of a linkage. THE SECOND HALF IS THAT THE INSTRUMENT COULD NOT ADJUDICATE IT ANYWAY: this line's own comparison is not resolvable below about 2 %, and its strongest surviving attack shows the protocol returning +1.54 % disjoint, −0.93 % interleaved and +0.30 % combined on the SAME pair of binaries against a within-build sd of ~900 nps. An IQR-gated bench at that magnitude returns a number that attack refutes in advance, and shipping it as a verdict would be the post-hoc threshold move the process forbids — CLAUDE.md's own answer to a cheap workload in doubt is replication and a second instrument with a registered agreement criterion, not one more run of the instrument already known to manufacture the sign. THE CODEGEN FACT IS REPRODUCED AGAIN AND AT A NEW REVISION, which is the only claim made: at `7b9e904` the release `pistol` digest is `eb055e40c137…` without the fifth attribute and `a7f519fade11…` with it, both halves taken in a separate worktree. THE PAIR IS NOT THE ONE ABOVE AND THAT IS NOT A DISCREPANCY — the digest is revision-specific, so `ff018398a886…`/`a9ea9d145777…` and this pair are two readings of one effect at two revisions, and only the DIRECTION is the claim. THE COUNT IS FOUR OBSERVATIONS ACROSS FOUR SESSIONS, stated exactly because an earlier revision of this very clause said "a third time by a third session" and undercounted: the first pair was found by one session and reproduced by a second, and this pair was reported by a REVIEW-impl reviewer and reproduced by the session that logged it here. `a7f519fade11…` is also the digest at the head of the fix round following `7b9e904`, byte-identical across it because nothing links `pistol-solver`, which re-confirms D-249's `p = 0` as a side effect. RULE 5 REOPENS the moment any line quotes `#[inline]` as a speed, or a bench with `p > 0` names the window enumeration as a measured hotspot; at that point the change to bracket is the REMOVAL of the attribute and not its addition, because the attribute is what ships. ONE TEST FROM THIS LINE'S COMMIT IS HALF TAUTOLOGICAL, RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: `windows_through_indexed_names_the_index_the_cell_occupies` asserts that `windows_through` equals the indexed enumeration with the index dropped, which cannot fail while the former is DEFINED as that map — it is a valid pin against a future reimplementation that splits the two, and its second half, that each window holds the cell at the index it names, is a real claim, so it stays as written rather than being rewritten into a form nobody needs. THREE COSTS, RECORDED BECAUSE “strictly better” MUST SAY WHAT IT COSTS. (1) THE MOVED MODULE'S DOC REVERSES: it argued the enumeration lived in eval BECAUSE the length is a backend property and not a rule, citing rule 2 and D-67 — moved verbatim into core it would assert, inside core, the opposite of what this line decides, citing the very rule and ADR it rests on. The doc is rewritten by this same commit, and the backend-length sentence moves to `pistol-eval`'s re-export where it becomes a forward reference to the Stage-2 codebook window. (2) THE CROSS-CRATE PIN BECOMES A TAUTOLOGY: `const _: () = assert!(WINDOW_LEN == WIN_LEN)` beside `pub const WINDOW_LEN: u32 = WIN_LEN;` in the same crate asserts nothing, so it is DROPPED; the assert that is not vacuous — `WINDOW_STEPS as u32 == WINDOW_LEN`, a length against a coordinate step count — is carried across with the module. (3) STAGE 2 IS RELOCATED, NOT DISSOLVED: there is one enumeration UNTIL the codebook lands and two again after, core's rules window and `pistol-eval`'s own length-eleven window; and this forecloses the length-parameterised alternative, because core's window is now a RULES object whose length is `WIN_LEN` by construction and a generic `Window<const N>` in core would re-open exactly the question D-67 settled. THE W3 DIGEST IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS INDEPENDENT MIGRATIONS — `daf1deb3…` for the design session, `691f7766…` for the reviewer, both search-identical to stock — so only the STOCK side may ever be pinned in advance, and this move lands in ITS OWN COMMIT AHEAD of the threat generator: WP-1.5a's H1 compares a fresh baseline snapshot taken AT THIS REVISION, and folding the two commits together would ABORT H1 on a digest change the design already knows about. ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LOG, NO AMENDMENT OWED: D-243's definitional pointer names `crates/pistol-eval/src/window.rs`, which is now a re-export. All four names stay importable from `pistol_eval::window`, so the pointer resolves, but a reader following D-243 to find the enumeration will not find it there. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, from the DECISION-RED-TEAM and carried verbatim: “the cost measurement is block-ordered and the protocol manufactures the result — twelve snapshots of two such binaries give +1.54 % for this protocol with disjoint groups, −0.93 % interleaved, and +0.30 % combined against a within-build sd of ~900 nps, so the same protocol would have licensed ‘W3 costs 2.2 %’ as readily as ‘W3 is free’, and ‘`#[inline]` was not required’ is not a conclusion an n = 1 arm can carry.” Flips only with rule 2.

D-254: `ThreatState`'s PER-WINDOW TABLE IS `std::HashMap<u64, WindowMasks>` WITH SPLITMIX64 AS A FIXED-SEED `BuildHasher`, KEYED BY AN ORDER-PRESERVING PACKED `u64` (D-225's key), AND IT IS ADOPTED ON LINE COUNT AT `p = 0`, ON NO SPEED WHATEVER. About FIFTY-FOUR lines over std against about ninety for hand-written open addressing — and the fifty-four is what the shipped file counts rather than what the design estimated: in `crates/pistol-solver/src/table.rs`, `SplitMix64` is 25 and `WindowTable` is 29 non-comment, non-blank lines, derive attributes included. THIS LINE FIRST SAID FIFTEEN, which was an estimate written before the file existed and never checked against it; corrected in place under a REVIEW-impl finding. THE DECISION IS UNTOUCHED — 54 against ~90 is still decisive at `p = 0`, and the ~90 was never measured against a shipped implementation either — but the ONE quantity this line is permitted to cite has to be the one the code has, which is the whole of why it is cited. THE RECORD IS A MASK AND NOT A PAIR OF COUNTS: six occupancy bits per side, so the counts are `count_ones()` and the EMPTY CELLS are `!(p1|p2)` with no board access — a `(own_count, opp_count)` record cannot say WHICH cells are empty, so a state carrying counts must hold or be handed a `&Board` on every query path, which is a second source of occupancy beside the one it already maintains and is the drift `EVAL_DESYNC` exists to catch. HASHING IS LEGAL HERE FOR ONE REASON AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL: the table is never iterated on a choice path. Every query answers out of the maintained SORTED sets (D-255), and the only enumeration of the table is `table_snapshot`, which returns a `BTreeMap` and is documented as being for oracles and diagnostics. The hash has written-down constants and no seed state — no `RandomState`, no per-process entropy (CLAUDE.md rule 4, D-32). AN ENTRY EXISTS EXACTLY WHILE ITS WINDOW HOLDS A STONE, pruned the moment it empties — D-62's rule for the eval's own map — which is what makes an unwound state EQUAL to a fresh one rather than merely equal in every answer, and what keeps the table's size a function of the position rather than of the search path that reached it. Pinned: `threat_apply_undo_roundtrips` asserts whole-state equality on the way back up, and a mutant that drops the pruning kills it. THE ALTERNATIVE THAT WAS NEVER A REAL OPTION: a multiply-only FxHash-style hasher collapses from a zero state to `n * K`, and since the low bits of a product depend only on the low bits of the operand while the packed key's low sixteen bits are the biased `r`, every window sharing an `r` collides — 27 distinct buckets, 81 per bucket, at every table size from 512 to 16384. A matrix that moved container and hash function together therefore never measured the option it recommended against. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, from the DECISION-RED-TEAM, carried verbatim and unsoftened: *Every positive performance ground this line states is refuted by the session's own second harness. The "~2 % on lookup and ~16 % on surgery" figures come from `minbench`, which constructs its store inside the timed region — the defect this line records for MIX-L and for no other harness — while `statebench`, the instrument the pre-registration actually registers, times the same two options on the same corpus and puts open addressing ahead on its table-only rows as well as its whole-state rows. The two readings differ by ~121 ns per apply/undo pair with opposite signs, and a shared additive enumeration constant cannot flip a sign, so at most one of them is a measurement. Corrected for the three defects in the registered instrument — it colours plies `i % 2` and so mis-colours 7 of 15 stones on every corpus position, it maintains six sets where ten are specified, and it builds its store inside the timed region — open addressing is ahead by 4.0–4.8 % with a replication spread under 1 %, the set share is 30.3–31.4 % rather than 36 %, and `k` is 1.649–1.681 rather than 1.683–1.757. The HashMap is adopted anyway and correctly, because at `p = 0` the only honest criterion is the ~85 lines of hand-written probing, backward-shift deletion and content-based equality the alternative costs and this does not. But this line must not cite a speed it does not have, and the flip is that open addressing is the faster option on every instrument that reads the corpus correctly.* AN OPTION NOBODY CONSIDERED IS RECORDED AND NOT PURSUED: per-axis line bitboards, where a stone touches 3 lines rather than 18 windows and window masks are recovered by shift and popcount, attacking the 68.6–69.7 % of the per-stone path that is not set maintenance — and the cost of deferring is that WP-1.5b's seam calcifies around a representation it removes, since every `&[Window]` this interface hands out is a commitment it would have to unwind. Flips when a bench with `p > 0` names window lookup as a measured hotspot, which is WP-1.5b's earliest opportunity; the replacement goes behind this same API and is a rule-5 change.

D-255: `ThreatState` MAINTAINS TEN SORTED WINDOW SETS — live at count 2, live at count 3, HOT (>= 4), WIN-IN-ONE-PLY (== 5) and COMPLETED (== 6), PER SIDE — AND NONE FOR COUNT 1; `LiveCount` is closed at `{Two, Three}` so count 1 is a COMPILE ERROR rather than a run-time refusal. Count 1 is not free: over the pinned corpus a side holds 32.8 count-1 windows on average at 15 stones and 55.9 at 35, against 9.6 at count 2 and 1.4 at count 3, so maintaining it pays several times the traffic of the set below it for a consumer that has asked for nothing, on every node. THE DECIDING NUMBER IS A ROOT-POSITION STATISTIC and this line says so rather than hiding it: the corpus shows own-side hot = 0.0 mean / 0 max at both stone counts, i.e. positions that do not exhibit the phenomenon the threat generator exists for. THE GROUND IS THE ABSOLUTE NUMBER AND NOT A RATIO: count-1 membership grows 32.8 -> 55.9 per side between the only two depths measured, so the memmove avoided grows with depth in absolute terms, whereas the own-side count-1:count-2 RATIO actually falls 6.19 -> 5.82 while the opponent-side one rises 3.01 -> 4.86 — the trend is mixed and a line resting on the ratio would be resting on nothing. MEMBERSHIP IS CONDITIONED ON LIVENESS: every class means `own == k && opp == 0`, so a window holding four own stones and one opponent stone is DEAD and is in no set. Writing the counts without the liveness conjunct puts a dead window in the hot set, which is why the condition lives in one function that computes a class SET from `(own, opp)` rather than in five predicates. THE SETS NEST RATHER THAN PARTITION — `own == 5` is in both hot and win-in-one-ply, `own == 6` in both hot and completed — which is why each is an independently maintained sorted `Vec<Window>` and why a "located splice" carrying one position per window is impossible here as well as unsound: one position cannot locate a window in two sets at once. `apply` AND `undo` ARE TWO-SIDED: placing a stone changes the mover's own count AND the opponent's LIVENESS in the same window, so both sides' sets are updated on every window touched, and a one-sided update leaves the opponent's dead window standing in its hot set — pinned by a fixture where the blocker enters an already-hot window, and by a mutant that restricts the update to the mover and dies there. The per-window bound is AT MOST TWO set operations, 36 per stone, established by exhaustive enumeration over every reachable `(own_mover, own_opp)`: mover operations require `own_opp == 0` and opponent removals require `own_opp >= 1`, so the two are mutually exclusive and no window ever pays for both. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK: *the deciding measurement is taken at root positions of a corpus whose own-side hot count is identically zero, so it is a measurement of the class sizes in positions the threat generator does not exist for; the depth argument that carries it to search interiors is asserted from two data points whose ratio moves in the wrong direction, and only the absolute count supports it.* Flips if a consumer needs count-1 windows, which is an additive set and a `LiveCount` variant.

D-256: THE INCREMENTAL THREAT STATE CARRIES AN ORACLE OBLIGATION AND ITS REGIME IS MECHANIZED IN THE TEST RATHER THAN CITED — D-68's pattern in full, third instance after the eval (D-68) and the search (D-106). A FROM-SCRATCH REFERENCE SHARING ONLY `pistol-core` IMPLEMENTS THE WHOLE QUERY SURFACE AND NOT THE TABLE, checked at every ply of seeded playouts against the incremental state, and itself checked on the golden fixtures against an independent bounding-box REGION SCAN that assumes nothing about where stones are. Scoping the reference to the table and running the shipped queries over it would compare the cover enumeration, the phase conditioning and the witness selection AGAINST THEMSELVES, and those are exactly where this design's two blocking defects were; so the reference enumerates covers by a different algorithm (all subsets within budget, then discard any with a proper subset that also covers), computes the minimum hitting set by trying sizes rather than by a per-budget predicate, and selects the witness by sorting candidates rather than by a running minimum. THE REGIME, REGISTERED: seeds `1..=12` with `Rng::new(seed)` by the eval crate's own convention, cap 150 plies, plies coloured by `GameState::place` and NEVER by ply parity, and — the part that is not obvious — ONE `random_ply` DRAW PER PLY, AND THAT DRAW IS THE PLY. The schedule is registered because it is load-bearing: the model this loop was copied from draws twice and plays the first, which advances the generator between plies and changes every trajectory, dropping the unblockable count from 205 to 41 and FAILING the floor below on a correct implementation. THE FLOORS ARE ASSERTED IN THE TEST — `REQUIRED_STEPS = 1000`, `REQUIRED_HOT_POSITIONS = 400`, `REQUIRED_UNBLOCKABLE = 100`, `REQUIRED_CROSS_WINDOW = 100` and `REQUIRED_HOT_CELLS = 1600` — because a shrunken playout is a shrunken oracle, not a pass. THE FIFTH IS ADDED UNDER A REVIEW-impl FINDING AND THE REASON IS A UNIT ERROR, not a number that drifted: `hot_window_empties_are_always_legal_placements` counts CELLS — every empty of every hot window, several per hot side-position — and asserted them against `REQUIRED_HOT_POSITIONS`, which is a floor on `(ply, side)` PAIRS. The regime produces 3330 cells against that 400, so the legality check could have shrunk by four fifths and still passed the floor that was supposed to stop exactly that. The new floor is about half the measured value, which is the ratio the other four already sit at (1000/1703, 400/805, 100/205, 100/266), and 3330 joins the measured census below. MEASURED AT THE REGISTERED REGIME AND REPRODUCED TO THE DIGIT by an implementation written independently of the session that registered them: 1703 plies, 805 hot side-positions, 205 unblockable, 266 cross-window instances, 3330 hot-window empty cells, about 11 s in a debug test binary. THE COMPARISON IS THE WHOLE SURFACE at every ply for both sides: the full window table as a sorted map of masks, all ten maintained sets, the three cell answers, `min_hitting_set_exceeds` at all three budgets, `blocking_covers` compared AS SETS OF COVERS rather than as a cell union, `can_win_this_turn` at both stones-left values INCLUDING the witness window, and `unblockable_double_threat` at both defender budgets; and on the way back up the state must be whole-state EQUAL to the one it had on the way down. AND EVERY REGISTERED ROW NAMES THE MUTANT IT KILLS, WITH THE MUTATION ACTUALLY MADE IN A SEPARATE WORKTREE AND RE-EVALUATED: thirteen mutants, thirteen killed — and the rule paid for itself again on the implementation, not only on the design, because `win_in_one_ply_requires_five_and_live` SURVIVED its own liveness mutant on first writing. The reason is worth recording: a dead five-window is FULL — five own stones and the opponent's in the sixth cell — so it contributes no empty CELL either way, and a row that asked only for cells could not see a mutant that put dead five-windows straight into the set. The row now asserts the WINDOWS and dies correctly. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK: *the registration whose coverage figures did not reproduce was written by the same session, in the same document, as the primitive whose empty-set case was wrong — a stated property the stated construction does not have, twice, which is evidence about the process that produced both and not only about the two artefacts.* Flips by ADR line on any change to seed, count, cap OR SAMPLING SCHEDULE.

D-257: `unblockable_double_threat` IS A STATEMENT ABOUT HITTING SETS AND NEVER ABOUT THE GAME, AND ITS COMPOSITION CARRIES TWO CONDITIONS THAT LIVE IN THE CALLER: (a) `side.opponent()` IS THE SIDE TO MOVE, and (b) `can_win_this_turn(side.opponent(), stones_left)` is `None`. D-243 consequence (3) conditions on the side to move, while this predicate describes the position AFTER `side` has moved, so (a) is not decoration: drop it and the rule is wrong in the commonest way there is — if `side` is itself to move it simply wins now, and asking whether its opponent can win asks about a turn that opponent does not have. AMENDED UNDER A RED-TEAM FINDING, AND THE AMENDMENT IS THE SHARPER HALF: ON A DECIDED POSITION (a) IS INERT AND (b) CARRIES THE RULE ALONE. `GameState::to_move()` freezes on the winning ply and reads as the WINNER, so the literal test the composition site glossed (a) with — `state.to_move() != side` — is satisfied by the side that LOST. A 20-ply `from_plies`-legal position exhibits it: P1 wins on turn 11, `to_move()` reads P1, and P2 still owns six hot windows whose minimum hitting set is 4, so `unblockable_double_threat(P2, Two)` is `true` for the side that lost, and clause (a) as written passes. The only thing between that and a mate score for the loser is (b)'s `?`, because `StonesLeft::from_state` answers `None` on a decided position. THE CODE IS RIGHT AND THIS PROSE WAS BACKWARDS — it called (a) the clause that is not decoration and treated (b) as the ordinary guard, when on this class it is the other way round — so the recipe now names the check that actually disposes of the class, `GameState::outcome()`, which `state.rs`'s module doc already carried and the composition site did not, and the `i.e. state.to_move() != side` gloss is dropped from that site. A design revision wrote (b) alone and concluded "P1 does not win" for a position P1 wins outright. The composition is pinned by a PAIR OF FIXTURES DIFFERING ONLY IN WHOSE MOVE IT IS — two padding stones appended, every other answer byte-identical — because that is the only pair that separates clause (a) from the rest, and a previously registered pair could not: at its second position BOTH clauses fail, so deleting (a) changes nothing there. AND THE EMPTY-FAMILY CASE IS PART OF THE PRIMITIVE: the minimum hitting set of an EMPTY family is 0, so it exceeds NOTHING at every budget. An algorithm that scans a universe for a covering cell finds none and answers `true`, which claims an unblockable double threat for a side owning no hot window at all — a mate score for the wrong side reached by arithmetic rather than by a missing guard, and it fires on the majority of this work package's golden positions (15 side-instances over 12 of the 16; 13 over 10 of the 14 when this line was written, before D-260 added two). The empty-family case is therefore decided FIRST, before any budget is looked at, and it is pinned by a test that enumerates every empty-hot side from the fixture rather than listing them by hand. THE CONDITIONING TYPES ARE CLOSED AND DISTINCT: `StonesLeft {One, Two}` is what the turn owes and `HitBudget {Zero, One, Two}` is what a cover may spend — conflating them in one integer is the error the pair exists to prevent, and both are closed at two because the cover enumeration is exact only for budgets of at most two over families of at most two cells. `StonesLeft::from_state` READS `GameState::stones_owed()` and returns `None` on a DECIDED position rather than contradicting core with `Two`: deriving `stones_in_turn(turn) - phase.index()` answers `Two` there, because `place` freezes the state with `phase` back at `First`. `Cover` DISTINGUISHES THREE ANSWERS — `NothingToBlock`, `Impossible`, and a NON-EMPTY `Minimal` — and returns SETS of cells rather than a cell union, because the union is provably insufficient: three hot windows with empties {a,b}, {b,d}, {d,e} have no one-cell cover and three minimal two-covers, and {a,e} is drawn from the same union and covers nothing in the middle. AND THE RECIPE'S ONLY WORKED EXAMPLE NOW FOLLOWS THE RECIPE, under a REVIEW-impl finding that is about TRANSMISSION and not about correctness. `composed_win` in `threat_query_tests.rs` is the one place this composition is written out, and it did not perform step (1)'s `GameState::outcome()` check — it relied on the `StonesLeft::from_state` path this line itself calls "correct, and it is thin". The code was right and stayed right; what was wrong is that a WP-1.5b author copying the exemplar got the thin version with nothing saying the exemplar deliberately differed. One line restores it. AND THE LINE IS INERT ON EVERY POSITION THIS SUITE HOLDS, which is said here rather than left for the next reader to discover: no golden record reaches the class where the check discriminates, because the only decided position in the fixture, `overline_seven_run`, gives the losing side no hot window at all. The position that DOES discriminate is the red-team's 20-ply construction described above and it is not in the golden set; adding it is what would turn this line from an exemplar into a pin, and that is a fixture addition under D-260's terms rather than a wording fix. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK: *both blocking defects this line fixes were in the arithmetic, not the prose — the doc comments were right and the algorithm was wrong in one case and the registered test was wrong in the other — so the line's real claim is that the arithmetic is now checked by something other than reading, and that claim rests entirely on the oracle of D-256.* Flips only with `WIN_LEN` or `TURN_STONES`.

D-258: AMENDS D-249's RECORDED STAKE FOR WP-1.9 — THE `k = 4.4-4.9` FIGURE IT CARRIES IS A TABLE-ONLY READING AND IS NOT USABLE AS A BRACKET, so the whole-engine 1.36x-1.62x it predicts must not be quoted as one. D-249 recorded that figure explicitly as a prediction off a micro-instrument and said WP-1.9's own `bench_delta.sh` run replaces it; this line says the sharper thing, which is that the instrument class is wrong for the quantity. A TABLE-ONLY `k` OVERSTATES WHAT A WHOLE STRUCTURE DELIVERS, here by roughly a factor of two — 4.4-4.9 table-only against 1.649-1.681 for the same options measured at the level of the whole state — because the maintained sets are 30.3-31.4 % of the per-stone path and no table choice touches them. WHAT WP-1.9 MUST DO, registered here so it is not rediscovered: measure at the level of the SHIPPED STRUCTURE and not an isolated table; colour plies through `GameState` and never `i % 2`, which mis-coloured 7 of 15 stones on every corpus position and agreed with the true board on 0 of 24; hoist store construction OUT of the timed region, which is worth about 40 % of the absolute lookup column; carry all ten maintained sets and not six; keep the comparand in the same run so the document can fail the decision it defends; and check the instrument against something OUTSIDE it, because a dry run whose registered criterion was that three backends agree on a checksum passed while all three shared the same wrong board. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK: *this line forwards a number it simultaneously says is not usable; a stake that cannot be quoted is a stake that will be quoted anyway by the next reader who needs one.* Flips when WP-1.9 runs and replaces the stake with a measurement.

D-259: `threat_v0.txt` IS A MACHINE-DERIVED FIXTURE AND `threat_v0_is_what_the_reference_prints` IS THE DERIVATION — every record is rendered from the from-scratch reference R1 over the committed ply lists and compared with the pinned bytes, line for line, every run. THE PREMISE THAT ARGUED AGAINST THIS WAS FALSE AND IS RECORDED AS FALSE: the implementing session believed the file could be reproduced only by an uncommitted scratch generator and was one step from declaring it hand-maintained in its own header, which would have put a false sentence in the document rule 7 exists to pin; a reviewer wrote a driver out of committed code only — `common::reference::Reference`, `common::play`, `common::window_list`/`cell_list` — and regenerated all 364 non-comment lines identically, which is why the generator is not committed and the header does not claim hand authorship. THAT 364 IS THE COUNT AT THIS LINE'S OWN COMMIT AND IS NOT MAINTAINED HERE: D-260's two records take the file to 416, of which this test derives 384, and D-264 carries the split and the exposure it measures. THREE GAPS CLOSE AT ONCE AND THE MIDDLE ONE WAS UNNOTICED. (1) The file is reproducible from the repository: nothing uncommitted stands behind it. (2) R1's OWN answers are compared against the file for the first time — the golden test compares the SHIPPED state against the file, so "computed by a from-scratch reference" was an authoring claim NO GATE ENFORCED, and a reference that had drifted from the file it produced would have been invisible. (3) The sha pin becomes a live derivation: an edited expectation must now be justified against R1 rather than merely re-hashed. THE THIRD IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — a reviewer edited a fixture's ninth ply so its own precondition no longer held, re-pinned the sha, and the whole suite stayed green because every expected answer read `-` either way. THIS IS A THIRD KIND OF FIXTURE AND THE LOG DID NOT SAY SO: `bench_positions_v1.txt` is produced by a SHIPPED binary (D-136, D-184), `tactical_v0.txt` is HAND-AUTHORED and its content IS the specification (D-122, D-204), and this one is MACHINE-DERIVED FROM R1 over the committed ply lists, regenerable by a named test, hand-maintained in nothing but the `plies` lines. THE RENDERER LIVES BESIDE THE PARSER for the reason the required-key set does — one grammar, one file — and the STATE ROW IS RENDERED FROM `GameState` AND NOT FROM R1, because a position's turn, phase and outcome are core's answer and a reference that restated them would be re-implementing the rules (CLAUDE.md rule 2). WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, said here so it is not read as more: it does not make R1 correct. R1's own checks are the independent region scan and the cross-session comparison, and a derivation is not a verification. AND THAT CROSS-SESSION COMPARISON IS NOW QUALIFIED WHERE IT IS CLAIMED: "336 of 336" is true of the values present on BOTH sides, while three row kinds here had no counterpart in the other record at all — `raise_cells`, the `win1` WINDOW lists (it carried win-in-one-ply cells), and the window a `canwin ... oneply` record names — so those rows rest on the region scan and on this regeneration. Flips if R1 is retired, or if the grammar gains a row R1 cannot print, in which case the file stops being wholly derived and the header must say which rows are not.

D-260: THE GOLDEN SET GAINS TWO POSITIONS THE REGISTERED PLAYOUT REGIME CANNOT PRODUCE, AND THE LIVENESS ROW GAINS THE PRECONDITION IT WAS ASSERTING WITHOUT — three rows whose killing power was absent, misdirected, or supplied only by a floor-gated playout, closed under a REVIEW-impl and a RED-TEAM against `5fdbf52`. (1) THE COVER-ARITHMETIC MUTANT: `min_hitting_set_exceeds` at `HitBudget::Two` walks pairs over `universe[index..]` and its own comment says `second == first` is deliberately included as the size-one case; changing that range to `universe[index + 1..]` broke NOTHING — not the fourteen fixtures, not the 1703-ply oracle. THE GAP IS STRUCTURAL AND WAS PROVED RATHER THAN GUESSED: over the registered regime's 805 hot side-positions the number whose hot-window empties union to a SINGLE cell is ZERO, so no floor and no longer playout closes it, and the obvious cheap remedy — asserting `min_hitting_set_exceeds == (blocking_covers == Impossible)` in the oracle — does not kill it either, for the same reason. `hot_universe_of_a_single_cell` is that configuration: five in a row with BOTH four-window extensions already dead, so the only hot window is the five-window and the universe is one cell. Mutant re-applied in a separate worktree after the fix: DEAD, at the new row and at no other row in the suite. (2) THE NON-VACUITY CONTROL GUARDED THE WRONG FIXTURE: the M5 row's control asserts `win_in_one_ply_windows(P1).len() == 2` on `win_in_one_ply_each_side` while the row's killing power comes from `win_in_one_ply_dead_when_opponent_enters`, whose precondition — two windows at five own stones with the opponent in the sixth cell — nothing pinned. Editing that case's ninth ply so P1 held FOUR left the whole suite green, because every expected answer of a position exhibiting nothing reads `-` either way; with the liveness mutant applied on top the row passed as well, and only the playout oracle still objected. The row now asserts `masks` for both windows — five own, one opponent, and FULL — so the fixture's precondition is stated where the row can see it, and both steps were re-run: the edit alone now fails there, and the edit plus the mutant fails there. (3) THE WITNESS TIE-BREAK'S SECOND HALF was pinned by the playout oracle ALONE: both reviewers confirmed independently that no cell in the fourteen positions is the single empty of TWO five-windows, so a determinism-relevant tie-break rested on a floor a shrunken regime would move. `two_win_in_one_ply_windows_share_their_cell` is two P1 lines crossing at `3,0`, both windows one stone from six. NOTE WHICH MUTANT VERIFIES IT, because the obvious one is EQUIVALENT: `win_in_one_ply_windows` is already sorted ascending, so the first window reaching the minimal cell IS the least, and only a mutant that keeps the LAST window at the minimal cell is a real break. It is dead at the new row, at the whole-surface comparison, and at the oracle. BOTH NEW RECORDS ARE MACHINE-DERIVED like the rest (D-259) — rendered from R1 through the fixture's own renderer, not written by hand — and the empty-hot census the suite asserts moves 13 -> 15, which is also why D-257's parenthetical is corrected in place. AND ONE THING THE DERIVATION DOES NOT DO, recorded because this session assumed otherwise and the assumption was wrong when it was run: the regeneration test does NOT catch (2). A `plies` line is an INPUT to the derivation, so an edited ply re-derives to the same expectations and the comparison passes; a derived fixture protects the ANSWERS while the QUESTION stays hand-maintained, and only a row asserting its own precondition covers that. Flips if the playout regime is ever shown to reach either configuration, in which case these two positions become redundant rather than wrong.

D-261: THE SOLVER'S PUBLIC SURFACE IS THE QUERIES AND THE STORE IS NOT PART OF IT, AND `min_hitting_set_exceeds`'s TOTALITY SENTENCE IS NARROWED TO ADDRESSABLE WINDOWS — one line because the second rests on the first. WHAT WAS EXPORTED AND USED BY NOTHING: `lib.rs` re-exported `WindowTable` and `Class`; `table.rs` published `pack`, `unpack`, `SplitMix64`, `FULL_MASK` and `empty_cells`; `sets.rs` published `Class`, `ClassSet`, `CLASS_COUNT` and `WindowSets`. A reviewer counted the uses across `tests/`: ZERO each, and only `WindowMasks` is forced public at all, by `masks()` and `table_snapshot()` returning it. THE GROUND IS D-254's OWN FLIP CLAUSE AND NOT TIDINESS: the store is its own file because the container-and-hash decision replaces EXACTLY that file and nothing else, and every internal name a consumer can reach is a commitment the replacement has to unwind — WP-1.5b is the consumer that would have seen them, and it has not been written yet, which is the only reason this costs nothing today. WHAT REMAINS: `ThreatState`, the eleven queries — `query.rs`'s eight and `cover.rs`'s three — the FOUR NON-QUERY METHODS on the same type (`masks`, `table_snapshot`, `window_count`, `is_empty`), the closed conditioning types (`StonesLeft`, `HitBudget`, `LiveCount`, `NearHot`), the answers (`Cover`, `MinimalCover`, `WinWitness`), `THREAT_DESYNC`, and `WindowMasks` with the FIVE accessors a caller reads (`own`, `opp`, `own_count`, `opp_count`, `empties`) plus its two public FIELDS `p1` and `p2`, which the region scan compares directly — `is_vacant` and `with` are the store's own and are crate-private with the rest. THIS ENUMERATION FIRST SAID FOUR ACCESSORS AND OMITTED THE FOUR NON-QUERY METHODS ALTOGETHER, corrected in place under a REVIEW-impl finding. It is D-254's "fifteen lines" that were fifty-four, in the line whose whole subject is the public surface, which is worse: a count cited in passing may be stale, but this line has no other job. AND THE SAME SENTENCE, HERE AND AT THE CRATE ROOT, CALLED `WindowMasks` WHAT "TWO OF THE ELEVEN" HAND OUT: none of the eleven returns one. `masks()` and `table_snapshot()` do, and both are outside the eleven. THE TOTALITY SENTENCE'S GUARD IS NOW MECHANIZED RATHER THAN LEFT AS PROSE, under a second REVIEW-impl finding: `min_hitting_set_exceeds` says the two doors to a non-addressable window, `unpack` and `empty_cells`, are "both crate-private", and a reviewer falsified that sentence in a single commit by re-publishing `pack`, `unpack`, `empty_cells` and `pub mod table` with clippy `-D clippy::all` at exit 0 and the whole suite green. The crate root now carries three doc examples: one that compiles through the public door, and two that must not compile through the store's. A BARE `compile_fail` PASSES ON ANY COMPILATION ERROR AND THE ERROR-CODE FORM DOES NOT REPAIR IT — measured, not assumed: this toolchain accepts `compile_fail,E0999` on code whose real error is `E0603`, so the annotation validates nothing and is not used, and an annotation that looks like validation and performs none is the EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER shape in another language. What makes the failing examples non-vacuous is the COMPILING one: every line of the longer failure appears in it and compiles there, so the only line it can fail on is the one that differs. Verified in a separate worktree both ways — green as shipped, and both failures turning RED under the reviewer's own re-publication. WHAT THE GUARD DOES NOT COVER, said here so this sentence does not rest on nothing either: a re-export of the same item under another path, `pub use table::unpack` at the root, leaves both examples failing; that door is judged at the `pub use` list and is not mechanized. THE TOTALITY CLAIM WAS FALSE AS WRITTEN, from the RED-TEAM, and hypothetical only — no in-crate caller reaches it: the doc promised totality over "windows not in this state's table", and the function is total over ADDRESSABLE windows only. `Window`'s fields are `pub` in `pistol-core`, so `Window::new`'s refusal belongs to that constructor and NOT to the type; a window written down at the far end of the lattice sends `empty_cells` through `Window::cell` into `Coord::step`, which panics with `COORD_OVERFLOW`. The second door was `unpack`, which built a `Window` directly, bypassing the addressability check, under a doc that called it "the inverse of `pack`, exactly". THE FIX IS THE SENTENCE AND THE VISIBILITY, NOT A RUN-TIME CHECK: refusing by name inside `empty_cells` would cost a `checked_step` per hot window per query on the path WP-1.5b calls PER NODE, to rename a panic that is already loud and already named; narrowing the promise costs nothing and is what the function actually delivers. SEALING `Window` IS NOT PROPOSED HERE and would not be this crate's to propose: the fields are public and used as such — the distant-cluster fixture row builds a translated window as a literal — so the type cannot be sealed without a `pistol-core` change and a call-site sweep, and this line records the gap rather than pretending the narrowing removes it. ONE MEASURED SIDE EFFECT: three "public documentation links to private item" warnings appeared in `state.rs` the moment the modules went private, and they are fixed by demoting three intra-doc links to code spans; `cargo doc -p pistol-solver --no-deps` is warning-free at this revision, which is worth stating because no gate runs it. Flips when a consumer outside this crate needs one of these names — additive, one `pub use` each. WP-1.9's instrument is the nearest candidate and is NOT one, because D-258 requires it to measure the whole shipped structure rather than an isolated table.

D-262: THE TWO CLASS THRESHOLDS THAT MOVE UNDER D-243's FLIP CLAUSE ARE DERIVED FROM THE CONSTANTS THAT CLAUSE NAMES, AND THE ASSERT BESIDE THEM IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE CLASSES RATHER THAN A RESTATED DEFINITION. `ClassSet::of` wrote `own >= 4` and `own == 5` as bare literals while writing `own == WINDOW_LEN` for `Completed` — so of the three numbers in that function, the ONE with a compile-time tie to the rules was the one that does not move, and the two D-243's flip clause (`WIN_LEN` or `TURN_STONES`) actually moves had none. They are now `HOT_MIN = WINDOW_LEN - TURN_STONES` and `WIN_IN_ONE_PLY = WINDOW_LEN - 1`, which is also how D-243 and the design derive them, so the code says what the theorem says instead of agreeing with it by coincidence. THE ASSERT IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT VACUOUS, in `pistol_core::window`'s own idiom (D-253's carried-across `WINDOW_STEPS` assert): both constants are DERIVED, so an assert restating either definition would pin nothing, and this one instead asserts `3 < HOT_MIN && WIN_IN_ONE_PLY == HOT_MIN + 1` — that the greatest live count this module maintains stays BELOW hot, without which `sets.rs`'s own "disjoint from hot" is false and a count-three window sits in two sets that are documented as apart, and that exactly ONE count separates hot from a win in one ply, which is what makes the sets nest as the module's table draws them. VERIFIED IN A SEPARATE WORKTREE rather than asserted: setting `TURN_STONES` to 3 in `pistol-core` fails the build with this assert's own message, at compile time, before a test runs. A THIRD CONJUNCT IS ADDED UNDER A REVIEW-impl FINDING, AND THE FINDING IS THAT THE TWO ABOVE GUARD THE VALUES AND NOT THE DERIVATION — so the assert missed the exact drift it was written for. Re-spell `HOT_MIN` as `WIN_IN_ONE_PLY - 1` and nothing moves at the constants as they stand, because it is still 4, and the whole suite is green; then at `TURN_STONES = 3` the two conjuncts read `3 < 4 && 5 == 5` and PASS while the hot threshold stays at 4 where D-243's counting identity says it must become 3. The flip clause fires silently, which is the one outcome this line claims to prevent. Both legs were reproduced in a worktree before the fix: the re-derivation alone lands green at 25 passed and 7 passed, and the re-derivation with `TURN_STONES = 3` BUILDS. The new conjunct is the counting identity itself, `HOT_MIN + TURN_STONES == WINDOW_LEN` — a turn's stones fill a hot window's slack exactly — and it holds under ANY spelling of `HOT_MIN`, which is the whole of what it adds. IT IS HONESTLY VACUOUS AT THE CONSTANTS AS THEY STAND, restating the definition three lines above it, and this line says so rather than claiming a third non-vacuous class assertion: its content is entirely that it survives a re-derivation and fails when the flip fires. Mutant re-run after the fix: DEAD at compile time with the assert's own message, and the original control — `TURN_STONES = 3` against the shipped derivation — still fails as before. THE COUNT-2 AND COUNT-3 LITERALS STAY, and the reason is worth writing down because it looks like an inconsistency: those two numbers ARE the classes' names — `LiveTwo` and `LiveThree` mean what they say and no rule change moves them — while under `TURN_STONES = 3` hot would reach DOWN to three and collide with `LiveThree`, which is exactly what the assert's first conjunct refuses rather than silently absorbs. NOTHING BEHAVES DIFFERENTLY: every constant evaluates to the number the literal held, and no test changes. Flips with D-243 — `WIN_LEN` or `TURN_STONES` — which is now a compile error here rather than a silent disagreement.

D-263: THE COVER ARITHMETIC IS WP-1.5b's PRE-REGISTERED HOTSPOT, NAMED NOW SO THAT THE FIRST PER-NODE CALLER DOES NOT DISCOVER IT — rule 5 wants the hotspot registered BEFORE the change that touches it, and WP-1.5b is that change: threat-first staged pair generation calls `blocking_covers` and `min_hitting_set_exceeds` PER NODE, and neither was written for that. THE SHAPE IS VERIFIED BY READING THE CODE AND NOT BY A CLOCK, which is why it is the part this line rests on: both are O(|U|² · |H|) with |U| <= 2|H|, hence O(|H|³) in the worst case, because `covers` walks every family for every candidate pair; `empty_families` allocates a fresh `Vec` per hot window on EVERY call, plus the universe's own; and there is no early-out for three PAIRWISE-DISJOINT families, which decides `HitBudget::Two` outright, two cells being unable to meet three disjoint families. THE TIMINGS ARE THE RED-TEAM's AND ARE EXPLICITLY NOT A RULE-5 CLAIM: about 2.5-3.0 µs at 12 hot windows, ~7 µs at 24, ~19-21 µs at 48 and ~133 µs at 144, taken on legal positions at 20 reps, NOT IQR-gated, with ~20 % run-to-run spread, and NOT reproduced by the session that logged them here. They are recorded as an order of magnitude and a growth shape, which is what a forward-looking registration needs; a rule-5 verdict needs a pre-registered hotspot, an expected gain bracket, an abort threshold and one IQR-gated bench reporting nps AND time-to-depth, and NONE of those is in this line. WHAT WP-1.5b OWES: measure these two at the candidate counts its own generator produces rather than at counts chosen to make a curve; and try the cheap remedies in order of directness before the algorithm — the three-disjoint-families early-out, then lifting `empty_families` off the per-call path (the hot set changes only when a stone lands, and the state is the thing that knows when), and only then a different enumeration. AND THE CAVEAT THAT OUTWEIGHS THE NUMBERS: a hot count of 144 is not a position this game reaches at a root — D-255 records own-side hot = 0.0 mean and 0 max over the pinned corpus — so a bench built at 144 measures a tail, and the honest instrument samples the counts the SEARCH produces at depth. Flips when WP-1.5b measures it, which replaces these readings with a rule-5 bench and this registration with a verdict.

D-264: THE ANSWER-INVARIANT PLY EDIT IS CLOSED AS A CLASS, AND THE CLASS IS CLOSED BY ADMISSION REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN BY NAME. D-260 recorded the principle — "the regeneration test does NOT catch (2)", because a `plies` line is an INPUT to the derivation — and then treated ONE fixture, leaving the only other member of the class untreated. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS WORK PACKAGE THAT A CORRECTION CLOSED ONE INSTANCE AND LEFT ITS SIBLINGS: D-244 corrected one stanza and left five, D-250's sweep was written in `tools/`'s vocabulary while the governing literal lived in `configs/`, and D-260 fixed one inert fixture and left its twin. The pattern is recorded here because it is about the process and not about the three artefacts. THE OPERATIONAL PREDICATE IS THE REVIEWER'S AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS MECHANIZABLE, so it is written down rather than paraphrased: the regeneration DOES catch a drifted ply whenever the drift moves any derived answer, since the record re-derives and the line-for-line comparison objects to every answer that changed. The residual hole is EXACTLY answer-invariant drift, and answer-invariance is TOTAL on a record with no positive expectation — every row reads `-`, `nothing` or `none` whatever the position turns out to be. So a record every one of whose rows is negative has NO PROTECTION FROM THE DERIVATION AT ALL, and there are exactly TWO: `single_hot_window_dead_when_opponent_enters` and `win_in_one_ply_dead_when_opponent_enters`. THE FILE'S ARITHMETIC, because it makes the exposure concrete: 416 non-comment non-blank lines over 16 records, of which 32 are the `case` and `plies` echoes parsed back out of the file, 16 are the constant `end`, and 368 are expectations; the derivation reproduces 384 — everything but the echoes — so the QUESTION is hand-maintained in 32 lines while the ANSWERS are machine-derived in 368. On an all-negative record the 22 side rows cannot object to any ply edit, and the state row objects only to an edit that moves turn, phase, stones owed or outcome, which a same-length same-colour substitution does not. WHAT LANDS: the twin gets D-260's precondition treatment inside the row that consumes it — `hot_window_requires_four_and_live` now asserts that `ConstR@0,0` holds FOUR P1 stones, that they are the SAME four the live position's hot window holds, and that it holds the one opponent stone that kills it — and a new row, `a_record_stating_nothing_states_its_own_shape`, closes the class. It is closed by ADMISSION REQUIREMENT and that is the whole design: a record whose every row reads negative must name in the row's own table the window that makes it the right fixture and what that window must hold, and the row asserts that the census of all-negative records equals the table's names EXACTLY. A third such record therefore fails the census until its author writes a shape down, instead of joining the hole silently; a bare list of two names would have failed the same way and taught the author nothing about why. VERIFIED IN A SEPARATE WORKTREE, ON BOTH RECORDS, BEFORE AND AFTER. Before, at `7b9e904`: substituting `-7,0` for `single_hot_window_dead_when_opponent_enters`'s eighth ply — dropping P1 to THREE in the window, so the record is non-hot on COUNT and proves nothing about liveness — and re-pinning `THREAT_V0_SHA256` leaves `cargo test -p pistol-solver --locked` at exit 0, 25 passed and 7 passed; the same substitution for the twin's ninth ply already failed, at D-260's row, which is the asymmetry this line removes. After: each drift kills TWO rows, its own consumer and the class row, and a third all-negative record — a copy of one member under a new name — fails the census by name. TWO IDENTIFIER HYGIENE FINDINGS, both of which cost a round to discover. THE FILE HAS SIXTEEN RECORDS AND NOT FIFTEEN: fifteen is `min_hitting_set_exceeds_is_false_on_an_empty_hot_set`'s empty-hot SIDE-INSTANCE census, 15 `(case, side)` pairs over 12 of the 16 cases, which is a different unit — and the miscount is not harmless, because one of the records it dropped is the one carrying this finding. AND ORDINALS ARE NOT IDENTIFIERS HERE: four records share `4,0` as their ninth ply, so "fixture 12's ninth ply" names no position; a case NAME is the only safe reference and every row above uses one. Flips if the grammar gains a row kind that is positive on every record, which empties the class and makes this row vacuous; or if the derivation gains a way to see an answer-invariant ply edit, at which point the shapes become redundant rather than wrong.

D-265: `grep` IN AN AGENT'S TOOL SHELL IS NOT `grep`, AND THE WRAPPER COMES FROM THE HARNESS RATHER THAN FROM THE USER'S PROFILE — an environment finding, recorded here because it collides with rule 4 and with the workflow rule that a gate claim cites the gate's own log output, and because the draft that raised it attributed it to the wrong place. WHAT IS TRUE, MEASURED: in the shell the Bash tool runs, `type -t grep` reports `function`, and the function's body execs `${CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH:-}` (falling back to `~/.local/bin/claude`) under `exec -a ugrep` with `-G --ignore-files --hidden -I --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.svn --exclude-dir=.hg --exclude-dir=.bzr --exclude-dir=.jj --exclude-dir=.sl` prepended to the caller's arguments. It is multithreaded and its output ORDER is nondeterministic: eight runs of `grep -rn 'WINDOW_LEN' crates/` through the function gave EIGHT distinct sha256 sums, while eight runs of `/usr/bin/grep -rn 'WINDOW_LEN' crates/` gave ONE. WHAT THE DRAFT GOT WRONG, AND WHY THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT: the draft said this was "a shell function wrapping ugrep in a shell initialised from the user's profile". It is not the profile — `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile` and `~/.profile` contain no `grep` alias or function (zero matching lines each), `~/.bash_aliases` does not exist, `ugrep` IS NOT ON `PATH` AT ALL, and a genuine login-interactive shell disagrees with the draft directly: `bash -lic 'type grep'` reports `grep is /usr/bin/grep`. The wrapper is injected by the tool harness into the agent's own shell and by nothing else, which changes the mitigation from "do not use a login shell" — which would have done nothing — to "a transcript an agent captured is not the output of the command a script runs", and that is the sentence a later session needs. A SECOND HAZARD, INDEPENDENT OF ORDER, because the injected flags change WHICH FILES ARE VISITED and not merely their sequence: `grep -rl pistol target` through the function reaches 1474 files where `/usr/bin/grep -rl pistol target` reaches 24455, since `--ignore-files` honours ignore files and `-I` skips binaries — so an agent-shell COUNT and a script's count of the same command are answers to different questions, which is D-221/D-223's class (a count that governed a document and was wrong) arriving by a second route. WHY IT HID FOR THREE REVISIONS OF ONE DOCUMENT: a query with a single hit is stable through both paths — ten runs of the `*Cargo.toml` attestation gave one hash — so the defect is invisible on exactly the small outputs a document is most likely to paste, and appears on the large ones nobody diffs. THE RULE THIS SETS: any command whose OUTPUT or COUNT is recorded, registered, or adjudicated on is written as `/usr/bin/grep` or `git grep`, pinned to a revision where the question is about committed state, and ordered by `LC_ALL=C sort`; a capture taken through an agent shell is evidence of shape and never quoted as "the exact output". Flips if the harness stops injecting the wrapper or ugrep becomes order-stable, at which point the sorting is still cheap and the attribution sentence is what needs amending.

D-266: `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md` IS ADOPTED AS THE CANONICAL THREAT REFERENCE, LANDED VERBATIM, AND ITS COMMUNITY ADOPTIONS STAY GATED — the operator supplied it as the consolidation of a three-phase derivation/literature/audit round, and from this line on tests, ADRs and dispatch prompts CITE ITS STABLE IDs (`LAW-FORCE`, `LAW-OVERLOAD`, `LAW-SUPPORT`, `LAW-HIT`, `LAW-RIPOSTE`, `LAW-LEDGER`, `LAW-DECOMP`, `RULE-EXACT`, `PAT-GAP`, `PROTO-NODE`, `PROTO-PAIR`, `ZONE-R`, `THM-WINDOW`, `E-PHASE`, `DEF-PLAN`, `DEF-T`, `BOUND-CONVERT`, `BOUND-FORK`) instead of restating the theory, which is the same anti-drift reason D-243 gives for writing the hot-window theorem down once. Landed BYTE-FOR-BYTE as supplied, sha256 `97eb3d3a3edec8abd8a26c2de367bc1ace737dad8d59d6a216a4b8dc26ce480f`; the file's own footer governs it — a new law or a status-tag promotion (`CONJ`→`PROVEN`, `OPEN`→settled) is an ADR line, so amendments to it are amendments to this log's subject matter and not to a scratch document. (a) THE CONVERGENCE IS RECORDED AS SOUNDNESS EVIDENCE, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST THING THIS LINE CARRIES: `LAW-FORCE`'s No-Counterattack corollary — "counter-threats never substitute for hitting, except win-now" — IS D-243 consequence (1), "THE ONLY ANSWER TO AN OPPONENT HOT WINDOW OTHER THAN HITTING IT IS WINNING THIS TURN", and the calculus's plan-bearing window (`DEF-PLAN`: an open window with at least four own stones, whose empty set has size at most two) IS D-243's HOT. The two were derived independently and by different arguments — D-243 from a counting identity between a hot window's slack (`WIN_LEN` − 4 = 2) and a turn's budget (`TURN_STONES` = 2) plus a move-order race, the calculus from `LAW-HIT`'s reduction of defence to hitting sets plus the `LAW-LEDGER` tempo accounting — and they land on the same theorem with the same threshold. An independent re-derivation is not a proof, but it removes the failure mode this project actually has, which is a theorem restated in two places and drifting in one; it also means a WP citing either ID cites the same result. `RULE-EXACT` and D-243 consequence (4) converge the same way, from opposite directions: D-243 forbids MINIMUM-cardinality covers in favour of the union over inclusion-minimal covers, and `RULE-EXACT` forbids reading `t` from a pattern table or deriving it by weight algebra — both are the refusal to let an upper bound stand in for the exact quantity. (b) THE COMMUNITY ADOPTIONS ARE LEADS, NOT TRUTHS, UNDER THE SAME LAW AS THE SEALBOT REGISTER (D-206): `ADOPT-FINISH` (the Finisher catalog) stays gated on `V-P3.8`'s per-shape `t`-audit — the calculus states its own falsifier, that any catalog entry with `t < 3` refutes it — `ADOPT-7/36` (anticonnective density) stays gated on `V-P3.7`'s independent tiling verification and LP lower bound, and `ADOPT-BOOK` (the opening corpus) stays gated on the same per-entry discipline before any of it seeds an arena book. Nothing in those three rows may drive a pistol code change, a fixture, or a threshold until its own registered audit is taken, and the audits amend the calculus entry by entry exactly as D-206 amends the register entry by entry. The `[PROVEN]`/`[LIT]` rows are not under this gate; the `[VERIFIED]`, `[CONJ]` and `[OPEN]` tags carry their own standing on the document's face, which is why the status vocabulary is part of what was adopted. (c) LANDING THE FILE CLEARS A CONDITION THAT WAS SILENTLY DISABLING AN INSTRUMENT, and this is the part with an immediate effect on a run about to be taken: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh:417` sets its `TREE` token from a bare `git status --porcelain`, so for as long as this file sat untracked in the worktree every snapshot this project took recorded `timing tree dirty` and `clean` WAS UNREACHABLE — not failing, unreachable, which is worse, because a token that can only take one value looks like a passing check. The WP-1.5a pre-registration had to replace a bare emptiness test with a two-part tolerance for exactly this reason. With the file tracked, `git status --porcelain` is empty and the token is once again a measurement. Flips per row by that row's own audit; the adoption itself flips only if the operator re-rules the document's standing, and a `[REJECT]` row promoted back into use takes its own ADR line naming the evidence that moved it.

D-267: THE SHIPPED `pistol-solver` SURFACE IS MAPPED TO CALCULUS IDs, WITH NO CODE RENAMES — D-266 makes the calculus the citation vocabulary while WP-1.5a's names were chosen from D-243, so without this line every later WP re-derives the correspondence and one of them gets it wrong. NO IDENTIFIER MOVES: the names are load-bearing in eleven public docs, two test suites and a golden fixture, a rename is a diff no reader can review for behaviour, and the calculus itself says algorithms transfer while its vocabulary is a citation scheme — so this is a DICTIONARY and not a refactor. THE MAP, each entry checked against the code rather than the doc comment: `ThreatState::hot_windows(side)` (`Class::Hot`, live and `own >= 4`) IS `DEF-PLAN`'s plan-bearing window set — the classes OVERLAP by construction, a five-stone window being both `Hot` and `WinInOnePly`, which is why `can_win_this_turn` re-filters on `own_count == 4` for its `Pair` arm and why "hot" is never the complement of "win in one ply". `ThreatState::threat_cells(side, out)` IS the deduplicated union of the plans' empty cells, and `DEF-PLAN`'s size bound is the same counting identity D-243 uses: at least four own of six leaves at most two empties, so every plan has size at most two and the hitting-set instance is vertex cover, which is `DEF-T`'s reason for being computable at all. `ThreatState::min_hitting_set_exceeds(HitBudget::Two, windows)` IS the `t >= 3` test, hence `LAW-OVERLOAD`'s criterion, WITH ONE STATED CAVEAT: it also answers `true` when some window in the family has NO empty cell — a `Completed` window, which is unhittable rather than merely three-hard — so the predicate reads "`t` exceeds two OR the family contains a won window", and a caller reaches it only after `PROTO-NODE` step 1 has already disposed of the won case. `ThreatState::unblockable_double_threat(side, budget)` IS that predicate applied to `hot_windows(side)`, and it is `LAW-OVERLOAD` MINUS ITS GUARD: the law's "defender cannot win this turn" clause is D-243 consequence (3) and lives in the CALLER, never in the primitive. `ThreatState::blocking_covers(defender, budget)` IS `LAW-FORCE`'s survival set, delivered as the inclusion-minimal covers rather than as a flat cell union, and its three answers are the law's three cases exactly: `Cover::NothingToBlock` is `t = 0` (an empty plan family, the `PAT-RHOMBUS` and `PAT-O3` case), `Cover::Impossible` is `t > budget`, and `Cover::Minimal` carries the covers whose UNION is the generator's licensed set — flattening it earlier is the failure `Cover::cells` warns about and `LAW-HIT` explains, since hitting is the only defensive mechanism and a cell that hits nothing is not a defence. `ThreatState::can_win_this_turn(side, StonesLeft)` IS win-now, `PROTO-NODE` step 1, and its `StonesLeft` argument IS `E-PHASE`: `StonesLeft::One` admits only `WinWitness::OnePly`, which is `LAW-SUPPORT`'s "at intra-turn phase 2 the win threshold is a plan of size at most one", while `StonesLeft::Two` additionally admits `WinWitness::Pair`, `k = 1`. `ThreatState::win_in_one_ply_windows` / `win_in_one_ply_cells` ARE the size-one plans, which is also where `PAT-GAP`'s Gap Trap lands — `X·XXXX` is a five-stone live window whose single empty is a SINGLETON must-hit, so every minimal cover contains the gap cell and a generator that never asks for the singleton misses the only move. `ThreatState::live_windows_at_count(side, LiveCount::Two | Three)` IS `LAW-SUPPORT`'s `k = 2` qualification — a forced win in two own turns requires an open window already holding at least `6 − 2k = 2` own stones — and it is therefore the COMPLETENESS LICENCE for WP-1.5b's Tier T rather than an ordering heuristic. `ThreatState::cells_raising_to_hot(side, NearHot::Three)` is the one-stone activation set, `BOUND-CONVERT`'s subject and §6's tempo `τ` domain; its type is closed at `Three` because no single cell lifts a count-2 window to hot. The exact branch-and-bound in `crates/pistol-solver/src/cover.rs` IS `RULE-EXACT` — `t` is enumerated, never read from a pattern table and never summed — which is the same refusal D-243 consequence (4) makes from the other side when it forbids minimum-cardinality covers in favour of the union over inclusion-minimal ones. AND THE ABSENCES ARE PART OF THE MAP, because a WP citing an ID that has no implementation must find that out from this line and not from a failing build: `PROTO-PAIR`'s intra-turn phase bit is `pistol-core`'s zobrist and NOT this crate's; `DEF-STAR`, `DEF-TEMPO`/`ADOPT-TEMPO`, `LAW-RIPOSTE`, `LAW-LEDGER`, `LAW-DECOMP`, `ZONE-R`, `THM-WINDOW` and `E-INIT` have NO counterpart anywhere in the shipped surface — `LAW-RIPOSTE` and `LAW-LEDGER` are WP-1.6's, `ZONE-R` and `LAW-DECOMP` are Stage 3's, and `THM-WINDOW`/`E-INIT` are eval's. Flips per entry when the code moves: a new query takes a line here naming its ID, and a calculus status promotion that changes what an ID MEANS re-reads this map, which is the concrete content of D-266's footer clause.

D-268: T1 IS DISPOSITIONED — THE GOVERNING-REVISION RULE ATTACHES TO THE INSTRUMENT AND NOT ONLY TO THE DOCUMENT, and the clause lands in CLAUDE.md in this same commit. D-235 recorded T1 open: "the added dry-run sentence resolves the collision for the PRE-REGISTRATION and not for the HARNESS", with D-220's own bench as the instance — that number was taken on a `tools/bench_delta.sh` revision whose review had FAILED and whose successor was still under review, so the run stood on an ARGUMENT and not on the text. D-242's rule is that the first session actually hitting one of the eight resolves it then, citing the T-number; this is that citation, and WP-1.5a hit T1 a second time in a different costume, which is why the disposition is a rule rather than a note. THE SECOND INSTANCE, and it is the one that shows the scope is wrong rather than merely thin: the WP-1.5a pre-registration's revision 1 declared T1 INAPPLICABLE on the ground that no `tools/` harness is modified — while the harness producing its registered number was a SCRATCHPAD bench, unpinned, reaching a sibling scratchpad directory by relative path, and revision 1's own text had the governed run SUBSTITUTE THE SHIPPED TYPE INTO IT. That is a harness modified, for the run it governs, reviewed by nobody, and it passed the `tools/`-shaped test because it was not in `tools/`. A rule whose trigger is a DIRECTORY is a rule an instrument evades by living somewhere else. THE CLAUSE, in CLAUDE.md's Process section beside the governing-revision paragraph: an artefact that produces a registered number — a `tools/` script, a scratchpad harness, or a command block the document prints — is NAMED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION WITH ITS REVISION, and a change to it reopens the review exactly as an amendment to the document does; `tools/` is where such artefacts usually live and living there is not what makes the rule apply. FORM FOLLOWS D-245's WORKED PRECEDENT and D-228's stated reason: a rule whose limits live only in a decision log is one the next reader applies without them, so the amendment and this line land together rather than the line promising an amendment. THE DEVIATION THE PREVIOUS SESSION NAMED IS CLOSED RATHER THAN INHERITED: that session held T1 for operator confirmation and recorded the hold as a deliberate conservative deviation by a session without commit authority — not as a claim that the ruling was the operator's by right — and a reviewer judged revision 1's situation to fall in D-242's EXCLUDED class, a defect licensing a run that should have been refused, which takes an amendment immediately. This session was dispatched to land it; the delay is what the deviation cost and nothing else. AND IT CLOSES A READING NOBODY HAD YET WRITTEN DOWN: the fresh-context re-derivation of the lost T-bucket items (D-270) independently produced "the literal commands can be identical while the INSTRUMENT they name changes underneath them, with no amendment, no reopened review, and no breach of a single word" — which is this clause's exact subject, arrived at from the paragraph text alone by a reader who had not seen T1. A rule proposed for one reason and re-derived blind for another is a rule with two independent grounds. Flips if a session is found pinning an instrument revision and still taking a run on a different one, at which point the clause needs a mechanized check rather than sharper words; and D-242's other trigger stands — if the bucket GROWS rather than closes, the paragraphs need rewriting rather than annotating.

D-269: T2 IS DISPOSITIONED — RECORDING IS NOT CHECKING, AND A REGISTERED CRITERION NAMES THE DEFECT CLASS IT EXCLUDES AND MUST BE FALSIFIABLE BY IT; clause in CLAUDE.md in this same commit. D-235's T2 has two halves: "the same sort of artefact, differing only in identity" constrains KIND and not REPRESENTATIVENESS, and "records the dry-run input and its output" requires RECORDING and not CHECKING — so D-221's `grep -c 'btree.*search'` defect would pass a compliant dry run on any real profile whose symbol table lacks the confusable substring. THE INSTANCE IS DR-6 AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE HYPOTHETICAL, because it happened: DR-6 used a REAL instance of the kind — the actual pinned corpus — recorded its input and its output, PASSED, and certified a whole-state instrument that coloured plies `i % 2` instead of rule 3's turn structure, mis-colouring 7 of 15 stones on corpus position 0 and agreeing with the true board on ZERO of 24 positions. DR-6 could not have caught it, because its registered check was that all three backends agree on a checksum and ALL THREE SHARED THE SAME WRONG BOARD. Internal agreement is invariant under a defect in a shared input. THE CLAUSE, sharpened past the three craft defects an earlier drafting had: it does NOT say falsifiability MEANS an externally derived referent (externality is a sufficient operationalisation, not a necessary one); it DOES require the pre-registration to name the defect class, without which "a property the defect class preserves" is uncheckable; and it is NOT scoped to dry runs. Registered criteria that pass vacuously are enumerated so a reviewer can recognise them: internal agreement between components sharing an input, output shape, plausible magnitude, and exit status. AND THE SCOPE IS THE POINT, established by this document's own GOVERNED criterion failing the same test: revision 4 of the WP-1.5a pre-registration registered four revision assertions as its SHOW-criterion, and a reviewer ran the composed block at HEAD with every guard passing — candidate `72316a7`, baseline `050961d`, eight commits apart, diff EMPTY, CONFIRMED — ON A REVISION CONTAINING NO WP-1.5a CODE AT ALL, because with `p = 0` the work package's binary is identical to its predecessor's BY CONSTRUCTION and that is the same observable as the work package never having landed. A rule that would not have caught that is not the rule this finding supports. THIS PARTIALLY REBUTS D-245's OWN REASONING and the rebuttal is recorded rather than smoothed: D-245 held T2 "OVER-satisfied" because stating in advance what a dry run must SHOW is stricter than the statute. DR-6 DID register what it must show and it bought nothing, because the criterion was one the defect preserved. Registering a SHOW-criterion is stronger than recording only when the criterion is externally derived or otherwise falsifiable by the named defect; that is a limit on D-245's reasoning and D-245's disposition of T5 is untouched by it. A THIRD INSTANCE, from the fix round, in the same class rather than a new one: the golden threat fixture is DERIVED — regenerated from the from-scratch reference, with a test asserting the committed bytes match — and that test cannot catch a drifted ply list, because the ply list is an INPUT to the derivation and a wrong position yields a self-consistent fixture that regenerates identically. A derived artifact protects its ANSWERS while its QUESTION stays hand-maintained, and the defect class the criterion must name is "the question drifted". The operationalisation follows without a new clause: the external referent for a fixture's question is its PURPOSE — the named mutant it must kill — since a drifted ply list stops killing that mutant and the mutation run is independent of the fixture file entirely. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, which is why this lands as law rather than as a note: the fresh-context re-derivation (D-270), reading only the two paragraphs and knowing nothing of T2, produced this reading almost word for word — "there is no verb of comparison anywhere in the paragraph, no registered expected value, and no state in which a dry run FAILS" — and graded it EXCLUDED-CLASS, exploitable against result integrity and not deferrable. Two readers, no shared context, one reading. Flips if a registered criterion is ever found that names its defect class, is falsifiable by it, and still passes on a defective instrument, at which point the clause needs a stronger operationalisation than externality; the enumeration of vacuous criteria is open and grows by amendment.

D-270: T6, T7 AND T8 ARE RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN RECOVERED, THEIR TEXT IS ON DISK, AND D-247's GAP CLOSES AS SUPERSEDED — the operator ruled archaeology exhausted (repository and session scratchpads both searched, nothing recoverable) and ordered a re-derivation, which D-247 anticipated when it wrote that "RECORDING A GAP IS NOT INVENTING ITS CONTENTS" and left the flip to the operator supplying the three sentences. THE METHOD, because the method is what makes the output admissible: one fresh-context subagent was given, verbatim and as its ONLY material, CLAUDE.md's governing-revision, dry-run and proportionality paragraphs plus the committed text of D-227 and D-228, and was instructed to read NO repository file — in particular not this log, which carries T1-T5, and not any pre-registration. It ran no tool. Its independence note is part of the record INCLUDING THE DISCLOSURE IT VOLUNTEERED, that the harness had injected a copy of CLAUDE.md and a memory index into its context before it saw the task, and that it confined the derivation to the quoted blocks and named three places it was tempted to look further and did not. That disclosure is what makes the corroboration mean anything: a reader who had seen the CONCLUSIONS could not corroborate them. THE VALIDATION, and it is the load-bearing result rather than the three new readings: the re-derivation reproduced FOUR OF THE FIVE KNOWN READINGS BLIND — T2's first half and T3 together as one item (KIND is not REPRESENTATIVENESS, with the one-instance case arrived at independently as its third bite), T2's second half almost word for word (RECORDING is not CHECKING), T4 (the self-judging cheapness trigger) and T5 (no consequence for disagreement, already resolved by D-245). A method that re-derives four known readings from the same text is a method whose novel readings are worth taking seriously. THE THREE THAT TAKE THE VACANT SLOTS, stated in full in `docs/process_readings.md` and compressed here: T6 — the rule calls the commands "literal" but never fixes WHICH ARTEFACT the command is, so a named script or an externally executed block can change underneath byte-identical literal commands with no amendment, no reopened review and no breach of a single word; T7 — the dry run must precede the review and must be RECORDED INTO the document, recording is an amendment, and an amendment reopens the review "however small the diff", so the text has no terminating condition and the sentence D-227 added to defuse this seam closes only its other half; T8 — the second-instrument clause imposes NO INDEPENDENCE CONDITION (two instruments sharing the suspect stage agree and are wrong together, satisfying every word), never ranks replication against the second instrument (replication answers noise and a second instrument answers bias, and a session with a decision in hand will cite the one that agrees with it), and sets no FLOOR on the registered consequence, so "disagreement is noted and the verdict stands" satisfies D-245's own amendment. THEY ARE NOT THE ORIGINALS AND NOTHING HERE CLAIMS THEY ARE: D-247 forbids reconstruction because "a plausible invention in [an append-only law log] is worse than an absent line", and the honest description is SUPERSESSION — the lost three are gone, these three are readings of the same two paragraphs produced by the same procedure, and D-242's count of eight is whole in NUMBER while three of the eight are not the ones it counted. T6 IS CLOSED BY D-268 IN THIS SAME ROUND, which is worth saying rather than tidying away: the reading was produced blind and the clause that answers it was proposed for a different reason, so the clause has two independent grounds and the reading is on disk anyway, because a reading disposed of in the round that found it is the one a later reader is most likely to re-derive and think new. T7 AND T8 ARE OPEN, and T7 is a live cost right now — the WP-1.5a pre-registration stands at revision 9 and every revision since 3 has re-run its own blocks. TWO ITEMS WERE GRADED EXCLUDED-CLASS BY THE RE-DERIVATION AND ARE THEREFORE NOT BUCKET ITEMS: T2's second half, which D-269 lands as law in this same round on exactly this corroboration; and T4 SHARPENED — cheapness is decided by a cost statement the same session writes BEFORE the run, nothing validates or reconciles it afterwards, and the EXPENSIVE branch is left wholly unlegislated, so an honest but wrong forecast of expense discharges the replication and second-instrument duty and re-licenses the single-sample-plus-derived-margin instrument D-228 exists to forbid. THE T4 SHARPENING IS RECORDED OPEN AND OWED A RULING RATHER THAN AMENDED HERE, and the reason is stated rather than assumed: this session was dispatched to land T1 and T2 and this is neither, it arrived from a re-derivation the same session commissioned, and a session promoting its own subagent's grading straight into CLAUDE.md is the shape D-242's bite-time rule exists to slow down. THE EXPOSURE WAS CHECKED AND IS PROSPECTIVE, NOT LIVE: the two documents it would govern already do what it asks — the WP-1.5a pre-registration's §6 states MEASURED costs and corrects two rows that were labelled measured and did not reproduce, and D-236 states its cost before the run (7-9 minutes, no operator attention) and confirms it after (433.3 s and 433.9 s) — so no standing verdict in this project rests on a forecast that was never reconciled. The proposed clause, for the operator to rule on: the cost statement is RECONCILED, the report states observed cost beside forecast cost, and a run that proves cheap owes the cheap-branch duties before its verdict counts. Flips for T7 and T8 when a session hits one and disposes of it under D-242, for the T4 sharpening on the operator's ruling, and for this line as a whole if the lost three are ever recovered — in which case they are recorded BESIDE these rather than replacing them, and the divergence between what was lost and what was re-derived is itself the finding.

D-271: MAJOR-1 STAYS A RECORDED GAP AND IS CLOSED WITHOUT RECONSTRUCTION — the last unrecovered item of the same archaeology D-247 and D-270 cover, and the operator's ruling is that no reconstruction is offered because its OPERATIVE CONTENT IS ALREADY LAW: rule 5's requirement that a perf-sensitive change ship with a pre-registered hotspot and an expected-gain BRACKET, together with the D-227/D-228 mapping of the dry-run and proportionality rules onto the artefacts that produce registered numbers. A finding whose remedy is already in force needs its remedy, not its text. WHAT IS ACTUALLY ON THE RECORD, checked rather than assumed: `MAJOR-1` appears in NO file of this repository and in NO surviving session scratchpad — the same search that returned nothing for T6-T8 returns nothing for it — so this line, like D-247's, records a MISSING THING and not a recovered one. WHY THAT IS TOLERABLE HERE ON A GROUND D-247 DOES NOT HAVE: D-247's three were AMBIGUITIES in law whose loss cost a session the ability to RECOGNISE it had hit one, and recognition is exactly what a bucket buys; MAJOR-1's content is a finding against a document, and the rules it argued for are in force whether or not anyone can read the argument. Nothing about a future run changes on either reading of it. THE COST IS THE SAME COST D-247 NAMES and it is named again rather than inherited silently: what is lost is provenance — a later reader who finds rule 5's bracket discipline or D-227's mapping unconvincing cannot read the finding that motivated them, and must re-derive the motivation or take it on this line's word. Flips if the operator supplies the finding, at which point it lands as its own line and this one says so; and if a THIRD such gap appears the pattern stops being archaeology and becomes an argument that review findings must land on disk in the round that produces them, which is the rule these three gaps are collectively evidence for.

D-272: H1's INSTRUMENT LEAVES THE PRE-REGISTRATION AND BECOMES TWO TESTED SCRIPTS, BECAUSE FOUR ROUNDS OF IN-PLACE REPAIR EACH INTRODUCED A NEW BLOCKING DEFECT AND NOTHING BUT A REVIEWER COULD RUN IT. THE PATTERN, which is the finding rather than any one defect: revision 7 fixed a dry run that cited a guard the block did not contain; revision 8 fixed a `git grep` under `pipefail` that adjudicated the strongest evidence for `p = 0` as its opposite, and introduced a `rustc -vV | head -1` SIGPIPE in the same commit; revision 9 fixed that and shipped an EXIT trap that returned 1 for a requested 0, 1 AND 2 — collapsing a three-way verdict by housekeeping; revision 10 fixed that and shipped an adjudicator that read a `[dev-dependencies]` entry as a refutation of `p = 0` and a probe scoped to one package of a workspace whose claim is workspace-wide, reaching a FALSE CONFIRMED on an edge the instrument it replaced would have refused. EVERY ONE WAS FOUND BY AN AGENT RUNNING THE DOCUMENT BY HAND, because a command block printed inside a pre-registration is a thing only a reader can execute. That is `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` item 10's diagnosis verbatim — "a number nothing tests is a number nothing defends" — and D-231's precedent exactly, where `tools/bench_delta.sh` produced this project's official perf verdict with zero tests until two rounds of defects forced some.
