WHAT LANDED: `tools/solver_edge_check.sh`, the `p = 0` adjudicator, taking a WORKSPACE ROOT and a CRATE NAME as arguments precisely so a test can drive it against workspaces it constructs rather than only against the one repository whose answer is already believed; and `tools/wp15a_h1.sh`, the H1 instrument, taking every binding from the environment with no defaults, so the pre-registration supplies the registered values and the script supplies none. Twenty-four tests in `crates/pistol-cli/tests/`, which `cargo test --workspace --locked` already runs as CI gate 3, in scratch git repositories and scratch cargo workspaces, WITH A CONTROL — `a_clean_workspace_reaches_confirmed` and `a_workspace_with_no_edge_at_all_is_accepted` — because item 10's named failure mode is a suite every assertion of which is satisfied by a gate that refuses everything. THE MUTATION EVIDENCE, taken in a separate worktree because a deliberate break in the tree being edited is indistinguishable from a regression: re-adjudicating on `cargo tree -i`'s EXIT STATUS, which is revision 10's defect verbatim, turns FOUR tests red including the dev-dependency case and the standing `p = 0` invariant; narrowing the probe from `--workspace` to one member, which is revision 10's other defect, turns THREE red. Four review rounds were needed to find those two; the suite finds them in 0.3 s. AND THE SUITE EARNED ITS PLACE ON ITS FIRST EXECUTION: `the_abort_path_is_replication_stable` failed, because `cargo tree` prints ABSOLUTE PATHS and the adjudicator was printing the `mktemp` clone's name into stdout — the same defect class as a `diff -u` header leaking its temporary paths, which two reviewers had independently graded BLOCKING one revision earlier, reintroduced through the new instrument and this time on the CONFIRMED path, where it would have voided every replicated run rather than only a failing one. It was found by a test before it was found by a reviewer, which is the whole of what this change buys. THREE DESIGN CHOICES, each closing a finding rather than a preference: (1) `p = 0` IS ADJUDICATED ON THE STDOUT OF A WORKSPACE-WIDE INVERTED TREE AND NEVER ON AN EXIT STATUS, because status conflates a real normal edge with a dev edge, a build edge and an off-target edge — all three exit 0 while `--edges normal` leaves the tree empty — and conflates "no such package", "ambiguous specification" and any other cargo failure at 101; the reading is that more than one line means a normal reverse-dependency, and the lines past the first NAME the dependents, which also makes the gate cite its own output rather than a wrapper's status. (2) THE SNAPSHOT RUNS INSIDE THE PRISTINE CLONE, which closes three findings with one change: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` roots itself at `dirname($0)/..`, so handing it the working tree's copy made its SCRIPT and its DATA INPUTS — config, corpus, openings — worktree files that `git update-index --assume-unchanged` hides from `git status`, from the `LANDING..HEAD` diff and from a blob pin alike, and a tampered config then reached H1-b as a VERDICT attributed to a defect class it does not belong to. Inside the clone every input is committed content at `LANDING` by construction, the record's `timing tree` token becomes a measurement instead of a constant, and the blob pin is not needed at all. (3) `tools` LEAVES THE BUILD-REACHING DRIFT PATHSPEC and the instruments are named with their revisions instead (D-268), because a drift assertion cannot both forbid new instruments and permit the one the current revision adds — this very change adds two. Flips if a defect is ever found in these scripts that the suite does not catch, at which point the finding names the missing test and the test lands with the fix; and the promotion itself flips only if the operator retires H1, which D-273's record of revision 10's verdict leaves open.

D-273: REVISION 10 OF THE WP-1.5a PRE-REGISTRATION FAILED ITS GOVERNING-REVISION REVIEW AND THE GOVERNED RUN WAS NOT TAKEN — recorded here because a verdict that is not written down is a verdict a later session re-derives, and because two of the findings are about H1 itself rather than about its instrument. TWO FRESH CONTEXTS, DISPATCHED IN PARALLEL AGAINST `2673da6` (revision 9) AND `7decc35` (revision 10), NEITHER SEEING THE OTHER. At revision 9 they INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME BLOCKING DEFECT — `diff -u` writing its `mktemp` paths and mtimes to stdout, so three replications of a genuine ABORT produced three distinct stdouts while the document voids a run whose replications disagree, converting an ABORT into a voided run by a temporary directory name — which is the strongest evidence this work package has produced about anything, since agreement between blind readers is the one thing a shared defect cannot manufacture. The review added a second BLOCKING at revision 9: the registered second-instrument agreement criterion was VIOLATED at the registered bindings, TRUE ⇔ FALSE, because `tools/bench_delta.sh` refuses only when two digests are EQUAL and they differ — and its registered consequence then forbade taking any verdict. AT REVISION 10 THE REPAIRS FAILED IN TURN, three BLOCKING between them: `cargo tree -i`'s exit status is not normal-edge membership, so a `[dev-dependencies]` entry — which this document elsewhere names as legitimate and relies on — produced `p = 0 REFUTED` on a bit-identical binary, with the error message naming a diagnostic command that prints `warning: nothing to print`; the probe was scoped to one package while §2's claim is that NO BINARY IN THIS WORKSPACE links the solver, so a normal edge into `pistol-arena` — which ships two binaries — reached exit 0 CONFIRMED with the offending manifest line printed two lines above the verdict, an edge the substring count revision 10 had just demoted WOULD HAVE REFUSED; and the instrument's data inputs carried the same worktree gap its script had just had closed, where `assume-unchanged` on `configs/instrument_v0.toml` left `git status`, the `LANDING..HEAD` diff and the blob pin all seeing nothing while a tampered config reached H1-b as a VERDICT attributed to a defect class it does not belong to. TWO FINDINGS ARE ABOUT H1 AND NOT ITS PLUMBING, and they are the ones a successor must answer: (a) H1-b IS A CRITERION H1's TARGET DEFECT PRESERVES — a crate linked but never called moves `binary_sha256`, which H1-b excludes, and moves none of the 54 lines that remain — so under D-269, the clause this document's own §7.1 produced, anchoring the second-instrument agreement duty to H1-b anchored it to the one criterion in the document that cannot falsify what it watches; and (b) THE AGREEMENT CRITERION WAS UNEVALUABLE IN THE BRANCH WHERE INSTRUMENT 2 DECIDES ALONE, because the edge check aborts before H1-a builds, so two of the biconditional's four corners have no producer and the registered consequence of disagreement cannot fire in the case where the two instruments actually disagree. WHAT SURVIVED, recorded because it is the larger half and because a document that only records its defects overstates them: no reviewer found an input producing a false CONFIRMED at revision 9; the red-team's sharpest attack at revision 9 — a real dependency edge hidden behind a `r` TOML escape, invisible to the substring count — was caught by H1-a at exit 1; the EXIT-trap repair held across twelve probes in four modes; `is_hex`, the kind-token check, the line-injection guards and the `SNAP_BLOB_PIN` check against clean filters all held; and the B-1 repair, once made, survived every attack both reviewers made on it. THE DISPOSITION, on the operator's ruling: the instrument is promoted and tested (D-272) rather than amended a fifth time in place, and the pre-registration is rewritten around it. H1 ITSELF IS NOT RE-RATIFIED BY THAT PROMOTION — findings (a) and (b) stand open against the hypothesis's structure, and §9's own admission that H1's answer is largely known now sits beside a demonstration that the one failure §9 keeps H1 for, an accidental edge, is the failure the instrument missed. Flips when a revision passes its governing-revision review, at which point the governed run may be taken; and separately if the operator answers (a) and (b) by retiring H1-b or the second-instrument clause, which would make this line the record of why.

D-274: THE CONTAINMENT-GUARD RULE IS `SHELL_CHECKLIST` ITEM 11, AND THE SWEEP THAT FOUND ITS SIBLING IS THE EVIDENCE — the operator's ruling on the `SUBJECT_PATH` near-miss, whose class matters more than its instance. THE INSTANCE: `tools/wp15a_h1.sh` guarded `SNAPSHOT_REL` against `/*` and `*..*` and left `SUBJECT_PATH` — THE ONE BINDING IT `rm -rf`s — unguarded, so an absolute value lying inside the real repository passed every check above the deletion and REMOVED THE OPERATOR'S WORKING TREE; at the registered bindings that is `crates/pistol-solver`, the work package under test. A `cd` is not a guard: `( cd "$ROOT" && rm -rf -- "$P" )` constrains relative paths and nothing else. Worse, the guard that DID exist covered the case git already refused (`..` fails as a pathspec) and missed the one nothing covered. THIS IS THE PATTERN THIS LOG HAS NAMED BEFORE — D-248's "an instance-scoped correction that leaves the class alive, which is silent drift wearing the costume of a correction" — recurring in the direction with the largest blast radius. THE SWEEP, MECHANICAL AND RECORDED RATHER THAN REMEMBERED, over every destructive site in `tools/` with each target traced to its ORIGIN: `wp15a_h1.sh`'s `SUBJECT_PATH` (caller-supplied, DELETE — guarded at `715be80`); `baseline_snapshot.sh`'s `OUT` (caller-supplied via `--out`, OVERWRITE — see below); and `WORK`/`PRISTINE`/`SEED`/`SCRIPT`/`BOUND`/`out` in `wp15a_h1.sh`, `bench_delta.sh`, `arena_smoke.sh`, `determinism.sh`, `ci.sh`, `file_justification_check.sh` and `baseline_snapshot.sh`, every one of them derived from `mktemp -d` or from `$WORK/…` and therefore script-created. TWO caller-supplied targets in the whole of `tools/`, and both were defective. THE SIBLING, SAME MECHANISM AND QUIETER BLAST RADIUS: `baseline_snapshot.sh` `cd`s to `$ROOT` before it does anything and then writes `--out`, so a RELATIVE `--out` resolved against the repository root rather than the caller's directory. MEASURED: `--out relative_probe.txt` issued from `/tmp` wrote its record INTO THE REPOSITORY ROOT — a file the caller never asked for, in a tree whose cleanliness `wp15a_h1.sh`'s own step 5 then voids a run over. Fixed by capturing `$PWD` before the `cd` and resolving a relative `--out` against it; every existing caller passes an absolute path, so nothing changed for them. A test drives the shipped script from a scratch directory and asserts the record lands in the caller's cwd and NOT in the repository root, removing the stray before asserting so a regression fails loudly without dirtying the tree for every later gate. THE RULE, as item 11: any binding consumed by `rm`, `mv` or a write is guarded so its resolved path is provably under the root the script means, and ABSOLUTE-VALUE ESCAPE IS THE ATTACK. It is item ELEVEN and not item ten: items 1-10 are cited BY NUMBER in this log, in `docs/experiments/` and in several scripts' own comments — 55 such citations — so renumbering to seat it beside its siblings would have silently retargeted every one, and the coverage rule stays 10 and stays the capstone. Flips if a destructive site is ever found whose target is neither script-created nor guarded, at which point the sweep is re-run and this line names what it missed; the rule itself flips only if a containment guard is shown to refuse a legitimate input, which is why the guard refuses shapes (`/*`, `*..*`) and not values.

D-275: THE INSTRUMENT PINS ARE CHECKED BY A TEST INSTEAD OF BY MEMORY, AFTER THE PRE-REGISTRATION REGISTERED THE WRONG REVISION OF ITS OWN INSTRUMENT — and the answer to "did anything run against it" is NO, which is what decides which law applies. THE FINDING, stated whole because half of it is not adjudicable: the document is `docs/experiments/wp15a_prereg.md` at revision 11; it registered `tools/wp15a_h1.sh` at blob `e20c8eb8…` in §0's instrument table AND again in §3.1's prose; `e20c8eb8…` is the blob at `301add3`, the PARENT commit, whose verdict ordering exits on a `p = 0` refutation BEFORE H1-a builds — which is precisely the ordering defect revision 11's own §6 was written to replace. So the document registered an instrument whose behaviour contradicts the document's own adjudication table. The shipped blob at the reviewed revision `ab5f43a` was `6cbb35d6…`, and it has since moved again to `42a05ab9…` with D-274's containment guard. WHETHER ANY RUN INHERITS IT: NO. No WP-1.5a results document exists (`docs/experiments/` holds wp13's results and no other); no ADR in this log records an H1 verdict; D-273 records `GOVERNED RUN WAS NOT TAKEN` twice. The correction is therefore a one-line fix plus a reopened review under the governing-revision rule, and NOT a verdict that inherits a mispinned instrument — had a run been taken, that run's verdict would have been void and this line would be recording a retraction instead. WHY A ONE-LINE FIX IS NOT THE FIX: the pin was wrong at two consecutive commits and would be wrong at every future one, because a hand-copied hex in prose is stale the moment the file changes — which is every time one of these defects is repaired. That is the same shape as D-274's own finding one directory away: A PIN MAINTAINED BY MEMORY DRIFTS EXACTLY LIKE A GUARD APPLIED BY MEMORY. So: the hexes are removed from §2.2 and §3.1, §0's table is the single source of truth, and `the_instrument_pins_in_this_document_match_the_shipped_scripts` compares that table against `git hash-object` on the WORKING TREE — not `HEAD:path`, so a script edited without its pin fails at the test rather than at the next commit. MUTATION EVIDENCE, in a separate worktree: pinning the stale `e20c8eb8…` — revision 11's actual defect — turns it RED with the file, the pin and the true hash all named; appending a comment to the script without touching the pin turns it RED too. Both in 0.00 s, against two fresh-context reviewers who each found the original by reading. Flips if the instrument table is ever the wrong place for the pin — a second document pinning the same script would need the check generalised rather than duplicated.

D-276: H1 IS RETIRED AND ITS CLAIM BECOMES TWO STANDING CI GATES — settled by an OPTION MATRIX attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM before selection, as the Process section requires, and the surviving option is one the matrix did not contain. THE MATRIX offered four: (A) repair the instrument a sixth time; (B) drop H1-b and keep H1-a; (C) retire H1 entirely and let the resolved-graph CI invariant be the whole claim; (D) turn H1-a into a standing CI test that builds the shipped binary with and without the crate and asserts bit-identity. It recommended D. THE DECISION-RED-TEAM KILLED THE RECOMMENDATION AND SUPPLIED (E), WHICH IS ADOPTED: assert from rustc's own dep-info that no source under `crates/pistol-solver` is an INPUT to any binary this workspace ships. WHY THE OTHERS FELL, each measured rather than argued: A fell on a NEW defect class, the sixth found by the sixth fresh context and the worst grade yet — H1-a HAS A FALSE CONFIRMED INSIDE ITS OWN REGISTERED DEFECT CLASS. §3 named build scripts in that class; a build script that reads the subject without declaring `rerun-if-changed`, with both builds sharing one target directory WHICH IS HOW `tools/wp15a_h1.sh` RAN THEM, leaves a stale `OUT_DIR` artefact so the second build compiles nothing and two identical digests are reported for a binary whose behaviour moved (22 → 77, digest unchanged; a fresh target directory catches it). Not RUN VOID, not ABORT — exit 0, CONFIRMED, with the edge check simultaneously reporting no edge so the registered agreement criterion was SATISFIED WHILE BOTH INSTRUMENTS WERE WRONG TOGETHER. C fell because `p = 0` on the resolved graph does NOT imply the crate cannot reach codegen: an `include_str!` across crate directories with zero manifest edges leaves the graph check answering exit 0 while mutating the crate moves the binary `6381813a…` → `b87fea44…`. C mistakes the graph claim for the codegen claim, and leaves uncovered precisely the accidental route §9 kept H1 for. B fell with A, because B keeps H1-a exactly as the build-script finding breaks it. D survived but only amended — two INDEPENDENT target directories and all five binaries — and E dominates it: no second build at all (0.6 s against two cold builds), five binaries where H1-a compared one of five, a refusal that NAMES THE OFFENDING FILE rather than printing two hexes (CLAUDE.md's own rule that a gate claim cites its log output), and no `BASE_REV`, so it survives the reuse limit §3.1a records — a future work package that CREATES a crate breaks H1-a outright and leaves E indifferent. THE STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK ON E, recorded verbatim as the Process section requires: "E trusts the toolchain's own bookkeeping to be complete, and it is measurably not: a build script that reads the subject without declaring `rerun-if-changed` puts the subject into the binary and leaves no trace in that binary's dep-info — measured, `app.d` naming only `build.rs` and `out/gen.rs` while the binary's answer moved 22 → 77. E is sound only while the companion invariant 'no crate in this workspace has a build script' holds, and that invariant is a fact about today's tree, not a property of the check." THE ANSWER TO IT IS IN THE GATE ITSELF AND IS THE REASON IT EXITS 2 RATHER THAN 0: `tools/solver_link_check.sh` enumerates `build.rs` across the workspace and REFUSES TO ANSWER when it finds one, so the blind spot is declared rather than hidden and a future crate that breaks the premise turns the gate red instead of silently narrowing it. Zero build scripts today, checked not assumed. TWO DEFECTS WERE DESIGNED OUT BECAUSE THE RED-TEAM FOUND THEM BY BUILDING E FIRST: rustc records dep-info paths AS WRITTEN, so a source reached from `src/bin/` appears as `…/src/bin/../../../pistol-solver/src/lib.rs` and a plain substring match returns ZERO hits on the file it exists to catch — EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER, `SHELL_CHECKLIST` class — closed by canonicalising every entry before matching; and an unscoped `target/*.d` glob picks up `libpistol_solver.d`, the subject's own library, reporting hits on a clean tree — closed by taking the binary set from cargo's own JSON. MEASURED, live workspace: 5 shipped binaries, 415 source inputs, 0.6 s, exit 0. SENSITIVITY, against the graph gate on the same inputs: a normal edge → both refuse; `include_str!` with no manifest edge → LINK 1 naming the file, GRAPH 0; a dev-dependency → both 0; a `build.rs` present → LINK 2, GRAPH 0. MUTATION EVIDENCE, in a worktree, REPORTED WHOLE INCLUDING THE SURVIVOR because overstating a suite's strength is the defect the previous round shipped: dropping canonicalisation turns 2 red, dropping the build-script premise 7, inverting the hit match 3, dropping the crate-path guard 2 — and DROPPING THE PER-BINARY INPUT FLOOR TURNS 0 RED, a defensive assertion with no reachable producer in the suite, recorded as such rather than counted as coverage. Flips if a defect is found in these gates that the suite does not catch, at which point the finding names the missing test and the test lands with the fix; and the retirement itself flips only if the operator reinstates a governed run, which would need an instrument that answers 0.1's build-script case.

D-277: T8 LEAVES THE BUCKET AND BECOMES LAW — a second instrument must not share the stage under doubt, and the pre-registration names that stage; clause in CLAUDE.md in this same commit. T8 was recorded OPEN in `docs/process_readings.md` as one of the three re-derived readings (D-270): the proportionality paragraph names replication and a second instrument, imposes NO INDEPENDENCE CONDITION on the second, and its bite is "two instruments sharing the suspect stage agree exactly and are wrong together". D-242's boundary excludes from the bucket anything "exploitable against RESULT INTEGRITY, where following the text as written produces a wrong number or licenses a run that should have been refused", and takes it as an immediate amendment rather than a deferral. **T8 IS NOW A CONSTRUCTED INSTANCE AND NOT A READING**: on the build-script route (D-276's 0.1) the resolved-graph instrument reports NO EDGE, the two-build instrument reports BIT-IDENTICAL, the registered agreement criterion is SATISFIED, and the run exits 0 CONFIRMED on a tree where the subject reached the binary. Both instruments were wrong in the same direction because both were blind to the same stage — what a build script read — and the criterion could not see it because agreement is invariant under a defect in a shared blind spot, which is §7.1's own sentence about internal agreement one level up. THE CLAUSE: a pre-registration naming a second instrument NAMES THE STAGE UNDER DOUBT and states how the second instrument does not share it; two instruments blind to the same stage are one instrument reported twice. WHAT THIS COSTS A DOCUMENT: one sentence, and the discipline of saying what the doubt is ABOUT before naming a comparand — which is the same demand D-269 makes of a SHOW-criterion and is answered the same way, by naming the defect class first. Note what it does NOT settle: T8's other two halves — that replication and a second instrument are unranked, and that a REGISTERED consequence can still be no consequence — stay open in `docs/process_readings.md`, because neither has produced a constructed instance and D-242's bite-time rule governs them. Flips if a pre-registration is found naming a stage and a genuinely independent second instrument and still agreeing wrongly, at which point independence is not the property the clause should have demanded.

D-278: THREE CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROUND'S OWN RECORD, appended rather than edited in. (1) D-272's THIRD DESIGN CHOICE OVERSTATED ITS GROUND. It says running the snapshot inside the pristine clone makes "every input committed content at LANDING by construction" and that "the record's `timing tree` token becomes a measurement instead of a constant". A reviewer reproduced that the clone is NOT at `LANDING` when the snapshot runs: `git checkout BASE_REV -- <path>` writes the INDEX, and the later bare `git checkout -- <path>` restores FROM that index, leaving the subject path modified and the clone's own status dirty. The token therefore reads `dirty`, not `clean`. WHAT SURVIVES: the `assume-unchanged` tampering gap IS genuinely closed and has a test, because `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` emits `timing tree` AFTER the `# timing` marker and `inv()` truncates there, so the token never reached a comparison and could not move a verdict. The design choice stands; its stated reason was wrong. (2) D-272's BASE-RATE CITATION points at the wrong lines: it says revisions 7-11 are "documented in D-272 and D-273", but D-272 covers 7-10, D-273 covers 9-10, and revision 11's defects are in D-275 and in reviews that reached the record only through D-276. The fact survives; the citation did not. (3) THE OPTION MATRIX THAT PRODUCED D-276 RECOMMENDED AN OPTION WHOSE FEASIBILITY IT LABELLED "needs measuring" AND WHOSE COST IT ESTIMATED WITHOUT MEASURING — "~30-60 s" against a measured 5.2-6.3 s, wrong by an order of magnitude IN THE RECOMMENDER'S OWN FAVOUR — in a decision whose entire argument is that unmeasured claims are this work package's failure mode. The decision red-team named it and it is recorded here rather than left in a scratchpad, because it is the same pattern the last five rounds were about, appearing one level up in the document that diagnoses it. Both measurements were available in eleven seconds.

D-279: D-276 AND D-277 WERE EACH APPENDED TWICE IN ONE COMMIT, AND THIS LINE SUPERSEDES THE FIRST COPY OF EACH — a defect in this log's own integrity, found by a fresh-context review, and repaired the way this log repairs things rather than by deletion. WHAT HAPPENED, mechanically: the commit that landed the retirement ran an append of D-276/D-277 and a CLAUDE.md edit in one step; the CLAUDE.md edit failed on a text mismatch, the step was re-run, and the append ran a second time. Nothing detected it because nothing checks this file for repeated keys. THE FILE'S OWN HEADER SAYS "Lines are never edited or deleted. A decision that changes is superseded by a new line that says which one it replaces", so both copies stay and this line does the saying: **THE SECOND COPY OF EACH IS OPERATIVE.** For D-276 the second is a strict superset — it adds the parallel measurement agent's finding that option D's two removal mechanisms have disjoint defects of their own (deleting the crate FALSE-FIRES on a legitimate `[dev-dependencies]` edge; stubbing it MISSES an unused normal dependency edge), the transitive dep-info counts `29/15/6/15/10/0`, and the sentence "BOTH GATES ARE KEPT because their blind spots are disjoint". For D-277 the two copies differ only in wording and the second is the one to read. WHY THIS IS MORE THAN TIDINESS: `D-276` denoting two different texts breaks the one property this log is cited for. `SHELL_CHECKLIST` item 11 exists because 55 citations point at numbered items; the same argument applies here with more force, since every ADR reference in the repository is by number. Flips if a mechanized check for repeated keys lands — `grep -oE '^D-[0-9]+' docs/decisions.md | sort | uniq -d` must be empty, which is one line and is the obvious next gate; it is NOT added here because a gate added in the same commit as the defect it would have caught is a gate whose own first run is its author's word, and this one belongs with the next `tools/` change that can carry a test.

D-280: THREE WRONG ANSWERS IN THE LINK GATE, FIXED AND TESTED; AND FOUR CLAIMS IN D-276 CORRECTED, INCLUDING ITS MUTATION COUNTS — a fresh-context REVIEW-impl + RED-TEAM against `407d662` found all of it, and the corrections matter more than the fixes because three of them are claims this log made about its own evidence. THE THREE WRONG ANSWERS, each reproduced by the reviewer and each now carrying a test. (1) `build = "custom_build.rs"` WALKED PAST THE PREMISE CHECK: `find . -name build.rs` does not see a build script named by the manifest's `build` key, so a script that read the subject and baked its length into the binary reached **EXIT 0** through the guard D-276 records as the answer to its own strongest surviving attack. Fixed by enumerating `custom-build` targets from `cargo metadata`, which reports both spellings; test `a_build_script_named_by_the_manifest_key_is_refused_like_any_other`. (2) A SYMLINKED SOURCE WAS RESOLVED OUT OF ITS OWN CRATE: `realpath -m` follows links, so `crates/subject/src/lib.rs` pointing at `crates/shared/real.rs` was recorded by dep-info under the crate and canonicalised away, **EXIT 0** on a tree whose binary observed the subject. Fixed with `realpath -ms`, which normalises `..` lexically — the reason canonicalisation was added — without following links; test `a_symlinked_source_under_the_crate_still_counts_as_the_crate`. **Note the shape: the fix for the `..` case created the symlink case.** (3) THE BREADTH CLAIM WAS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE CHECK: `cargo build --workspace --bins` silently skips bin targets with unmet `required-features` and packages under `[workspace] exclude`, so the gate printed a narrower count and answered 0 with no hint it had narrowed. Fixed by comparing cargo's DECLARED bin-target count against the number actually built and refusing on a mismatch; test `a_binary_behind_an_unmet_feature_is_refused_rather_than_silently_skipped`. FOUR CORRECTIONS TO D-276. (a) ITS MUTATION COUNTS DO NOT REPRODUCE. It claims "dropping canonicalisation turns 2 red, dropping the build-script premise 7, inverting the hit match 3, dropping the crate-path guard 2". The reviewer's measurements over clean, `bash -n`-valid spellings: canonicalisation **1**, build-script premise **1** by every behavioural spelling tried, hit match **2** narrowed or **5** truly inverted, crate-path guard **1**. The 7 is reachable only by deleting one line and leaving the next dangling — a SYNTAX BREAK, not a behaviour change — and with only 8 tests in the suite, 7 was never achievable behaviourally. **A count that appears only when the script stops parsing is not evidence of coverage**, and D-278(3) had already self-corrected exactly this pattern one level up in the same commit. (b) "4 OF 5 MUTATIONS KILLED" IS THE WRONG DENOMINATOR: over 26 clean mutants the reviewer measured **11 killed and 15 survived**. The survivor D-276 discloses is verified real — and is 1 of 15, not 1 of 5. The material survivors are the ones the ADR quotes as evidence: the five-binary breadth (fixed by (3) above), the reported counts `5 shipped binaries, 415 source inputs`, `--locked`, `--workspace`, and a dep-list parse that can be gutted to one entry per binary with all tests green. (c) "ZERO BUILD SCRIPTS TODAY, CHECKED NOT ASSUMED" IS TRUE ONLY OF WORKSPACE MEMBERS: four registry dependencies — `proc-macro2`, `quote`, `serde`, `serde_core` — declare and run build scripts in every build of this workspace, and dep-info records nothing about what any of them read either. The gate's scope is now stated in the script rather than implied: `--no-deps` means members, which is the only half a workspace author controls. (d) D-278(2) CORRECTS A CITATION THAT DOES NOT EXIST: it says D-272 claims revisions "7-11" are "documented in D-272 and D-273", and no such sentence is anywhere in the repository — `git log --all -S` finds it only in D-278 itself. The corrections D-278(2) makes are individually accurate; the document it attributes them to is not the one that said it, and the likeliest true target is an off-repository option-matrix scratchpad. WHAT THE REVIEW CONFIRMED RATHER THAN BROKE, recorded because it is the larger half: the sensitivity table, the transitive dep-info counts `29/15/6/15/10/0`, the `5 binaries / 415 inputs` reading, §0a's controlled repetition rebuilt from scratch in two pristine clones with `Compiling pistol-solver` = 0 in each, §0a's diffstats, the baseline provenance and its digests, and that the retained revision-11 body is BYTE-IDENTICAL to its parent. Flips per finding when a test covers what it names; the surviving-mutant list is the standing work item and is recorded here rather than in a scratchpad so the next session inherits the list rather than the count.

D-281: THE SURVIVING-MUTANT LIST IS RECORDED IN FULL, D-280's CLAIM TO HAVE RECORDED IT IS CORRECTED, AND THE METHODOLOGY ERROR THAT ALMOST PUT WRONG NUMBERS BESIDE IT IS RECORDED TOO. D-280 says "the surviving-mutant list is the standing work item and is recorded here rather than in a scratchpad so the next session inherits the list rather than the count", and then records FIVE of the fifteen. That is the same defect it was written to correct, one paragraph later, and it is corrected here by listing them. RE-MEASURED AT HEAD, against a baseline verified green (11 passed, 0 failed) and with every mutation checked to have APPLIED before its result was read: **S1 — the binary set truncated to the first executable — is now KILLED** by the declared-versus-built breadth check D-280 added, which is the one place the fix reached. TEN STILL SURVIVE, each a real behaviour change no test in `solver_link_check_tests.rs` distinguishes: A5 the per-binary input floor; **S2 dropping `--workspace` from the build** — which an earlier draft of this correction claimed was killed and is not, because every fixture is a single package and cannot tell the two invocations apart; S4 dropping `--locked`; S5 the missing-dep-info refusal; S8 the `BIN_COUNT >= 1` refusal; S9 the `sort -u` dedupe, so duplicate inputs are recounted; S10 the hit match losing its trailing slash, so a sibling `crates/pistol-solver-x` would count as the solver; S11 the root-`Cargo.toml` refusal; S13 the `realpath`-on-PATH refusal; and S29 `${line#*: }` → `${line##*: }`, which keeps only the LAST dependency per binary and leaves all eleven tests green. THE PATTERN ACROSS THEM, which is what a successor should act on rather than the list: every survivor is a guard whose violation the FIXTURES CANNOT PRODUCE — a single-package workspace cannot exhibit `--workspace` narrowing, a fixture that always has dep-info cannot exhibit its absence, a fixture with one crate cannot exhibit a sibling-prefix collision. The suite tests the gate's ANSWERS and not its ENUMERATION, and closing that needs fixtures with a second package, a sibling crate sharing a name prefix, and a corrupted dep-info file. AND THE METHODOLOGY ERROR, recorded because it nearly became the record: the first re-measurement of this list was taken against a baseline that was RED for a reason unrelated to any mutation — `/tmp` is RAM-backed on this machine and this session had filled it, so `cargo` failed with `Disk quota exceeded (os error 122)` and every "mutation" appeared to kill seven to twelve tests. The numbers were nonsense and were caught only because twelve failures out of eleven tests is arithmetically impossible. A mutation run whose baseline is not shown green is not a measurement, and the harness now prints the baseline first. THE OPERATIONAL HAZARD IS REAL AND IS NOT ONLY A MEASUREMENT PROBLEM: the suite's fixtures live under `/tmp/pistol-testscratch-`, so a full `/tmp` turns the standing gate red through a legitimate RUN VOID — `cannot build the workspace's binaries` — which is the correct direction (it refuses rather than passing) but will read to a future session as a solver-link regression. Flips when the enumeration fixtures land, at which point this line names which survivors they killed.

D-282: FINISH-B IS RATIFIED CLOSED BY THE OPERATOR, AND THE STANDING GATES ARE RECORDED AS HAVING A KNOWN EXPIRY. THE RATIFICATION: FINISH-B's DONE condition read "WP-1.5a governed run taken and recorded", and no governed run was taken. The operator rules that D-276's retirement plus the two standing gates SATISFY THE INTENT of that condition — the claim H1 would have measured once is now checked on every commit by `tools/solver_edge_check.sh` and `tools/solver_link_check.sh` — and closes the work package on that basis. Recorded here rather than assumed, because a DONE condition that was not met and is nonetheless closed is exactly the kind of thing a later reader reconstructs wrongly: the run was not taken, it was not deferred, and it will not be taken; the hypothesis it belonged to no longer exists. AND THE GATES HAVE A KNOWN EXPIRY DATE, MEASURED NOW SO THAT NOBODY DISCOVERS IT MID-IMPLEMENTATION: WP-1.5b's first structural act is `pistol-search` taking a dependency on `pistol-solver` — that is what staged threat-first generation IS — and the instant that edge is declared BOTH GATES GO RED. Measured in a clone at this revision by adding exactly that edge: `solver_edge_check` exit 1, `solver_link_check` exit 1, and CI gate 3 with them. THIS IS NOT A DEFECT IN THE GATES; it is their registered property expiring on schedule, and the only failure available here is meeting it by surprise. So WP-1.5b's DESIGN must decide, BEFORE implementation and as a named design decision with its own DECISION-RED-TEAM, which of two things happens at the linking commit: the gates RETIRE with the linkage, their property having expired; or they INVERT to "the solver is linked exactly where declared" — `pistol-search` yes, `pistol-cli`/`pistol-engine` as the design states, nothing else — which keeps a live guard against the accidental edge in a world where a deliberate one exists. The second is not obviously right: an inverted gate must be told what "as declared" means and becomes a list maintained by memory, which is D-275's own lesson. Flips when that decision lands, at which point its ADR line supersedes this paragraph's framing of the choice; and the ratification itself flips only if the operator reinstates a governed run for H1, which would need an instrument answering the build-script case D-276 records.

D-283: EVERY ARENA ENGINE SEAT IS BOUND TO A BINARY BY CONTENT, AND A FILE THAT IS NOT THAT BINARY VOIDS THE RUN BEFORE A GAME IS PLAYED — closing the residual D-252 registered with the stake named, on the four OPERATOR-RUN SPRT documents CLAUDE.md rule 6 makes the judge of every search and eval change. THE MECHANISM: `[engine_a]`/`[engine_b]` gain a REQUIRED `binary_sha256`; `ArenaConfig::validate` checks its SPELLING only — 64 lowercase hex, so an uppercase transcription, a truncated paste and a `0x` prefix are each refused at their own key rather than surviving to a comparison that would report them as a stale binary and send the operator to look at the wrong end of it; and `identity::capture` digests the file at `binary` and refuses `EngineBinaryDigestMismatch` BEFORE `Channel::start`, so a mismatched build never becomes a process, never plays a game and never writes a report. WHY THE DOCUMENT IS THE SEAM, checked and not assumed, as D-252 checked it: the arena has no `--binary` flag — `crates/pistol-arena/src/bin/arena.rs` matches only `["--config", c, "--out", o]` in either order plus `--help` — so the only binding available is the one the arena reads paths out of, which is the config. D-252's option (a), an override flag, is not adopted and is not needed: a required document key cannot be forgotten the way a flag can, which was that option's own recorded defect. WHY REQUIRED AND NOT OPTIONAL. An optional binding is a binding nobody has, and the documents that would have gone without it are exactly the four this line exists for; CLAUDE.md rule 1 also forbids a code-side default for a tunable, and "absent means unchecked" is that default wearing a different word. WHY AT RUN START AND NOT AT VALIDATION: D-21 keeps `validate` pure and offline, so `tools/config_check.sh` still passes on a fresh clone where nothing has been built — the shape is a document property and the content is a machine property, and they are checked in the two different places those live. THE SMOKE GATE IS A DIFFERENT CASE AND IS TREATED AS ONE: `tools/arena_smoke.sh` BUILDS its engine, so it rewrites `binary_sha256` beside `binary` from cargo's own artifact stream, counts BOTH rewrites against the document's own stanza counts, and refuses a document that binds one seat and not the other — `crates/pistol-cli/tests/arena_smoke_gate_tests.rs::arena_smoke_refuses_a_config_that_does_not_bind_every_seat_by_content`, whose control asserts that the digest the gate PRINTS is the digest of the binary it BUILT and not the one committed. The stub arena in that suite now carries the declared digest into its report line, so the report attests a seat that a process really occupied rather than a string the gate wrote. THE COMMITTED VALUES ARE REAL AND WILL GO STALE, WHICH IS THE POINT: `a7f519fade1124780463293b86e27cbdd0732540a84aa75acaed4de4689f03ce` is `sha256sum target/release/pistol` after `cargo build --release --locked --bin pistol` at `d6f6cbb` with rustc 1.97.1 on the development machine, recorded in all five documents with that provenance in a comment beside it. THE PROVENANCE WAS CHECKED AND NOT ASSERTED, because the binary was built in a tree that already carried this round's `pistol-arena` changes: a PRISTINE `git worktree` at `d6f6cbb`, in a different directory, rebuilt `--bin pistol` and produced `a7f519fade…` byte-for-byte — which confirms both that `pistol-cli` takes no dependency on `pistol-arena` (it does not; `crates/pistol-cli/Cargo.toml` names core, engine and three serde crates) and that this build is path-independent. A rebuild makes it wrong; a wrong digest is a loud refusal; and an operator who re-records it has named the build their SPRT is about. THE SWEEP IS IN THE CLASS'S OWN WORDS (D-251's ruling): `every_committed_arena_config_binds_every_seat_by_content` enumerates `configs/arena_*.toml` — the SAME predicate `tools/config_check.sh` uses to decide what an arena document is — and asserts two `binary` lines, two `binary_sha256` lines and well-formed hex in every one, so a sixth document cannot land unbound, and `sprt_config_missing_digest_is_named_error` strips the key from each committed document IN TURN and requires the named `Config` refusal. Both drive the committed files rather than a synthetic one, because the question was never whether the code can refuse — it is whether the binding reached the documents. RESIDUALS, NAMED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. (i) D-199's window is unchanged: the binary is still not re-digested per spawn, so a swap landing after run-start verification is invisible to this. (ii) The digest attests the FILE, not what the process read at runtime — the eval weights are covered by D-198's engine-side attestation and nothing here extends to any other input. (iii) A document whose digest is stale refuses the whole run, including a run the operator wanted; that is the intended direction and it is stated because it is the cost. THE OPTION MATRIX AND ITS STATUS. The choice between (a) an arena flag, (b) an existence-and-executability check, and (c) a document key was written in D-252 and the operator's amendment sheet SELECTED (c); the sub-choices settled here — required rather than optional, run-start rather than validation-time, and a gate that rewrites rather than a document that is exempt — are recorded above with their reasons and HAVE NOT BEEN ATTACKED BY A FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAM, because this session was directed not to dispatch subagents. That review is outstanding against the revision this lands at and this line is what it reads. Flips if the arena ever gains an explicit engine binding of its own, at which point the document key becomes the fallback rather than the seam; and the required-versus-optional choice flips if a legitimate arena document is ever found that cannot know its binary in advance — none exists today, and the smoke gate, which comes closest, answers it by rewriting.

D-284: THE DUPLICATE-KEY GATE FOR THIS LOG LANDS AS CI GATE 14, AND THE COMMAND D-279 REGISTERED FOR IT CONTRADICTS D-279's OWN REPAIR — the second half is the larger finding and is why the gate is not spelled the way it was ordered. WHAT D-279 SAID: «a mechanized check for repeated keys — `grep -oE '^D-[0-9]+' docs/decisions.md | sort | uniq -d` must be empty — is one line and is the obvious next gate; it is NOT added here because a gate added in the same commit as the defect it would have caught is a gate whose own first run is its author's word». That deferral was right and is honoured: the gate lands in a different commit from the defect, with `crates/pistol-cli/tests/decision_key_check_tests.rs` driving the SHIPPED script over a scratch git repository, a control, and a SEEDED VIOLATION so a pass cannot come from a gate that never fires. WHAT D-279 ALSO SAID, in the same line: that both copies of D-276 and D-277 STAY, on this file's own «lines are never edited or deleted» rule, with the ambiguity resolved by a RULING that the second copy of each is operative. THOSE TWO SENTENCES CANNOT BOTH HOLD, and the first run of the gate is the measurement that shows it: spelled exactly as registered, the pipeline prints `D-276` and `D-277` and the gate is RED ON ARRIVAL — it always would have been, against the very file the line that registered it was appending to. The registered command was never executed against its own subject. That is D-278(3)'s pattern again and one level up from where anyone was looking: a line diagnosing an unrun check, prescribing a check, and not running it. SO THE RULE THE GATE ENFORCES IS THE ONE THAT IS TRUE: no key repeats EXCEPT the two D-279 dispositioned by name. THE EXEMPTION IS CLOSED AND CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — a repeat outside it is a refusal, and a key IN it that is no longer repeated is also a refusal, so the list cannot outlive its subject and cannot quietly become the place repeats go — and it is PRINTED on every run rather than sitting unread in the source. That is D-275's lesson about lists maintained by memory, applied to a list this line is knowingly creating and says so. THE OTHER REFUSALS, each with a test: the gate reads the TRACKED BLOB via `git ls-files -s -z` + `git cat-file blob` and not the worktree path, because staging a repeat and overwriting the worktree copy is the exit-0-wrong-answer the sibling gate had (SHELL_CHECKLIST item 5, D-233), and `the_key_gate_reads_the_index_and_not_the_working_tree` reproduces exactly that; an extraction that finds NO key at all is refused as a broken extraction rather than passed as a clean file; a `D-<n>` cited MID-LINE is prose and not an appearance, which is what the `^` anchor is for and what `a_key_mentioned_mid_line_is_prose_and_not_a_second_appearance` pins; and ARGUMENTS ARE REFUSED rather than ignored, which is D-251's MINOR-3 class deliberately not joined. ITEM 3, ANSWERED PRECISELY BECAUSE THE PASSING CASE IS `grep` FINDING NOTHING: the extraction carries `|| true` and its empty result is then refused by name, while `sort` and `uniq -d` carry nothing, because both exit 0 on empty input — naming which of the three needs it and why the other two do not is the item, not a blanket `|| true` down the pipeline. COST: the gate reads one blob and runs three commands; it is last in `tools/ci.sh` beside the other tracked-bytes gate, and the gate count in that script moves from 13 to 14 with every existing gate keeping its ordinal, because two test files cite `gate 12 of 13` and `gate 8 of 13` by number and renumbering would silently retarget them (SHELL_CHECKLIST item 11's reasoning); both citations are updated to `of 14` in this same commit. Flips if the operator ever rules that the two grandfathered copies may be deleted after all, at which point the exemption goes and the gate becomes the one-liner D-279 wrote; and the stale-exemption refusal is what will make that removal impossible to do halfway.

D-285: SCRATCH SPACE IS PREFLIGHTED AND A SHORTAGE IS A NAMED RUN VOID, NOT A RED GATE — `tools/scratch_preflight.sh`, `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` ITEM 12, and the exit-code distinction carried across the seam into the tests. THE MEASURED GROUND, which is not hypothetical and not old: `/tmp` on this machine is RAM-backed at 24 GiB (`df -Pk /tmp` reports a 24622376-block tmpfs); a session filled it; `cargo` answered `Disk quota exceeded (os error 122)`; `tools/solver_link_check.sh` did exactly the right thing and exited 2 with `cannot build the workspace's binaries` — and what reached the log, and what the standing test asserting `exit 0` reported, was a RED SOLVER-LINK GATE, indistinguishable from the solver having been linked into a shipped binary (D-281's own disclosure of the hazard). The gate was honest; the vocabulary was cargo's, and cargo's vocabulary describes cargo. THREE OBLIGATIONS, WHICH IS WHAT ITEM 12 SAYS. (1) A CODE PER KIND — 0 the answer is yes, 1 the answer is no, 2 no answer was taken — and a gate with no void class says so in its usage block rather than leaving a reader to infer it. (2) PREFLIGHT WHAT THE RUN NEEDS AND VOID EARLY: `tools/scratch_preflight.sh <directory>` reads `df -Pk` and refuses as a void naming the filesystem, the mount, what is available and what was wanted. It is called by `tools/solver_link_check.sh` before its build and by `tools/ci.sh` before gate 2, which unpacks the whole tracked file set into `$TMPDIR` and builds it. (3) THE DISTINCTION SURVIVES THE SEAM: `solver_link_check_tests.rs` gains `assert_code`, whose failure message says what EACH of 0, 1 and 2 would have meant, and the standing invariant test now goes through it — a bare `assert_eq!(code, Some(0))` is a test that reports a void as a regression, which is precisely the reading above. THE FLOOR IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, which is this round's own clause (D-291) applied to itself: the largest scratch consumer in `tools/` is ci.sh gate 2, and `du -sk` on its temporary clone after `cargo build --workspace --locked` reports **340552 KiB** at `d6f6cbb` — about 333 MiB, the checkout and its whole debug target tree. The floor is 1048576 KiB, three times the measurement, which leaves room for the stub workspaces the test suites build under the same `$TMPDIR` and is still under 5% of this machine's `/tmp`. THE FLOOR CAN BE RAISED AND NOT LOWERED. `PISTOL_MIN_SCRATCH_KIB` exists because item 10 wants a test driving the SHIPPED script and nothing else can make a 24 GiB tmpfs look full; it is combined with the constant by MAXIMUM, so the binding can only ever tighten the check, and `a_floor_below_the_constant_does_not_lower_it` asserts that rather than describing it. `tools/ci.sh` GAINS AN EXIT CODE and its usage block says so: 2 is now RUN VOID, no gate adjudicated. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT, ENUMERATED BY THE CLASS'S OWN PREDICATE (`grep -ln mktemp tools/*.sh`) RATHER THAN BY MEMORY, because a list this line writes from memory is the defect D-251's ruling (5) is about: eight scripts take a `mktemp -d` — `ci.sh`, `arena_smoke.sh`, `baseline_snapshot.sh`, `bench_delta.sh`, `decision_key_check.sh`, `determinism.sh`, `file_justification_check.sh` and `solver_edge_check.sh` — and only `ci.sh` preflights. The other SEVEN do not. Under CI they are covered, because ci.sh preflights once before any of them runs; standalone they are not. That is the residual, it belongs to WP-1.10 with the rest of the `tools/` sweep (D-289), and it is written here rather than left for a fourth round to rediscover — a sweep scoped to the two scripts where the accident actually happened is a list wearing a class's clothes, and this line says which it is. Flips when the sweep lands, and the floor flips whenever gate 2's footprint is re-measured — the number above is a measurement with a revision on it, not a constant with a story.

D-286: SEVEN OF D-281's TEN NAMED MUTANTS ARE CLOSED, THREE SURVIVE AND ARE LISTED BY NAME WITH A DIAGNOSIS EACH, AND ONE OF THE THREE IS AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT RATHER THAN A COVERAGE GAP — which corrects D-281's own characterisation of it. THE PATTERN D-281 DIAGNOSED WAS RIGHT and is what the fixtures were built from: every survivor was a guard whose violation THE FIXTURES COULD NOT PRODUCE, because the suite tested the gate's ANSWERS and not its ENUMERATION. THREE FIXTURE CLASSES, EACH NAMING WHAT IT KILLS. (a) A SECOND PACKAGE OUTSIDE `default-members`, whose binary reads the subject — `a_binary_in_a_non_default_workspace_member_is_still_examined`. Every earlier fixture was a workspace whose default members ARE all its members, so `cargo build --bins` and `cargo build --workspace --bins` did the same thing and nothing could tell the two invocations apart. KILLS **S2**. (b) A SIBLING CRATE SHARING A NAME PREFIX, `crates/subject-x`, which the binary reads while the subject itself is untouched — `a_sibling_crate_sharing_a_name_prefix_is_not_the_subject`. The test asserts BOTH directions, that the subject answers 0 and that the sibling itself answers 1, so the exit 0 is a discrimination and not a tree where nothing reaches anything. KILLS **S10**. (c) A CORRUPTED DEP-INFO FILE, in three spellings: empty (KILLS **S5**), a first line with a well-formed separator and no inputs after it (KILLS **A5**), and a first line carrying a SECOND `": "` (KILLS **S29**). MEASURED, AND IT CHANGED THE FIXTURE'S SHAPE: cargo REWRITES `target/debug/app.d` on every build, including one that recompiles nothing — checked directly, by writing `CORRUPT` into it, rebuilding and reading the honest first line back — so a corruption written before the gate runs is gone by the time the gate looks. The corruption is therefore applied by a `cargo` shim that forwards every invocation to the real cargo and overwrites the dep-info after a `build` returns, which is exactly the moment a real corruption would arrive. AND S29 NEEDED A GUARD, NOT ONLY A FIXTURE. `${line#*: }` and `${line##*: }` agree on EVERY well-formed dep-info line, because rustc writes exactly one `": "` per first line — a path containing a space is escaped as `\ `, so `": "` cannot occur inside one — which is why eleven tests left it alive and why D-281's description of it as «keeps only the LAST dependency per binary» is true only of a malformed file. The gate now requires every dep-info entry to NAME A FILE THAT EXISTS: a mis-split yields an entry ending in `:` that names nothing, and refusing it by name is the difference between a wrong parse and an answer about a file set nobody built. THE GUARD WAS MUTATED TOO, as **N1**, and dies. TWO MORE CLOSED BEYOND THE THREE PRESCRIBED CLASSES, because their fixtures were cheap and their absence was the same shape: **S4** (dropping `--locked`) by a workspace that gains a member with no `generate-lockfile` after it, where `--locked` voids and its absence silently relocks and answers about a graph nobody committed — `cargo metadata --no-deps` was checked not to touch the lockfile first; and **S11** (the root-`Cargo.toml` refusal) by a directory that is not a workspace, where removing the guard does not change the exit code but moves the DIAGNOSIS from the caller's path to cargo's expense, which is what SHELL_CHECKLIST item 8 is a claim about. THE RUN: in a separate `git worktree` at the WIP revision, never the live tree, with a harness that PRINTS THE BASELINE FIRST and refuses to read any mutation result unless it is green — `test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed` before the batch and the same after every mutation was restored — and that checks each mutation APPLIED, is present in the file, and leaves `bash -n` clean, because a count that appears only when the script stops parsing is not evidence of coverage (D-280(a)). KILLED: S1, A5, S2, S4, S5, S10, S11, S29, N1. **SURVIVED: S8, S9, S13**, and each is diagnosed rather than counted. **S8** — the `BIN_COUNT >= 1` refusal — is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT and not a gap, and D-281's «each a real behaviour change no test distinguishes» is wrong about this one: `[ -n "$EXECUTABLES" ]` refuses first, a non-empty `EXECUTABLES` holds at least one non-empty line, and the loop counts exactly those, so `BIN_COUNT` cannot be zero where the mutant differs. That is a proof by reading and is labelled as one; the honest disposition is to delete the guard or to keep it as documentation, and neither is done here without a reviewer. **S9** — the executable `sort -u` — is reachable only if cargo emits one executable path twice in a single build stream, which no fixture can force; if it ever fired, the declared-versus-built breadth comparison would refuse the run rather than miscount it, so the dedupe is defence in depth behind a check that already exists. **S13** — the `command -v realpath` refusal — is a diagnosis-only guard like S11: without it the first `realpath -ms` fails and the gate still voids, with a message pointing at canonicalisation rather than at a missing tool. It is killable, by a fixture that runs the gate with a minimal `PATH` holding symlinks to `cargo`, `jq`, `sed`, `dirname`, `df` and `awk` and NOT `realpath`; that recipe is recorded here rather than built, because a fixture that reconstructs a PATH is the most environment-fragile thing in this suite and the guard it defends is a message. THE MUTATION SPELLINGS ARE RECORDED HERE AND NOT LEFT IN A SCRATCHPAD, which is D-281's own lesson about inheriting the list rather than the count, applied to the instrument as well as to the result — each is an exact single-occurrence replacement in `tools/solver_link_check.sh`: **S1** append `| head -1` to the `EXECUTABLES` pipeline; **A5** `[ "$this_bin" -ge 1 ]` → `-ge 0`; **S2** `cargo build --locked --workspace --bins` → `cargo build --locked --bins`; **S4** the same line → `cargo build --workspace --bins`; **S5** `[ -s "$dep" ]` → `[ -e "$dep" ]`; **S8** `[ "$BIN_COUNT" -ge 1 ]` → `-ge 0`; **S9** `LC_ALL=C sort -u)` → `LC_ALL=C sort)`; **S10** `"$CRATE_ABS"/*) HITS=` → `"$CRATE_ABS"*) HITS=`; **S11** delete the `[ -f "$ROOT/Cargo.toml" ]` refusal; **S13** delete the `command -v realpath` refusal; **S29** `deps="${line#*: }"` → `deps="${line##*: }"`; **N1** neutralise the `[ -e "$abs" ]` dep-info entry check. Flips per survivor when a fixture covers it, and S8 flips when a reviewer rules on whether an unreachable guard should be deleted or documented.

D-287: THE CALCULUS'S §5 PATTERN TABLE IS A SHA-PINNED FIXTURE PACK WITH EXACT `t` PER PATTERN, THE TWO WEIGHT-ADDITION COUNTEREXAMPLES ARE CI REGRESSIONS, AND THE GAP TRAP IS MUTATION-GATED — V-P3.2 and V-P3.5 of `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md` §11, landed. WHAT IS PINNED: `crates/pistol-solver/tests/fixtures/pattern_v0.txt`, eleven records — PAT-O5 (t=2, both end singletons are plans), PAT-O4 (t=2, three plans), PAT-GAP (t=2, the singleton must-hit at the gap), PAT-C4 (t=1, one plan), PAT-4IFF in BOTH branches (two-deep on both sides t=2, one-deep on one side t=1, which is the `else t <= 1` the document states as an inequality and the test asserts as one), PAT-RHOMBUS (t=0, empty plan family), PAT-O3 (t=0), and four ALG- records for the counterexamples. THREE READINGS AGREE ON EVERY RECORD, and the third exists because of a CEILING: `common::reference` (R1) answers the shipped query surface, whose `HitBudget` is closed at two, so R1's own minimum-hitting-set carries `CEILING = 2` and cannot say `t = 3` — which is the entire content of the counterexamples. So `common::plans` (R3) computes `t` EXACTLY and unbounded, by trying hitting-set sizes smallest first, and enumerates windows BY POSITION the way the region scan does, so the pack does not inherit R1's central assumption either. Every record is checked against R3's exact value, against R1 through the budget ladder, and against the SHIPPED `ThreatState` through the same ladder, with the ladder's MONOTONICITY asserted rather than assumed. THE FILE IS DERIVED AND THE NUMBERS IT IS FOR ARE NOT. `pattern_v0_is_what_the_definitions_print` re-renders every `expect` row from R3 and compares it with the bytes, so an edited expectation is a red test rather than a re-hash (D-259's discipline); and `SECTION_FIVE` in the test file is the document's table TYPED OUT BY HAND and compared against the pack, because a derived fixture checked only against its own generator agrees with a broken generator. THE ALL-NEGATIVE CLASS IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY A CENSUS: every record carries a `support` row — DEF-SUPPORT, the largest own count over that side's open windows — so PAT-RHOMBUS (support 2) and PAT-O3 (support 3), whose every other answer is negative, are separated by a POSITIVE claim that an answer-invariant edit cannot leave true (D-260, D-264). THE GAP TRAP'S MUTATION GATE, WITH THE MUTATIONS RECORDED. `gap_trap_singleton_plan_detected` asserts three things about `X.XXXX` open right: that the plan family CONTAINS the singleton `{1,0}`, that the SHIPPED state's hot set contains the five-window that carries it, and that a plan survives the forced block at the gap — which is why t is 2 and not the 1 a named-shape taxonomy reads. Both mutations were made in a separate worktree against a baseline shown green first: **GT-1**, `sets.rs` `own >= HOT_MIN` narrowed to `own == HOT_MIN`, which drops five-windows out of the hot set; and **GT-2**, R3's plan enumeration `own >= 4` narrowed to `own == 4`. Each turns this test RED. THE FIRST DRAFT DID NOT CATCH GT-1 and that is the part worth recording: `win_in_one_ply` and `hot` are two sets, the first was untouched by the narrowing, and t is 2 either way on this shape — the singleton is contained in two other plans — so a test watching only the NUMBER would not have moved. The hot-set assertion is what closes it. A third mutation, **GT-3** (the hitting-set predicate's `all` weakened to `any`), turns `threat_number_is_never_additive` red, so the counterexample rows are not inert either. V-P3.5, STATED AS THE PARTS AND THE WHOLE. Crossing fours: an open four on ConstR and one on ConstQ meeting at an EMPTY cell that lies in a plan of each; the two parts are taken from ONE position by axis, so no second position has to be trusted to be the same fours, each part is t=2, and the exact answer is 3 — weight algebra reads 4. Same-line double: two open fours sharing the single gap between them; the parts are two records at t=2 each, the whole is t=3, and the mechanism is that four windows now hold FIVE stones with the same forced singleton. Both are `assert_ne!` against the sum, which is RULE-EXACT as a regression rather than as a sentence. V-P3.0's DISPOSITION, decided here: the enumeration lives in the TEST TREE and does not move to `tools/`. It VERIFIES and produces no recorded number — nothing outside the test binary reads it — and `tools/` membership is what pulls in SHELL_CHECKLIST's coverage rule and the pre-registration instrument rules. Promotion is a FUTURE ADR, owed the day anything records a number from it. Flips if a §5 row is ever re-derived to a different `t`, which changes the hand-written table and the pack together; and the pack grows when V-P3.8's Finisher-catalog audit lands, which is the next thing that will want this shape.

D-288: D-252's OPTION (c) IS RELABELLED — IT WAS A DEFERRAL AND IT SAID "ADOPTED", AND THE LABEL HAD TEETH. The line reads «(c) ADOPTED: leave the literal, register the exposure, and schedule the binding», and what (c) actually did was decline to bind the four operator-run SPRT documents and record the exposure. That is a DEFERRAL. THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT VOCABULARY: an option recorded as ADOPTED in an option matrix is one that has been SELECTED, and CLAUDE.md settles a named design decision with more than one viable option by a matrix attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM BEFORE selection — so a successor picking up WP-1.10 and reading (c) as adopted would have found the decision already taken, the matrix already spent, and no red-team owed, on a choice that had never been attacked. D-252 says as much about option (a) in its own next breath — that adopting it without a red-team «would be the breach that rule names» — and then labels (c) adopted in the same sentence-group. The correct labels: (a) RECOMMENDED, NOT ADOPTED, as written; (b) REJECTED ON THE MERITS, as written; **(c) DEFERRED — the exposure registered, the binding scheduled, and NO OPTION SELECTED.** THE TEETH, IN ONE SENTENCE: the binding that landed at D-283 is a SELECTION and it owes the DECISION-RED-TEAM that (c)-as-adopted would have discharged, which is why D-283 records its sub-choices with their reasons and states in its own text that they have not been attacked. Flips never — this is a correction of a label, and D-283 supersedes the disposition it labelled.

D-289: THE FOUR ITEMS D-251 REGISTERED AS **WP-1.10** ARE EACH GIVEN AN OWNER RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT, AND ONE OF THEM IS SPENT. This session was directed not to do WP-1.10 work; it was directed that none of these may stay silent, so each carries a disposition here. (1) THE COVERAGE OBLIGATION — WP-1.10, UNCHANGED IN SIZE, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS STATED BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO GET WRONG IN THIS ROUND'S FAVOUR. Two scripts land here WITH suites that execute them — `crates/pistol-cli/tests/decision_key_check_tests.rs` and `crates/pistol-cli/tests/scratch_preflight_tests.rs` — but they are NEW scripts, so they add to the driven side without removing anything from the undriven one. RE-ENUMERATED at this revision by the execution sites rather than by mentions (`grep -rn 'arg(repo("tools/' crates/*/tests`, ten hits): DRIVEN are `arena_smoke.sh`, `artifact_check.sh`, `baseline_snapshot.sh`, `bench_delta.sh`, `decision_key_check.sh`, `file_justification_check.sh`, `scratch_preflight.sh`, `solver_edge_check.sh`, `solver_link_check.sh` and `tactical_check.sh`; UNDRIVEN, and still five, are `config_check.sh`, `determinism.sh`, `movetime_check.sh`, `perft_check.sh` and `search_oracle_check.sh` — five of FOURTEEN gates now rather than of thirteen, which is a change in the denominator and not in the debt. The rest of what `tactical_check.sh` records is still driven by nothing. OWNER: WP-1.10. (2) THE `command -v` SWEEP — OWNER: WP-1.10, AND THE COUNT IS RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN CARRIED, because carrying a stale count is the defect D-251's own ruling (5) is about and D-251's list is now stale for TWO separate reasons. It recorded «EIGHT SITES ACROSS SEVEN FILES» and named them; since then `tools/solver_edge_check.sh` and `tools/solver_link_check.sh` landed with D-276, adding FOUR sites in TWO files that D-251 could not have counted, and this round adds FOUR more in `tools/arena_smoke.sh` (`sha256sum`), `tools/decision_key_check.sh` (`git`) and `tools/scratch_preflight.sh` (`df`, `awk`). RE-COUNTED AT THIS REVISION, by `grep -n 'command -v' tools/*.sh` and by reading each hit to separate the terse idiom from the corrected five-branch one: **SIXTEEN sites across ELEVEN files** — `arena_smoke.sh` 2, `ci.sh` 2, `scratch_preflight.sh` 2, `solver_link_check.sh` 3, and one each in `solver_edge_check.sh`, `determinism.sh`, `decision_key_check.sh`, `search_oracle_check.sh`, `tactical_check.sh`, `file_justification_check.sh`, `movetime_check.sh`. The corrected idiom remains in-tree at `baseline_snapshot.sh` and `bench_delta.sh` only, and both of those take a CALLER-SUPPLIED name, which is D-251's own caveat about not copying the five-branch block wholesale into a fixed-name probe. The four new sites carry the terse form KNOWINGLY: writing the corrected form in two new scripts while fourteen existing sites keep the terse one would make the sweep's enumeration wrong in the other direction. (3) THE SHELL_CHECKLIST ITEM 8 AMENDMENT for the fourth case bash admits — a non-executable regular file, which `command -v` ACCEPTS and exec answers with 126 — OWNER: WP-1.10, untouched. Item 12 landed in this round beside it and deliberately did not renumber or absorb it. (4) THE TWO MINORS. **MINOR-2** — `tools/tactical_check.sh`'s header calls the fixture sha-pinned and the script enforces no digest, so STANDALONE it will pass a mutated fixture — OWNER: WP-1.10, unchanged, and the CI-level cover D-251 records (gate 3 runs before gate 8) still stands. **MINOR-3** — arguments silently ignored by `tactical_check.sh`, `determinism.sh`, `perft_check.sh` and `movetime_check.sh` — OWNER: WP-1.10 for those four; NOT JOINED by the two scripts landing here, both of which refuse arguments by name with a test. AND THE FIFTH ITEM, THE ONE D-252 ADDED, IS SPENT: the explicit engine binding for the four operator-run SPRT configs landed at D-283, so WP-1.10's entry in `docs/ROADMAP.md` loses it in this same commit rather than carrying an item already fixed — which is the failure D-251's own «WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE» clause committed and recorded. PRIORITY, since the amendment asked for slots and not only owners: WP-1.5b is next and neither WP-1.9 nor WP-1.10 sits on its critical path; both stay LICENSED AND NOT SCHEDULED, and the order after 1.5b is WP-1.10 before WP-1.9, because 1.10 hardens the instruments every Stage-1 strength claim is read through and 1.9 is a storage change whose own recorded stake (D-258) is a table-only reading that must not be quoted as a whole-engine bracket. Flips per item as each lands.

D-290: T4 IS DISPOSED — A GOVERNED-RUN REPORT STATES **MEASURED** COST BESIDE **DECLARED** COST, AND A MISMATCH GREATER THAN 5x IS A **FINDING**, NOT A VIOLATION; THE EXPENSIVE BRANCH STAYS UNLEGISLATED. Operator ruling, closing the reading `docs/process_readings.md` records as «OPEN, AND OWED A RULING» and D-270 records as excluded-class-and-owed. WHAT T4 FOUND: CLAUDE.md's proportionality paragraph gates its only substantive obligation on «where the run is cheap», cheapness is decided by a cost statement THE SAME SESSION WRITES BEFORE THE RUN, nothing validates it and nothing reconciles it afterwards, and the expensive branch is left wholly unlegislated — so an honest but wrong forecast of expense discharges the replication and second-instrument duty and re-licenses exactly the single-sample-plus-derived-margin instrument D-228 exists to forbid. THE RULING: the forecast is RECONCILED. A report that carries a governed number states what the run actually cost beside what the document declared it would, and a run that proves cheap owes the cheap-branch duties — replication, and a second instrument with a registered agreement criterion and a registered consequence — before its verdict counts. The remedy is retroactive and affordable by construction, because replicating a cheap run is cheap. A MISMATCH IS A FINDING AND NOT A VIOLATION, and the distinction is the whole of the ruling's shape: a forecast is a forecast, a session that guesses badly and says so has done nothing wrong, and treating a wrong number as a breach would teach the next session to write a wide range instead of a number. 5x is the threshold at which the mismatch stops being noise about the machine and starts being evidence about the estimate, and it is a judged number stated as one. EVIDENCE, AND IT IS THE REASON THE THRESHOLD IS NOT HIGHER: D-278(3) records an OPTION MATRIX that estimated «~30-60 s» against a measured 5.2-6.3 s — wrong by an order of magnitude, IN THE RECOMMENDER'S OWN FAVOUR, in a decision whose entire argument is that unmeasured claims are this work package's failure mode, and both measurements were available in eleven seconds. That is one instance and it is the only one this project has; a 5x threshold catches it with room to spare and does not catch a run that took twice as long as somebody thought. THE EXPENSIVE BRANCH STAYS UNLEGISLATED, DELIBERATELY: no expensive governed run exists in this project — D-236 declared 7-9 minutes and measured 433.3 s and 433.9 s, the WP-1.5a pre-registration's §6 states measured costs — and legislating a branch nothing has taken is how the last five rounds went. This is D-228's own reasoning applied to D-228's sibling clause, which is what makes it a disposition rather than a new rule. IT LANDS AS AN ADR LINE AND NOT IN CLAUDE.md, ON THE OPERATOR'S INSTRUCTION, AND THE COST OF THAT IS NAMED: D-228 says in its own text that «a rule whose limits are stated only in a decision log is a rule the next reader applies without them», and this ruling now sits where that sentence warns about. It is recorded that way because the reconciliation duty binds a REPORT rather than a pre-registration and no report has yet been written under it — the clause moves into CLAUDE.md's proportionality paragraph the first time a governed run is taken under it, and that is the flip. `docs/process_readings.md`'s T4 entry is updated to CLOSED by this line. Flips as above; and the 5x threshold flips on a second instance, in either direction, since one data point is what it currently rests on and this line says so.

D-291: A NUMERIC CLAIM IN AN OPTION MATRIX IS MARKED **MEASURED** OR **ESTIMATED**, AND AN ESTIMATE THAT COULD HAVE BEEN MEASURED IN SECONDS IS A FINDING — one sentence added to CLAUDE.md's DECISION-RED-TEAM clause, in this same commit. THE GROUND IS TWO INSTANCES IN ONE SESSION, both inside the FINISH-B round and both in matrices whose own argument was about unmeasured claims. (i) D-278(3): a cost estimated «~30-60 s» against a measured 5.2-6.3 s, wrong by an order of magnitude in the recommender's favour, with both measurements available in eleven seconds. (ii) The same round's matrix RECOMMENDED an option whose feasibility it labelled «needs measuring» — a recommendation resting on a claim the document itself said was unchecked, which is not a bad estimate but an absent one presented as a live option. THE CLAUSE IS ABOUT MARKING AND NOT ABOUT FORBIDDING. An option matrix is written before the work and most of its numbers cannot be measured yet; what the sentence forbids is a number that LOOKS measured and is not, because that is what a red-team cannot attack — an estimate labelled as one invites the attack «why not measure it», and an unlabelled one deflects it. WHY A FINDING AND NOT A BREACH, the same shape as D-290: the red-team names it, the matrix is corrected or the number is taken, and the decision proceeds. Nothing is void for having estimated. WHAT «IN SECONDS» MEANS IS JUDGED AND NOT MECHANIZED, and that is stated rather than left implicit: the test is whether the measurement was AVAILABLE to the session writing the matrix, on the machine it was standing on, without a build it had not already made — which is exactly the eleven seconds D-278(3) records. A number that would need a governed run to obtain is an estimate and stays one. THIS ROUND APPLIED IT TO ITSELF, which is the only evidence a new clause can offer on its first day: D-285's scratch floor is stated as `340552 KiB, measured at d6f6cbb` rather than as «a few hundred megabytes», and the measurement took one build. Flips if a matrix is ever found where the marking cost more than it caught, or if a mechanized check for it is found — a matrix's numbers are not machine-readable today and this clause is judged, like the two rules it sits beside.

D-292: D-290's 5x THRESHOLD IS RETRACTED AS UNEARNED AND ITS TWO SUPPORTING FACTS ARE CORRECTED; THE RECONCILIATION DUTY STANDS UNCHANGED — the DECISION-RED-TEAM D-290 was landed without (its own text names no matter) has now run, at 6b03899, and the threshold did not survive it. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, recorded as CLAUDE.md's option-matrix clause requires: the 5x threshold is load-bearing for nothing — every duty in D-290 triggers on the measured cost's ABSOLUTE position relative to "cheap" and none on the ratio, so the FINDING it declares carries no registered consequence, which is the criterion-without-consequence shape CLAUDE.md's own proportionality paragraph forbids; and both of the threshold's premises are falsified by files in this tree in seconds. (1) "a 5x threshold catches it with room to spare" is FALSE on the conservative reading of its own sole data point: the declared cost is a BRACKET («~30-60 s») and the measured cost a RANGE (5.2-6.3 s), D-290 states no reduction of either to a point, and nearest-endpoint gives 30/6.3 = 4.76 — the threshold MISSES the one instance it was derived to catch, by 5%. Midpoints give 7.83 and farthest 11.54, so the verdict is a function of an unstated rule, which is the defect, not the number. (2) "That is one instance and it is the only one this project has" is FALSE, and is falsified by a document D-290 itself cites: docs/experiments/wp15a_prereg.md revision 7's cost table «was wrong in both directions» — tools/bench_delta.sh billed at its 9 s refusal path against a governed 6 m 18 s = 378 s (42x UNDER-declared) and tools/baseline_snapshot.sh billed 33 s x 4 = 132 s for a run that took ZERO snapshots (a ratio no ratio rule can express). The two directions also fail DIFFERENTLY — over-declaring expense wrongly buys the unlegislated duty-free branch, under-declaring wrongly commits to duties and is self-correcting — and one unsigned threshold cannot say so. (3) "no expensive governed run exists in this project" is FALSE in one multiplication over committed files: configs/arena_wp13_r2_vs_r3.toml records openings_take = 2000, n_workers = 4 and a calibration probe of 4.9 s per game, and docs/experiments/wp13_results.md records «4-worker runs of 4000 and 3182 games», so 4000 x 4.9 s = 19600 s = 5.44 CORE-HOURS, about 82 minutes wall. D-252 states WP-1.5b's acceptance runs on a document of exactly this shape and D-289 schedules WP-1.5b next, so the branch declined as untaken has been taken and is one work package away. WHAT THIS LINE CHANGES: the 5x number is withdrawn; a governed-run report still states MEASURED cost beside DECLARED cost, and a mismatch is still reported on the document's face. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not install a replacement threshold. A replacement is a named design decision with at least five viable shapes (no threshold; a ratio band; a two-sided asymmetric rule; a ratio defined on the declared BRACKET; a size-scaled threshold), it is owed an OPTION MATRIX attacked before selection, and deriving one here from the four-instance corpus this attack assembled would be the after-the-numbers move the paragraph forbids. WHAT FLIPS IT: a matrix that survives attack, at which point the surviving shape lands with its consequence stated. D-290's T4 entry in docs/process_readings.md is REOPENED to the extent of the threshold; the reconciliation duty it also created is not under attack and stays closed.

D-293: D-291's GROUND IS CORRECTED FROM "TWO INSTANCES" TO ONE MATRIX WITH TWO DEFECTS, ITS BASE RATE IS STATED AS ONE IN FOUR, AND THE CLAUSE STAYS IN CLAUDE.md WITH ITS AUTHORITY AND ITS ESCAPE NAMED — the DECISION-RED-TEAM D-291 never had has now run, at 6b03899, and the clause's TEXT survives while its RECORD does not. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, recorded as the option-matrix clause requires: the clause's ground is not two instances but ONE MATRIX COUNTED TWICE — D-291's (i) («a cost estimated ~30-60 s against a measured 5.2-6.3 s») and its (ii) («The same round's matrix RECOMMENDED an option whose feasibility it labelled needs measuring») are the two halves of D-278(3)'s single sentence about the single matrix that produced D-276, and D-291's own (ii) says «the same round's matrix» while its headline says «both in matrices», plural; decisively, D-290 AT LINE 625 OF THIS SAME FILE, LANDED IN THE SAME COMMIT ON THE SAME EVIDENCE, WRITES «That is one instance and it is the only one this project has». A commit that says "one instance" at one line and "TWO INSTANCES" at the next, about the same matrix, and whose subject at that next line is UNMARKED NUMERIC CLAIMS, is the clause failing its own test inside its own text. THE BASE RATE, absent from D-291 and measured here in one grep: this project has written FOUR option matrices — D-196, D-225, D-252, D-276 — and the defect is confined to ONE of them, D-276's; D-225's numbers are already marked inline («measured 1.30x/1.54x/1.89x») which is the behaviour the clause mandates, arrived at WITHOUT the clause. And the defect was CAUGHT: D-278(3) records in its own words that «The decision red-team named it», so the evidence is evidence that the fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM works on first contact — which is D-290's own «legislating a branch nothing has taken» argument turned on its sibling, in the same commit, unanswered. THE TWO RULINGS APPLY OPPOSITE STANDARDS OF EVIDENTIAL SUFFICIENCY TO EACH OTHER'S SHAPE while citing each other for it, and neither names the tension. WHY THE CLAUSE NEVERTHELESS STANDS: it is cheap, it is one sentence, its cost falls on the writer of a matrix rather than on any run, and its first-day self-application is genuine and checked (D-285's «340552 KiB, measured at d6f6cbb», re-derived at this revision). What it lacked was not merit but a record. WHAT THIS LINE ADDS, because the attack showed the text underdetermined: (1) THE AUTHORITY IS NAMED — D-291 carries no operator attribution in its own text and, unlike D-283, does not declare its review outstanding; this line is that declaration, discharged. (2) MARKING-THEATRE IS CLOSED — a matrix carries AT LEAST ONE **MEASURED** CLAIM OR STATES WHY NONE WAS AVAILABLE, because the compliant equilibrium of marking every claim ESTIMATED satisfies the clause on its face while measuring nothing, and the clause's own theory of value («an estimate labelled as one INVITES the attack why not measure it») requires the label to discriminate.
