(3) THE ADJUDICATOR IS THE RED-TEAM AND THE CLOCK IS THE MATRIX-WRITING SESSION'S, which D-291 already says; what it does not say and this line does is that availability-in-principle is arguable in hindsight for almost any number, so the finding is owed a NAMED COMMAND that would have produced the value, not an assertion that one existed. WHAT FLIPS IT: a matrix that measures nothing and states a defensible reason, twice, makes (2) a tax rather than a guard. THE CHEAPEST COMPLIANCE REMAINS UNCLOSED AND IS RECORDED AS A RESIDUAL: D-283, the largest decision in the same commit, states NO cost number at all and therefore satisfies D-291 vacuously — stating no numbers is a cheaper escape than marking them, and this line does not close it.

D-294: D-283's "A MISMATCHED BUILD NEVER BECOMES A PROCESS" IS FALSE AS WRITTEN AND IS QUALIFIED HERE; THE BARE-NAME HOLE IS CLOSED AND THE PER-SPAWN WINDOW'S STATED JUSTIFICATION IS WITHDRAWN — RED-TEAM and DECISION-RED-TEAM at 6b03899, both of which D-283 declared outstanding on its own face. TWO COUNTS, one closed and one recorded. (1) CLOSED: a `binary` naming no path separator is digested from the WORKING DIRECTORY by `identity::digest_of` (`std::fs::read`) and spawned through `$PATH` by `Channel::start` (`Command::new` -> `execvp`), so where both resolve the digest attests one file and every game is played by another — reproduced end-to-end, 18 of 18 invocations to the PATH file, arena exit 0, report attesting the other file's digest. This is D-226's decided class, closed in tools/bench_delta.sh:48-52 and tools/baseline_snapshot.sh:297 with `command -v` and `realpath`, and re-entered through the Rust seat; REVIEW-impl's spawn-domination reading missed it because it assumed `fs::read(binary)` and `Command::new(binary)` name one file. Refused at validation as a spelling property (D-21). (2) RECORDED, NOT CLOSED: `identity.rs` already discloses that the binary is not re-digested per spawn, so the window is honest — but its stated reason, that re-digesting «buys a case nobody has observed», does not survive. The case IS observed and is in-tree: `tools/arena_smoke.sh` rebuilds the binary as CI gate 12, and a rebuild was measured to change the inode, which is exactly the swap; reproduced twice (`mv` and symlink retarget) at 12 of 18 invocations running a never-digested binary, exit 0. And the cost the reason rests on was ESTIMATED where it could have been measured in seconds — D-291's own clause, landed in the same commit: MEASURED here, a digest is 7.85 ms, about 0.1% of configs/arena_wp13_r2_vs_r3.toml's run and about 3x the whole of tools/arena_smoke.sh. So the window's disclosure stands and its justification is withdrawn; the honest statement of D-283's claim is «a mismatched build never becomes the FIRST process of a run», with every later spawn unbound. WHAT FLIPS IT: a per-spawn re-`stat` of (dev, ino, size, mtime) at about 1 microsecond catches every accident of this kind and no adversary, and is the cheapest complete answer to the accident class; adopting it is a named choice and is owed a matrix. STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK on the required-versus-optional sub-choice, recorded as the option-matrix clause requires: the flip condition D-283 declares unmet — that no legitimate document exists which cannot know its binary in advance — is met BY D-283's OWN COMMIT, since `tools/arena_smoke.sh:206-209` overwrites the committed `binary_sha256` into `$WORK/bound.toml` before every use, so the one document CI runs has its binding neutralised, while the four documents carrying a live binding are referenced by no script in tools/ or crates/ and are therefore run by no gate — leaving NO committed document whose run-start comparison is ever exercised against a real build. Recorded, not repaired: the smoke rewrite is the right mechanism for a document whose binary is built by the gate itself, and naming that case properly is a separate decision. FURTHER, UNREPAIRED AND RECORDED: `crates/pistol-arena/src/openings.rs:161` accepts UPPERCASE hex (`is_ascii_hexdigit`) at the openings digest while `validate.rs:216` refuses it at `binary_sha256`, in the same document; and the lowercase rationale D-283 inherits from D-205 — two spellings of one experiment — cannot apply at this key, because `identity.rs` stores the COMPUTED digest and the document's string never reaches `experiment_sha256`. The strictness may be right; the reason recorded for it is not this one.

D-295: D-287's PACK MUTATION-GATES THE TEST-SIDE ORACLE AND NOT THE SHIPPED ONE, ITS ALL-NEGATIVE CLAUSE IS FALSE FOR PAT-O3, AND "FOUR ALG- RECORDS" IS THREE — RED-TEAM at 6b03899, per-fixture, every construction run rather than argued. THE COUNT FIRST: the pack holds ELEVEN records, of which EIGHT are PAT- and THREE are ALG- (ALG-CROSS-BOTH, ALG-SAMELINE-RIGHT, ALG-SAMELINE-BOTH); D-287's «four ALG- records» is wrong and its «eleven records» is right — the same-line double's left half is PAT-O4 QUOTED (`pattern_calculus_tests.rs` binds `left = pattern_case("PAT-O4")` and asserts the stones match) rather than a fourth ALG- record. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: the pack's entire contact with crates/pistol-solver/src is 33 booleans — three `HitBudget` rungs across eleven records — plus four `hot_windows` assertions; every other assertion runs against `crates/pistol-solver/tests/common/plans.rs`, which is TEST CODE that the fixture file is itself derived from. Measured consequence: replacing the whole hitting-set enumeration in `cover.rs` with two arbitrary counting thresholds (`universe >= 4` for One, `windows >= 6` for Two — coincidences that hold on all eleven records) leaves the pack 9 of 9 GREEN with `covers()` dead. And the forbidden thing passes: a shipped `t` computed by WEIGHT ADDITION, summing exact per-axis values, answers 4 on ALG-CROSS-BOTH where the exact answer is 3, and the pack is green — because `HitBudget` saturates at `AboveTwo`, so both 3 and 4 are the same boolean, and `threat_number_is_never_additive` reads `case.t` off the derived fixture and never calls the shipped solver. So V-P3.5 is a regression on the TEST-SIDE oracle; RULE-EXACT's «never derived by weight algebra» is unpinned in src. RESIDUAL, and it is structural: no fixture shaped as a `HitBudget` query can separate t=3 from t=4, the type being closed at two for a stated reason — closing this needs a differently-shaped shipped surface (`blocking_covers`, whose cover SETS carry structure a rung does not), not another record. THE ALL-NEGATIVE CLAUSE IS FALSE AS WRITTEN: D-287 says PAT-RHOMBUS (support 2) and PAT-O3 (support 3) «are separated by a POSITIVE claim that an answer-invariant edit cannot leave true», and the fixture header repeats it. Reproduced: PAT-O3's plies replaced by PAT-RHOMBUS's, re-derived through the pack's own renderer and re-pinned — 9 of 9 green, `support` having re-derived from 3 to 2 with the edit, because `support` sits on the DERIVED side of the file and so cannot stand against it. Only PAT-RHOMBUS's 2 has an independent referent, hard-coded in `rhombus_has_empty_plan_family`, which is why one direction dies and the other does not. IT COMPOUNDS: on the pristine pack, widening the hot threshold dies on PAT-O3 alone; with that swap applied first the same mutation is green, so the edit the pack claims to prevent removes the pack's only gate on the hot threshold's lower side. THREE RECORDS ARE PINNED BY A SINGLE INTEGER and were each swapped for an unrelated position with the suite green — PAT-C4, PAT-O3 and ALG-SAMELINE-RIGHT; the worst is ALG-SAMELINE-RIGHT, whose whole role is TO BE THE RIGHT HALF, and which with PAT-O4's plies makes `threat_number_is_never_additive` assert "each half alone is a t=2 open four" about the same half twice, and pass. WHAT SURVIVED ATTACK AND IS CREDITED: the sha pin does gate (an unpinned edit turns 5 of 9 red); a deleted record is caught BY NAME with both lists printed; malformed lines and unknown keys are refused by name; PAT-GAP is the best-pinned record in the pack and D-287's declared GT-1 fires exactly as recorded; and two further mutations were correctly diagnosed as EQUIVALENT rather than as holes. WHAT FLIPS THE FRAMING: D-287 calls the pack a mutation gate for «the threat oracle»; measured, the whole-crate gate is `threat_incremental_matches_reference_on_random_playouts`, which killed 5 of the 6 mutations the pack missed. The pack's real and considerable value is that it pins `common::plans` tightly; that is what it should be recorded as.

D-296: D-284's GRANDFATHER EXEMPTS THE KEY AND NOT THE MULTIPLICITY, SO A THIRD TEXT UNDER AN EXEMPTED KEY PASSES — REVIEW-impl at 6b03899, reproduced with a seeded violation. THE MECHANISM, stated as mechanism rather than as summary: D-279 registered «`grep -oE '^D-[0-9]+' docs/decisions.md | sort | uniq -d` must be empty», which is RED on this log by design, superseded duplicates remaining in an append-only file; the shipped gate runs the same anchored extraction against the GIT BLOB rather than the worktree path and then, instead of requiring emptiness, requires SET EQUALITY between the duplicate set and a frozen two-key exemption via `comm` in both directions. So the divergence is not the extraction but the acceptance test, and the exemption is an ALLOWLIST — a frozen set of KEYS, inline as a here-string, not a count, a date or a line cutoff. THE DEFECT: `uniq -d` prints a key ONCE however many times it occurs, so the comparison cannot distinguish the two copies D-279 ruled on from a new third copy. Reproduced: a third D-276 with a third different text, staged so the gate's tracked-bytes read sees it, `git cat-file blob :docs/decisions.md | grep -cE '^D-276:'` = 3, and the gate printed «294 decision keys in docs/decisions.md, no repeat outside the exemption» and exited 0. D-284's stated property is that one key denotes one text; a key denoting three texts is that property broken, reported as no repeat. FIXED by exempting the MULTIPLICITY rather than the key: the exemption is now `D-276 2` / `D-277 2`, the duplicate set is built with `uniq -c`, and a third copy becomes `D-276 3`, which is in neither direction of the comparison and refuses by name. WHAT WAS ATTACKED AND HELD, recorded because these are the properties the gate exists for: a NEW duplicate key is provably caught (a second D-100, seeded and staged, printed «repeated key: D-100» and exited 1); the exemption cannot outlive its subject (deleting the second D-277 printed «exempted but not repeated: D-277» and exited 1, so the both-directions check is real); and an unstaged duplicate correctly leaves the gate green, the index being what commits (SHELL_CHECKLIST item 5, and ci.sh gate 2 reads the index for the same reason). WHAT FLIPS IT: a ruling that a superseded key may legitimately gain a third text, at which point the exemption carries the count it is granted.

D-297: D-285's PREFLIGHT READ THE WRONG `df` COLUMN AND WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS ON A MOUNT SOURCE CONTAINING A SPACE; IT NOW ASKS `stat -f`, WHICH HAS NO COLUMNS — RED-TEAM at 6b03899, reproduced on a real tmpfs under an unprivileged user namespace, not simulated. THE DEFECT: `awk '{ print $4 }'` over `df -Pk` assumes a one-word Filesystem field. `df` un-escapes the mount source, so a source containing a space shifts every column left and field 4 stops being Available and becomes USED — and the script's own comment asserted that `-P` «is what makes field 4 a field rather than a guess», which is the one thing that is not true here. MEASURED, both directions on one filesystem mounted as `my dev`: EMPTY at 2 GiB, the shipped script printed «has 0 KiB available» and VOIDED a healthy run; the same filesystem with about 1 MiB left printed «has 2096132 KiB available, floor 1048576 KiB» and EXITED 0 — a pass on a filesystem that could not hold a tenth of what the next step would write. The spelling guard (item 8) cannot see either, because Used is also a well-formed decimal; this is EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER in its column-shaped form, and the field-1 name was truncated to `(my)` in the same messages. REACHABLE, not exotic: CIFS `//server/my share`, NFS `server:/my export`, and docker and overlay sources. THE FIX IS NOT A BETTER PARSE BUT NO PARSE: `stat -f -c '%a %S %c %d'` answers one field per directive and has no columns to shift; the filesystem is named by `stat -c '%D'`, a device number, never by a mount source, that field being exactly the one whose spacing broke the parse. TWO FURTHER DEFECTS CLOSED IN THE SAME PASS. (i) INODES ARE SPACE TOO and exhaust separately: a tmpfs with 64 MiB free and zero free inodes refuses every create, and the shipped script exited 0 on it; `%c`/`%d` now void it by name, with `%c == 0` (btrfs and others, which do not report inodes) correctly not read as an exhaustion. (ii) THE FLOOR FAILED OPEN ABOVE 2^63-1: `[ x -le y ]` on a larger value is an ERROR rather than a comparison, and an erroring `[` in a CONDITION is exempt from `set -e` (item 2), so `PISTOL_MIN_SCRATCH_KIB` above the boundary left the floor at the constant and the check passed — falsifying the header's own «can only ever tighten» invariant. The boundary is now exact and both sides are tested: 9223372036854775807 still REFUSES with exit 2, one past it is a caller bug with exit 1. WHY THE SUITE DID NOT CATCH ANY OF IT, which is the finding under the finding: every refusal in `scratch_preflight_tests.rs` was manufactured by raising `PISTOL_MIN_SCRATCH_KIB`, which exercises the COMPARISON and never the READING, so a script reading the wrong column satisfied all of them. The suite now carries an EXTERNALLY DERIVED REFERENT — the printed number must agree within 1% with `stat -f` computed outside the script — which shares the directory with the gate but not the parse; mutation-gated, a script reading the neighbouring field reports 974662656 KiB against a referent of 866100432 and the test fires. CORRECTED ON THE FACE OF THE SCRIPT: the header said the floor is «three times» the measured 340552 KiB; 1048576 / 340552 = 3.079, the constant having been rounded up to 1 GiB and the prose not.

D-298: D-289's RE-ENUMERATION IS RIGHT AND THE COMMAND RECORDED BESIDE IT IS WRONG — REVIEW-impl at 6b03899. D-289 states the ten driven `tools/` scripts were «RE-ENUMERATED at this revision by the execution sites rather than by mentions (`grep -rn 'arg(repo("tools/' crates/*/tests`, ten hits)». Run verbatim at that revision the command yields EIGHT hits over FOUR scripts, because the suites use two idioms — `.arg(repo("tools/X.sh"))` for four of them and `.arg(root.join("tools/X.sh"))` for arena_smoke, bench_delta, decision_key_check, file_justification_check and tactical_check — and the cited grep sees only the first. THE CONCLUSION IS NONETHELESS CORRECT: re-enumerated independently by execution context rather than by either idiom, the partition is exactly the one D-289 records — ten driven, five undriven (config_check, determinism, movetime_check, perft_check, search_oracle_check), five of fourteen gates. So the number is right and the INSTRUMENT recorded beside it is wrong, which is the class CLAUDE.md's dry-run clause names — «a command that counted the wrong symbols passed a synthetic dry run and still shipped» — arriving from the other side: a command that counts the wrong symbols recorded beside a number obtained another way. A successor who re-runs the recorded command gets 8 over 4 and concludes the enumeration drifted. AMENDED, AND THE HONEST FORM IS WEAKER THAN THE ONE THIS LINE FIRST REACHED FOR: there is NO single grep that yields ten, and a replacement citation was attempted and withdrawn. There are THREE idioms, not two — `.arg(repo("tools/X.sh"))`, `.arg(root.join("tools/X.sh"))`, and `repo().join("tools/X.sh")` copied to a scratch path and run there, which is how `artifact_check` is driven. Matching all three by name yields nine and misses `artifact_check`; dropping to any `tools/*.sh` outside a `//` comment yields TWELVE, because `perft_check` and `search_oracle_check` appear in `#[ignore]` REASON STRINGS naming the script that runs them — and those two are on D-289's UNDRIVEN list, so the looser command counts as driven exactly the two scripts whose being undriven is the finding. The enumeration is therefore recorded as what it is: ten, by READING each execution site, and the three idioms are named here so the next count does not rediscover them. A number obtained by reading is not worse than one obtained by a command; a number obtained by reading and PRESENTED as a command's output is, which was the defect. WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: an artefact that produces a registered number is named in the pre-registration WITH ITS REVISION and a change to it reopens the review, so a recorded command that does not produce the recorded number is an instrument nobody can re-run — the same defect the instrument-revision clause exists for, in the decision log rather than in a pre-registration.

D-299: ITEM 12 IS APPLIED TO THE GATES THE DIFF THAT AUTHORED IT SHIPPED, AND THE DISTINCTION NOW REACHES THE LOG — REVIEW-impl and RED-TEAM at 6b03899, which found the item unevenly applied to its own commits. `tools/solver_link_check.sh` and `tools/scratch_preflight.sh` discharged all three obligations; nothing else did, and the item is not mechanized, so nothing said so. FIVE REPAIRS. (1) `tools/decision_key_check.sh`, NEW IN THE SAME COMMITS, had NO VOID CLASS: absent git, a directory that is not a repository, an unreadable blob and a failed `mktemp` all exited 1 — the same code as «a key repeats» — while the usage block ASSERTED there was no void class rather than saying so, which obligation 1 asks for explicitly. Through `ci.sh` that is `ci: FAIL: decision key check`, indistinguishable in a log from the log actually carrying a duplicate. Reproduced by copying the gate out of the repository (it resolves its own root from `BASH_SOURCE` and `cd`s there, so that is the only way its root is not one): exit 1 before, exit 2 with `RUN VOID` after. (2) OBLIGATION 3, TWICE: `decision_key_check_tests.rs` and `arena_smoke_gate_tests.rs` asserted only `status.success()`, which is satisfied by 1, 2, 127 and a signal death alike, so neither could have SEEN a void misreported; `assert_code` is lifted from `solver_link_check_tests.rs`, which this diff got right, into the suites it did not. (3) `tools/ci.sh` ERASED THE DISTINCTION AT THE SEAM: `fail` exits 1 and every gate was invoked `tools/X.sh || fail "..."`, so a gate's exit 2 was reported as a FAILURE at 14 of 15 sites — the distinction the gates were given dying one call away from the gates that make it. A `gate` wrapper preserves it, driven with stub gates at each code: 0 continues, 1 is `ci: FAIL` and exit 1, 2 is `ci: RUN VOID ... this is NOT a regression` and exit 2. (4) THE PREFLIGHT ASKED ABOUT ONE FILESYSTEM WHILE THE LARGER CONSUMER WENT UNASKED: `$TMPDIR` holds gate 2's clone and gate 3's stub workspaces, but gates 3, 4 and 8-12 build into `$ROOT/target`, and MEASURED here those are different devices (38 and 3a, a 24 GiB tmpfs and an nvme partition). Both are preflighted now, in `ci.sh` and again in `arena_smoke.sh`, which takes a `mktemp -d` and runs a release build and had neither preflight nor void class. (5) TWO EXIT TRAPS did not preserve the body's status (item 7) and two `mktemp` sites died silently under `set -e` (item 1); both are named refusals now. WHAT WAS CHECKED AND LEFT ALONE, recorded so it is not rediscovered: `tools/solver_link_check.sh` and `tools/solver_edge_check.sh` are the only other void-capable scripts and are NOT in `ci.sh`'s fourteen-gate roster, which first read as item 12's discipline living where CI never runs — it does not hold, because both are driven by their test suites under gate 3 and so do execute in CI, as diagnostics rather than as roster entries. The roster is unchanged; the gate count is cited in D-284 and in several test headers, and moving it is a separate decision. ALSO REPAIRED, from the same round: three gate-number citations named the wrong place — two test headers cited `ci.sh:63` and `ci.sh:92` for gates this diff's own preflight block had moved (63 is gate 4, 92 is blank), the same edit having updated «of 13» to «of 14» in the same sentence and left the numbers; and `tools/config_check.sh` called the smoke gate «CI gate 11» when it is 12 of 14, wrong at `d6f6cbb` too. WHAT FLIPS ANY OF IT: a gate that acquires a void class acquires the obligation to spell it, and a suite that drives a gate acquires the obligation to assert its code rather than its success.

D-300: THE LINK GATE'S VERDICT NO LONGER DEPENDS ON THE CALLER'S WORKING DIRECTORY — REVIEW-impl at 6b03899, attacking the S29 guard from the FALSE-ABORT side, which is the direction a gate that refuses legitimate builds fails in. `realpath -ms` resolves a RELATIVE dep-info entry against the process's cwd, and the entry loop runs wherever the caller stood: the two `cargo` calls above it `cd` only inside their own subshells. Cargo emits relative prerequisites whenever `build.dep-info-basedir` is set, which is a supported config key. MEASURED on a stub workspace with that key set, one tree and one set of arguments giving three verdicts as a function of `cd`: at `d6f6cbb` from a foreign cwd, EXIT 0 WITH THE WRONG ANSWER («NO source under crates/subject is an input»); at 6b03899 from the same cwd, exit 2, an honest void, because the S29 existence check had landed; and from the workspace root, exit 1, the correct answer. THE S29 GUARD IS CREDITED AND IS NOT THE DEFECT: converting a wrong answer into a void is exactly what it was added to do, and it survived every other false-abort construction attempted against it — a path containing a space (refused as a void, and the parser says so), `$`, `#`, glob metacharacters, a source deleted between build and check, a dangling symlink, a live symlink under the crate, an empty prerequisite list, a make line-continuation, a zero-length `.d`, and a target containing `: ` (which cargo itself refuses first). It did not make the verdict cwd-INDEPENDENT, and for an instrument that produces WP-1.5a's whole claim — under a rule that an artefact producing a registered number is named with its revision, so that a change to it reopens the review — a verdict that moves with `cd` is a defect one notch below answering wrong. Entries are now anchored to the ROOT the gate was given. A fixture sets `dep-info-basedir` and drives the gate from a THIRD directory, because without one an anchored resolve and a cwd-relative one are indistinguishable on every well-formed line — which is the same shape as the S29 mutant that survived eleven tests, and is why this could ship. ALSO, item 8 in the same file: the preflight's exit 1 («the caller called this wrong») was folded into its exit 2 («the run is void»), so a malformed `PISTOL_MIN_SCRATCH_KIB` printed «the RUN VOID above names the filesystem» above a line that named no filesystem and asserted a shortage that did not exist — the right exit class with the wrong diagnosis, which sends the reader at the wrong thing. WHAT FLIPS IT: a decision to require the gate be run from the workspace root, which would make the anchor unnecessary and the fixture a check on the requirement instead.

D-301: D-255 IS WRONG ON A NUMBER IT STATES, AND THE DECISION IT CARRIES IS UNAFFECTED — found while WP-1.5b re-derived the same corpus, reproduced twice independently before this line was written. D-255 says "the corpus shows own-side hot = 0.0 mean / 0 max at both stone counts, i.e. positions that do not exhibit the phenomenon the threat generator exists for". MEASURED over the same 24 positions of `crates/pistol-cli/tests/fixtures/bench_positions_v1.txt`, replayed through `GameState` and `ThreatState`: own-side hot is **0.0417 mean, max 1**, at corpus index 16, 31 stones — which sits in the band whose centre is 35 (that fixture's `# param band centre 35 width 5`), so the claim is false for the 35-band specifically and true for the 15-band. Seven of the 24 roots hold an OPPONENT hot window. WHY THE DECISION STANDS ANYWAY, said here so a reader does not over-correct: D-255's deciding argument is the ABSOLUTE count-1 traffic (32.8 own count-1 windows at 15 stones against 55.9 at 35, versus 9.6 at count 2), and its own STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK already records that the corpus is measured at roots "in positions the threat generator does not exist for" — this line sharpens that attack rather than answering it, because the phenomenon is present at a rate of one window in twenty-four roots rather than at zero. `LiveCount` stays closed at `{Two, Three}`. Flips if a consumer needs count-1 windows, which is D-255's own clause and is untouched.

D-302: D-299(2) IS HALF FALSE AT THE REVISION THAT SHIPPED IT, AND THE GATE IT NAMES STILL CANNOT TELL A VOID FROM A FAILURE — found by WP-1.5b's Item-0 DECISION-RED-TEAM at `ec8f7fb` and reproduced by grep before this line was written. D-299(2) records that `decision_key_check_tests.rs` and `arena_smoke_gate_tests.rs` "asserted only `status.success()`, which is satisfied by 1, 2, 127 and a signal death alike, so neither could have SEEN a void misreported; `assert_code` is lifted from `solver_link_check_tests.rs`, which this diff got right, into the suites it did not". MEASURED: `fn assert_code` exists in exactly TWO files, `crates/pistol-cli/tests/solver_link_check_tests.rs:151` and `crates/pistol-cli/tests/decision_key_check_tests.rs:120`. `crates/pistol-cli/tests/arena_smoke_gate_tests.rs` contains no `assert_code` and still asserts `!ran.status.success()` at lines 347, 410 and 441. So the lift reached one of the two suites named. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT COSMETIC AND IS THE POINT: D-299(4) gave `tools/arena_smoke.sh` a scratch preflight and a void class in that same round, so the gate now HAS an exit 2 and its own suite cannot distinguish it from exit 1 — which is obligation 3 of `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` item 12 unmet at the gate the same commit set created it for. Recorded rather than fixed: the fix is three assertions in a suite outside WP-1.5b's mandate, and it belongs to WP-1.10, whose subject is exactly this. Flips when that suite asserts codes.

D-303: `tools/solver_edge_check.sh` CANONICALISES ITS ROOT WITH BASH'S LOGICAL `pwd` WHERE ITS SIBLING USES `pwd -P`, SO A SYMLINKED ROOT DEFEATS THE `<workspace>` SUBSTITUTION THAT KEEPS ITS OUTPUT MACHINE-INVARIANT — found by WP-1.5b's Item-0 DECISION-RED-TEAM, reproduced there, and confirmed by reading. Line 103 is `ROOT_ABS="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"`; `tools/solver_link_check.sh:67` is `ROOT_ABS="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"` and says why in its own comment. Cargo prints PHYSICAL paths, so where the caller reached the workspace through a symlink the substitution matches nothing and the gate prints absolute per-run directory names — the same class its own header calls out ("printing the tree verbatim puts a per-run directory name into a record that a pre-registration requires to be byte-identical across replications"), arriving through the one line that was supposed to prevent it. NOT REACHABLE FROM THE SHIPPED TEST TODAY, which is why it is a latent defect and not a red gate: `common::repo_root()` canonicalises, and `/home/tom/Projects/HeXO-AlphaBeta` is not itself reached through a symlink. It is reachable from the registered command block a report is required to cite, and from any hand replication. A SECOND ENVIRONMENT DEPENDENCE IN THE SAME OUTPUT, measured with it: `CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always`, or `[term] color = "always"` in a cargo config, puts ANSI escapes around the tree glyphs even when the output is piped — `cargo tree` offers `--color never` and this gate does not pass it. Both matter only for a gate whose output is compared byte for byte, which is what WP-1.5b's Item 0 proposes to do. Flips when the gate takes `pwd -P` and `--color never`, which is a `tools/` change and therefore a SHELL_CHECKLIST review.

D-304: WP-1.5b's POPULATION CENSUS IS A COMMITTED INSTRUMENT THAT RECORDS NUMBERS AND STAYS IN THE TEST TREE, WHICH IS THE CASE D-287 RESERVED FOR A FUTURE ADR LINE — this is that line. D-287 keeps `crates/pistol-solver/tests/common/plans.rs` test-tree-only BECAUSE "it VERIFIES and records no number, so it does NOT move to `tools/`; promotion is a future ADR owed the day anything records from it". `crates/pistol-solver/tests/wp15b_census.rs` records from it: every population figure WP-1.5b's Tier-T option matrix rests on. IT DOES NOT MOVE TO `tools/` EITHER, and the reason is what `tools/` membership is FOR: it pulls in `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md`'s coverage rule and the shell instrument rules, both of which exist because shell under `set -euo pipefail` parsing unvalidated output fails as EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER. This artefact is a Rust integration test driven by `cargo test`, with no parse, no exit-status reading and no shell; the coverage rule's intent — that an artefact producing a recorded number carries a test driving it — is met by the artefact BEING a test. WHAT REPLACES THE REVISION PIN, and it is the substantive half: the census RENDERS the table `docs/experiments/wp15b_design.md` carries, and `the_design_document_carries_this_censuss_table_verbatim` compares the two BYTE FOR BYTE on every `cargo test`. A recorded SHA discharges the instrument clause only if someone re-reads it, and it measurably did not: WP-1.5b registered the census at a revision emitting three sampling regimes while a whole column of its own tables came from a fourth added in the same commit as the document. The pin fails the build instead. This is D-259's discipline for a derived fixture, and D-284's substitution of a gate for a property nobody was checking, applied to a design document's numbers. THE RESIDUAL IS NAMED: the pin covers the TABLE. Prose about the census — what a regime means, which population a sentence is about — stays judged, and so does `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh`, whose output that document does not carry. Flips if a consumer outside a test needs the census, at which point `tools/` membership and its whole rule set arrive with it.

D-305: A REPAIR IS NOT DONE UNTIL EVERY CLAIM RESTING ON THE REPAIRED THING HAS BEEN RE-READ, AND WRITING THAT SENTENCE DOWN DOES NOT ACHIEVE IT — the process finding of WP-1.5b's design round, recorded because it is a measured base rate rather than an impression. Across six revisions of `docs/experiments/wp15b_design.md`, four fresh-context REVIEW-designs found NINE instances of one shape: a number or a rule was corrected in one section and the sections resting on it were not. Revision 2 broke three claims that way; revision 3 one; revision 4 one, inside the ADR list itself; revision 5 four, in the revision whose §16 wrote the lesson down. THE LESSON IS NOT THE FIX. The cause is structural — the same number lived in five or six places, so propagation was done by memory, which is D-275's own finding ("a list maintained by memory") arriving in a document instead of a gate. WHAT WORKED, and it is the only thing that did: mechanization. The instrument now renders the numbers and a test pins the document against it, so a repair that misses a copy is a red build rather than a reviewer's finding. WHAT IS NOT MECHANIZED AND STAYS JUDGED: a cross-reference, a prose claim, a SHA, and the composition arguments — which is the same boundary CLAUDE.md draws for its own dry-run and proportionality rules ("neither is mechanized, and neither catches a run whose answer is already known before it is taken — that defect is judged, not checked"). ALSO MEASURED IN THE SAME ROUND, and recorded because D-276 treated its single instance as notable: FOUR of the six option matrices recommended an option that a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM then dominated — M0 to (f), M2 to W-E, M3 to S-E, M5 to M5-E — and in three of the four the dominating option cost LESS rather than more. One such instance is an anecdote; four in one work package is a base rate about self-review, and it is the strongest argument this project has for the fresh-context requirement being load-bearing rather than ceremonial. Flips if a later round finds the mechanization catching nothing, or finds a repair-propagation defect it cannot see.

D-306: `PISTOL_MIN_SCRATCH_KIB` IS REMOVED — THE SCRATCH FLOOR IS A NAMED INSTRUMENT CONSTANT IN `tools/scratch_preflight.sh` AND IS READ FROM NOWHERE ELSE. Operator ruling; the class is INVISIBLE CONFIG and the ground is hard rule 1, which puts a default in exactly one schema place and admits no code-side or environment-side second one. The override made the number a gate applies a function of the CALLER'S ENVIRONMENT: two runs of the same script on the same filesystem could answer differently, with nothing in the repository saying so, and the record the script prints (`floor <n> KiB`) named a figure no committed document contained. That it could only ever TIGHTEN the check is not a defence — rule 1 is about where a tunable LIVES, not about which direction it moves — and the tightening invariant was itself falsified once already, by the arithmetic boundary D-297 found failing open above 2^63-1. WHAT PAID FOR THE OVERRIDE WAS ITEM 10's COVERAGE RULE, and the replacement is stronger rather than merely equal: the shortage branch is now driven against a REAL 1 MiB tmpfs mounted inside an unprivileged user + mount namespace — the same facility D-297's red-team used — so `a_filesystem_too_small_for_the_floor_is_a_named_run_void_and_not_a_failure` exercises the READING and the comparison together and checks the printed number against the size the filesystem was made at. Every refusal the override could manufacture exercised the comparison ALONE, which is precisely how a script reading the wrong `df` column satisfied the entire suite (D-297); the retired instrument was the weaker one. MEASURED, driving the shipped script: the 1 MiB filesystem prints `1024 KiB available` and exits 2 as a named RUN VOID, and the control on this machine's `/tmp` prints `8160516 KiB available, floor 1048576 KiB` and exits 0. WHAT WENT WITH IT, enumerated rather than left to be rediscovered: the floor's spelling guard, its 2^63-1 boundary guard and their two tests have no subject any more and are deleted — the hazard they defended against was reachable only through the binding. A test asserting the RETIRED NAME no longer moves the floor is kept in their place, because "the override is gone" is a claim about behaviour and a deleted `if` is only evidence of it. `tools/solver_link_check.sh`'s exit-1-versus-exit-2 comment cited the malformed binding as its example; the example is marked retired and the distinction it illustrates is still live, the preflight exiting 1 on its own arguments. WHAT FLIPS IT: NOTHING. The override class is banned by rule 1, so a future need for a different floor is met by changing the constant, or by a schema key if a floor ever becomes configuration rather than an instrument constant — never by an environment binding. The FLOOR ITSELF still flips whenever gate 2's footprint is re-measured (D-285), which is a measurement with a revision on it and not a tunable.

D-307: WP-1.5b's SPRT GOVERNED RUN IS **EXPENSIVE**, REVERSING THE CHEAP JUDGMENT D-245 RECORDS FOR THIS PACKAGE — THE REPLICATION CLAUSE LAPSES, THE SECOND-INSTRUMENT DUTY DOES NOT. Operator ruling. D-245 is not edited; this line is the reversal, per rule 10's append-only log. THE GROUND IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A FORECAST, which is the whole difference between this and the move D-245 warns about. D-292 records `configs/arena_wp13_r2_vs_r3.toml`'s 2000-opening shape at 5.44 core-hours and about 82 minutes wall; that anchor DOES NOT TRANSFER, because its 4.9 s per game came from a calibration probe whose games ran to at most 13 turns. MEASURED on a same-kind reconstruction of WP-1.5b's own dry-run matchup, over games of 26-40 turns: **16.3 core-seconds per game** — 3.3x the anchor — which scales to **≈18 core-hours** at the same shape, and which the second reviewer reproduced independently at 16.6. A run of that size is not one the replication clause was written for: CLAUDE.md gates it on «where the run is cheap», and answering doubt about the instrument by taking the run twice costs 36 core-hours to defend 18. D-245'S OWN WARNING IS THE THING THIS LINE HAS TO ANSWER, and it is quoted rather than skirted: «a package that judged itself EXPENSIVE in order to escape the clause would be a different instance entirely, and it is the one T4 is still waiting for». THIS IS THAT INSTANCE, AND THE ESCAPE IS REFUSED. What lapses is REPLICATION, on a measured per-game cost. What does NOT lapse is the SECOND INSTRUMENT with its registered agreement criterion and its registered consequence: D-245 registers that duty for this document BY NAME, and CLAUDE.md's clause is about a DOUBT — a stage no single instrument can see past — not about a price. The consequence stands verbatim: on disagreement the work package does not land on the SPRT alone. A reversal that shed the duty along with the clause would be the breach D-245 describes; this one keeps the duty and says which half moved. WHAT THIS LINE DOES NOT DO: it does not certify the criterion. The second review finds §7A's agreement criterion invariant under the very stage §7A names as under doubt — conditioned on `h1`, satisfied by deeper-and-weaker, and mostly ties on a small integer — and that is a defect in the criterion, repaired in the pre-registration, not licensed here. Nor does it touch the RECONCILIATION duty: D-290 as retracted-in-part by D-292 binds the run's REPORT to state measured cost beside declared, and an expensive run owes that exactly as a cheap one does. D-290'S OWN FLIP IS NOW LIVE, and it is recorded here rather than left for a later round: D-290 left T4's expensive branch «wholly unlegislated, DELIBERATELY», on the stated ground that «no expensive governed run exists in this project». That ground is false as of this line. `docs/process_readings.md`'s T-R5/T4 entry is the place that owes the update, and legislating the branch is not attempted here — a rule written in the same session that first needs it is the failure mode D-290 names. WHAT FLIPS IT: §9.3. `openings_take` is an OPERATOR-CONFIRM slot and the cost is roughly linear in it; a slot filled small enough that the run costs minutes makes it cheap again, and the replication clause re-arms with it. The 16.3 s/game figure flips on a re-measurement at the staged seat's own per-game cost, which is still unmeasured — every figure above is a radius-policy matchup standing in for it.

D-308: THE ATTRIBUTION CHAIN'S LINK 1a COUNTED ITS OWN NON-VACUITY PER RUN INSTEAD OF PER GAME, AND A SEAT SWAP CONFINED TO THE GAMES IT COULD NOT ATTRIBUTE PASSED ALL THREE LINKS — REVIEW-impl at 5ed1e84 and e9a5145, against `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md`, one BLOCKING and four MAJOR. THE DEFECT: `tools/wp15b_attribution_check.py` refused only when the discriminating count over the WHOLE RUN was zero. Link 1b does not read labels at all and link 1c DERIVES seat A's score from the very `game` line a label swap corrupts, so on a game where the two engines answer every replayed turn alike NOTHING in the chain can see the swap — and one discriminating pair carried an undiscriminating one. MEASURED on one input, the same report through both versions: the shipped aggregate guard printed `1a: 8 turns replayed, 4 of them discriminating … PASS — 0 failure(s)`, exit 0, on a report whose second pair had been inverted from `bucket p0 score_a 0.0` to `bucket p4 score_a 1.0` with `counts` and the pentanomial mirrored to match; the per-game guard prints `2 of 4 games attributed` and refuses by name, exit 1. That is the criterion's OWN named defect class, partially applied, passing — which is what CLAUDE.md means by a criterion resting on a property the defect PRESERVES. IT WAS NOT LATENT IN THEORY ONLY: the dry run's own output reads `8 of 16 turns discriminating`. On that workload every game happened to have one discriminating turn (verified: a single-game swap in the real report is refused), so the governed run was not at risk through this input — but the governed run's workload is a different book against an engine that does not yet exist, and the guard, not the luck, is what has to hold. The guard is now per game, a game with no discriminating replayed turn is a FAILURE and not a note, and the attack is kept as `a_seat_swap_confined_to_games_link_1a_cannot_attribute_is_rejected` with its honest twin — an unattributable report is refused even when nothing is wrong with it, because an instrument that certifies what it did not verify is the same defect wearing a pass. FOUR MORE FROM THE SAME ROUND. (1) The instrument exited 1 — "a link disagrees" — on pure VOID conditions: a missing report, an engine binary that was never built, a malformed field. Under the pre-registration's own registered consequence that sends a reader hunting a seat-attribution defect because a `cargo build` was skipped; every such path now exits 2 (item 12). (2) It replayed at a HARDCODED `go nodes 50000` and never read the report's own `budget` line, so a run at another budget was silently replayed at a different search, and a `movetime_ms` budget — a legal member of the closed `Budget` enum — would have made link 1a nondeterministic and produced spurious FAILs on an honest report. It now reads the budget and refuses any kind but `nodes` as a void. (3) The void distinction died at the seam in BOTH new test files: `assert_eq!(code, Some(n))` reports a void as a regression, which is D-285's own finding re-committed; both files now carry `assert_code`, and the tmpfs harness prints a SENTINEL after the mount succeeds so that "this machine cannot make a small filesystem" and "the gate did not void" are two readings and not one — `unshare` being absent is an `Err`, but user namespaces disabled by sysctl leave the binary present and return a non-zero status that would have landed on the shortage assertion. (4) Two notions of "line" over one document: Python `splitlines()` breaks on `\r`, `\x0b`, `\x0c`, U+2028 and U+0085 while every `re.M` read beside it breaks on `\n` alone, so an interior `\r` in an engine's VERBATIM refusal — free text this format copies through unquoted — injects a record (item 9); and `fields()` let a duplicated key win last where a human reads first (item 8). Both refused by name now. AND D-306 IS CORRECTED ON TWO COUNTS, since its own reservation is spent. (a) IT OVERCLAIMS: "the shortage branch … exercises the READING as well as the comparison" is FALSE for the field-selection class. MEASURED on a fresh 1 MiB tmpfs, `%a`, `%f` and `%b` are all 256 — the fields collapse and no assertion on that filesystem can separate them, and the reviewer's `%a` → `%f` mutant SURVIVES the whole suite because `/tmp` here is itself a tmpfs with no root reservation and the referent test reads the same directory. What the small filesystem genuinely catches, and what the retired override could not, is a WRONG DIRECTORY: mutation-gated, `stat … -- /tmp` in place of `-- "$DIR"` fails the void test and passes the referent test. The residual — no test in this suite separates `%a` from `%f` while the scratch directory lives on a tmpfs — is recorded here and belongs with the rest of the `tools/` sweep (D-289). (b) ITS ENUMERATION IS SHORT BY ONE: it names "the floor's spelling guard, its 2^63-1 boundary guard and their two tests"; THREE test functions were deleted, the third being `a_floor_below_the_constant_does_not_lower_it`, which pinned the MAXIMUM combine that D-285 names by name. That hazard is genuinely gone with the binding and the replacement is stronger — the environment now moves the floor not at all rather than only upward — so this is a completeness defect in the sentence that exists to prevent rediscovery, not a coverage one. WHAT THE REVIEW CLEARED, recorded so it is not redone: the override's removal is complete (nothing reads the name); the mount really is private to the namespace, verified on the host before and after; and GAME RULE 3 HOLDS AGAINST `pistol-core` for link 1b — `state.rs` sets the winner to the mover and only on the mover's own placed stone, so for `end normal` the winner played the last recorded turn without exception, and forfeits and capped games are skipped conservatively. Flips if a later round finds a game shape where the winner did not play the last recorded turn, which would retire link 1b; or if the `%a`/`%f` residual is closed by moving the scratch directory off a tmpfs, which would make the referent test discriminate the field class and is the sweep's business, not this line's.

D-309: WP-1.5b's DESIGN REACHED REVISION 7 AND FAILED ITS FRESH-CONTEXT REVIEW-design AT `6feb40a` — 7 BLOCKING, 7 MAJOR, 9 MINOR — SO THE STANDING NO-REVISION-8 RULE FIRES AND THE DOCUMENT IS RESTRUCTURED RATHER THAN REVISED AGAIN IN PLACE. Revision 7 is CLOSED. The review's own ground for restructure rather than another pass is two findings taken together, and both are reproduced here because the report file is session-scoped: B1 — the document contains exactly three tables headed `| Option |` (§4.2 M0, §5.6 M5, §6.3 M1) for six named matrices, so M2, M3 and M4 have carried no matrix since revision 2 and the sixth review round was the first asked to check them and could not; and B7 — the mechanization revision 7 rests its own stopping decision on is GREEN at that SHA while six census figures stand restated outside the block it pins, because `crates/pistol-solver/tests/wp15b_census.rs` scans only unambiguous four-decimal renderings and the document's restatements are percentages (`70.8 %`) and three-significant-figure roundings (`6.83`, `23.2`) — a criterion resting on a property the named defect class PRESERVES, which is the vacuity CLAUDE.md forbids and which this document charges against S-C and against its own §12.5. The restructure is settled by an OPTION MATRIX, landed VERBATIM AS ATTACKED at `eea480b` together with the selection record, so this log cites a retrievable text and not a chat message. WHAT FLIPS IT: NOTHING. This line records a completed review verdict, not a judgement that could be re-taken; a later round that disagrees with a finding amends that finding's own line and does not reopen revision 7, which no longer exists as a review target. **AMENDMENT: THE "SESSION-SCOPED" PREMISE ABOVE IS FALSIFIED.** The revision-7 review report is landed, verbatim and unedited, at `docs/experiments/wp15b_design_rev7_REVIEW.md` (commit `7d0418e`) — it is no longer a scratchpad file that dies with its session. The citation above is retargeted to that landed report rather than to this line's own reproduction of B1 and B7, and the finding counts this line opens with (7 BLOCKING, 7 MAJOR, 9 MINOR) are read from the landed report's own `## VERDICT` line, which confirms them unchanged.

D-310: RESTRUCTURE OPTION D IS SELECTED — WP-1.5b SHIPS STAGES F AND T ONLY, AND THE QUIET STAGE WITH ITS WIDENING SCHEDULE DEFERS TO A FOLLOW-UP WORK PACKAGE CARRYING ITS OWN DESIGN, ITS OWN MATRIX AND ITS OWN SPRT — selected by the architect after a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM against the matrix at `eea480b`, whose full findings are recorded beside it in `docs/experiments/restructure_selection_15b.md`. THE STRONGEST ATTACK SURVIVING AGAINST THE FIELD, which is what unseated the matrix's own recommendation of option A: A's central ground is that the recurring defect class — a repair landed in one section with the claim resting on it left un-re-read in another — is SIZE-DRIVEN, so the smallest cut that isolates every blocker wins. MEASURED against the document's own history and false: revisions 1–6 (`ec8f7fb` 726 lines → `2d07ff6` 1770) added 1044 lines and produced the NINE instances D-305 records, or **0.86 per 100 added lines**; revision 7 (`2d07ff6` → `d94dc0a` 1906) added 136 and produced TEN — three self-declared, seven found by the review — or **7.35 per 100 added lines**. That is 8.5x the rate at one-eighth the growth, and the variable that moved is the number of REPAIRS, not the number of lines. Option A does not reduce repairs; it multiplies the boundaries each repair must cross and relocates them BETWEEN FILES, where the two blockers of exactly this class (B4's undefined gate `(b)`, B5's four disagreeing config counts) were both found by grepping ONE file, and where the single mechanized check that could have caught one resolves a hard-coded path (`crates/pistol-solver/tests/wp15b_census.rs:638`) and would stay green over the files it no longer reads. THE SELECTION CARRIES FIVE REGISTERED CONDITIONS, each one a red-team finding that would otherwise ride free: (1) the carve produces a SECTION-OWNER TABLE in which every one of the 1975 lines has exactly one owner, §2.2, §10 and §18.3 named explicitly, because option A's four units left 923 lines — 46.7 % — owned by nobody and the travelling item that was to place B5 had no referent; (2) the matrix-restoration item is SPLIT, because `W-E` and `S-E` occur ZERO times at `ec8f7fb`: M4 alone is a mechanical recovery to be diffed against the text its red team attacked, M3's S-E is a FRESH matrix owing a fresh round, and M2's W-E defers with stage Q as recorded debt in the follow-up stub; (3) the pin is either re-targeted to the carved files with per-file paths or RETIRED with an honest note — a green pin over unread files is banned; (4) IMPL ORDER IS BINDING even though review order is free, because `pistol-solver` is absent from `[workspace.dependencies]` and from `crates/pistol-search/Cargo.toml`, so the node-protocol unit is the commit that creates the edge the gate-supersession unit's two gates fire on at exit 1; (5) the four-way cut's own flip clause was incoherent — its trigger named units 1 and 4 and its remedy deferred unit 3, retaining both — and the cut adopted here is the corrected one. THE STRONGEST ATTACK SURVIVING AGAINST D ITSELF, recorded rather than answered: the M2 matrix round and stage-Q strength are DEFERRED DEBT, NOT ESCAPED — the follow-up work package is the only place that debt can be paid — and WP-1.5b's own SPRT delta shrinks by exactly the axis D removes, which is a real cost even though the two grounds the matrix cited against D were both void (the pre-registration is a draft that governs nothing and owes a fresh-context review under every option including do-nothing, and `depth_at_500ms` is demoted to below-marker CONTEXT, ADVISORY, and absent from the ROADMAP exit criterion). WHAT FLIPS IT: the follow-up work package is never scheduled, which converts the deferral into a silent drop and makes stage Q a capability this project decided against without ever deciding it; or the F+T SPRT delta fails to clear its registered bound, which says the shipped half was not the half carrying the strength and re-opens the cut rather than the pre-registration.

D-311: A REVISION LABEL BUMPS ON ANY APPEND TO A REVIEWED DOCUMENT, HOWEVER SMALL AND HOWEVER ADDITIVE — because an unbumped append makes «a review of revision N» name two different texts, and the ambiguity is not theoretical: `d94dc0a` produced WP-1.5b design revision 7 and `6feb40a` appended 69 further lines (§18, the OPERATOR-QUEUE) under the same label, so the sixth review round had to state in its header which of the two it had read. This is the same rule CLAUDE.md already applies to reviews — «an amendment reopens the review, however small the diff» — carried back to the label the amendment is supposed to move, and it is the document-side twin of the instrument clause: an artefact whose revision does not move when its bytes do cannot be cited. It binds every document a review is dispatched against: designs, pre-registrations, option matrices and selection records. WHAT FLIPS IT: NOTHING. A label is free and the ambiguity it prevents cost one review round a header paragraph and this log a line. **AMENDMENT: A ROUND-LABEL — ONE u-rev SPANNING A MULTI-COMMIT REPAIR ROUND — IS REJECTED, AND THE PER-COMMIT BUMP STANDS UNCHANGED.** `U4_soundness_instrument.md`'s u-rev 9 OPEN bullet ("THE u-rev LABEL BUMPS PER LANDED COMMIT...") raises this as a request rather than granting itself the exemption, after `wp15b_U4_REVIEW_urev8.md` MAJOR 7 measured a round-label reading of this line against its own ground and found it made `u-rev 8` name six texts 289 lines apart — the exact ambiguity this rule exists to remove, reproduced at a larger span. A round-label is an AGGREGATE: it reports "this round did X" over several commits as if it were one claim about one text, which is the self-state-claim shape D-346 and D-338 already name and narrow — a document's claim about its own revision history is exactly what repair manufactures instances in, and an aggregate label is a wider instance of the same claim than a single-commit one. Per-commit bumping has no aggregation to go stale: each label names exactly the text one commit produced, permanently. This closes the OPEN request; it is not reopened by a future round finding a multi-commit label convenient. **SECOND AMENDMENT: THE LABEL ITSELF IS RETIRED.** Under the closure `D-351` records, U1–U4, `WPQ_seed.md` and `section_owner_table.md` stop being REVIEW-design subjects — the ambiguity this rule was written to remove, «a review of revision N naming two different texts», cannot occur once no further review is dispatched against them. **REVISION IDENTITY FOR THESE SIX DOCUMENTS IS THE COMMIT SHA, AND THE IN-DOCUMENT `u-rev N` HEAD/FOOT LABEL IS STRUCK, not merely stopped from bumping.** The label was itself an INSTANCE OF THE DEFECT CLASS this rule's own per-commit-bump amendment narrows — a SECOND, HAND-MAINTAINED COPY of a fact `git log` already carries exactly, and MEASURED to be defect-prone rather than merely redundant: `e42ca88` appended 14 lines to `U4_soundness_instrument.md` WITHOUT bumping its head label, so `u-rev 9` came to name two different texts — the exact ambiguity this rule exists to remove — produced by the very commit that amended this rule to reaffirm the per-commit bump the label had just broken. `tools/label_consistency_check.sh` drops its head/foot check accordingly and keeps its counted-forms checks (the summand line, the group-count line, and the summand-against-table-row check), which name no revision and are not this defect's class. WHAT FLIPS IT: a document among these six is reopened for REVIEW-design under D-351's own flip clause, at which point that document's revision needs a citable identity again and the commit SHA already supplies one — no label is reinstated.

D-312: D-304 IS AMENDED — THE CENSUS PIN'S REFERENT IS NO LONGER `docs/experiments/wp15b_design.md`, WHICH NO LONGER EXISTS, BUT THE SET OF CARVED DOCUMENTS, AND THE TEST THAT CARRIES THE CLAIM IS RENAMED WITH IT — amended rather than restated because rule 10 forbids silent drift and D-304's text names a file the tree no longer holds. At `cf74594` the carve (D-310, option D) DELETED `docs/experiments/wp15b_design.md`, all 1975 lines of it, retrievable at `6feb40a` and nowhere else, and replaced it with `U1_gate_supersession.md`, `U2_node_protocol.md`, `U3_tier_t.md`, `U4_soundness_instrument.md`, `WPQ_seed.md` and `section_owner_table.md`. D-304's gate `the_design_document_carries_this_censuss_table_verbatim` — one hard-coded path, one file — is renamed `the_carved_design_units_carry_this_censuss_table_verbatim` and now resolves its documents through the `CARVE_MARKER` line each carved file carries. THE RENAME IS NOT COSMETIC AND IS THE WHOLE POINT: the old gate would have gone GREEN over a file it no longer read, which is `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md`'s EXIT-0-WRONG-ANSWER wearing a Rust test's name, and it is travelling item T4' of the restructure selection record. Two further gates land with the rename so that the marker set cannot drift out from under the pin: `the_census_pin_reads_every_carved_document_it_names` fails if a named document is missing or unread, and `the_pins_document_list_is_the_set_of_carved_documents_on_disk` fails if the marker-carrying set on disk and the pin's list disagree in either direction. D-304's RESIDUAL is unchanged and is not narrowed by this amendment: the pin covers the TABLE, prose about the census stays judged, and `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` stays outside it. Flips if the carve is itself superseded, at which point the referent moves again and this line is amended rather than reinterpreted.

D-313: THE DOMINANCE-PRUNING HALF OF ROADMAP WP-1.5's SUPERSESSION SENTENCE IS DEFERRED TO WP-1.5c, NOT DROPPED, AND `docs/ROADMAP.md` SAYS SO IN ITS OWN TEXT — because `docs/ROADMAP.md` changes only by ADR and the deferral had been living in a design document's §15 as an unlanded debt (superseded §15 item 9, now carried by `docs/experiments/WPQ_seed.md`), where nothing reading the ROADMAP would ever meet it. The ROADMAP commits WP-1.5 to "threat-first staged pair generation **with dominance pruning** SUPERSEDES the radius policy": ONE SENTENCE, TWO COMMITMENTS, and only one of them has an owner. WP-1.5a is the threat generator and prunes nothing; WP-1.5b's design states, and its §14 pins, "no dominance pruning beyond the staged scheme" — the tier structure itself, which orders and batches candidates but discards no move on a dominance argument. So the pruning half was owned by no scheduled package while the ROADMAP read as though WP-1.5b discharged it, which is exactly the drift rule 10 exists to refuse. It is scheduled with WP-1.5c (D-315), the package that already owes the quiet stage and the widening schedule, because dominance pruning is a claim about which candidates may be DISCARDED and Tier Q is the tier where discarding first has anything to bite on. Flips if a measurement shows dominance pruning is soundness-relevant to stages F or T alone, in which case it returns to the threat core's critical path and is not WP-1.5c's to hold.

D-314: ROADMAP WP-1.5's SUPERSESSION IS COMPLETED BY THE OPERATOR'S SPRT, NOT BY WP-1.5b, AND THE ROADMAP RECORDS THE DISTINCTION — because "staged generation SUPERSEDES the radius policy as the PRIMARY candidate source (radius stays as a config-selectable fallback)" describes a COMMITTED-CONFIG state, and no design document can reach that state by being implemented. WP-1.5b performs the PARENTHETICAL only: it makes staged generation selectable and leaves radius as the selectable fallback, and `a_radius_policy_search_is_byte_identical_to_the_committed_engine` is the test that pins the committed engine as still the radius one at WP-1.5b's exit. What moves the committed config is the operator's SPRT clearing its registered bound, which is why D-204's flip clause is NOT fired by WP-1.5b and fires there instead. This lands as an ADR line rather than as design prose (superseded §15 item 10, now `docs/experiments/U2_node_protocol.md`'s) for the reason the ROADMAP itself gives: it changes only by ADR, and a work package that quietly reads as discharging a ROADMAP commitment it has not discharged is a stage gate scored against the wrong evidence. Flips if the ROADMAP's exit criterion for Stage 1 is ever rewritten to make selectability rather than SPRT-confirmed primacy the supersession — a rewrite that would itself need an ADR line, at which point this one is amended.

D-315: WP-1.5c IS SCHEDULED — THE QUIET STAGE, ITS WIDENING SCHEDULE AND THE DOMINANCE-PRUNING HALF, WITH `docs/experiments/WPQ_seed.md` AS ITS INPUT AND NOTHING IN THAT SEED INHERITED AS SETTLED — because D-310 cut WP-1.5b to stages F and T and its own strongest surviving attack is that the excised axis is DEFERRED DEBT, NOT ESCAPED: WP-1.5b's SPRT delta shrinks by exactly the axis removed, this package is the only place that delta can be recovered, and D-310 flips if it is never scheduled. Scheduling it here is what stops that flip clause from being an unowned sentence. The designation is not new: superseded §15 item 8 already cites "WP-1.5c" for the Tier-Q ball scan, so the choice is between binding that citation to a scheduled package and leaving it a forward reference to nothing — and D-249 records what it costs when two packages carry one designation, which is the failure this avoids rather than repeats. WHAT IT OWES IS STATED SO IT CANNOT BE READ AS PARTLY DONE: its own design, its own option matrix over the widening schedule, its own fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM before any option is selected, and its own SPRT. Matrix **M2** in particular is a FRESH matrix and not a recovery — MEASURED, restructure red team F7: `W-E`, the candidate the seed's text adopts, occurs ZERO times at `ec8f7fb`, the revision M2 would be recovered from, where the field was `W-A`..`W-D` recommending W-A; W-A then fell to a red team and W-E was supplied by that red team, never by a matrix. So the adopted-looking text in the seed has never been attacked as an option among options, and the seed says so on its own face. The seed is explicitly NOT REVIEWABLE and a reviewer asked to review it should decline. PRIORITY: after WP-1.5b, not blocking WP-1.6, because the quiet stage's candidates are ordered by an eval the quiescence WP does not change. Flips if the F+T SPRT delta clears its registered bound by a margin that makes the quiet stage's marginal contribution unmeasurable at this deployment budget, which would demote this package from SCHEDULED to LICENSED, NOT SCHEDULED — it would not cancel it, because the ROADMAP sentence D-313 defers into it would then have no owner at all.

D-316: WP-1.5b's SOUNDNESS GATE DROPS ITS LETTER SCHEME AND NAMES ITS FOUR PARTS — THE TACTICAL SUITE UNDER STAGED, THE DIFFERENTIAL GATE, THE COLONY FAMILY, THE PATTERN FIXTURES UNDER STAGED — WHICH IS B3's REPAIR, SHAPE 2 — because the letters measurably failed in the one way a name cannot. `(b)` was defined at revision 1 (`ec8f7fb:502`, "a differential gate", its instrument matrix headed `| Option | (b)'s instrument |`); revision 2 deleted that enumeration together with matrix M3; and the document then shipped FIVE further revisions with `(a)–(d) plus S-E` wired into CI, naming a component that had no definition anywhere and listing S-E TWICE — once as `(b)`, once as itself — through five REVIEW-design rounds that did not catch it. A letter can lose its referent and stay in the sentence; a name cannot. Shape 1, the rejected option, reinstated the four-part lettered bar verbatim, and its own cost cell conceded the ground the selection turns on: "a lettering scheme that has already lost its own definition once, in a document that then shipped four revisions without noticing". THE RETIRED LETTERS ARE KEPT AS A LOOKUP AND NOT ERASED: `docs/experiments/U4_soundness_instrument.md` §8.3 opens with a table mapping `(a)`/`(b)`/`(c)`/`(d)` to their gates, so an existing "§8.3(a)" in another unit, in the superseded document's history or in a landed ADR line still resolves — which discharges shape 2's one stated cost rather than paying it. MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE COMPARISON THE SELECTION RESTS ON, recorded because it errs toward the selected option: shape 2's cost cell said THREE cross-references outside §8 retarget; executing it, the count is SIX — the cell counted only the sites outside the unit and missed three inside it (U4's head B4 sentence, its U4-A lineage row, its U4-Z lead-in). The correction does not move the selection, because the cell's own closing sentence is that the count is not the argument. THE RESIDUAL IS NAMED AND IS THE ARCHITECT's: this was settled by ARCHITECT RULING on the two-shape comparison in U4-Z — which states both options, both costs MEASURED and each option's failure mode, but carries no recommendation and WAS NEVER PUT TO A FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAM. The Process section wants a named design decision with more than one viable option settled by an attacked matrix; this one was not attacked, and that is recorded here rather than left implicit, because an unattacked selection nobody writes down is exactly the silent drift the rule refuses while one that is written down is a debt the architect may pay or accept. Flips if the named-gate wiring is found to have lost a part the lettered bar carried — the four names are the script's whole enumeration, so a fifth gate arriving must be named in §8.7 and here, not appended as a letter.

D-317: MATRIX M3 — THE DIFFERENTIAL GATE'S INSTRUMENT — WAS AUTHORED, ATTACKED, AND EVERY OPTION FELL; NOTHING IS SELECTED AND NO SURVIVOR IS FORCED — because the standing rule for this work package is that a red team killing the whole field stops the matrix rather than promoting the least-wounded row, and this round killed nine options. The matrix is `docs/experiments/matrix_M3_soundness_instrument.md`, authored fresh at `f8e73e4` — it had never existed at any revision, MEASURED: `S-E`, the option the design writes as adopted, occurs ZERO times at `ec8f7fb` and was supplied by the DECISION-RED-TEAM that killed S-C. The attack is `docs/experiments/matrix_M3_REDTEAM.md`. THE DECISIVE ATTACK, which is why this is a measured stop and not a procedural one: S-E asserts EQUALITY against the union over INCLUSION-MINIMAL covers, verified by a referent "written against the plan-family definition" — and the plan-family definition D-266 makes canonical, `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md`, contains `inclusion` ZERO times while its `DEF-T` states the opposite convention, "exact MINIMUM hitting set". On a legally reachable FILTERED node the two readings give `{(-1,0),(-1,5),(4,0)}` against `{(-1,0)}`. So INDEPENDENCE AND GREENNESS ARE IN TENSION: a referent genuinely written from the canonical reference turns the gate RED on a correct engine, and a green one has consulted `cover.rs`, which is D-295's defect under a new name. The design's own mutation M4 already recorded that the two conventions differ on a reachable position; the recommendation rested on a five-word sentence instead of on that ledger row. THREE FURTHER ATTACKS STAND: the matrix killed S-F "on landed ADR lines, not on judgement" while S-E's own primary mechanism — widening `pistol_search::staged` to `pub` for a test — is what D-115 forbids by name; ground 3's "the split is FORCED by the tree" dies to a one-word edit that builds clean; and a flip clause's remedy moves the criterion to a population MEASURED firing it at 3.1 % against the corpus's 25.0 %, weakening the gate where the clause promises coverage. AND THE AUTHOR'S OWN NUMBER DID NOT REPRODUCE: fact 5 claimed "MEASURED 8 plain `assert!`" in `pvs.rs` as evidence that an always-on assertion is the house idiom; production `pvs.rs` carries exactly ONE, at line 244, the count having swept in a comment and six `#[cfg(test)]` asserts. That is the SECOND matrix in one session by one author whose MEASURED cell did not reproduce, both in cells supporting the recommendation, and D-291's clause has now recurred often enough in this work package that the pattern is the finding rather than the instance. WHAT IS BLOCKED: the DIFFERENTIAL GATE has no instrument, U4-Z item 4 stays blocked, B1 stays open, and `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` cannot be specified for that gate — the other three named gates of D-316 are unaffected. WHAT IS OWED: a SECOND AUTHORING ROUND over a field including the four rows the red team named as missing — the S-E-plus-reduced-S-C composite the design actually writes as adopted, a calculus-lower-bound containment criterion stated in `DEF-T`'s own convention, a per-node census, and reuse of the from-scratch referent that ALREADY EXISTS at `crates/pistol-solver/tests/common/reference.rs:223`, which the matrix's own `ls` printed and did not read. Two of those four are immune to the attack that killed S-E. It is the architect's round to schedule and explicitly not this session's to author: a revision 2 written by the session that wrote revision 1, over options the red team supplied, is the pattern D-305 measures and this matrix existed to stop. Flips when that second round selects an option, at which point this line is superseded rather than amended.

D-318: MATRIX M4 — THE SNAPSHOT'S CONFIG SEAM — IS STOPPED AFTER TWO AUTHORED REVISIONS AND TWO FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAMS, WITH NOTHING SELECTED, AND THE STOP IS NOT THE "EVERY OPTION FELL" ONE — options survived round 2 (N-J outright; N-E, N-K, N-L, N-F wounded), and it stops anyway for three reasons each of which is sufficient. FIRST, REVISION 2's OWN REASON FOR EXISTING IS FALSE. It declined to select from revision 1's field because that field omitted "the seam this project's own D-252 option matrix SELECTED after its own red team, and which D-283 landed". Neither conjunct is true: D-252's option (c) is "leave the literal, register the exposure, and schedule the binding" — the shape this matrix calls N-L — and **D-288 exists in this tree for the sole purpose of relabelling it "DEFERRED — the exposure registered, the binding scheduled, and NO OPTION SELECTED"**, stating the harm in words that describe revision 2 exactly: a successor reading (c) as adopted "would have found the decision already taken, the matrix already spent, and no red-team owed, on a choice that had never been attacked". D-283 further states in its own text that its sub-choices have not been attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM. Both were one `grep` away and neither was run; the fact cell carrying the claim invoked a command that reads D-283 and cannot see D-252 or D-288. SECOND, EVERY PRECEDENT GROUND IS THEREFORE VOID AND NO SURVIVING GROUND DISCRIMINATES. This tree holds no attacked selection for how an instrument binds a per-run input — D-252 selected nothing (D-288), D-283's review is outstanding by its own admission, and D-316's recorded residual says the same of B3's two-shape comparison. Grounds 1, 3 and 4 of the recommendation fall with the precedents they read; ground 2 survives, and ground 2 — refuse the silently-wrong-config record — argues equally for N-E, N-J, N-K, N-L and N-F, none of which carries a default. Selecting one of five on a ground that separates none of them is forcing a survivor under another name. THIRD, THE FIELD IS STILL INCOMPLETE AT THE SECOND REVISION, and the missing row dominates the recommended option on the matrix's own trigger: hard rule 1's mechanism, which ground 1 invokes, is a CLOSED ENUM, and a required `--config {instrument|staged}` selector over the committed set satisfies grounds 1 and 2 identically to N-E while owing far fewer guards, because caller-relative resolution and the three path refusals exist only because a caller may name an ARBITRARY path. The framing "any option that lets a caller name the path" excluded it by presupposition for two revisions running, as it excluded a sixth row, binding the config through the already-caller-named corpus fixture. AND THE AUTHOR'S OWN MEASUREMENT RECORD IS PART OF THIS LINE, because it is a pattern and not an incident: three cells this session that the author marked MEASURED did not reproduce — M4 fact 6b ("one invocation site"; there are three), M3 fact 5 ("8 plain `assert!` in `pvs.rs`"; there is one, at line 244), and M4 revision 2's replacement fact 6d, whose five-site enumeration contains a non-site since patching `go()` and test 1205 alone leaves the suite 29/29 green — every one of them in a cell supporting the author's own recommendation, and the second arriving in the revision written to repair the first. D-291's clause has now recurred so often in this work package that the recurrence, not the instance, is the finding. WHAT IS BLOCKED: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` has no config seam, so no Staged snapshot can be taken and the registered above-marker quantity has a BEFORE and no AFTER; U4-Z item 15 stays blocked and B2 stays open. WHAT IS OWED: a THIRD round, the architect's and explicitly not this session's, since a third field authored by the session that wrote the first two — now populated with rows both red teams supplied — completes D-305's measured pattern instead of breaking it. It must carry the two missing rows, drop the framing that excluded them, mark every number including the zeros, and rest on no precedent that has not itself been attacked. Flips when that round selects an option, at which point this line is superseded rather than amended.

D-319: **TIER Q STAYS IN U2's NODE PROTOCOL, SPECIFIED BUT UNARMED — THE D-SCOPE THAT SHIPS IS STAGES F AND T, AND PROTOCOL SCOPE IS NOT SHIPPING SCOPE.** Architect ruling, landed as text at `56b0bec` (one sentence in `docs/experiments/U2_node_protocol.md` at the Tier Q definition, one in `docs/experiments/WPQ_seed.md` where stage Q is picked up, both units bumped to u-rev 2 under D-311). The distinction the ruling turns on is the one D-310 left implicit and three reviewers then had to re-derive: **a protocol may SPECIFY a tier the shipped configuration never fills.** U2's node protocol routes BATCHED rows to "Tier T ∪ Tier Q" and defines Tier Q; D-310 cut the WORK PACKAGE to stages F and T; `docs/experiments/wp15b_sprt_prereg.md` registers F+T only. All three are simultaneously true and none of them is in tension, because what D-310 deferred is the WIDENING SCHEDULE and the strength claim that rides on it (D-315, WP-1.5c), not the protocol's account of what a tier is. **CONSEQUENCE FOR REVIEWERS, stated because it was costing rounds: the presence of Tier Q text in U2 §5 is NOT a scope finding**, and a review that reports it as one is reporting the ruling rather than a defect. What WOULD be a finding is Tier Q text that ARMS it — a config document committing a non-empty `quiet_top_k` for a shipped seat, a gate whose criterion needs Tier Q candidates, or a registered quantity that only a widened set can produce. Flips if the F+T pre-registration is amended to register a stage-Q quantity, at which point the tier is armed and this line is superseded rather than reinterpreted; it does NOT flip on U3-Z's open question of whether the shipped config surface keeps `quiet_top_k` and `widen_schedule` as keys, which is a `deny_unknown_fields` completeness question and is the architect's separately.

D-320: **B3's REPAIR — THE SOUNDNESS GATE'S FOUR NAMED PARTS, SHAPE 2 — WAS ADOPTED BY ARCHITECT RULING WITHOUT AN OPTION MATRIX, AND THAT IS A BREACH OF THE MATRIX LAW, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT.** D-316 named this residual in its own text: the two-shape comparison in U4-Z "states both options, both costs MEASURED and each option's failure mode, but carries no recommendation and WAS NEVER PUT TO A FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAM", and the Process section wants a named design decision with more than one viable option settled by an ATTACKED matrix. **The breach is acknowledged, not argued away.** THE RETRO-MATRIX IS WAIVED, on two grounds stated together because neither carries it alone. First, PROPORTIONALITY: the decision is a naming scheme for four gates that already exist as gates — shape 1 reinstates a lettered bar, shape 2 names the four parts — and the whole of what a matrix would add is a red team's attack on a comparison whose two cost cells were already MEASURED and whose losing option's own cell conceded the ground the selection turned on ("a lettering scheme that has already lost its own definition once, in a document that then shipped four revisions without noticing"). Second, INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ALREADY HAPPENED, and it is the part that makes this a waiver rather than an excuse: the fresh-context REVIEW-design at `docs/experiments/wp15b_U4_REVIEW.md` verified the six-site retarget the correction predicted, independently and against the tree, and its scope-1 verdict on the named-gate wiring is PASS. So the thing a retro-matrix would most plausibly have caught — a gate silently lost between the lettered bar and the named one — was checked by a session that did not make the choice. WHAT THIS LINE DOES NOT DO: it does not license adoption-without-matrix as a practice, and it does not convert D-316's residual into a clean record. It converts an unattacked selection that nobody wrote down into a debt the architect has now paid in the only currency available after the fact, which is disclosure. Flips if a GATE-NAMING DEFECT surfaces — a part of the soundness gate that the four names do not reach, a citation that resolves under the retired letters and not under the names, or a fifth gate appended as a letter — at which point the waiver was wrong, the matrix is owed retroactively, and this line is superseded by the round that runs it.

D-321: **ERRATA — `DEF-T` AND `cover.rs` STATE DIFFERENT CONVENTIONS, THE CALCULUS IS NOT AMENDED, AND WHICH CONVENTION A SOUNDNESS CRITERION MUST ASSERT IS RECORDED AS OPEN THEORY.** Architect ruling R8, recorded against the criterion S-E needs. THE FACTS, MEASURED at `d48824f` with the commands in `docs/experiments/matrix_M3_soundness_instrument_rev2.md` facts 4 and 7: `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md` — the canonical threat reference under D-266 — contains `inclusion` **ZERO** times, and its `DEF-T` defines the threat NUMBER `t(F)` as the "exact **minimum hitting set** over plan family F (plans have size ≤2 ⇒ vertex-cover instance)"; `crates/pistol-solver/src/cover.rs` enumerates the **INCLUSION-MINIMAL** covers; and U4 §8.4's mutation M4 is literally "minimum-cardinality covers instead of inclusion-minimal", so the project's own mutation ledger already treats the choice as a live axis. **THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME QUESTION AND THAT IS THE ERRATUM'S CONTENT:** `DEF-T` fixes a CARDINALITY, the quantity tempo arithmetic consumes; `LAW-HIT` fixes the hitting-set frame; `LAW-FORCE` fixes that every non-losing move hits all opponent plans. **None of the three states which covers a sound candidate generator must carry**, and that — not a contradiction inside the calculus — is what is open. THE QUESTION HAS A MEASURED SIZE rather than a rhetorical one: over the seeded playout regime `threat_oracle_tests` already uses, the two conventions give different unions on **84 of 300** legally reachable FILTERED side-positions — **28.0 %** — carrying 2.587 cells per node against `DEF-T`'s 2.027. It is live, not vestigial. WHAT THIS LINE DOES: it marks the question OPEN, it binds any option whose criterion depends on inclusion-minimality to carry the mark **DEPENDS-OPEN-THEORY** and to be unable to beat an immune option ON THAT GROUND, and it records that `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md` is **NOT amended** — the calculus changes by its own amendment rule and not by a matrix's convenience. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not find a defect in `cover.rs`, whose enumeration is correct for what it enumerates and is checked against an independent referent at `crates/pistol-solver/tests/common/reference.rs` with 0 disagreements over 3406 side-positions; and it does not settle the question, which is theory work owing its own evidence. Flips when the convention is settled in either direction — by an amendment to the calculus under D-266, or by an ADR line adopting `cover.rs`'s convention as the project's — at which point every DEPENDS-OPEN-THEORY mark this line licenses is lifted and the matrices that carry them are re-read.

D-322: **D-321's MEASURED SIZE FOR THE OPEN CONVENTION QUESTION IS CORRECTED — IT IS 22 OF 174 FILTERED NODES, 12.6 %, NOT 84 OF 300 AND 28.0 % — BECAUSE THE POPULATION THE FIGURE WAS TAKEN OVER IS NOT THE ROW THE PROTOCOL SPECIFIES.** Found by the fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM of MATRIX M3 revision 2 (`docs/experiments/matrix_M3_REDTEAM_round2.md`, F3) and INDEPENDENTLY RE-RUN by the session that wrote the number before this correction was written. THE DEFECT: `docs/experiments/U2_node_protocol.md` §5.3 evaluates the FILTERED row ONCE PER NODE, for `us` — the side to move — at the phase-derived `StonesLeft::from_state(state)` and `HitBudget::from(left)`.
