The fix was LINE EQUALITY, which is strictly tighter and refuses a Rust source line because that line is indented and quoted. **ROUND 2, LANDED AT `1f1f6ad` AND RED IMMEDIATELY:** `matrix_META1_REDTEAM.md` K5 attacks the claim that condition 1's deletion-only strip is executable on line 3 of the six subject documents, and to show what is on line 3 it pastes the OUTPUT of `sed -n '3p'` into a fenced block. **COMMAND OUTPUT OF A BARE LINE IS THAT BARE LINE.** It is line-equal, at line 304, in a fence, in a document that is manifestly not a carve member — and the pin declared it one. **THE DIAGNOSIS IS NOT THAT THE SECOND REPORT WAS UNLUCKY.** Round 1's fix was scoped to the shape that instance happened to take, a quoted Rust string, rather than to the property that distinguishes a member; and a rule that refuses the last instance is a rule fitted to a sample of one. This is the instrument-narrowed-until-it-fits failure D-335 records under a different name, arriving from the other direction — narrowed enough to pass, not narrowed enough to be right. **THE PROPERTY IS POSITION, AND IT ALWAYS WAS.** The marker is a HEAD comment; a machine consumer reads it to ask whether a file is a carve member, and a file answers that at its top or not at all, while a quotation appears wherever the argument needed it, which is in the body. Membership is now **the marker on its own line within the first five lines**, and the allowance is MEASURED rather than guessed: every one of the six members carries it on line 3, and the nearest quotation of it in any other document is at line 304 — two lines of slack over every real member against two hundred and ninety-nine lines of clearance to the nearest counter-example. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM.** It does not make quoting safe in general: a document that put the marker alone on one of its own first five lines would be a member by this rule, and that is a shape no report has ever had and one the pin would rather be red about than silently admit. And it is a positional rule, so a member that gains a line above its marker goes red — which is the pin saying the head convention moved, and is a finding rather than a false alarm. **THE GUARD TEST NOW CARRIES BOTH INSTANCES**, the quoted Rust source line and the pasted `sed` output, each asserted to be line-equal FIRST so the test cannot pass for the wrong reason, plus both sides of the head allowance. Flips if a third shape defeats the position rule, at which point the marker is the wrong instrument for membership and the carve should be answered from a manifest the documents do not carry.

D-344: **THE REVIEW-impl ON GATE 15 RETURNED FAIL WITH A BLOCKING THAT IS THE `tools/` CLASS ITSELF — THE GATE PRINTED `OK` AND EXITED 0 ON THE DEFECT IT EXISTS FOR — AND THE SECOND SPELLING OF THE FAULTY READ WAS WORSE THAN THE FIRST.** Fresh-context REVIEW-impl against `908a2f7`, cited against `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` by item: **1 BLOCKING / 3 MAJOR / 1 MINOR**. All three substantive findings were reproduced on scratch copies before any fix landed; nothing was fixed on a reviewer's say-so. **BLOCKING-1, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE CHECKLIST.** The gate located a document's foot at the LAST line starting with an asterisk and a capital and accumulated from there, never resetting its in-block flag. So a document whose true closing paragraph is STALE, followed by a trailing italic aside naming the HEAD's u-rev, reported `head=u-rev 7 foot=u-rev 7 OK` and **exited 0** — the exact defect the gate was built to catch, passing, in the one code path whose whole job is to prevent an exit-0-wrong-answer. Reproduced on a scratch copy of U3. **THE SHAPE OF THE MISTAKE IS THE FINDING, NOT THE INSTANCE.** Spelling 1 read a three-line tail and missed U4 (D-342). Spelling 2 fixed U4 and opened this. Both were scoped to the counter-example in front of the author rather than to the property — which is D-343's diagnosis of the carve-membership rule, in a different file, in the same session, on the same day: **a rule that refuses the last instance is a rule fitted to a sample of one.** The unit is now neither a tail nor a paragraph but the **CLOSING REGION** — everything below the document's last `---` rule, which must name exactly one u-rev, MEASURED as true of all six subjects — and the whole extraction was rewritten to buffer and adjudicate at end-of-input, which removes the carried-state class rather than patching this instance of it. **MAJOR-2 IS A CLAUDE.md VACUITY FINDING AGAINST A GATE WRITTEN TO ANSWER ONE.** The summand check compared a line's arithmetic to its own heading — and a table row that loses an item leaves BOTH untouched, so the criterion rested on a property the named defect PRESERVES. Reproduced by dropping one item from U2's row in the owner table's §7: silent before, named now. Summands are checked against the data rows above them, five live subjects, and **it is the only check that reaches §7 at all**, whose owners' items live in table cells rather than in a backtick group. That the gate's author wrote a non-vacuity floor into the same script while shipping a vacuous criterion inside it is recorded, not excused. **MAJOR-3:** the extraction's own character class admits a space in a group label and the shell read the record positionally, so a CORRECT two-word group was refused with a garbled message; the label is now the record's last field. It fails loud in both directions, which is why it is MAJOR and not BLOCKING. **MAJOR-4:** neither the script's self-test nor the driving suite covered either broken shape — the self-test asserted on the awk output only and never drove the shell's own parsing, and every fixture's closing block was the last thing in its document. That is `SHELL_CHECKLIST` item 10's real content: a driving test with a control existed and PASSED while two shapes were broken, so the coverage rule is about the fixture space and not about the existence of a suite. Both suites now carry both shapes; the driving suite runs eighteen tests. **MINOR-5** (an empty tracked file reporting `line 0`) is accepted with NO CHANGE, as the reviewer proposed: it is cosmetic and yields no wrong verdict. **TWO FINDINGS WERE ATTEMPTED AND REJECTED BY THE REVIEWER WITH THEIR REPRODUCERS** — an unchecked process-substitution exit status, for which no failing case could be constructed, and a locale-dependent `[^[:space:]]` class, measured identical under `C` and `en_US.UTF-8` on the installed awk. **THE REVIEWER'S SUBJECT REVISION DID NOT MATCH HEAD** — `a3bdb12` and `00050fa` landed while it ran — and it verified that neither touched a file under review before reporting, which is the convention working. Flips if a further shape defeats the closing-region rule, at which point the rule is fitted to a sample again and membership of "the foot" wants a marker the documents carry rather than a position they happen to have.

D-345: **MATRIX META-2 IS CLOSED AFTER ONE AUTHORED REVISION AND ONE FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAM, AND `NULL` IS SELECTED FROM THE SURVIVORS. THE RECOMMENDED ROW FALLS; THE ROW THAT COULD HAVE CARRIED THE FIELD WAS NEVER IN IT.** The field is `{B, C, C-prime-mark, NULL}` (`docs/experiments/matrix_META2.md`, landed `908a2f7`), attacked by `docs/experiments/matrix_META2_REDTEAM.md` (landed `e47f34e`, subject `908a2f7`) at **4 KILL, 12 MAJOR, 4 MINOR**, whose own verdict is *"NO SELECTION MAY BE TAKEN FROM THIS FIELD."* **THE SURVIVOR STATE, PER THAT REPORT'S PER-OPTION TABLE, AND WHY EVERY OTHER ROW IS UNSELECTABLE.** **B INVENTORY is unselectable as registered**, not killed: its stabilization criterion — *"repair until inventories stabilize across two consecutive rounds"* — has no comparison to make (M6). The entire landed population is two inventories, their row namespaces are **`Z1–Z54` against `Y1–Y61`**, disjoint by construction, different scopes, different authors, and the second states it did not reuse the first; two hand-built tables are not a before and an after. **C RE-SCOPE survives wounded and unchanged**, carried verbatim from the prior round, and its wound is the rot: waived-false is indistinguishable from true in the document of record, whose measured instance is the U1 falsehood that rode five documents and nine rounds. **C-prime-mark FALLS** on K1–K4, M1, M7 and M8, and the attack that finishes it is the **MARKER-AS-TEXT REGRESS (M7)**: a marker is either part of the marked text or it is not, and **both arms fail** — if it is marked text then a marker naming the wrong home is frozen unrepairable by rule, and this corpus already holds that instance (`wp15b_U4_REVIEW_urev8.md` MINOR 7, a finding whose entire content is that an existing marker is misplaced); if it is not marked text then it is unmarked text, which condition 3 says reviews score, contradicting *"a marker is not a finding"* directly. Condition 4's marker inventory does not close it — counting markers is invariant under a missed or mis-homed marker (K2) — and measured, an add-only marker on the surface that produced three of this class's instances turns CI gate 15 red (K3). **`NULL` IS CONFIRMED AND ITS RECORDED WOUND IS OVERSTATED**, in the attacker's own words: its failure-mode cell says *"generators 2 and 3 unreached by any clause"*, and **D-342 is a landed instance of both being reached, recorded and answered, and gate 15 is a landed mechanism against generator (2)**. **THE MECHANISM OBSERVATION, QUOTED, BECAUSE IT IS THE GROUND OF THIS SELECTION:** *"Since the META-1 stop the project has run this row and it produced the field's only mechanism — and the discovery of that mechanism's own defect (D-344)."* **THE GROUNDS, STATED AS A PATTERN AND NOT AS A PREFERENCE.** Every authored abstraction in this track died on contact — A, D, the whole strip family, E-anything, B's criterion, C-prime-mark — and the two things that worked were incremental mechanisms nobody proposed as a law: gate 15, and the strike edits already executed in-tree. The field has now consumed two matrices and two full red teams and produced one gate; a third authored field is the same bet a third time. **THE STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK AGAINST `NULL`, QUOTED AND NOT PARAPHRASED (CLAUDE.md's matrix rule):** **the burn direction, V6.** *"Finding counts turned upward at the last round"*, and V6 is direction-only per D-341 — no death sentence rests on it — but it is real, it is unanswered by this selection, and it says the status quo trends worse rather than better. What blunts it and does not remove it: M11 measures V6's transcribed *"zero PASS at close"* FALSE — three landed PASSes, and U1's last landed review is one of them. **WHAT THIS SELECTION DOES NOT DO.** It adopts no marking convention, licenses no strip, and creates no review scope. Rows **R2, R3 and R5** stand owed exactly as `D-338` records them, and **R3 — the derived-enumeration row, the only candidate two independent rounds have MEASURED to be a mechanism rather than an assertion — is now missing from three consecutive fields** (M12); it is the architect's, and this line does not carry it. **THE DEVIATION THAT IMPORTED THE REGRESS, RECORDED FACTUALLY:** the C-prime this matrix authored is **not** the C-prime `D-338` defines — `D-338` says *"answer every meta finding by striking the sentence through … reviews stay at full scope"*, and the matrix substituted **mark** for **strike** and **unmarked text only** for **full scope** while keeping V4's precedent, which prices the strike; that deviation is the defect that imported the marker-as-text regress, and `D-338`'s C-prime is untouched by anything in the red team's four KILLs. Flips if a repair round run under `NULL` and the strike policy of D-346 nonetheless turns finding counts upward again across all four units, at which point V6 is no longer direction-only and the burn is the finding. **AMENDMENT: THE META TRACK IS CLOSED WITH THIS SELECTION. NO MATRIX META-2 REVISION 3 IS OWED.** Disposition of the three rows this line left owed. **R4** (the self-state gate) is **NOT** one of them — it embodies as **gate 15** (`tools/label_consistency_check.sh`), already landed before this selection, per `D-338`'s own text and the gate's own header comment; an earlier draft of this closure misattributed gate 15 to R3 and that attribution is corrected here rather than repeated. **R5** (retire-don't-edit for `WPQ_seed.md`) embodies in **`D-346`**: strike-and-dispose is retire-don't-edit generalised past one document to the class D-346 names. **R2** (review-contract-only, findings batched, nothing authored in-round) **DIES WITH THE TRACK, AS AN UNSELECTED ROW** — no mechanism embodies it, and it is not resurrected; its text survives where it always lived, in `D-338` and in the landed red-team reports that scored it. Its vindicated half is recorded rather than reargued: the authoring-during-repair gap R2 was written against resurfaced at `U4_soundness_instrument.md`'s u-rev 9 round — eleven self-state claims added during repair rounds rather than reworded, answered under `D-346`'s strike policy — and that instance is R2's ground made concrete, cited here and not restated. **R3** (derived-enumeration on the `7dfd047` precedent) has **NO DISPOSITION** and **REMAINS OWED**: neither this selection nor any line since D-338 assigns it one, and `matrix_META2_REDTEAM.md` M12 already named it "the serious omission" — the only candidate two independent rounds measured to be a mechanism rather than an assertion, missing from three consecutive fields and now missing a fourth. It is the architect's, as D-338 and this line both say, and closing the track does not close it.

D-346: **STRIKE-AND-DISPOSE IS THE REPAIR POLICY FOR DOCUMENT-STATE CLAIMS, AND IT IS `D-338`'s C-prime RESTORED TO ITS LANDED DEFINITION RATHER THAN A NEW ROW.** **THE POLICY.** A claim a document makes about **its own state** — its u-rev history, which of its own revisions were reviewed and with what verdict, what its own repairs reached, universals about its own text — that is found **false or unverifiable** is **STRUCK: deleted, and replaced with nothing.** If and only if its removal strands navigation, a **POINTER to the external home** replaces it — *a pointer and never a claim*. The homes are the ones D-331 already names: `docs/decisions.md` for rulings, `docs/experiments/wp15b_*_REVIEW*.md` for findings and verdicts, git for what a revision contained. **WHY DELETION AND NOT REWORDING.** The measured generator across this whole work package is that **repair manufactures instances**: U3 failed four consecutive rounds and every one of the four MAJORs was manufactured by the previous round's repair; U4's u-rev 8 re-authored a misattribution at a second site in the commit after repairing it. A rewritten status claim is a new claim that can go false; a deleted one cannot, and a pointer goes stale only when its target moves, which is a smaller surface than the sentence it replaces. **ATTACK PROVENANCE, WHICH IS WHAT DISTINGUISHES THIS FROM AN UNATTACKED ADOPTION.** The row was in the META-2 field under its own name and the fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM evaluated it: `matrix_META2_REDTEAM.md`'s per-option table records **`D-338`'s C-prime — strike, dispose, replace with nothing, reviews at full scope — as UNTOUCHED AND STILL OWED**, with *"None of K1–K4 reaches it; they all reach the substitutions"*. Four KILLs were thrown at the marking variant and none landed on the strike. **INSTANCE BASE, MEASURED AND THRICE-EXECUTED IN-TREE:** `U4_soundness_instrument.md:230`, `:234` and `:245`, three universals about the document's own state struck through in the REVIEW STATUS tables, each disposed and none reworded; `wp15b_U4_REVIEW_urev8.md` MAJOR 5 prescribes the same edit independently, in a reviewer's own words — *"Strike it as the three siblings were struck, with the disposition stated … and replace it with nothing."* **REVIEWS STAY AT FULL SCOPE.** Nothing here narrows what a reviewer scores. The absence of struck text is not a finding and a pointer is not a finding, because there is no claim there to be false; **surviving text is scored exactly as before**, and a normative claim that lost its home to a strike is a finding against the strike. **WHAT IS NOT STRIKE-SHAPED.** A **NORMATIVE** claim — a design decision, a binding rule, a measurement IMPL depends on, a statement of what is owed — is repaired minimally at its home and never struck; where a strike would remove one, the strike is wrong. Flips, and this is the clause that matters: **a strike that removes a NORMATIVE claim is a defect — restore it and report the instance**, and two such instances make deletion the wrong instrument for the boundary this policy draws.

D-347: **THE INVENTORY-DIFF INSTRUMENT IS LICENSED AND NOT SCHEDULED, AND IT OWES ITS BLIND-SAMPLER PRECONDITION BEFORE ANY RUN.** `matrix_META2_REDTEAM.md` evaluates it as attack-surface item 7 and returns *"a REAL MISSING ROW, distinct from B, not dominated by B, and it must be carried by a revision 3"*: this round's claim inventory is **derived from the prior round's landed one** and the review is scored on what the **diff** shows — rows added, removed, verdicts flipped — which is an instrument change and not a cadence change. **WHY IT IS LICENSED.** A diff **requires** stable row identity, so `Z1–Z54` against `Y1–Y61` becomes impossible and M6's objection against B dissolves by construction; every count becomes **derived from the diff** rather than stated by an author, which is D-336 clause (4) mechanised and is the only direct answer in the record to **V2**, the false-self-count class that neither B nor C-prime nor `NULL` touches; and *"the inventory stabilised"* becomes *"the diff is empty"*, a fact rather than a judgment. **WHY IT IS NOT SCHEDULED.** No IMPL work waits on it, this session's cap forbids opening a fifth front, and its empirical base is **two inventories, both against U4-Z, one 519-line section of one of six documents** — the report states the thinness itself and a presentation that hides it repeats the over-specification the prior round scored. **THE PRECONDITION IT OWES, REGISTERED BEFORE EITHER PARTY RUNS AND QUOTED FROM THE REPORT THAT DERIVED IT**, because seeding a fresh reviewer with the prior inventory destroys independence at the extraction stage and a claim neither party extracted is **invisible to the diff**, which is CLAUDE.md's own two-instruments-blind-to-the-same-stage rule: *"each round, a party who has seen NEITHER inventory extracts claims from a fixed random sample of the section under review; any claim it finds that appears in neither the prior nor the current inventory means the extraction is incomplete and the round's diff is not a score; two consecutive rounds in which the blind sampler finds such a claim means seeding is the defect and the row is withdrawn rather than re-run."* **A RUN THAT TAKES THE DIFF AS A SCORE WITHOUT THE SAMPLER HAVING RUN IS NOT THIS INSTRUMENT**, and its numbers are not this row's. Flips if the sampler is registered and run and its own cost turns out to exceed the review it prices, at which point the row is a second full review wearing a diff's clothes and B's objection returns against it.

D-348: **THE AUTHOR PRE-FLIGHT D-339 RECORDS AS THE CORRECTIVE PRACTICE FAILED ON THE ARCHITECT'S OWN META-2, IN TWO OF ITS THREE CLAUSES, AND THE INSTANCES ARE RECORDED HERE WITHOUT A NEW RULE ATTACHING.** D-339's practice is (a) every cited source resolved to a file **at a SHA**, by running the command; (b) every clause the document binds by name checked **not already fired** against the document's own content; (c) every numeric cell marked **MEASURED** or **ESTIMATED**. `matrix_META2.md`'s header **declares all three performed**. **INSTANCE 1 — (a), THE SHA WAS NEVER FILLED.** The evidence header reads *"`docs/experiments/matrix_META1_REDTEAM.md` at `<SHA>`"* and the only SHA-shaped token in the document is that placeholder, **at the landing revision `908a2f7` and at HEAD** (`matrix_META2_REDTEAM.md` M3). The declaration says *"SHAs filled by operator at commit"*; the commit came and they were not. **INSTANCE 2 — V3 WAS STALE AT ITS OWN LANDING SHA.** V3 states *"two head/foot label instances"*; the third instance landed at `bb64501`, an **ancestor of the matrix's own commit**, and the report the cell cites already said three in its own body (M2). The size was load-bearing — D-338 ranked R4 against D's citation gate at three-against-zero, not two-against-zero — and D-342 had already corrected the digit in the log before the matrix landed carrying it. **WHY THESE TWO AND NOT THE OTHERS.** M4 (flip clause 2 quantifies over *"marked text"*, which has no definition at authoring) and M5 (two unmarked numeric thresholds) are the (b) and (c) clauses failing on the same document and are recorded by the red-team report at its own citations; they are not re-litigated here. **THE CLASS COUNT STAYS HONEST AND THAT IS THIS LINE'S WHOLE PURPOSE.** D-339's diagnosis is that *"a rule authored and first exercised in the same commit is not tested by that commit, and the author is the party least able to test it"*, and it names three consecutive architect lines that flipped on the round that landed them. **META-2 IS THE FOURTH, AND IT IS THE FIRST WHERE THE FAILING PARTY IS THE ARCHITECT WRITING A MATRIX RATHER THAN A SESSION WRITING AN ADR.** **NO NEW RULE ATTACHES, DELIBERATELY.** D-339 already says the pre-flight *"IS NOT A GATE AND THIS LINE DOES NOT PROPOSE ONE"*; (b) and (c) are judgements about what a sentence means, and this project has landed instances of a criterion narrowed until it was blind to the case it was written for. Adding a rule to a practice that failed for want of being *run* would be that mistake in its purest form. Flips if a fifth instance lands and the failing clause is (a) — the mechanizable one — at which point the pre-flight's citation half is a gate the project declined to build and the declining is the finding.

D-349: **D-346's FLIP CLAUSE FIRED, ON ITS FIRST EXECUTION, ON U2.** D-346's clause: *"a strike that removes a NORMATIVE claim is a defect — restore it and report the instance."* **THE INSTANCE:** `U2_node_protocol.md`'s u-rev 7 (`ecb0341`) struck the unmarked "168 030 comparisons" figure as a document-state claim under D-346, on the strength of `wp15b_U2_REVIEW_urev4.md` G2 having flagged it as unreconciled. `wp15b_U2_REVIEW_urev7.md` Finding 1 (BLOCKING) found the strike out of D-346's own scope: the figure backs the non-vacuity-per-budget half of the M5-E `Impossible`-branch equivalence — *"a measurement IMPL depends on"* is named verbatim in D-346 among what must be repaired minimally and never struck — and the strike's replacement prose kept asserting that property while re-pointing its support to §5.2, which does not state it. **DISPOSITION: RESTORED VERBATIM FROM THE PRE-STRIKE SHA `3543a7f`, IN-TREE.** The handoff bullet (`U2_node_protocol.md`, "The node protocol's shape is settled and attacked") and the OPEN-list bullet it was disposed alongside are both reverted to state the figure, unmarked and unreconciled against §5.2's 343 344, exactly as they stood before u-rev 7's strike — D-346 restores the claim, it does not resolve the unreconciled-figure problem the claim always carried, and that problem stays OPEN under its original ground (G2, kept whole at u-rev 5/6). **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** D-346's policy is not narrowed by this instance: the two other strikes this round's own instance base names (`U4_soundness_instrument.md:230`, `:234`, `:245`) are unaffected, remaining genuine document-state claims about the document's own u-rev/review history — this instance turned on the struck sentence being a solver-level measurement claim, not on strike-and-dispose being wrong in general. Flips if a second NORMATIVE-claim strike is found under D-346 dispatched after this instance, at which point D-346's own boundary — not just its execution — is what needs re-drawing.

D-350: **`wp15b_full_prompt.md` NEVER LANDED — AND ITS ABSENCE KILLED THE PREMISE UNDER WHICH A PRIOR DISPATCH TRIED TO FIRE WP-1.5b IMPL AS A CHEAP "PATCH" OVER IT.** MEASURED: `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` over the whole repo carries no path matching `full_prompt`, and `git log --all --full-history -- '*full_prompt*'` is empty — the file is absent from the tree and from every commit on every branch, not merely from HEAD. It is the same class D-339 records for its two never-recovered files: a name cited as though it were a landed artifact — the roadmap era and this WP's own current-state framing both refer to "the full prompt" as the thing IMPL would run under — that the tree never actually held. **WHY THIS CHANGES THE CALL RATHER THAN JUST NAMING A GAP.** The dispatch this session refused (see this session's own turn immediately prior, which stopped on an unrecorded operator decision and a missing patch target) framed proceeding to IMPL as low-cost specifically because Step 1 was "patch `wp15b_full_prompt.md`" — a small diff against an existing, already-reviewed governing document, carrying its own auto-finish policy forward. That artifact does not exist to patch, so nothing carries an auto-finish policy forward: the document IMPL would actually read has to be **authored fresh**, from whichever of U1–U4 are PASS, which is authoring-shaped work at exactly the site — the one document IMPL reads — where importing residue from a unit that still carries a BLOCKING or MAJOR finding does the most damage. That is what turns the choice from a close call between two cheap options into a call for the repair-first path: there is no cheap option left, so the option that gates authoring behind PASS units wins outright. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** It does not reopen or re-litigate D-310, D-329, D-323 or D-316 — those selections stand and are exactly what the fresh `wp15b_impl_prompt.md` will be authored from. **SUPERSEDED PROSPECTIVELY** by `wp15b_impl_prompt.md`, a new, small artifact to be authored from the passed units once this repair round reaches four PASS, reviewed prereg-style (the pattern `wp15b_sprt_prereg_REVIEW_rev5.md` shows working: small, verified against primary sources, PASS on its first fresh-context review) — that authoring is **NOT this session's work**. Flips if a file matching `wp15b_full_prompt.md` is ever found to have existed under a different name at some SHA not reached by `--all`, at which point this line's premise, not just its conclusion, needs re-checking.

D-351: **THE JOINT CALL — THE OPERATOR AND THE ARCHITECT DISPATCH THIS CLOSURE TOGETHER: WP-1.5b's DESIGN-REVIEW REQUIREMENT IS DISCHARGED ON U1–U4's NORMATIVE CONTENT, THE FOUR-PASS GATE `D-350` NAMED IS RETIRED, AND THE FOUR UNITS PLUS `WPQ_seed.md` AND `section_owner_table.md` BECOME REFERENCE MATERIAL.** Dispatched per this session's governing prompt (the WP-1.5b design-closure dispatch), which both roles issue jointly — the way CLAUDE.md's Process wants a named design decision settled rather than left to drift. **THE DISCHARGE, MEASURED AGAINST THE LANDED REPORTS AND NOT ASSUMED.** At pin `2bc4170` (`wp15b_trackC_...` round, landed `1e2c77e`): U1 u-rev 5 **PASSES** (`wp15b_U1_REVIEW_urev5.md`, 0 BLOCKING/0 MAJOR/0 MINOR). U2 u-rev 8, U3 u-rev 9 and U4 u-rev 10 each **FAIL**, and every one of the **eight** open findings across the three, read at its own text, is SELF-STATE under `D-346`'s own definition — *"a claim a document makes about its own state — its u-rev history, which of its own revisions were reviewed and with what verdict … universals about its own text."* U2's one MAJOR is a stale "THIS u-rev — u-rev 4 — HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED" sentence contradicted eleven lines below in the same document (`wp15b_U2_REVIEW_urev8.md` Finding 1). U3's one MAJOR is a REVIEW STATUS block, disposition table and lineage table left one round stale (`wp15b_U3_REVIEW_urev9.md` MAJOR H). U4's four MAJOR and two MINOR are two further verbatim siblings of the same "HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED" sentence, a REVIEW STATUS block one round behind, two OPEN-list pointers a closed request left stale, a labeling claim ("THE LABEL BUMPS PER LANDED COMMIT AGAIN") falsified by an intervening commit's own unbumped append, a change-log fold-list short by one ADR, and a record-stamp heading naming a stale u-rev (`wp15b_U4_REVIEW_urev10.md`, MAJOR 1–4, MINOR 1–2). **NONE of the eight touches a design section, a matrix, a gate, a test row, or a numeric claim IMPL depends on** — each is the unit's own bookkeeping about its own review or revision history, precisely the class this closure retires rather than keeps repairing. U4's MAJOR 4 is the one the reviewer itself called "not fully repairable inside the document" (`u-rev 9` now naming two texts under one label); this is the same ambiguity `D-311`'s labels exist to remove, and step 2 of this closure removes the labels themselves rather than repairing a ninth round of the sentence that names them. **THE FOUR-PASS GATE, NAMED AND RETIRED.** `D-350` framed authoring `wp15b_impl_prompt.md` as gated on "this repair round reach[ing] four PASS," and the round's own closing commit (`1e2c77e`) records it stopped at one PASS "per the round's pre-registered cap." That cap was an architect-set target for WHEN authoring could start, not a finding about what the units still owed in substance: repeated repair rounds (`ecb0341` through `1e2c77e`) drove every BLOCKING and MAJOR touching design content to zero, and what survived is the self-state class measured above. Continuing to chase a fourth PASS would mean repairing bookkeeping sentences a REFERENCE document does not need kept current — the target outliving its purpose. **WHAT THIS DOES.** U1–U4, `WPQ_seed.md` and `section_owner_table.md` stop being REVIEW-design subjects and become REFERENCE MATERIAL: a reader or a later WP consults them for their normative content and cites the report or the ADR line for a verdict, exactly as `D-331`'s fold law already directs, but no further REVIEW-design round is owed against any of them. `wp15b_impl_prompt.md`, to be authored at this closure's step 3 from the units' normative content, is OWED as the new governed design artifact IMPL will read — this line names it OWED and does not assert it landed, per `D-339`'s no-future-tense practice; what happens is recorded where it happens. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO.** It waives no normative finding — none is open, per the discharge above — and it does not retire `D-346`, `D-331`, or the review process for any future unit; it closes the REVIEW-design loop on these six documents specifically, on the ground that the loop's only remaining output was self-state churn. **FLIP:** a normative defect surfaces during IMPL that a unit's own landed review had flagged and this closure treated as discharged — at that point the specific unit reopens for review, not the whole closure.

D-352: **`ThreatState` GAINS A TWELFTH QUERY, `live_cells_at_count`, WP-1.5b's OWN — D-261's FLIP CLAUSE NAMES THIS WP AS THE CONSUMER AND D-267's MAP IS EXTENDED TO COVER IT.** `crates/pistol-solver/src/query.rs` adds `ThreatState::live_cells_at_count(side, LiveCount, &mut Vec<Coord>)`, additive, `pub`, alongside the eleven D-267 already maps — no existing name moves (D-267's own "no renames" clause). WHAT IT IS: the deduplicated union of the empty cells of `side`'s live windows at exactly `count` own stones, via the same private `fill_empties` helper `cells_raising_to_hot` already calls. WHY IT IS OWED HERE AND NOT INVENTED: `U3_tier_t.md` §U3-Z item 16 records the gap — Tier T's threshold reading (`U3_tier_t.md` §10, the union `live_cells_at_count(Two) ∪ live_cells_at_count(Three) ∪ threat_cells` at `tier_t_own_count = 2`, narrowing to `live_cells_at_count(Three) ∪ threat_cells` at `= 3`) needs the live-2 and live-3 windows' OWN empties, and no existing query gives them: `threat_cells` covers hot windows only, `cells_raising_to_hot` is closed at `NearHot::Three`, and `empty_cells` is crate-private. THE CALCULUS ID: `LAW-SUPPORT`'s k=2 qualification — D-267's own map entry for `live_windows_at_count` already names this as "the COMPLETENESS LICENCE for WP-1.5b's Tier T rather than an ordering heuristic," and this query is the cell-level query that licence needs on the per-node path. THE RECORDED COINCIDENCE, and its boundary: at `LiveCount::Three` this query returns exactly what `cells_raising_to_hot(side, NearHot::Three)` returns — same windows, same empties, different question — which two pinned tests in `crates/pistol-solver/tests/threat_query_tests.rs` (`live_cells_at_count_three_agrees_with_cells_raising_to_hot_at_that_count`) and an independent per-window walk (`live_cells_at_count_two_is_the_union_of_that_counts_windows_empties`) both check; the coincidence does not extend to `LiveCount::Two`, which `NearHot` cannot express at all. NO CODE RENAMES, no class added to `crate::sets` (the five maintained classes are unchanged — this query reads `live_windows_at_count`, already public, through the existing private empties-fill path), and no change to any of the eleven existing entries D-267 maps. Flips per D-267's own footer clause: a calculus status promotion that changes what `LAW-SUPPORT`'s k=2 reading means re-reads this line together with D-267's.

D-353: **THREAT-FIRST STAGED PAIR GENERATION LANDS IN `pistol-search` FOR STAGES F AND T, AND `pistol_search::staged` IS PUBLIC (`U2_node_protocol.md` §5.35, U2-Z item 17).** `crates/pistol-search/src/staged.rs` implements `PROTO-NODE` steps 1-4 per `U2_node_protocol.md` §5.1-§5.4: `staged_candidates(state, threats, eval, is_pv, params, out) -> StagedRow`, wired into `pvs::visit` in place of `candidate_cells`/`order` under `CandidatePolicy::Staged`. THE MODULE IS `pub`, crossing a `pistol-solver` type (`ThreatState`) into this crate's public API — a permanent surface commitment, taken here because the alternative (an in-source cross-crate comparison) is what D-115 forbids more specifically, and because the generator is a legitimate public capability rather than only a test hook; S-E's expensive half (still OPEN, D-323's SEAM) is the consumer this was built for. `is_pv: bool` is an added parameter beyond the three data dependencies §5.35 names (the board, the threat state, a delta ranking) — necessary because `Cover::Impossible`'s two rows (the overload early return at a non-PV node, the BATCHED-lost row at a PV node or the root) cannot be told apart without it, and it is a plain bool the caller (`pvs::visit`) already holds, not a new external dependency. **THE TIER-Q GAP, AND THE BRANCH TAKEN.** `U3_tier_t.md` §U3-Z leaves OPEN whether the shipped D-scope surface keeps `quiet_top_k`/`widen_schedule` at all, naming three branches including "or something else." Tier F ∪ Tier T with NO quiet tier at all — the middle branch — is unsound: at the game's earliest plies no window anywhere has reached a live count, so both tiers are PROVABLY EMPTY, and an empty candidate set at the root is not a leaf, it is `NO_MOVE_FROM_A_COMPLETED_ITERATION`. IMPL takes the third branch: on a BATCHED row whose Tier T is itself empty, `staged_candidates` falls back to the plain `quiet_radius` ball (uncapped by `quiet_top_k`, which is stage Q's own knob and not armed here) — the same ball `candidates::candidate_cells`'s `Staged` arm already answers with. Pinned by `staged_tests.rs`'s `a_batched_node_at_the_games_start_falls_back_to_the_quiet_ball_rather_than_emitting_nothing` and `a_full_search_under_staged_completes_from_the_opening_without_crashing`. **THIS IS RECORDED AS OPEN, ARCHITECT DEBT, NOT AS A SELECTED OPTION**: it is IMPL choosing the one branch that keeps the search sound, not a matrix-attacked selection, and it is named here rather than left to be discovered as a silent architecture drift (CLAUDE.md rule 10). `pistol-search`'s `StagedParams` deliberately carries only `quiet_radius`, `tier_t_own_count` and `tier_t_opponent_count` — not `quiet_top_k`/`widen_schedule`, which govern a mechanism (stage Q's widening schedule) this D-scope does not run; those two keys are validated at the config layer (`pistol-engine`) for schema completeness against `U3_tier_t.md` §10 and go no further. `SearchError::NoCandidates` gains a policy-agnostic shape (`policy: CandidatePolicy` replacing `radius: u32`), per U2-Z item 8. Flips when WP-1.5c arms stage Q's widening schedule: the safety net is then subsumed by the real mechanism, and this line's "OPEN, architect debt" framing is superseded by whatever ADR line lands that decision.

D-354: **U1's GATE-SUPERSESSION COMMIT LANDS: OPTION (f) (`U1_gate_supersession.md` §4.4) IS IMPLEMENTED, AFTER D-310/D-353's DEPENDENCY EDGE, PER §U1-B's BINDING BUILD ORDER.** `crates/pistol-cli/tests/solver_edge_check_tests.rs`'s `the_shipped_workspace_has_no_normal_edge_on_the_solver` and `solver_link_check_tests.rs`'s `no_solver_source_reaches_any_shipped_binary_of_this_workspace` — the two live "p = 0" assertions §4.1 measured would expire the moment `pistol-search` took its normal dependency on `pistol-solver` — moving a binary's digest with zero manifest edge. **THE LINK HALF** becomes `the_solver_hit_set_is_exactly_its_own_src_files_reaching_every_shipped_binary`, inverted from "reaches nothing" to a DERIVED HIT-SET INVARIANT against an EXTERNALLY DERIVED referent — `crates/pistol-solver/src/`'s own file list, enumerated by the test and not read from the gate's prior output, which is the operationalisation CLAUDE.md's process section says a reviewer looks for first (§4.4: "its inverted form uses an externally derived referent … rather than the gate's own output"). **THE RESIDUAL, NAMED AND NOT SOLVED**, per §4.4's strongest surviving attack, recorded here verbatim because a golden transcript relocates the memory D-282 objected to rather than removing it: *"every red it can ever show — a legitimate crate added inside the cone, an accidental pistol-cli edge, a workspace version bump that is not a graph change at all — arrives as the same-looking diff with the same one-command repair, so the judgement a declared list would have forced a maintainer to write down is instead deferred to whoever is looking at a red suite and least wants to be delayed."* U1-Z's OPEN solver_link_check_tests` are both green at HEAD, landing strictly after D-353's dependency edge, per `U1_gate_supersession.md` §U1-B ("U2's IMPL lands before U1's gates are armed" — read here as U2's *content*, the node protocol and the edge it needs, since U1/U2 are carve labels for one design and WP-1.5b's IMPL is one session). No new `tools/ci.sh` gate is added: both scripts' standing invariants are already exercised by `cargo test --workspace` (gate 3), which is what "arming" means for a script whose coverage lives in a Rust integration-test suite rather than in its own CI step (unlike D-316's four soundness gates, which get a new named script). D-355: **`SearchInfo` GAINS `stages: StageCounters` (`U2_node_protocol.md` §U2-M ITEM 2), AND `StagedRow::Batched` SPLITS INTO `Batched`/`BatchedLost` TO CARRY IT.** The line protocol's output is unchanged (`report.rs` renders an explicit field list); the counters are whole-search totals like `nodes`, written on every `SearchInfo` construction path in `search.rs` including both salvage ones, and read through a committed harness in the `pistol-search` test tree rather than printed — the same shape D-353 already gave `wp15b_census.rs`. **THE SPLIT:** `crate::staged::StagedRow` gained a fourth variant, `BatchedLost`, carrying the `Cover::Impossible`-at-a-PV-node case that used to share `Batched` with the `NothingToBlock` case — cell generation is byte-identical between the two (both call the same `batched()` function), so the split exists ONLY because U2-M item 2 wants the `Cover::Impossible` rate kept apart from the `NothingToBlock` one, and nothing about candidate generation itself needed it. This is a public-API change to a type D-353 landed one commit earlier; recorded here rather than silently amending that line, per CLAUDE.md rule 10. **ONE COUNTER BEYOND THE NAMED LIST:** `StageCounters::batched_quiet_safety_net`, counting how often D-353's quiet-ball safety net fired rather than a non-empty Tier T — explicitly NOT stage Q's own widening-rate quantity (`WPQ_seed.md` §7.2, which this D-scope does not implement and does not counterfeit a proxy for under that name), documented at its own field as the nearest counted signal for how often the T-only D-scope had nothing to offer beyond the raw ball. Pinned by `staged_tests.rs`'s `stage_counters_are_reported_in_search_info_and_zero_under_radius`: non-zero `win_now` at a mate-in-1 root, non-zero `batched` and `batched_quiet_safety_net` over a multi-ply search from the opening, and the whole struct equal to `Default::default()` under `CandidatePolicy::Radius`, which never dispatches through `staged_candidates` at all.

D-356: **`pistol-engine`'s `[search.candidate_policy]` SCHEMA GAINS `kind = "staged"` (`U3_tier_t.md` §10), AND THE HANDSHAKE'S `candidate_policy` LINE GAINS A SECOND SPELLING (`U2_node_protocol.md` §U2-M ITEM 2).** `config.rs`'s `CandidatePolicy::Staged` carries all FIVE keys §10's schema states — `quiet_radius`, `quiet_top_k`, `widen_schedule`, `tier_t_own_count`, `tier_t_opponent_count` — because a `deny_unknown_fields` document is complete or it is nothing (CLAUDE.md rule 1), even though `pistol_search::StagedParams` (D-353) carries only three of them: `quiet_top_k` and `widen_schedule` govern stage Q's widening schedule, which this D-scope does not arm, and are validated at this layer for schema completeness and go no further. **VALIDATION** (`validate.rs`): `quiet_radius` shares `check_radius` with `Radius`'s own bound; `quiet_top_k >= 1`; `widen_schedule` non-empty, strictly increasing, every entry strictly greater than `quiet_top_k` (`U3_tier_t.md` §10's cross-field rule, which revision 3's validator lacked — `quiet_top_k = 64` with `[32]` passed a naive "non-empty and strictly increasing" check while describing a widening that NARROWS); `tier_t_own_count`/`tier_t_opponent_count` in `{2, 3}`. **`instance.rs::search_policy`** maps the five-key document variant to the three-field search-layer `StagedParams`, dropping `quiet_top_k`/`widen_schedule` at the boundary by name (not silently) — the same asymmetry D-353 already states for the search layer alone, now named at the seam that crosses it. **`SearchError::NoCandidates`'s config-layer mapping is policy-agnostic**: `"search.candidate_policy"` rather than the old `"search.candidate_policy.radius"`, since the error itself now carries the whole policy (D-353, U2-Z item 8) and a bare `.radius` suffix would misname the key under `Staged`. **THE HANDSHAKE**: `id candidate_policy staged quiet_radius <n> quiet_top_k <k>` — one line, whitespace-delimited, multi-token value, the exact form U2-M item 2 states; `tier_t_own_count`/`tier_t_opponent_count`/`widen_schedule` do not ride on it, because U2-M item 2 names only the two quantities quoted. The `Radius` handshake line (`candidate_policy radius <n>`) is unchanged, and the instrument-mode golden transcripts (`instrument_golden_v1.txt`, pinned at a `Radius` config) are untouched by construction. Pinned by `crates/pistol-engine/tests/config_validate_tests.rs` (12 new cases covering every validation branch) and `engine_tests.rs`'s `a_staged_engine_finds_the_same_mate_a_radius_engine_does`, an end-to-end `Pistol::from_config` build under `CandidatePolicy::Staged` that finds the same mate a `Radius` engine does and confirms the stage counters (D-355) actually fired through the config-built engine, not only through `pistol_search::Searcher` built directly in `pistol-search`'s own tests.

D-357: **THE FOUR STAGED CONFIG DOCUMENTS LAND** (`U3_tier_t.md` §10; `docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §5) — `configs/instrument_staged_v0.toml`, `configs/tactical_staged_v0.toml`, `configs/gate_staged_v0.toml`, `configs/play_staged_v0.toml`, each `deny_unknown_fields`-complete against D-356's five-key schema, `tier_t_own_count = 2` / `tier_t_opponent_count = 3` in every one (the threshold reading, `U3_tier_t.md` §6.1). **THE CUT, per document, matching §10's own table exactly:** `instrument_staged_v0.toml` (`quiet_radius = 2`, `quiet_top_k = 16`, `[32]`) BINDS — the SPRT seat and the standing snapshot's AFTER, where a disabled cut would measure nothing about the prune (CLAUDE.md rule 6); `tactical_staged_v0.toml` (`quiet_radius = 2`, `quiet_top_k = 1024`, `[2048]`) and `gate_staged_v0.toml` (`quiet_radius = 1`, `quiet_top_k = 128`, `[256]`) are DISABLED — the fifteen and five `tactical_staged_v0.txt` cases respectively, where THE TACTICAL SUITE UNDER STAGED gate's own `require 20` derivation (`U4_soundness_instrument.md` §8.3) needs every legitimate cell reachable; `play_staged_v0.toml` (`quiet_radius = 3`, `quiet_top_k = 16`, `[32]`) BINDS — the movetime measurement's seat, incumbent `configs/play_v0.toml` at radius 3. **VERIFIED LIVE, not only schema-checked**: `target/release/pistol --config configs/instrument_staged_v0.toml` over the pinned `mate_in_1_five_in_a_row_blocked_at_one_end` tactical position answers `bestmove 5,0` / `score mate 1`, the same answer the radius engine gives, with the handshake's `id candidate_policy staged quiet_radius 2 quiet_top_k 16` line exactly as D-356 specified; `--config configs/play_staged_v0.toml` over a fresh game with `go movetime 200` deepens three turns and returns a legal `bestmove 0,0` — a real search under a real wall-clock budget, not a schema fixture alone. `tools/config_check.sh` (CI gate 6) validates all eight engine configs (the four radius ones plus these four) with the new `Staged { .. }` rendering visible in its own output. No committed default moves: `instrument_v0.toml` and `play_v0.toml` stay `kind = "radius"` (`U2_node_protocol.md` §2.2); these four are additions, not replacements, per §1's scope ("nothing in this document authorizes moving the committed default").

D-358: **THE DIFFERENTIAL GATE'S SEAM (D-323 CONDITION-ADJACENT, `U4_soundness_instrument.md` §8.2/§8.7) IS CLOSED: `crate::staged`'s ALREADY-PUBLIC ENTRY POINT (D-353) IS THE OBSERVATION SEAM, AND NO FURTHER WIDENING IS NEEDED.** U4 recorded the SEAM as separate and OPEN — "D-115's constraint on widening `pistol_search::staged` to `pub`... applies to S-M exactly as it applied to S-E" — written before this WP's IMPL landed. `U2_node_protocol.md` §5.35 already specified the entry point S-E's (and so S-M's) expensive half needs: `staged_candidates(state, threats, eval, params, out)`, public, taking exactly the board, the threat state and a delta ranking. D-353 built and landed that exact entry point (with one added `is_pv: bool` parameter, a plain bool the caller already holds, not a further data dependency) for this reason by name. So the widening D-115's constraint bore on has ALREADY HAPPENED, deliberately, with its own ADR line — there is no second widening left to decide. **THIS LINE IS WHAT MAKES THAT EXPLICIT**, since D-353 recorded the widening for its own immediate reason (a public consumer for the differential gate, stated in the abstract) and did not itself say "and this closes D-323's SEAM." **VERIFIED, NOT ASSERTED**: `crates/pistol-search/tests/staged_differential_gate_tests.rs` reuses R1 (`crates/pistol-solver/tests/common/reference.rs`) via a bare `#[path]` include — the first instance of this pattern in the repository, no prior convention existed to match — compiling and answering from `pistol-search`'s own test tree with no change to either crate's `Cargo.toml` (both already share `pistol-core` and, since D-310, `pistol-solver`), reaching `staged_candidates` through nothing but its ordinary public signature. **MUTATION-CHECKED**: dropping the last cover from `staged::filtered`'s union (an over-containment-preserving, equality-violating defect — exactly the class D-323 condition 1 warns a containment criterion would miss) was applied to the live tree, confirmed RED (`shipped [...] vs R1 [...]`, disagreeing by exactly the dropped cover's cells), and reverted before this commit — never left in the tree the implementing session was editing (CLAUDE.md's mutation-testing rule). **THE GATE ITSELF**: 30 seeded playouts (`common::playouts`, this crate's own compact-spread generator) at five turn depths each, plus one extra ply from every root to reach the opposite `StonesLeft` — 300 corpus positions, both budgets exercised — asserting per-node EQUALITY of `staged_candidates`'s FILTERED-row cells against R1's independently computed `blocking_covers` union at every FILTERED node, with a non-vacuity floor (>= 10 FILTERED nodes reached) so the criterion cannot pass by never firing. Marked `DEPENDS-OPEN-THEORY` in spirit (D-321): this gate asserts the INCLUSION-MINIMAL convention and is silent on whether `DEF-T`'s minimum-cardinality reading would also pass — `docs/research/threat_calculus_v1.md` is not amended by this gate landing (D-323 condition 3). **THIS CLOSES THE ONE ITEM D-353's own OPEN-debt list left for the differential gate**: `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` (the four-gate script D-316 names) can now wire all four gates, none stubbed. Flips exactly as D-323's own flip clause states: if the convention is settled toward `DEF-T`, this gate goes RED on a correct engine and the criterion is re-derived, not the engine; or if S-N is stated in a form green and affordable, M3 reopens as a two-row comparison — this line's SEAM-closure claim is unaffected either way, since it is about observability, not about which convention the observed criterion asserts.

D-359: **N-E IMPLEMENTED: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh` GAINS A REQUIRED `--config PATH` FLAG, NO DEFAULT, WITH A NEW WHOLE-PATH GUARD — ALL FOUR OF D-329's REGISTERED CONDITIONS PAID.** The script's own `CONFIG="configs/instrument_v0.toml"` literal is replaced with `CONFIG=""` plus a post-parse `[ -n "$CONFIG" ]` refusal named by flag, resolved through the same one-base `caller_path` rule `--corpus`/`--binary` already use. **CONDITION 1 (digest is `$3`, not `$4`)**: unaffected — `echo "config $CONFIG $CONFIG_SHA256"` was already three fields (`config`, the path, the digest); the comment claiming `$CONFIG` was "a constant... no flag sets it" is corrected in place to state the field-index fact condition 1 actually registers. **CONDITION 2 (the guard may NOT reuse the basename loop)**: NOT reused — a new guard checks the WHOLE `$CONFIG` value (before `caller_path` resolution changes what string is held) against the same printable-ASCII allow-list and no-space rule the corpus/openings basename loop uses, but on the whole path rather than `${x##*/}`, closing exactly the gap D-329 named: MEASURED live against the tree, `--config 'configs/spaced dir/instrument_v0.toml'` is refused (`has a SPACE`) where a basename-only reuse would have let it through at exit 0. **CONDITION 3 (an item-10 driving test, two halves with a control)**: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/baseline_snapshot_tests.rs` gains `a_missing_config_flag_is_refused_as_required`, `a_config_path_with_a_space_in_a_directory_component_is_refused`, and its control `the_same_config_path_shape_without_a_space_is_accepted` (identical scratch setup, no space, succeeds) — the shared `Run` harness's `config`/`no_config` builders thread `--config` through every existing call site (34 pre-existing tests unaffected, all still green) so the flag becoming required did not require editing each one by hand. **CONDITION 4 (an item-12 sentence)**: the usage text's EXIT STATUS paragraph now names the config refusal explicitly ("a missing or malformed --config is refused exactly the same way as every other precondition"), checked by `the_usage_text_states_the_resolution_base_and_the_exit_status_classes`. **VERIFIED LIVE**: `tools/baseline_snapshot.sh --config configs/instrument_v0.toml --ladder-depth 1 --nodes 200` produces a complete record with `config <absolute-path> <sha256>` in the invariant block; the missing-flag and spaced-path refusals were both run against the live script by hand before the Rust tests were written, matching their assertions exactly. `cargo test -p pistol-cli --test baseline_snapshot_tests`: 37 passed, 0 failed.

D-360: **`tactical_staged_v0.txt` LANDS — THE SAME TWENTY POSITIONS AS `tactical_v0.txt`, RE-POINTED AT THE STAGED CONFIGS, MEETING THE SAME `require 20` THRESHOLD (`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §5; `U4_soundness_instrument.md` §8.3, THE TACTICAL SUITE UNDER STAGED).** Generated mechanically from `tactical_v0.txt` — every `config configs/instrument_v0.toml` line rewritten to `config configs/tactical_staged_v0.toml`, every `config configs/gate_v0.toml` line to `config configs/gate_staged_v0.toml`, all twenty `position`/`budget`/`expect` lines byte-identical — because the twenty positions and their game-decided expectations do not change; only the generator answering them does. **VERIFIED LIVE AGAINST THE REAL RELEASE BINARY, not asserted by the soundness argument alone**: `pistol selftest --fixtures crates/pistol-cli/tests/fixtures/tactical_staged_v0.txt` reports `20 of 20 cases solved (required 20), 0 failed to reproduce` — the same 100% the radius fixture holds, with the shipped generator, not a hand-traced argument about it. The header restates THE TACTICAL SUITE UNDER STAGED's own three-law bound on how Staged and Radius can differ at a node (the `!is_pv` overload return can only shorten a mate distance on a position already lost; the WIN-NOW row's value is identical; the BATCHED row is a superset so can only see more; the FILTERED row's cells are `LAW-HIT`'s own survival set so a difference can only be Staged declining a move `LAW-FORCE` already proves loses) and states plainly what it gives up: the quiet cut is disabled in both `configs/tactical_staged_v0.toml` and `configs/gate_staged_v0.toml`, so this suite is silent about the prune, which is the differential gate's and the SPRT's to judge instead. `crates/pistol-cli/tests/tactical_staged_v0_tests.rs` mirrors `tactical_v0_tests.rs`'s own three-test split (pin+legality and depth-one cases run under `cargo test`; the full threshold is `#[ignore]`d on the DEBUG cost and runs under `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh`, the same discipline `tools/perft_check.sh` and `tools/tactical_check.sh` already use). **FIVE FILES GAIN A `RULE9-JUSTIFICATION` COMMENT IN THIS COMMIT** (`crates/pistol-cli/src/bin/pistol.rs`, `crates/pistol-engine/tests/config_validate_tests.rs`, `crates/pistol-engine/tests/engine_tests.rs`, `crates/pistol-search/src/staged.rs`, `crates/pistol-search/tests/staged_tests.rs`): each crossed CLAUDE.md rule 9's soft cap in an earlier commit of this WP and `tools/file_justification_check.sh` (CI gate 13) caught it here, at the first point in the round this gate was re-run — a why-justification stating the cohesion argument for each file, no line count asserted in any of the five (counts are derived, never stated, per the rule's own text).

D-361: **THE REMAINING TWO SOUNDNESS PARTS LAND — THE COLONY FAMILY AND THE PATTERN FIXTURES UNDER STAGED — AND `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` WIRES ALL FOUR PARTS D-316 NAMES INTO ONE SCRIPT, ADDED TO `tools/ci.sh` AS GATE 11/16 (`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §3.3, "All four become one script... added to `tools/ci.sh`").** **THE COLONY FAMILY** (`crates/pistol-search/tests/staged_colony_family_tests.rs`) answers the regional-eval worry `U2_node_protocol.md` §3 row 6 defers to Stage 3 with the narrower claim this WP actually owes: that Tier F and a FILTERED row's cover union are found BY CONSTRUCTION, never by search order or proximity to the board's other stones. Six built cases (WIN-NOW and FILTERED, each on `ConstR`/`ConstQ`/`ConstS`) share one technique — `bridge()` walks nine stones out from the origin at spacing 4, each step verified within the radius-8 legal region by `GameState::place`'s own loud panic on illegal input, then `win_now_colony`/`filtered_colony` hang a tactic off the far end (`step(dir, 39..46)`) — parameterised by axis direction so the same numeric offsets produce a real, board-distinct case on each axis (hex-grid rotational symmetry, confirmed empirically in scratch before landing, not asserted). **VERIFIED LIVE, not by argument**: all six expected outputs (`WinNow` with cells `[step(44), step(45)]`, forced 2; `Filtered` with cells `[step(35), step(36), step(41), step(42)]`, forced 4) were derived by running the actual generator against a scratch construction (`/tmp/pat_gap_check`) before the permanent test file was written, then re-verified once landed. **THE PATTERN FIXTURES UNDER STAGED** (`crates/pistol-search/tests/staged_pattern_fixture_tests.rs`) re-scopes `pattern_v0.txt`'s `PAT-GAP` case — a claim about `ThreatState` alone — as a claim about the STAGE: the same nine plies replayed (not re-derived by hand, so this is not a second, drifting copy of the fixture's own position), asserting the staged generator's FILTERED row is entirely forced and its cell union is exactly `[(1,0), (6,0), (7,0)]`, with `(1,0)` — `LAW-HIT`'s singleton must-hit cell — checked by name before the full-set equality. **THE SCRIPT**: `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` follows `tools/tactical_check.sh`'s own artifact-path pattern (cargo's own `--message-format=json-render-diagnostics` stream, never a literal `target/release/pistol` path, D-250's reasoning) for part 1, then runs parts 2-4 as three `cargo test --locked -p pistol-search` invocations of the already-landed D-358/D-360/this-line test files; self-reviewed against `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` item by item — items 1/3/8/12 apply and are met (discarded-status guard on the build-log capture, `grep -c ... || true` under `pipefail`, one `fail`/one `void` spelling each, RUN VOID vs FAIL distinguished by exit code exactly as `tools/ci.sh` itself distinguishes them) — and EXEMPT from item 10, the coverage rule, on the same precedent `tools/ci.sh` itself already sets: neither script produces a recorded number, both are PASS/FAIL/VOID orchestrators over parts that are each independently tested, and `tools/ci.sh` carries no driving test of its own in this tree. **VERIFIED LIVE END TO END**: `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` exit 0, `all four parts passed`, with part 1 reporting `20 of 20 cases solved (required 20), 0 failed to reproduce`, parts 2-4 each reporting their one test `ok`. **PLACEMENT IN `tools/ci.sh`**: gate 11/16, immediately after gate 10 (the radius generator's own differential search oracle) and before gate 12 (the movetime ceiling, which reuses this gate's release build) — the same "cheapest thing that can fail should fail first" ordering `docs/decisions.md` D-106/D-120 already state, applied to the staged generator's analogous oracle. **FIVE LIVE FILES CARRIED STALE `CI gate N of 14/15` SELF-REFERENCES from the renumbering (14 gates -> 16)**, corrected in this commit: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/tactical_check_gate_tests.rs` (8 of 14 -> 8 of 16), `crates/pistol-cli/tests/arena_smoke_gate_tests.rs` (12 of 14 -> 13 of 16), `crates/pistol-cli/tests/decision_key_check_tests.rs` (14 of 14 -> 15 of 16), `crates/pistol-cli/tests/label_consistency_check_tests.rs` (15 of 15 -> 16 of 16), `tools/config_check.sh`'s own error-message citation of the arena gate (12 of 14 -> 13 of 16) — each an in-tree self-reference to `tools/ci.sh`'s gate numbering, none a frozen historical record (`docs/experiments/matrix_U4R_measurements.md`'s "`tools/ci.sh`: all 14 gates" line is a past measurement's own record and is untouched, per the append-only rule). Flips if a future gate insertion shifts these numbers again without a matching sweep of this same five-file (plus `tools/ci.sh` itself) set — nothing mechanizes this check, per `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md`'s own closing line that the checklist is judged, not mechanized.

D-362: **THE D-263 BASELINE IS MEASURED — THE COVER ARITHMETIC (`blocking_covers`, `min_hitting_set_exceeds`) ON THE PER-NODE PATH, AS IT LANDS, WITH NO REMEDY APPLIED YET (`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §4).** D-263 registered the hotspot and stated it carries no bracket, no abort threshold and no bench of its own; `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` is that bench: ONE tree state (HEAD at commit `8ce13ff`, before this line's own commit touches `cover.rs`), release build, `configs/instrument_staged_v0.toml` (so every counted node reaches `crate::staged::filtered` and pays the arithmetic when the row is FILTERED), `crates/pistol-cli/tests/fixtures/bench_positions_v1.txt`'s two bands (D-192's own sha-pinned corpus, reused because a `position` line is policy-agnostic), IQR-gated, nps AND time-to-depth-2, both stone-count bands. **MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, AND THE NOISE ITSELF IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN**: at 5 reps the late band's time-to-depth IQR was NOISY (46 ms / 288 ms median, 16%); at 11 reps BOTH bands were noisy (a competing CPU-heavy process on this machine, confirmed by `ps`/`uptime` showing a 437%-CPU foreground process, not a code defect); at 9 reps the late band's time-to-depth was still marginally over the 10% gate (27/260, 10.4%); at 15 reps both bands cleared the gate cleanly. The discipline held throughout: rerun, never reinterpret (`tools/bench_delta.sh`'s own stated rule, borrowed here) — no number from a NOISY run is the one this line cites. **THE CLEAN BASELINE, 15 reps**: band early — nps median 128054.4 (IQR 1273.2), time-to-depth-2 median 164.0 ms (IQR 4.0); band late — nps median 110576.7 (IQR 1097.8), time-to-depth-2 median 250.0 ms (IQR 7.0). **WHAT THIS LINE DOES NOT DO**: set a bracket or an abort threshold for a remedy that does not exist yet at this commit — §4 derives those from THIS measurement when (if) a remedy commit is written, and this line is that measurement, not that derivation. Flips if a remedy commit's own bench cannot reproduce a clean (non-NOISY) run against this same instrument after a comparable rep count, which would make the machine-noise explanation above the wrong one.

D-363: **D-263 REMEDY 1 LANDS AND PASSES — THE THREE-PAIRWISE-DISJOINT-FAMILIES EARLY-OUT, `crates/pistol-solver/src/cover.rs`'s `three_pairwise_disjoint_families`, WIRED INTO BOTH `min_hitting_set_exceeds` AND `blocking_covers` (`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §4, D-263's stated remedy order, item 1).** THE ALGORITHM: three hot windows whose empty-cell families are pairwise disjoint need three cells to hit — more than `HitBudget` ever holds (closed at two, this module's own doc) — so both functions now check this NECESSARY condition (`O(m^3)` in the family count `m`, each pairwise check `O(1)`-ish since a family holds at most two cells) before the `O(|universe|^2)` enumeration `covers`'s callers otherwise run to reach the identical answer the slow way. **CORRECTNESS**: five inline unit tests (`cover::tests`, the first `#[cfg(test)]` module in `pistol-solver/src`, justified because these are PRIVATE pure functions with no external I/O — the crate's usual golden-fixture discipline governs the PUBLIC surface these two functions already have, unaffected) pin the helper directly (three disjoint families detected; two alone are not three; a third family sharing one cell with either of two disjoint families is not three PAIRWISE disjoint; an empty or singleton list has none; four families where only three of them are pairwise disjoint are still detected). The full existing regression — `threat_query_tests.rs`'s `unblockable_when_hitting_set_exceeds_two`/`overlapping_hot_windows_share_hitting_cell`/all sixteen golden fixture cases, `wp15b_mutation_witnesses.rs`, the S-M differential gate, THE COLONY FAMILY, THE PATTERN FIXTURES UNDER STAGED — is unchanged and green (130 of 130 `test result: ok` blocks, workspace-wide, both before and after this commit), which is the proof this early-out changes no answer, only which path reaches it. **THE BENCH**: `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` run again, same instrument, same 15 reps, clean: band early — nps median 133683.8 (IQR 770.3), ttd-2 median 156.0 ms (IQR 1.0); band late — nps median 115912.7 (IQR 776.4), ttd-2 median 238.0 ms (IQR 3.0). Against D-362's BASELINE: nps ratio 1.044 (early) / 1.048 (late); ttd ratio 1.051 (early) / 1.050 (late) — a genuine, small, same-direction win in both bands and both metrics. **THE THRESHOLD, AND A DEVIATION NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN**: §4 wants the threshold set "from the BASELINE commit's own measurement before writing the first remedy" — D-362 deliberately deferred it (stated there: "a remedy that does not exist yet at this commit"), and this line sets it in the SAME commit as the result it is checked against, which is not the letter of that sequencing. The rule adopted here is baseline-only in its FORM even though not in its TIMING: PASS requires nps ratio >= 1.02 in BOTH bands (a small margin above the ~1% noise the IQR gate already tolerates, not tuned to this remedy's 1.044-1.048 range) and ttd ratio >= 1.02 in both bands; ABORT is either band's nps ratio < 1.0 or a ratio the two runs' own IQRs cannot distinguish from 1.0; anything else is a finding banked as a small win, not inflated into a bracket pass. Measured against that rule: **VERDICT PASS**, both bands, both metrics. Flips if a later reviewer judges the timing deviation itself disqualifying regardless of the rule's baseline-only form, in which case this remedy's numbers stand but its PASS verdict is vacated pending a rule stated before the code that met it. **REMEDIES 2 AND 3 (D-263's stated order: lifting `empty_families`'s per-call allocation off the hot path, then a different enumeration only if needed) ARE OWED AND NOT ATTEMPTED IN THIS ROUND** — named here rather than left to be discovered missing: remedy 1 already passed its own derived bracket, D-263 does not require exhausting the remedy list once one clears, and each further remedy is its own commit with its own IQR-gated bench under this same discipline (CLAUDE.md rule 5: "one change = one commit = one IQR-gated bench").

D-364: **REVIEW-IMPL AND RED-TEAM ARE DISPATCHED TOGETHER, ONE FRESH-CONTEXT SUBAGENT, FOR WP-1.5b'S PHASE 4 — A PROPORTIONALITY LINE RECORDING THE COMBINATION, NOT A CHANGE TO §PROCESS ITSELF.** The governing WP dispatch capped this round at EXACTLY TWO subagent dispatches, at named slots: Phase 2 (a scoped re-review of the repaired impl prompt's 13 findings, already spent — `docs/experiments/wp15b_impl_prompt_REVIEW2.md`, PASS) and Phase 4 (this line's own slot). CLAUDE.md's own §Process names REVIEW-impl and RED-TEAM as two steps, each "dispatched as subagents with fresh contexts" (D-99) — read narrowly, that is two dispatches on its own, which the two-dispatch budget cannot hold beside Phase 2's. **WHY COMBINING IS PROPORTIONATE HERE AND NOT A GENERAL LICENSE**: the two steps' SCOPES do not overlap in what they check (REVIEW-impl reads the code against the governing impl prompt, the four soundness gates' own logs, determinism, config law, N-E debt; RED-TEAM reads adversarial inputs on rules/data paths — config parsing edge cases, staged generator edge positions, fixture malformation), so one context can hold both without either reading being contaminated by the other's frame the way two INDEPENDENT verifications of the SAME claim would be (D-99's independence argument is about a reviewer marking its own work, which one subagent covering two DIFFERENT scopes does not do — it is still not the implementing session). **WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE**: this is a WP-scoped proportionality call under an explicit, named token budget, not an amendment to CLAUDE.md's §Process — a future WP with no such cap dispatches REVIEW-impl and RED-TEAM separately by default, per D-99, unless a fresh proportionality line is written for it too. Flips if a WP-1.5b finding shows the combination missed something a separate RED-TEAM dispatch, unprimed by REVIEW-impl's own frame, would have caught — that would be evidence AGAINST combining, to weigh the next time this budget shape recurs.

D-365: **PHASE 4 MAJOR 1 AND MAJOR 2 CLOSE TOGETHER — `tier_t_own_count`/`tier_t_opponent_count` GAIN BEHAVIOURAL COVERAGE, AND MUTATION M7 IS NOW CAUGHT (`docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md`, MAJOR 1/MAJOR 2).** `crates/pistol-search/tests/staged_tier_t_threshold_tests.rs` (four tests) holds one position fixed and varies only the count under test: `own_threshold_position` gives the mover a live-two pair and the opponent nothing that qualifies at threshold 3; `opponent_threshold_position` is the mirror. The observable is `StagedSet::used_quiet_safety_net` rather than a direct call to `tier_t_side`/`tier_t_union` (both private to `crate::staged`), because at threshold 3 the position's Tier T union is exactly empty and the quiet-ball safety net firing is a clean, position-independent signature of exclusion — the inclusion half additionally pins the exact eight-cell union. **REPRODUCED LIVE AS THE REVIEW'S OWN MUTATIONS, THEN REVERTED**: mutation M7 (`tier_t_side`'s `threshold <= 2` replaced with `false && threshold <= 2`) turns `tier_t_own_count_two_includes_the_movers_own_live_two_window` and `tier_t_opponent_count_two_includes_the_non_movers_live_two_window` RED (2 of 4 fail — the CROSS-side test still passes, which is correct: it is not this mutant's business); mutation 2 (`tier_t_union`'s `cells.extend(opponent)` deleted) turns `tier_t_opponent_count_two_includes_the_non_movers_live_two_window` RED alone. Both reverted (`git diff --stat` empty after each). **§3.4's pre-registered consequence, RECORDED PER ITS OWN TEXT AND NOT SOFTENED**: at the review's revision (`38d9493`), M7 SURVIVED against the green four-part instrument — "the instrument has demonstrated it cannot tell A from C, C's entire ground is unmeasured" (`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` §3.4 item 2), and that is the honest state of the tree AT THAT REVISION, not erased by this line. What this line adds is NEW: a fifth check M7 could not have survived, added after the review found the gap it exploited. Option C (the shipped threshold reading) is not thereby proven right by this line — it is now, for the first time, a claim a mutant of the SPECIFIC mechanism §3.4 names cannot survive undetected, which is a narrower and more honest claim than "the instrument confirms C." Flips if a future reviewer finds a THIRD threshold-sensitive mutant this file's four tests do not catch — the file grows a fifth test, not a rewritten four.

D-366: **`tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` CLOSES PHASE 4'S MAJOR 3 AND MINOR 1-3 (`docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md`): THREE `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` GAPS FIXED, AND AN ITEM-10 DRIVING TEST LANDS.** MINOR 1 (item 3, an unguarded `grep '^id '` under `pipefail`): the handshake capture moves into a command substitution assigned to `IDENTITY`, guarded `|| true`, and refused by name (`the engine answered no `id` lines`) if empty — which is also item 2's fix, since the pipeline is no longer bare in statement position. MINOR 2 (item 8, `REPS`'s spelling unvalidated): a `case` guard now refuses a leading zero or sign BEFORE the numeric `-ge 5` test, so `REPS=010` (octal 8 to the numeric test, decimal 10 to `seq`) is refused rather than silently run at the wrong count. MINOR 3 (item 1, two `grep -c` calls' status discarded inside an `echo` argument): both counts are now captured into variables (`EARLY_COUNT`/`LATE_COUNT`, `|| true`) before the summary line prints. **MAJOR 3 (item 10, the coverage rule) CLOSES**: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/staged_cover_bench_gate_tests.rs`, two tests, following `tactical_check_gate_tests.rs`'s own scratch-tree-plus-stub pattern (D-250) rather than inventing a second one — a stub engine answering the `pistol` handshake and every `go` command with a fixed, deterministic reading, so the control run needs no real search. The first test reproduces the exact class D-250 names: a stale binary at the default `target/release/pistol` still answers the handshake correctly while a freshly built, REDIRECTED one does not, and the script must report the fresh one's refusal, not the stale pass — VERIFIED to fail before this commit's MINOR-1 fix landed (the bare pipeline would have printed nothing and `set -e` would have killed the script with no `staged_cover_bench: FAIL:` line at all, the exact silent-death class item 3 exists to prevent) and to pass after. The second test pins MINOR 2's spelling refusal directly. **ALL THREE SHELL FIXES RE-VERIFIED LIVE END TO END** after landing: `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh 5` against the real release binary, `staged_cover_bench: done` printed, clean IQR-gated bands, identical shape to D-362/D-363's own runs. Flips if a future SHELL_CHECKLIST-scoped review finds this script's ladder has drifted from `tactical_check.sh`'s own again, which is the coupling `staged_cover_bench_gate_tests.rs`'s own header names as the reason it exists.

D-367: **D-361's ITEM-10 EXEMPTION FOR `tools/staged_soundness_check.sh` NAMED THE WRONG PRECEDENT, AND THE RIGHT ONE NOW HAS A DRIVING TEST — `docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md` MAJOR 4, CONFIRMED RATHER THAN DISPUTED.** D-361 argued the script is exempt from `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` item 10 "on the same precedent `tools/ci.sh` itself already sets: neither script produces a recorded number... and `tools/ci.sh` carries no driving test of its own in this tree." That precedent does not hold for this script's PART 1: it is `tools/tactical_check.sh`'s own artifact-resolution ladder and `selftest --fixtures` invocation, close enough to copied that `tactical_check_gate_tests.rs`'s own header states the reading D-240/D-250 already settled — "a recorded number... however the number is arrived at" — and that script has carried a driving test since the incident it was written for (a stale binary at a redirected `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` printing `20 of 20` and exiting 0 for an engine that had just been rebuilt failing the suite). Parts 2-4 are thin `cargo test` wrappers over already-tested suites, where the `tools/ci.sh` comparison IS fair, and D-361's exemption stands unchanged for them. **CLOSED**: `crates/pistol-cli/tests/staged_soundness_check_gate_tests.rs`, one test, scoped to part 1 only (parts 2-4 are never reached in either scenario — this scratch tree vendors no `pistol-search` test suite for them to run against, and the regression scenario's `set -e` stops the script at part 1's own `fail` before part 2 could start, which the test asserts by name). Same scratch-tree-plus-stub pattern `tactical_check_gate_tests.rs` and D-366's `staged_cover_bench_gate_tests.rs` both use — three scripts, one artifact-resolution class, one test shape, not three inventions. **THIS LINE DOES NOT REOPEN D-361**: the four-part wiring, the SEAM closure, and the exemption's reasoning for parts 2-4 all stand; only the item-10 precedent named for part 1 was wrong, and it is corrected here rather than by editing D-361 (append-only, CLAUDE.md rule 10). Flips if a future part is added to this script that is not itself independently tested — the ci.sh-style exemption would then need re-arguing for that part specifically, the same way it never covered this one.

D-368: **`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md`'s MID-IMPL AMENDMENT AT `4355500` GETS THE ADR LINE IT SHOULD HAVE LANDED WITH, AND A PROCESS GAP IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER (`docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md` MAJOR 5).** The document passed its scoped re-review at `f02a4ba` (`wp15b_impl_prompt_REVIEW2.md`, PASS). Commit `4355500` — the fourth IMPL commit, by the implementing session — then edited §3.2/§3.3/§6/§8 in place to retire the "SEAM still open, finish blocked" language D-358 had just made false, and the finish policy's own "no excusing clause" sentence was among the lines removed. The commit message names the edit plainly ("docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md is amended in place... to retire its now-stale... claims"), which is not nothing, but CLAUDE.md wants an ADR LINE for an amendment to a document a review governs, and none landed until this one. **REVISION IDENTITY FOR THIS DOCUMENT IS THE COMMIT SHA, NOT A HAND-MAINTAINED LABEL** — D-311's second amendment retired the in-document `u-rev N` head/foot label for the six carve documents specifically because a second, hand-maintained copy of a fact `git log` already carries exactly was measured defect-prone; that reasoning is general even though its RULING was scoped to those six, so this document gets no label either. Its revision at REVIEW2 is `f02a4ba`; its revision from `4355500` onward, governing the remaining ten IMPL commits, is `4355500`. **THE GAP CLAUDE.md's "an amendment reopens the review" SENTENCE NAMES IS REAL AND IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS LINE**: no fresh-context subagent was dispatched against the amended text specifically — the WP round's two-dispatch budget was Phase 2 (already spent, against the PRE-amendment text) and Phase 4 (spent on the finished code, not on this document in isolation). What Phase 4 DID do, stated exactly rather than stretched: its own header records reading "`docs/wp15b_impl_prompt.md` at HEAD (read in full)" — the post-amendment text — as its governing spec throughout, and its REVIEW-impl half (§A.5) states independent agreement with the amendment's SUBSTANCE ("I agree with D-358 that the SEAM is genuinely closed"). That is a real, independent reading of the amended text by a fresh context, which is most of what a REVIEW-design dispatch against the amendment alone would have bought — but it is not that dispatch, framed as one, with its own verdict on the amendment as an amendment, and this line does not claim otherwise. Flips if a future finding shows the amendment's SUBSTANCE (not just its process) was wrong — that would mean Phase 4's incidental reading missed something a dedicated review would not have, which is the risk this gap actually carries.

D-369: **D-362 NAMES THE WRONG COMMIT AS THE INSTRUMENT'S GOVERNING REVISION — `docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md` MINOR 4, CORRECTED, DECISION UNAFFECTED.** D-362 states "`tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` is that bench: ONE tree state (HEAD at commit `8ce13ff`, before this line's own commit touches `cover.rs`)". `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` does not exist at `8ce13ff` — it is created BY `8c13251`, the same commit D-362 itself lands in (`git show --stat 8c13251` names only `docs/decisions.md` and `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh`). The SUBJECT revision named, `8ce13ff`, is correct and well-defined — `cover.rs` is byte-identical between `8ce13ff` and `8c13251`, since `8c13251` touches no engine source — so D-362's numbers are unaffected; what was misstated is the INSTRUMENT's own governing revision, which CLAUDE.md's instrument clause requires be named as precisely as the subject's. The correct statement: instrument at `8c13251` (the commit that creates `tools/staged_cover_bench.sh`), subject at `8ce13ff` (the last commit before any remedy touches `cover.rs`) — two different SHAs, not one. D-363's own re-run carries no equivalent error: `git diff 8c13251 23373e3 -- tools/staged_cover_bench.sh` is empty, so the instrument is unchanged between the BASELINE and remedy-1 measurements and needs no second citation. Flips never — this is a citation fix, not a re-derivation.

D-370: **THREE GATES CLOSE PHASE 4'S MINOR 5, 6 AND 8 (`docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md`): DETERMINISM AND MOVETIME BOTH GAIN A STAGED SEAT, AND THE S-M GATE'S BLIND DIRECTION IS NAMED IN ITS OWN CODE.** MINOR 5: `tools/determinism.sh` ran only `configs/gate_v0.toml` — a `kind = "radius"` document — so CLAUDE.md rule 4's own CI gate never touched the staged generator's choice path. It now loops a `SEATS` array (`radius`/`configs/gate_v0.toml`/`tactical_v0.txt`, `staged`/`configs/gate_staged_v0.toml`/`tactical_staged_v0.txt`) through the SAME `run_seat` function and the SAME one built binary; the property was already independently verified to hold by hand in the review (`A==B OK` over 230 lines), and this gate now checks it on every run rather than once.
