D-383: **THE §9.5-ADJACENT ATTRIBUTION-WINDOW-WIDENING DESIGN FAILS ITS FRESH-CONTEXT REVIEW-DESIGN — 2 BLOCKING.** `docs/experiments/wp15b_attribution_window_design.md` (rev `6039ad9`) proposed replacing Criterion 1's fixed 2-turn replay window with an adaptive walk over each game's own real history, to resolve the 5-of-58-opening vacuity `wp15b_vacuity_diagnostics.md` found. `wp15b_attribution_window_design_REVIEW.md` FAILS it. **BLOCKING 1, the load-bearing one**: the design's premise — that replaying a later turn via a fresh subprocess is "doing more of the same valid thing" as replaying each engine's first free search — is FALSE. `crates/pistol-engine/src/instance.rs`'s `set_position` never clears the searcher's transposition table (only `new_game` does), and the arena runs one persistent subprocess per engine per game (`pistol-arena/src/game.rs`/`schedule.rs`), so a LIVE engine's second-or-later search runs on a WARM TT while a fresh replay subprocess is always COLD. REPRODUCED LIVE on the exact registered binary/configs: walking opening 44 (games 88/89) to turn 11, `r2` replayed fresh answers `-2,5/4,-1`; `r2` played LIVE at that identical prefix answered `-1,4/4,-1` — the SAME engine disagreeing with its own live self, which the walk would have printed as a link-1a attribution FAILURE on an opening that has no labeling defect at all. Widening the window in ANY form (fixed or adaptive) is therefore unsound without a materially different, more expensive replay mechanism (a persistent subprocess replaying the full turn sequence, matching live TT state) that was neither designed nor scoped. **BLOCKING 2**: no OPTION MATRIX was built (CLAUDE.md rule), and the diagnostic's own Result 5 "tolerate a registered rate, no code change" option — which BLOCKING 1 now shows would have been the correct call — was never named or weighed. Two further MAJOR findings (a wrong "cost unchanged" claim — the true effect is CHEAPER for 66 of 116 games, not unchanged; missing `Turn::Single` fixture coverage) and one MINOR (a table/prose range mismatch) are in the review. IMPL was not started; nothing in `tools/wp15b_attribution_check.py`, the prereg, or its tests was touched. This session's next step is the operator/architect's, per this WP's standing rule that a session does not re-attempt a design its own review just failed.

D-384: **TOLERATE-WITH-ROBUSTNESS SELECTED FOR CRITERION 1, ARCHITECT RULING.** Widening the replay window is DEAD, on D-383's BLOCKING 1: the cold-subprocess-replay-vs-warm-live-TT confound was reproduced live (opening 44, r2 disagreeing with its own live self at turn 11) and no fixed or adaptive window escapes it without a materially different replay mechanism. Provenance is D-383's own review, which killed the widen alternative on mechanism and separately named TOLERATE as the option that would have been correct given BLOCKING 1. **SELECTED: TOLERATE-WITH-ROBUSTNESS.** A confirmed-attribution requirement (links 1b/1c, unchanged, universal, per game) is combined with a ROBUSTNESS check over the vacuous pairs specifically, rather than either refusing on any vacuity (today's rule) or silently ignoring it (a bare tolerance number). **Criterion 1', quoted verbatim, the text that governs from this point**: "A report is a measurement iff (a) zero confirmed inversions under links 1b/1c applied to all games, and (b) the verdict is invariant under adversarial reassignment of every link-1a-vacuous pair, recomputed from the report's own pentanomial and LLR machinery." **WARM-REPLAY IS LICENSED, NOT SCHEDULED**: the persistent-subprocess, matching-TT-state replay mechanism BLOCKING 1 showed widening would need is not built now and is not owed now. **THE FLIP**: any run whose verdict fails robustness under 1', or any run where a link-1b/1c-confirmed inversion coincides with a link-1a-vacuous pair, builds warm-replay before any verdict from that run is read — the tolerance is conditional on the numbers, not unconditional. **Run 1 (D-381) is NOT re-read under Criterion 1' and stands exactly as recorded** — 1' governs runs taken after its own registration, per this WP's standing rule that an amendment governs prospectively.

D-409: **STEP 3 — WARM REPLAY IS A SECOND MODE ON `arena`, `arena --replay <report> --out <path> --workers <n>`, AND IT DRIVES BOTH SEATS OF EVERY GAME.** `crates/pistol-arena/src/replay.rs` spawns each game's two engines through `seats::with_seats` (D-408) — the identical function `schedule::one_game` calls, so protocol behaviour including `NEW_GAME` is inherited rather than described — feeds the report's own recorded move list turn by turn, and at every turn a seat searched asks that seat through `exchange::ask`, the same function `game::play` calls. **BOTH SEATS, not one, and this is D-406's BLOCKING 2 answered in code**: revision 3's design had narrowed to "one credited engine", which cannot support the inert-pair theorem (that theorem needs BOTH games' credited engines fully replayed) and disagreed with its own ~1x cost claim. Driving both is also what makes the replay the REAL loop: each engine sees precisely the sequence of `position`/`go` exchanges it saw live, so its transposition table is in precisely the state it was in, which is the entire difference from D-383's dead cold-window design (`crates/pistol-engine/src/instance.rs`: `set_position` never touches the searcher, only `new_game` clears it). **NO EARLY STOP, and `schedule::run` is NOT reused — D-406's BLOCKING 3 answered in code rather than in a corrected sentence**: `schedule::run` takes an `ArenaConfig` and `Openings` rather than a report, hardcodes its call to `one_game`, and runs `score::first_crossing_pairs` SPRT early-stop logic that would truncate a replay pass. `replay::run` is its own worker pool over the report's games — same pre-sized slot vector, same failure latch, no stop — because a criterion over SOME of a report's games is a criterion over a sample nobody registered. A pass that does not cover every game writes `warm_replay_aborted` and carries no `divergences` line at all, so no consumer can read one off it (`report.rs`'s own D-160 pattern). **THE HALT RULE**: the first disagreement ends that game's replay, because feeding an engine past a divergence feeds it a move it did not choose and desynchronises its table from what the run had. **REFUSES BY NAME, BEFORE ANY GAME**: a report that carries no verdict, a schema this build does not write, any budget but `nodes`, an engine whose identity is no longer the one the report attests (`replay::verify_engines` runs `identity::capture`, the generation path's own run-start function, and compares against the capture the report's `engine_id` lines carry — strictly stronger than live's own check, which only compares against itself), a move list that does not replay legally, a repeated key on a record, a path with whitespace this format cannot round-trip. Exit 0 clean, 1 a divergence or an abandoned pass (document still written), 2 refused (no document) — the generation path's own exit contract. **WHAT FLIPS THIS**: a replay that needed to drive one seat only — a cost problem, not a correctness one — would break the inert-pair theorem's own precondition and needs a new theorem before it needs new code.

D-410: **THE REPORT PARSER IS NAMED, AND IT IS `crates/pistol-arena/src/transcript.rs`.** D-406's MAJOR 5 recorded it as the single largest missing component of the design: recovering engine identity, config and budget from a report that carries no `--config`. It reads a REPORT and not a config document on purpose — a replay parameterised by a config could be pointed at a different experiment than the one it claims to check, whereas a report is the only artefact that attests the engines, their digests, the budget, the book length and every game's move list TOGETHER. D-412: **CRITERION 1'' CLAUSE (b) HAS A SATISFACTION CONDITION FOR A CLEAN REPORT — POINT 3'S THEOREM RUN IN REVERSE, WRITTEN OUT — AND THE REPLAY'S COST IS NOW MEASURED.** D-406's MAJOR 1 was that a zero-divergence report has no "first divergence" to attribute by, and the covering argument was nowhere written. It is written in `tools/wp16_warm_attribution_check.py`'s own header and implemented in `clause_b`: take any pair. **If its two games' recorded move lists are IDENTICAL and neither forfeited**, both credited engines warm-replayed every move, so the two seats are behaviourally indistinguishable at every position either game reached; swapping the labels could not have changed a board at any ply, so whichever PLAYER INDEX wins one game wins the other, the two games swap which LABEL holds that index, and the pair is a FORCED 1-1 split — INERT, bucket p2 whichever engine is stronger. The checker ASSERTS that bucket rather than assuming it: an inert pair recorded at anything else contradicts the theorem and is a finding. **If the move lists DIFFER**, let t be the first turn they differ at. Both games agree up to t, so the board at t is identical and the mover at t is the same PLAYER INDEX in both — and that index's occupant searched exactly the same prefixes in both games, so its warm table is in the same state in both. The replay measured the seat credited in game one answering m1 there and the seat credited in game two — the OTHER label — answering m2 != m1 there. Inverted labels would require one engine to answer both m1 and m2 to the same position with the same history, which instrument-mode determinism forbids. So the pair is DIRECTLY ATTRIBUTED at t. **A non-inert pair with no such t** — one game's moves a strict prefix of the other's, which only a forfeit or a cap produces — is neither excluded nor attributed and is reported a clause (b) FAILURE by name. **DRIVING TEST (i), ON THE REAL ENGINE, MEASURED THIS SESSION** — `configs/arena_wp16_dryrun.toml` (`staged_q(defensive_and_offensive)` vs plain `staged`, `openings_v1.txt` take 4, binary `sha256 b8d0dc963a2453e1eff69823629c37b23bafe419b9225f8af2401df519bc2673`, NOT D-401's book or matchup, which stays unread forever): run `14.356 s`, `artifacts/wp16_replay_drivingtest_run.txt` `sha256 83c4db107935f4676353b1fcd299082a4fa1d36f4b7c867f613ebeeea9004ba4`; warm replay `14.319 s` at 4 workers, `artifacts/wp16_replay_drivingtest_replay.txt` `sha256 9993c67127b7bead0cd49484eff5f7e5d6f1b7a194135721ae258e7d5d2754b4`, **8 of 8 games, 0 divergences, 201 compared turns, and every game's per-seat node count EQUAL to the run's own**; checker `PASS — 0 failure(s)`, `4 pair(s) directly attributed`, `0 unattributable`, exit 0, in `0.028 s`. **THE COST CLAIM IS THEREFORE MEASURED AND NOT DECLARED: 14.319 / 14.356 = 1.003x the original run**, against the design's DECLARED "~1x". **AND THE WINDOW IS MEASURED TOO**: the old cold instrument reached `16 turns replayed` on this same report; the warm one compared `201`, a **12.6x** wider window, every one of them confirmed. Equal node counts on a clean game are the referent the replay does not compute about itself — the same searches in the same order at the same budget must cost the same — and unequal ones take the determinism-violation exit, which is its own driving case.

D-418: **STANDING RULE FOR EVERY PRE-REGISTRATION IN THIS PROJECT FROM HERE: A CRITERION SECTION QUOTES ITS INSTRUMENT AND NEVER PARAPHRASES IT.** Stated as a rule rather than as revision 5's own habit, because D-417's fifth instance is enough evidence that the defect is structural. **THE RULE**: every sentence in a criterion section that says what an instrument DOES carries a receipt from the shipped instrument at the governing revision — the exact exit code, the exact message text the instrument prints, or the name of the test that drives that path. A sentence that cannot be traced to one of those three is a defect by construction, and a reviewer may say so without argument. **WHY THOSE THREE AND NOT "a file:line cite"**: D-405's Ruling A already required receipts as file:line, and D-406 still failed — because a line number is a pointer to code that may be read correctly and DESCRIBED wrongly one sentence later. There is no way to test that a paraphrase is faithful — testing that is what the reviewer is for — and a gate that grepped for backticks would be satisfied by a quotation of the wrong string. It is judged, like CLAUDE.md's own dry-run and second-instrument rules, and it is written here so a reviewer has something to judge AGAINST. **WHAT FLIPS IT**: an instrument whose messages are themselves generated from the document — the inverse direction, document as source of truth — would make quotation circular rather than corroborating; nothing in this project works that way today, and a WP that proposed it would need to say what replaces the receipt.

A failure of the instrument's OUTPUT CHANNEL, or a signal death, terminates on CPython's own status and is outside the invariant." §5 gains a row registering a termination that is none of 0/1/2/3 as A VOID ABOUT THE INVOCATION ENVIRONMENT — the invocation is re-issued, and nothing is read about the engines. **AND A FIFTH REGISTERED CHECK IS ADDED, CHOSEN BECAUSE THIS DEFECT CLASS COULD FALSIFY IT**: no registered command pipes or redirects the checker's stdout, quoted from §8.2's and §8.6's own code blocks, all three carrying no `>`, `>>`, `|` or `tee`. Closed BY RULE and not by a longer list: kind (i) is any exit 2 taken before a `game`, `replay` or `pair` record was read, so nothing about the report's CONTENT is in evidence; the four categories survive as EXAMPLES. **THAT IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS WORK PACKAGE THAT AN ENUMERATION STANDING IN FOR A RULE HAS BEEN THE DEFECT** — D-419's MAJOR A, D-420's exception tuple, and now this — and the document says so in those words. **MINOR 3** — revision 6 wrote "the instrument HAS 49 `die()` call sites", revision 5's figure carried forward un-remeasured in the present tense; it is **50** at `43e8a86`. Corrected to the past tense against a NAMED revision and marked MEASURED with its receipt: 52 raw occurrences less one definition and one prose mention at `:867`, cross-checked by counting `ast.Call` nodes, which needs no subtraction. **NOT FIXED, AND SAID SO**: the reviewer's FIFO observation is pre-existing at `bfdf933`, outside the diff, and fixing it would move the governing revision — see D-422.

D-422: **STANDING DEBT, RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED: `tools/wp16_warm_attribution_check.py` ACCEPTS A FIFO AS A DOCUMENT PATH AND BLOCKS FOREVER, UN-INTERRUPTIBLY. ITS SCHEDULED HOME IS THE FINAL-CLEANUP WORK PACKAGE, ALONGSIDE D-414's OWN RECORDED GAP.** D-421's reviewer found it while answering `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` items 8 and 12 by name: `slurp` opens whatever path it is handed and a FIFO with no writer never returns, so the instrument hangs instead of refusing. **WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE, stated so the deferral is a decision and not an oversight.** It is PRE-EXISTING at `bfdf933` — it is not something `43e8a86` or any revision of this document introduced — so it is outside the diff the cap licenses a fix round for; and fixing it would move the instrument's governing revision a second time, re-pin §7A.1 and §10, and convert the licensed SCOPED re-review into a whole one, which is the same cost D-421's ruling declined to pay for a larger finding. The exposure is to a hostile or careless invocation, not to the registered workload. **WHAT WOULD FLIP IT**: any decision to accept checker inputs from an untrusted source, or to run the instrument on a path the operator did not create, at which point it becomes a live defect rather than debt.

D-423: **THE SCOPED RE-REVIEW FAILS `docs/experiments/wp16_sprt_prereg.md` REVISION 7 (`1618467`): 0 BLOCKING, 2 MAJOR, 2 MINOR. ':(exclude)docs/'` prints nothing, and a per-section sha256 over all 28 sections found exactly FOUR changed — the header, §5, §7A.1 and §11 — so every out-of-scope section is byte-identical, the header's account of itself is COMPLETE AND TRUE (the D-416 MINOR 4 / D-419 MINOR G defect did not recur a third time), and `tools/SHELL_CHECKLIST.md` correctly did not apply this round. **MINOR 3 IS FULLY CLOSED, INDEPENDENTLY RE-MEASURED**: `ast.Call` gives 50, the raw grep gives 52 on 52 distinct lines, and the set difference is exactly lines 167 and 867 — the two the receipt names — with `:867` confirmed to be comment prose. Reproduced by this session. **AND THE RULE ITSELF MISCLASSIFIES ONE OF ITS OWN EXAMPLES**: "a missing or unrunnable engine" refuses at `:236` via `cold_answer` ← `classify` ← `main():816`, which is AFTER `read_report` and `read_replay` have read `game` and `replay` records, so the new rule ("any exit 2 taken before a `game`, `replay` or `pair` record was read") makes a genuine VOID into kind (ii). The rule is not merely unpropagated; it is wrong at its own boundary. **MAJOR 2 — THE FIFTH REGISTERED CHECK CANNOT FALSIFY THE DEFECT CLASS IT WAS ADDED FOR, AND THIS ADR's OWN PREDECESSOR SAYS OTHERWISE.** D-421 registered it as "chosen because this defect class could falsify it", and revision 7 headlines it "ONE THIS DEFECT CLASS COULD HAVE FALSIFIED". Five green checks and a false invariant would have been precisely as consistent as four. The check is a real reduction in EXPOSURE (the workload never redirects the channel) but it is not a FALSIFIER, and the rev-6 reviewer's criterion asked for a falsifier in those words. **THE SHAPE OF THIS IS THE FINDING.** D-419's MAJOR A was an enumeration standing in for a rule; D-420 closed it with a rule and an exception catch-all; D-421's MINOR 2 found the new rule was still an enumeration; revision 7 replaced it with a rule and left the second copy un-updated. What has failed three times running is the GOVERNING DOCUMENT, not the measuring apparatus. **WHAT THE JOINT CALL HAS TO DECIDE**, recorded rather than pre-empted: whether a fourth revision of this pre-registration is the right instrument at all, or whether the exit-taxonomy prose — which has now produced a MAJOR in each of revisions 5, 6 and 7, each time in the paragraph written to fix the last one — should be cut down to something a document can state once rather than twice.

D-424: **OPERATOR OVERRULE, AND A STANDING RULE FOR THE CLASS. THE EXIT-2 PARTITION IN `docs/experiments/wp16_sprt_prereg.md` IS DELETED RATHER THAN REVISED A FOURTH TIME, BECAUSE BOTH ITS SIDES CARRIED THE SAME REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE AND SO LICENSED NO DIFFERENT READING OF ANY NUMBER.** **THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT**: the partition produced exactly one MAJOR in each of three consecutive governing reviews, every one of them inside the paragraph written to fix the previous one — D-419 MAJOR A (an enumeration presented as complete: 49 `die()` sites, 7 quoted), D-421 MINOR 2 (a "closed list of four" whose fifth member a reviewer found in minutes), D-423 MAJOR 1 (a rule that misclassified one of its own examples, applied to one of the two sections that stated it). Three revisions, three reviews, three fix rounds, and the defect was never the wording. **WHAT THE PARTITION WAS FOR, AND WHY THAT IS NOTHING.** Kind (i) a VOID and kind (ii) a REFUSED REPORT resolved to the identical registered consequence — the run is not a measurement, the verdict is not read, nothing about either engine is in evidence in either direction. The ONLY difference was operational: re-run, or go and find out how a report the arena could not have written came to exist. That is not a threshold, not a reading, and not something pre-registration exists to fix. **Pre-registration exists to stop a reading being chosen after the numbers are seen, and neither kind permits reading the numbers at all**, so no after-the-numbers choice was available on either side of the line the document kept trying to draw. §5 now carries ONE exit-2 row and the operator reads the instrument's own printed message for what to do next. **THE STANDING RULE, added to CLAUDE.md's Process section in three parts.** (1) **THE OPERATOR OVERRULE** is a first-class move, not an escape hatch: where the CODE is done — tested, green, mutations dying — and what blocks it is a claim in a governing DOCUMENT or a rule of CLAUDE.md itself, the session states the finding, why the blocked claim does no work, and what would be deleted, in a SHORT paragraph, and asks. The operator's answer is an ADR line and the deletion is the fix. **THE TEST IS WHETHER THE DISPUTED CLAIM CHANGES WHAT ANYONE MAY CONCLUDE**; where both sides of a distinction license the same conclusion it is not a distinction and is DELETED rather than refined. **IT IS NOT A LICENCE OVER CORRECTNESS** — a finding that names a way the code can produce a wrong answer is never overruled, only fixed, and the overrule reaches only prose that constrains nothing. (2) **A pre-registration registers only what constrains the CONCLUSION**; operational guidance lives in the instrument's own printed message, is not registered and is not reviewed. (3) **A CLAIM THE DOCUMENT MAKES TWICE IS A DEFECT WAITING** — state it once in the section that owns it and have every other section POINT at that section, because a fix then lands once instead of needing to land twice and the second site is what gets missed. Each part carries its own MEASURED instance from this work package rather than being asserted as good practice. **WHAT WAS NOT OVERRULED, STATED SO THE SCOPE OF THIS ADR IS NOT OVER-READ.** Every finding about the INSTRUMENT was fixed, not waived: D-421 MAJOR 1's output-channel defect and D-422's FIFO hang are both closed in code by `385631f`, each with a driving test against the shipped script and each verified by a mutation that makes that test fail. The exit codes, the guards, the tests and the mutation table are untouched by this ruling and remain the standard. What was deleted is prose that constrained nothing. **AND THE THIRD FINDING THE OVERRULE DOES NOT REACH, ANSWERED IN CODE INSTEAD**: D-423 MAJOR 2 said the fifth registered check could not falsify the defect class it was added for — MEASURED green at `3a198de`, where the defect was live. That was a correct finding about a real gap, so revision 8 does not argue with it; it replaces all five greps with `an_answer_that_cannot_be_delivered_is_no_answer_and_not_a_finding`, which drives the shipped script against `/dev/full` buffered and unbuffered, and which mutations M6, M7 and M8 each make FAIL. A check that cannot fail is not a check, and that is the general lesson: **a registered check over a document's TEXT cannot falsify a defect in an instrument's RUNTIME, and where the claim is about runtime the check must execute the instrument.**

D-425: **REVISION 8 FAILS ITS GOVERNING REVIEW — 0 BLOCKING, 3 MAJOR, 4 MINOR — AND THE FIRST MAJOR IS A CORRECTNESS DEFECT THE OVERRULE DOES NOT REACH, SO IT IS FIXED IN CODE. ALL SEVEN ARE CLOSED IN ONE ROUND.** Report at `docs/experiments/wp16_prereg_rev8_REVIEW.md`. **WHAT VERIFIED CLEAN FIRST**: all three §7A.1 pins HELD, with the two binary digests reproduced BYTE-EXACTLY from an independent worktree at `bfdf933` under the login-shell toolchain; the header's self-account HELD, verified by digesting every section at both revisions rather than by hunk arithmetic — §1-§4, §6, §7, §7A.2, §8 and §9 byte-identical, so the D-416/D-419 self-account defect did not recur a fourth time; the D-422 regular-file guard correct in BOTH directions (FIFO, directory and device refused instantly and by name on both path arguments, while symlink, plain file and `/dev/stdin` are still accepted); the honest control exits 0 and the seeded swap still fails with 8 confirmed inversions; 8 of 9 mutations killed as claimed, M9 taking 10.01s because `timeout 10` fires and the test asserts `!= 124` FIRST, so the hang-test cannot itself hang. **AND THE OVERRULE'S PREMISE SURVIVED ATTACK**: the reviewer could find no exit-2 refusal licensing a different reading, so D-424 is right on the merits. **MAJOR 1 — THE DELIVERY FUNNEL WAS ITSELF AN ENUMERATION, AND MISSED A CLASS.** `say()` used `print`, and with stdout CLOSED (`>&-`) CPython sets `sys.stdout` to None and `print` SILENTLY RETURNS — so a refusal was recorded as DELIVERED when nothing had been written; `leave()`'s `sys.stdout.flush()` then raised `AttributeError`, which is not `OSError`, escaped the guard, re-entered the `BaseException` handler and raised again inside it: EXIT 1 WITH A TRACEBACK AND NO `CANNOT READ:` LINE. **Worst case MEASURED and reproduced by this session: a NONEXISTENT REPORT FILE — a pure VOID — exited 1**, the code §5 registers as an attribution finding. That is D-419 MAJOR B's own shape, for the third time, and the third time the cause is the same: **a guard that enumerates the ways a thing can fail rather than treating any failure as failure.** `say()` now uses `sys.stdout.write` (which raises on None instead of silently succeeding) and both `say()` and `leave()` guard with `BaseException`. All four delivery modes now exit 2 with EMPTY stderr: closed stdout on an honest report, closed stdout on a pure void, `/dev/full` buffered, `/dev/full` unbuffered. **THE MUTATION STORY IS RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE ITS HONEST FORM IS UNUSUAL.** M10 (revert `say()` to `print`) and M11 (revert `leave()` to an OSError-only guard) each SURVIVE, and that is not a coverage gap: the two guards are REDUNDANT BY DESIGN, so either alone still catches the None case and produces exit 2. M12, reverting BOTH at once, is KILLED, and under that mutant the raw command reproduces `exit=1` on a pure void. The property is covered; no single-edit mutant can show it because defence in depth is what makes the single edit survivable. Claiming M10 and M11 as kills would have been false, and the redundancy is deliberate rather than accidental. **MAJOR 2 — THE PARAGRAPH D-424 DELETED WAS STILL IN THE DOCUMENT.** §7A.1 carried a SECOND exit table, headed "Consequence, registered here", with `CLOSED list` / `kind (i)` / `kind (ii)` intact and per-kind instructions OPPOSITE to §5's single row. It contradicted the header, §7A.1's own text, D-424, and CLAUDE.md's brand-new "state it once" rule — **violated in the very commit that introduced that rule**. This is D-423 MAJOR 1 repeated exactly, by the same mechanism: the fix landed at one of the two sites. Deleted. **THE LESSON IS MECHANICAL AND IS NOW ACTED ON**: before a revision lands, the terms it claims to have removed are grepped for. Reasoning about whether the second copy exists has now failed twice; grepping takes a second. **MAJOR 3 — §11 still told the next reviewer the review was "SCOPED to revision 7's three fixes" under a cap D-423 had declared exhausted**, contradicting the header and §11's own revision-8 row. Had the reviewer obeyed it, neither MAJOR above would have been found. Corrected to REOPENED WHOLE. **THE FOUR MINORS, closed**: §7A.1's "~50 `die()` sites" was wrong again (56 measured) so the COUNT IS REMOVED ENTIRELY rather than corrected a third time — a count goes stale on every instrument edit and has now done so twice (D-421 MINOR 3, this); §10's digest row said "unchanged by revision 6" where §7A.1 says revisions 6, 7 and 8; §5's signal row claimed what remains is "what no process can catch" when SIGTERM is catchable and lands there at 143, so the row now names the property (a death this process did not choose) instead of enumerating instances — the same defect class as the exit-2 partition, inside the row written to describe its retirement; and the delivery test's control assertion now says what each other exit code would mean, per SHELL_CHECKLIST item 12 obligation 3. **THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THE REVIEWER RAISED AND THIS ADR ACCEPTS**: the OPERATOR OVERRULE's precondition "the CODE is done — tested, green" is SELF-CERTIFIED by the interested session, and this review measured that self-certification false in a neighbouring claim. The overrule remains sound as written — every correctness finding here was fixed and only prose was ever waived — but the precondition is a claim a reviewer should test rather than accept, and D-424's rule is read with that in mind.

D-426: **REVISION 9 FAILS ITS REVIEW — 0 BLOCKING, 4 MAJOR, 3 MINOR — AND THE OPERATOR OVERRULES THE NEXT REVIEW ROUND UNDER D-424, BECAUSE EVERY REMAINING FINDING IS PROSE OR REPOSITORY HYGIENE AND THE CODE WAS VERIFIED CLEAN BY AN ADVERSARIAL REVIEW THAT COULD NOT BREAK IT.** Report at `docs/experiments/wp16_prereg_rev9_REVIEW.md`. **THE REVIEWER'S OWN BOTTOM LINE IS THE GROUND FOR THE OVERRULE**: "No finding requires touching the instrument. MAJORs 1-3 are document-only; MAJOR 4 is a decision about what belongs in the repository." **AND THE DELIVERY INVARIANT HELD AGAINST A GENUINELY BRUTAL ATTACK**, which is the thing that mattered: closed stdout with stderr ALSO closed or on `/dev/full`, a read-only fd, `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER`, SIGPIPE three ways, `ulimit -n 3`, a `MemoryError` under `ulimit -v` on a 400 MB report where the handler formats `{why!r}` OUT OF MEMORY and still exits 2, `PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii`, a hostile `sitecustomize` whose stream raises `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit(77)`, and SIGINT with stdout closed. **Exit 120 is now structurally unreachable.** M12 KILLED as claimed, and the reviewer independently confirmed that "redundant by design" is an honest account of M10/M11 surviving rather than a rationalisation, by checking each guard alone yields exit 2. Pins 1 and 3 held with the binary digests reproduced BYTE-EXACTLY, and the header's self-account held under a per-section digest. **MAJOR 4 IS NOT OVERRULED AND IS FIXED, because it is not prose**: `git add -A` in `6c929da` swept **143 agent-harness files** into the repository — `.agents/` and `.claude/`, including three unreviewed shell scripts — with no mention in the message. Untracked and gitignored here. The lesson is narrow and mechanical: `git add -A` is never the right command in a repository whose gates enumerate tracked files, and the artifact gate does not catch it because harness scripts are not artifacts. **MAJOR 1 — the pin named the revision BEFORE the one that moved the instrument.** Revision 9 changed `tools/wp16_warm_attribution_check.py` in `6c929da` while §7A.1 item 2 still read `385631f`, and §10's cell contradicted itself in one sentence. The pin now names THE LAST COMMIT THAT TOUCHED THE INSTRUMENT — `6c929da` — which is a formulation a document-only revision leaves standing, so the circularity that produced the error cannot recur. **MAJOR 2 — A THIRD COPY of the per-kind exit-2 reading survived**, at §7A.1's premise-refusal section, present-tense, contradicting §5 and §7A.1's own "does not restate §5's table". D-425's grep missed it because that grep was AN ENUMERATION OF TERMS and this copy used none of them — the same defect, one level up, inside the fix written to prevent it. **THAT IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE IN THIS WORK PACKAGE** (D-419 MAJOR A, D-420's exception tuple, D-421 MINOR 2, D-425's own grep) and it is why CLAUDE.md's rule is "state it once and POINT at it" rather than "grep for the copies": a search for known phrasings cannot find a copy phrased differently, and only single-sourcing can. **MAJOR 3** — §7A.1 still described its registered check as the `/dev/full` legs alone, which the reviewer MEASURED green at `385631f` where a pure void exited 1, and cited M6/M7/M8 without M12. **THE THREE MINORS**: two stale revision lists, and §5's signal row saying "deliberately does NOT enumerate them" immediately after enumerating three — now stated as a property with the examples marked illustrative. **WHAT THE OVERRULE COSTS AND WHY IT IS ACCEPTED**: revision 10 lands without a fresh review, so its prose is unverified by a fresh context. That is a real reduction in assurance and it is recorded as one. It is accepted because the four review rounds on this document have converged — every round since revision 8 has found only prose defects while the instrument passed progressively harder attacks — and because D-424's test is met exactly: none of these findings changes what anyone may CONCLUDE from the governed run. **THE GOVERNED RUN PROCEEDS UNDER THIS ADR.**

D-427: **THE SLOT PASS CAUGHT A STALE `openings_skip` IN THE EXPERIMENT CONFIG, AND IT WOULD HAVE RE-PLAYED THE RETIRED SAMPLE.** `configs/arena_wp16_defensive_only_vs_staged.toml` was authored at prereg revision 2 (`c7132fb`), when §3 drew the book from the top, and it still read `openings_skip = 0` at launch. Revision 4 changed §3 to `openings_skip = 500` — **a FRESH SLICE, disjoint by construction from the `skip 0, take 500` that D-401's run drew** — and that change is the reason revision 4 exists at all. The config was never brought forward. Had the run launched as the file stood, it would have played the EXACT 500 openings D-402 retired as evidence for anything this WP concludes, under any criterion, ever, and the resulting report would have been a fresh number over a retired sample — the one thing the fresh-slice requirement exists to prevent. **CORRECTED TO 500 AT THE SLOT PASS**, which is what a slot pass is for: §9's slots are filled at the run's own launch precisely because the document and its configs drift apart between revisions. **WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT**: `tools/config_check.sh` validates the config's SHAPE and passed it at `0` and at `500` alike; nothing compares a config's values against the prose of the pre-registration that governs it, and nothing in this project does. **THAT IS RECORDED AS A GAP RATHER THAN FIXED HERE** — a gate that read §3's table and diffed it against the arena config would have caught this and would catch the next one, and it is the natural companion to `tools/label_consistency_check.sh`, which already does the analogous job for carve documents. Its scheduled home is the final-cleanup work package, alongside D-414's and D-422's own recorded gaps. **THE OTHER SLOTS WERE CLEAN**: `binary_sha256` on both seats matches the live `sha256sum target/release/pistol` (`b8d0dc96…`), so §9.2's "rebuild means re-record" is discharged NO-CHANGE; `openings_take = 500`, `turn_cap = 40`, `n_workers = 4`, `hang_timeout_ms = 120000`, the `nodes 50000` budget and the `elo0/elo1/alpha/beta` block all transcribe §3 and §9.1/§9.3 exactly; and engine A is the quiescence-extended seat, which §2's H1 requires and which reading the sign backwards afterwards would have inverted.

D-428: **WP-1.6's GOVERNED RUN IS TAKEN, IT IS A MEASUREMENT UNDER CRITERION 1'', AND THE VERDICT IS `h0`. THE `defensive_only` THREAT-ONLY QUIESCENCE EXTENSION IS NOT ACCEPTED. WP-1.6 CLOSES AS A PLANNING FINDING — PREMATURE AT EVAL v0 — AND NOT AS A THRESHOLD MOVE.** Run at `a4d5fbb`, governed by `docs/experiments/wp16_sprt_prereg.md` revision 10. **THE NUMBERS**: `verdict h0`, `n 450` games / **225 pairs** (comfortably over §2's 100-pair floor), `distinct_n 448`, `wins_a 110`, `losses_a 153`, `capped 187`, `capped_fraction 0.4156`, **`forfeits 0`**, pentanomial `p0 23 p1 63 p2 85 p3 42 p4 12`, `llr_pair last -2.9787` against the `h0` boundary of `log(beta/(1-alpha)) = -2.9444` — an SPRT EARLY STOP, which is why 225 pairs and not 250. Seat A was the quiescence-extended seat by construction (§3), so the sign is not read backwards. `openings_skip 500`: the FRESH slice, disjoint from D-401's retired draw, and D-427 records how close that came to being wrong. Wall `707 s` at 4 workers, against §7's ESTIMATE of 35-50 min — the estimate was conservative by roughly 3x, recorded rather than quietly ignored. **CRITERION 1'' PASSES, exit 0**: `450 game(s) accounted for — 450 replayed in full with every node count equal to the run's, 0 halted at a divergence`; `0 divergence(s), 0 confirmed inversion(s), 0 unexplained`; `2 inert pair(s) excluded by theorem, 223 pair(s) directly attributed at their first differing searched turn, **0 unattributable**`; the inert cross-check a no-op leaving `h0` unchanged, as the theorem requires; link 1b over 263 decided non-forfeit games and link 1c over all 450 games and 225 pairs. **AND THE SECOND INSTRUMENT DISAGREES ON ITS OWN EXIT CODE WHILE THE REGISTERED AGREEMENT CRITERION HOLDS — THIS IS THE OUTCOME §5 REGISTERED IN ADVANCE, NOT A SURPRISE.** `tools/wp15b_attribution_check.py` exits 1 with `1a: 900 turns replayed, 494 of them discriminating, 350 of 450 games directly attributed` and a clause-(b) robustness FAIL naming 50 vacuous pairs whose adversarial reassignment moves `h0` to `inconclusive_at_game_cap`. That is CRITERION 1', which this document SUPERSEDED, failing exactly where D-383 MEASURED that a cold two-turn window must fail. §5's own row covers it: "**A robustness FAILURE under the old Criterion 1' clause (b)** — Superseded, and kept so the supersession is visible rather than silent." **THE REGISTERED AGREEMENT CRITERION IS NOT "BOTH EXIT 0" AND WAS CHECKED AS WRITTEN**: every game the cold checker attributes by a discriminating replayed turn must be `status clean` in the warm pass — all 450 replay records are `status clean`, so every subset it could name is clean — and every game it calls a confirmed inversion must be a warm `divergence` — both are 0. HOLDS on both clauses. **AND THE GAP BETWEEN THE TWO INSTRUMENTS IS THE MEASUREMENT OF WHAT WARM REPLAY BOUGHT, ON ONE RUN**: the cold instrument leaves **50 of 225 pairs (22.2%) vacuous**; the warm instrument leaves **0 (0.0%)**. D-401's retired run was 31.2% vacuous under the cold instrument and that vacuity is what stopped it being a measurement. This run would have failed the same way under Criterion 1' and does not fail under Criterion 1''. That is the whole justification for D-384 through D-412, measured rather than argued. **THE RESOLUTION, per D-396's FLIP clause and §5's `h0` row.** The committed instrument config does NOT move: `configs/instrument_staged_v0.toml` keeps `q_depth_turns = 0`, so the extension stays GATED OFF and no commit is needed to keep it that way. **THIS IS A PLANNING FINDING AND EXPLICITLY NOT A LICENCE** to re-read `elo1`, change the budget, change the book, or run until a favourable stop — §6 registered that prohibition before game one and it binds now. **WHAT IT MEANS, FRAMED AS §6 REGISTERED IT: PREMATURE AT EVAL v0.** The narrowest, cheapest defensible width — one gated defensive trigger, one turn of extension — does not buy `+15` normalised Elo against D-398's MEASURED 2.80x ttd tax, at 50 000 nodes on `random_openings_v1` with a 40-turn cap. D-430: **WP-1.7's MECHANISM, AS IMPLEMENTED — the six non-obvious calls, each with its strongest surviving attack recorded (the red team's own discipline, CLAUDE.md's matrix rule).** (1) **GATES LIVE IN THE STAGED VARIANT** of `[search.candidate_policy]` (`killers`/`history`/`countermove`, three required booleans, `false` in all seven committed staged configs): variant-scoped like `q_depth_turns`/`q_triggers`, so Radius configs state nothing they never read. (2) **UNFORCED-ONLY BOUNDARY (M8)**: only cutoffs whose cell sits at or after `forced` update the tables, and promotions never touch `cells[..forced]` — the index test provably excludes winning placements, since on every row with an unforced range `can_win_this_turn` is `None` and no placement wins at all. (3) **PROMOTION ORDER (M9)**: TT move → killer slots → canonical pair (phase-First plies only) → countermove (phase-First only) → single history argmax → the delta-ranked rest — the report's line 83 stack mapped onto the staged tiers, with the forced prefix keeping absolute priority. (4) **PAIR KEYING (M3/M4)**: one canonical-pair slot per phase-First ply (D-5/D-51), promoted cell-by-cell in canonical order; strongest surviving attack, RECORDED NOT ADOPTED: play-order storage would compose with the phase-Second single-cell killer to reconstruct the whole refuting pair and is free at write time — ruled out because the dispatch's own keying is the canonical pair. (5) **HISTORY (M2/M5/M7)**: flat `+1` per cutoff, floor-halved at each `begin_search`, read as one argmax over the remaining unforced candidates — the deliberately minimal composite the design's §4 owns in one sentence; strongest surviving attacks: the thin-residue reading (a single-cutoff cell ages to nothing) and the first-stone-credit alternative that would erase the pair table — ruled out by the dispatch's own credit contract ("the stone that produced a beta cutoff"). (6) **QUIESCENCE SCOPE CUT**: the heuristics run in `pvs::visit`'s ordering only, never inside `crate::quiescence` at any `q_depth_turns` — a scope cut, not a claim that quiescence nodes would not benefit; `q_depth_turns = 0` in every seat this WP runs. **LIFECYCLE**: tables live in `Searcher` (history and countermove persist across a game's searches like the TT; killers reset per search because ply keying is mover-consistent only within one search); `Searcher::clear` (newgame) empties everything; the determinism gate's THIRD seat (`configs/gate_staged_heuristics_v0.toml`) exercises the ON path in CI. **WHAT WOULD FLIP IT**: the SPRT — on `h0` the committed configs keep all three gates `false` and top-K promotions / depth-scaled bonuses / play-order pairs are the licensed-not-scheduled relaxations.

D-431: **WP-1.7's RULE-5 BENCH: WITHIN THE BRACKET, AND THE BRACKET'S OWN EXPECTATION WAS WRONG IN THE INTERESTING DIRECTION.** Pre-registered in the design's §7 (revision 2, `232a175`) before measuring: hotspot = the heuristics' per-node overhead (≤ 6 validation probes, ≤ 6 rotations, one history lookup per unforced candidate; NO second per-candidate eval roundtrip, D-192); bracket = band-aggregate nps ratio ON/OFF ≥ 0.85 in both bands; abort < 0.85. **MEASURED at the implementation revision `f745d90`, 24 positions × 5 reps × 2 configs (`artifacts/wp17_bench_v1.txt`, `sha256 e34a6931…`): early band 1.0590, late band 1.0644 — inside the bracket and ABOVE 1.0.** The honest reading is recorded rather than the flattering one: the ratio is not "the heuristics are free", it is an ordering-QUALITY effect — earlier cutoffs change the node mix toward cheaper nodes, so the same node count spends less wall time; the depth column is the real signal (one early-band position completes `depth_turns 4` with the gates ON where OFF stops at 3; one late-band position loses its depth-4 — mixed at this sample size, as a per-position effect should be). IQR gate: ZERO violations at the D-215/D-362 convention (≤ 10% of median). Mutation receipts, each in its own worktree at `f745d90`: validation disabled → all four validation tests die; `newgame` clear skipped → `search_with_heuristics_on_double_run_identical` dies; history aging removed → `history_scores_are_halved_at_each_new_search` and `killers_reset_history_ages_and_countermove_survives_a_new_search` die. **The WP proceeds to its SPRT pre-registration. D-443: **CLAUDE.md IS RESTRUCTURED (214 LINES, DOWN FROM 241) WITH A NEW CODE-STYLE SECTION AND A HEADER BAN, AND THE MECHANICAL SWEEP THAT ENFORCES THE BAN DOES NOT PRODUCE A BYTE-IDENTICAL BINARY — MEASURED, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR.** A fresh-context REVIEW-impl caught seven places where the first-pass compression silently dropped real normative content under a "meaning preserved" label (the instrument-mode definition, the fixed-seed-hasher clause, the option-matrix ADR-line requirement, REVIEW-impl's "checks against the design", the governing-revision review-before-first-run clause, "a mutation is a deliberate break", and the "rule that cannot change any reading" instruction) — all seven restored verbatim-in-substance, which is why the file lands at 214 rather than the ~200 target: correctness of "nothing weakened, nothing silently dropped" is the harder constraint and wins the tradeoff over the line count. Root file reorganized to commands / map / hard rules (1-11, unchanged numbering) / process / code style / environment / pointers, per the "keep the always-loaded file terse, disclose detail behind a pointer" reading of D-424 applied to CLAUDE.md itself; the densest pre-registration methodology (dry-run discipline, the criterion/defect-class rule, the cost/replication/second-instrument rule, the instrument's-own-governing-revision rule, the tools/ review coverage rule) moved near-verbatim to new docs/process.md, one pointer sentence left in its place. Game rules 1-6 and Hard rules 1-11 keep their exact numbers and near-verbatim wording — both are cited by number elsewhere in the tree (`crates/pistol-core/src/board.rs` cites "rule 4"/"rule 5"; D-252 cites "CLAUDE.md rule 6") and renumbering was out of scope. THE OPERATOR OVERRULE paragraph (D-424's three-part rule) is preserved word-for-word except its trailing WP-1.6 evidentiary sentence, cut because that precedent already lives verbatim at D-424 in this file — a second application of "state it once, point" to a passage that itself states that rule. A stale duplicate was caught in the process: CLAUDE.md's old Map section re-listed all six docs/ROADMAP.md stage names, which ROADMAP.md already carries as its own "## Stage 0" through "## Stage 5" headers; the new Pointers section cites the file instead of re-stating its contents. **CODE STYLE (new section): rustfmt + clippy are mechanical law; comments say WHY never WHAT; no file-top narrative headers; `//!` permitted only at a crate root, a few lines, only if rustdoc needs it; `///` on public items; RFC 430 naming; behavior-named tests; reviewability beats brevity on conflict.** **THE SWEEP: 274 of 275 non-crate-root `.rs` files had their `//!` header block (and at most one following blank line) mechanically removed — every file in the workspace used this convention, crate roots included, so the ban is a real behavior change for every module and test file, not merely a written rule.** One file, `crates/pistol-search/src/params.rs`, was skipped and left untouched: its header carries a ` ```compile_fail ` doctest fence, confirmed live and passing (`cargo test --doc` reports `params.rs - params (line 8) - compile_fail ... ok` both before and after) — removing it would have deleted a test, which the WP's own "no code edits to force a removal" cap forbids. Six OTHER files' headers also carry fenced blocks, but every one is tagged ` ```text `, which rustdoc does not compile or run, so those five were swept normally with no test-count change. The sweep is purely subtractive: `git diff --stat -- '*.rs'` shows 274 files changed, 0 insertions, 5384 deletions, and grepping the diff for any added non-blank, non-`//`-prefixed line returns nothing. **THE DIGEST GATE, AS LITERALLY WRITTEN ("byte-identical or the sweep touched code and the commit is rejected"), DOES NOT PASS — AND THE REASON IS NOT A CODE CHANGE.** Pre-sweep pins (same as D-442, confirming no drift): `pistol` `sha256 bba3d955a5a846533ae59d9dbc3734a4f47031888922e28c0df81796e964a745`, `arena` `sha256 76a53f17dc9a745dc79650b00ef2681808b7925de3be102d7a9756c77f4f2045`. Post-sweep: `pistol sha256 da899fc2abe67fc0aeeade75fe209883523a61e138c26fffeec29a1cb032c486`, `arena sha256 b2ea0a09a8bfe17cefee783a757056b4ffb497a5f8c6c390d2274b8a654a7b24` — both reproduced by rebuilding from a `git stash`/`stash pop` round-trip at the same HEAD. MEASURED, not assumed: `pistol`'s string table holds the identical entry count before and after (22399 = 22399); every one of the 466 differing entries is an `.llvm.<hash>` suffix on a mangled or anonymous symbol, zero are human-readable text. `arena`'s string table is likewise identical in count (16537 = 16537); of 250 differing entries, 248 are the same `.llvm.<hash>` pattern and the remaining 2 sit at the fixed ELF build-ID offset immediately after the `/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` interpreter string — a hash OF the binary's own bytes, which is definitionally expected to move whenever anything else does. THE MECHANISM: `#[track_caller]` and the standard panic machinery (`.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, slice indexing, `assert!`) embed `file!()`/`line!()`/`column!()` as compile-time constants; removing a leading comment block shifts every later line's number, which changes the LLVM IR content those constants sit in, which changes the content-hash suffix LLVM assigns to the symbol — pervasively, across every function whose enclosing file had ANY line removed above it, with no change to any instruction that isn't itself a location literal. **THE PRECEDENT THIS SETS FOR ANY FUTURE COMMENT-ONLY SWEEP: "byte-identical" is not an achievable or the right criterion for a change that shifts source line numbers in a `#[track_caller]`-using language — the achievable and sufficient criterion is the one applied here: identical string-table entry COUNT, and every differing entry independently attributable to a `.llvm.<hash>` symbol suffix or a content-derived identifier (build-id) rather than to any human-readable text, literal, or instruction.** A future sweep that fails THIS test — a differing entry that is not hash/build-id-shaped, or a change in entry count — is the real gate and is rejected exactly as the original wording intended. Flips if a future Rust/LLVM toolchain stops embedding `file!()` line numbers in codegen-unit hashes (at which point literal byte-identity becomes the achievable bar again and this precedent is retired), or if a future sweep's diff contains ANY string-table difference that does not fit the hash/build-id shape.

D-458: FOUR SITES NOW WALK THE TURN STRUCTURE AND TWO OF THEM DISAGREE ON ONE INPUT CLASS, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN REFACTORED IN SESSION: `replay::group_turns`, `distance::last_of_turn_flags`, `census::owner_of` and `audit::audit_game` each spell the same `stones_in_turn(n).min(remaining)` walk, and none re-implements geometry or win detection, so this is not a rule-2 breach on its face — but for a turn whose RECORDED first stone completes a line and is followed by a second recorded stone, `audit.rs` reports `continued past a win` (a rule-4 defect) while `replay.rs` routes the pair through `Turn::pair`, which canonicalizes, so the winning stone may land second and the game is filed `Eligible` under the non-fatal `Probe::StoneAfterWin`; one tool would call the corpus metadata wrong where the other calls the game usable. D-461: **WP-1.8c'S FAST PATH: ONE df-pn VISIT COSTS 25-30x LESS AND THE SOLVER'S ANSWERS DO NOT MOVE.** Four legs, each required to be OUTPUT-IDENTICAL and measured to be: (1) child keys by zobrist delta instead of playing and unplaying every child on both the `GameState` and the `ThreatState` — MEASURED 79.6% (CORPUS) / 78.3% (ANCHOR) of the committed solve wall, the term `wp18b_m4_design.md` §2 registered as "the child-key apply/undo cost one layer later"; (2) `legal_placements` hoisted out of `blocking_pairs`' minimal-cover loop; (3) arm A's DEF-PLAN filter as an O(1) predicate over the raiser set and the live-two windows' empties instead of an apply/undo probe per candidate pair — MEASURED 93.0% of `threat_pairs`' wall once (1) lands; (4) `region_cells` by row sweep instead of `|stones| x 217` `BTreeSet` inserts — MEASURED 56.4% of what remains. **THE COMMISSIONING DISPATCH NAMED THE WRONG SITE AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO**: arm B's own construction is 0.15% of the wall; its `|R|.|L|` count is real and is paid one layer later. **Endpoints, timer-free and uncontended, cap 4096: CORPUS 2,630.11 -> 88.53 us/visit (29.71x), ANCHOR 1,975.53 -> 81.70 (24.18x), node counts IDENTICAL (72,794 and 263,640) on every rung of the ladder.** The per-leg ladder is five `git stash create` revisions (T0 `18b3d8a2`, T1 `277ae0cd`, T2 `e0c99ce4`, T3 `654abd43`, T4 `9eb1245b`) so every number has a revision that reproduces it — the BLOCKING finding of revision 1's own review, which registered one revision for three trees. Identity receipts: 109 cases 0 differing; REVIEW-design's own 23.3M filter decisions and 184.6M child keys, 0 disagreements; leg 4 differentially verified at the i16 lattice edges over 1,000+ boards; and the externally derived one, `wp18b_probe_v1_results.txt`'s `1599/1543` and `397/387` reproduced under `solver_v0_narrow.toml` by a build that shares no leg with the one that wrote them. **THE MUTATION ROUND FOUND THREE OF ITS OWN GATES VACUOUS AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY RE-TAKEN**: the TT gate left a slot empty so `store` never consulted the replacement law; the budget gate ran a position that answered in a few hundred nodes against a 20,000-node budget, so no budget check of any kind was reached, and it ran at the ONE cap where the broken check hides — two capped calls at 2048 move the derived total by close to four check intervals, which PRESERVES the residue, while at 1024 the same broken check spends 11,264 nodes against a 4,000-node budget; and REVIEW-impl found a TENTH mutant nothing killed — dropping only the LOW half of leg 4's `i16` clamp, which every gate passed while putting 63 out-of-ball cells into the region and un-sorting it, because the lattice-edge test only ever placed a stone at the MAX corner. All three gates are strengthened and all twelve mutants now die at named gates (`artifacts/wp18c_mutations_v1.txt`). Flips if any oracle gate, the perft oracle or the `legal_placements` agreement test ever disagrees at a later revision.

D-462: **THE SOLVER'S TT REPLACEMENT LAW WAS NOT EPOCH-AWARE, AND A SOLVE'S ANSWER DEPENDED ON THE SOLVES BEFORE IT.** Found by WP-1.8c's cap ladder, not looked for: on the anchor set `g002-t39-p1` answers `win` at 714 nodes under caps 1024 and 2048 and `unknown` at 4,096 visits under cap 4096 — a larger cap losing a proof that costs a third of the smaller one. **Reproducer**: the same position, the same cap 4096, the same config, `win`/714 alone and `unknown`/4,096 as the 61st case of an 85-position run, IDENTICAL on the committed binary and the prototype — a WP-1.8a/b property, not a WP-1.8c one. **Mechanism**: `lookup` filters on the epoch so a stale entry reads as absent, but `may_replace`'s proven-retention clause carried NO epoch guard and its generation test treated a stale occupant as worth keeping, so a stale PROVEN entry was invisible to every read and unevictable by every displacement and the live table shrank with every preceding solve. `Searcher` resets the `Solver` only at `newgame`, so the silting is across MOVES within a game and the determinism gate (fresh process per seat) cannot see it. NOT unsoundness (`Unknown` never launders as `NoWin`) and NOT a D-7 violation (a deterministic function of the solve sequence). **Fixed**: a stale occupant is always replaceable; the law is untouched WITHIN an epoch. MEASURED at cap 4096 over 85 anchor positions, 3 win / 23 nowin / 59 unknown -> 5 / 24 / 56 on 2.8% FEWER nodes, and the wall 9.2% HIGHER per visit — it buys strength with wall, which is reported because this WP's subject is the wall. All four oracle gates green with it in the tree, every count identical to D-437's (61 / 38 / 29 / 118,135 / 26,865). **What it does NOT buy, measured**: cross-solve INDEPENDENCE, which a finite shared table cannot give — at a 256-entry table `decoy-2` still answers differently in company, so the registered gate asserts the mechanism and not the symptom. Flips if a later revision needs a per-solve clear after all, which D-437 costed and rejected.

D-463: **THE NODE BUDGET WAS NOT ENFORCED ON THE GATE-ON SEAT: IT SPENT A MEASURED MEAN 156,313 NODES AGAINST 50,000, MAXIMUM 648,192.** `should_stop` tested `total_nodes().is_multiple_of(1024)`; `total_nodes()` is `search_nodes + solver_nodes` and a solver call absorbs its whole count at once, so an exact-multiple test on a counter that jumps by thousands steps OVER the multiples and does not fire. D-441 registered the overshoot as bounded by one capped call per intervening visit; **that claim is false**, and it is false where it matters — rule 6's premise for every SPRT is equal per-side compute, and a seat spending 3x its budget is not an arm. Gate-off never showed it because `solver_nodes` is 0 there and the derived total moves by one. **Fixed** by masking on `search_nodes` (which lands on every multiple) and checking unconditionally once any solver node has been absorbed: gate-off is byte-identical, and the ON seat's overshoot is bounded by one visit's own two capped calls — what D-441 claimed and did not have. Flips if the mask itself is ever retired, which would move every recorded node count in the project.

D-464: **`bench_solver_positions_v1.txt` WAS NEITHER SHA-PINNED NOR LOADABLE, SO THE TRIGGER-RICH HALF OF WP-1.8b'S REGISTERED BRACKET HAD NEVER BEEN RUNNABLE.** `wp18b_design.md` §7 registered it as "committed and sha-pinned per rule 7"; nothing pinned it, nothing read it — no test, no `tools/` script, no binary — and its tails were CELLS where the `start moves` grammar wants TURNS, so the shipped engine refused the first line by name. **Repaired** by pairing the plies into canonical turns (all 20 positions then load, 0 refusals), pinned in `corpus_document_tests.rs` beside the other two fixtures, and driven by a NEW test that parses and replays every line — because a digest attests bytes and says nothing about whether they mean anything, which is exactly how the original shipped. A why kept beside the code it argues about is a why a comment-only sweep can delete by accident, which IS the defect, so the fix is the relocation and not the restoration. **CLAUDE.md rule 9 NOW ASKS FOR THE ENTRY AND NOT THE COMMENT**, because a governing rule that still commands the deleted thing would have sent the next author's compliant comment straight into a red gate — the review's own reproducer, and the reason this is an amendment rather than a mechanization detail. D-472: **THE WP-1.5b WORKTREE HELD A SECOND COPY OF ITS REVIEW REPORT; THE VARIANT IS EXPORTED, THE MAIN-TREE COPY GOVERNS, AND THE CLOSED VERDICT IS NOT RE-READ.** `.claude/worktrees/agent-a383215a2f97832b8` (HEAD `38d9493`, kept alive by branch `worktree-agent-a383215a2f97832b8`) carried exactly ONE path outside `target/` that git did not have — an untracked `docs/experiments/wp15b_IMPL_REVIEW_REDTEAM.md`, sha256 `7b10134d…`, mtime 2026-08-23 16:08:10, nine minutes OLDER than the tracked main-tree copy `ee6f5f99…` (mtime 16:17:06, committed `98ffe81`); it had no `artifacts/` or `sessions/` directory at all, and `git ls-files --others --ignored` outside `target/` was empty. D-476: **WP-1.5d STOPS AT THE MATRIX GATE. NO OPTION IS SELECTED, NO DESIGN IS WRITTEN, NO ENGINE CODE WAS TOUCHED — AND THE CAP THE DISPATCH NAMES IS THE ONE THAT FIRES.** `docs/experiments/matrix_M2.md` was authored (revision 1, `5b2c972`), attacked by a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM (`docs/experiments/matrix_M2_REDTEAM.md`, `c075bcc`, **FALLS**), given its ONE fix round (revision 2, `f8754b8`, eleven rows against seven, four refuted claims withdrawn, a different recommendation), and re-attacked (`docs/experiments/matrix_M2_REDTEAM_round2.md`, `27b1c3d`, **FALLS** again). *"Caps: one fix round per review; any cap exhausted = STOP (WP-1.5c's precedent is the model)"* — that is this WP's shape exactly, and D-318's own disposition points the same way: **the field is still incomplete at its second revision and the missing row changes the selection.** **THE DEFECT IS STRUCTURAL AND NOT EDITORIAL, WHICH IS WHY A THIRD AUTHORING WOULD BE A NEW FIELD RATHER THAN A FIX.** Every row's identity in M2 rests on a PLY-SCOPE axis; the engine chooses in TURNS. D-9 and rule 3: a turn is two same-side plies, `ply` increments once per STONE (`crates/pistol-search/src/pvs.rs:397-399`, `PlyOutcome::TurnContinues => self.child(depth_plies - 1, alpha, beta, ply + 1, index == 0, true)`), and the returned move is the first `Turn` of the ply-indexed principal variation (`crates/pistol-search/src/search.rs:328-329`) — **plies 0 AND 1**. So revision 2's selected row, `except-ply0`, caps the node that chooses the SECOND STONE of the turn the engine plays, and its leading ground — *"it introduces no exclusion at the node where the move is chosen"* — is false. **VERIFIED BY THIS SESSION ON A SEPARATELY WRITTEN COUNTER BEFORE THE FINDING WAS ACTED ON** (`artifacts/wp15d_ply_share_verification_v1.txt`, sha256 `b1e3fb2c…`): at `movetime 500`, `quiet_radius 3`, K = 8, of the safety-net rows the cap binds at, **162 of 162 are ply-1 rows at 99 stones and 368 of 368 at 51 stones** — the two positions whose completed depth 0 is the whole reason this package was scheduled. The red team measured 165/165 and 363/363 on its own instrument; the difference is the deadline's granularity and the agreement is between independent instruments. `/usr/bin/grep -c "ply 1\|second stone\|root turn" docs/experiments/matrix_M2.md` returns **0** across 643 lines. **THE STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, quoted as the matrix rule requires**: *"The row's benefit and the exclusion ground 1 denies are the same object"* — a scope exempting the root TURN (`ply > 1`) is MEASURED inert exactly where the debt is (`sn_capped = 0` at 51 and 99 stones, completed depth back to the incumbent's 1/0/0/0), so 100 % of the selected row's spread-class effect and 58 % of its book lift ARE the ply-1 cap. **WHAT IS LEFT STANDING AND IS NOT RE-DERIVED BY THE NEXT SESSION**: the class is measured (`artifacts/wp15d_m2_evidence_v1.txt` sha256 `db8a8793…`, `wp15d_m2_evidence_v2.txt` sha256 `455aef9e…`, with complete instruments `081c928a…` and `f73608dd…`); W-W falls to a structural fact about this recursion (F4); W-CFG cannot reach the debt at its own floor (§2); the transposition store is sound under every UNIFORM ply scope and carries `WPQ_seed.md` §7.1(3)'s poisoned-entry class under the non-PV one (0 disagreements in 3 329 995 observations against 821 in 1 254 229); completed depth on this class is a DEGENERATE MAXIMAND and cannot rank the field (the deepest seat measured anywhere plays beside the origin of a 99-stone line); and the decisive uncosted comparison is that capping ply 0 alone — 5 400 rows of 520 164 on the SPRT book — buys 644 openings at completed depth ≥ 3 while capping everything below the root turn — 1 593 643 of 1 724 042 — buys 524. Flips when a THIRD authoring re-derives the scope axis in TURNS rather than plies, prices the root turn's two nodes separately, and is attacked before selection; that is a new round and the operator's call, not this session's.

D-477: **STANDING LESSON, AND IT COST TWO RED-TEAM ROUNDS TO LEARN INSIDE THE SESSION THAT APPENDED D-474: AN AXIS IS A PREMISE.** D-474 binds a dispatcher's claim about a MECHANISM to a quoted `file:line`. It does not reach the case that stopped WP-1.5d, where every mechanism claim was quoted correctly and the AXIS the options were arranged along — ply scope — was never checked against the unit the engine decides in. The consequence is not a wrong cell; it is a field whose rows are not the rows. **So: a matrix's own axis is a premise and is quoted at `file:line` like any other**, and where the axis is a unit (plies against turns, cells against pairs, nodes against calls) the quotation names the line where that unit is CONSUMED, not where it is defined — here `search.rs:328-329`, which turns the ply-indexed line into the answer, and not `pvs.rs`'s `ply` parameter, which reads correctly in isolation. MEASURED cost of not doing this: two DECISION-RED-TEAM rounds, both **FALLS**, the second on a ground the first could not have found because revision 1 recommended a scope where the defect is invisible (`every-ply` caps ply 0 and ply 1 alike). Flips never; it is a reading rule, and its own test is whether a reader can name the line where the axis's unit is spent.

D-478: **WP-1.5d RE-SCOPE, OPERATOR RULING.** MEASURED: the D-95 spread class dies at the ROOT — the incumbent completes depth 0 at root widths 756 / 1 836 / 3 564 (21 / 51 / 99 stones) and depth 1 at 396 (11 stones) — and is therefore fixable only by pruning inside the PLAYED TURN: no exempt-root scope touches it, **0 prune events at 21 / 51 / 99 stones** (`except-root-turn`, K = 8, `quiet_radius 3`; receipt `artifacts/wp15d_turn_axis_v1.txt`, sha256 `5a64034e…`). **THE WP'S SELECTED OPTION IS THE TURN-COHERENT `ply > 1` SCOPE**, whose value case is the BOOK-OPENING class and is to be earned at SPRT. **THE D-95 DEBT STAYS OPEN** and re-points at a LICENSED, NOT SCHEDULED package: a root-turn cap on safety-net rows, owing its own matrix and its own fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM, whose registered hypothesis is that on completed-depth-0 positions a K-capped root searching deeper dominates the incumbent's answer there (ESTIMATED; the cap-ply-0-only row's MEASURED `2 / 2 / 2 / 2`, from COMPLETED iterations, is its existence proof). **ALL MOVETIME-DERIVED NUMBERS ARE SCOPING-ONLY; THE REGISTERED CALIBRATION AND BENCH ARE RE-TAKEN UNDER `Stop::Nodes` PER D-22**, which refuses `MovetimeMs` in instrument mode because wall-clock is not reproducible and instrument mode is the source of every strength claim (rules 1, 4, 6). **TWO CLAUSES OF THE DISPATCHED TEXT ARE CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN LANDED, WHICH IS D-477 APPLIED TO THE LINE THAT CITES IT.** (1) The dispatched text describes what the follow-up package would beat as *"the incumbent's unsearched top-1 play"*. **It is neither.** MEASURED this session on those same positions: the provenance is `Provenance::PartialRoot`, and `Run::salvage`'s own doc (`crates/pistol-search/src/pvs.rs:174-186`) states that a ply-0 promotion happens only on a COMPLETED child subtree, so *"the line is turn-whole and the score exact"*; the engine's genuinely unsearched answer is `Provenance::Fallback` (`crates/pistol-search/src/search.rs:434`, scored as the root's static value) and **it does not occur on these positions**. Nor is it top-1: the answer is the exact depth-1 argmax over **337 of 756**, **530 of 1 836** and **957 of 3 564** root children at 21 / 51 / 99 stones. A hypothesis registered against an *unsearched top-1 play* would be registered against a comparator that does not exist — the identical defect round 1 found in matrix M2 revision 1, which D-476 records as fallen. (2) The dispatched range pairs "depth 0" with 396–3 564 root candidates; at 396 the incumbent completes depth **1**, so the depth-0 band is 756–3 564. **PROCESS STATE RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE INFERRED**: the `ply > 1` row has not yet appeared in an OPTION MATRIX attacked by a DECISION-RED-TEAM before selection — it exists as a measured row in round 2's report and in the receipt above — so matrix M2 revision 3 and its red team are what ground this selection, and until they land the selection rests on this operator ruling alone. Flips if the architect rules that D-471's "WP-1.9" meant the eval storage package, in which case D-471's ordering sentence is the thing that needs amending, not the ROADMAP.

D-494: Roadmap amendment to D-471: WP-1.9 (eval window-map storage per D-225/D-249) runs after WP-1.5d closes and before the Stage-3 detector — it touches engine code and is therefore serial, not parallel Stage-2 prep; on its closure Stage 1 is recorded complete and the detector package opens; D-471's flip condition is unchanged and now lands on prepared substrate.

D-495: Two-track law for substrate refactors: a package claiming bit-identical outputs proves it by incremental-vs-oracle agreement plus gate-off byte-identity and takes NO strength run (identity is the strongest oracle); a single output mismatch flips the package to the full SPRT track mechanically, no discretion; the claimed track is verified by harness before it binds.

D-496: WP-1.9 (eval window-map storage) RUNS NOW: the `docs/ROADMAP.md:294-296` and `:320-323` precedence of WP-1.10 is displaced BY NAME, on the verified grounds recorded in `docs/experiments/wp19_storage_scope_memo.md` that neither recorded reason is a technical blocker at HEAD — gate-off byte-identity is a direct two-binary diff per the WP-1.5d(A) precedent (D-484) and does NOT route through `search_oracle_check.sh`, and `tools/bench_delta.sh` is on D-289's DRIVEN list. The Stage-1 arc closure will record Stage 1 **CLOSED WITH NAMED RESIDUE** — WP-1.4 (D-95, the HeXO forfeit risk) and WP-1.10 (`tools/` gate hardening) carried open, licensed, and LISTED IN THE CLOSURE LINE — never a silent completeness claim. Flips if a Stage-1 claim is later found to have been read through one of WP-1.10's undriven scripts in a way the two-binary diff does not cover, at which point the precedence is reinstated for whatever package makes that claim.

D-497: The storage OPTION MATRIX plus a fresh-context DECISION-RED-TEAM is owed and is added to the WP-1.9 round as its FIRST DESIGN STEP (matrix -> red-team -> selection -> design, the WP-1.5d shape); an unattacked matrix is the breach CLAUDE.md says it is, Track E's being settled notwithstanding — **the track is settled, the container is not**. This strikes `docs/ROADMAP.md:291-292`'s "the storage shape WP-1.5a's matrix selects" as stale: D-249 moved the eval storage change out of WP-1.5a, WP-1.5a selects no eval storage shape, and no eval-storage matrix exists in the tree.
