D-498: D-225's blanket "NEVER ITERATED" licence is **NARROWED, not struck**. `self.windows` is reached by the derived `PartialEq` on `HandcraftedV0` (`crates/pistol-eval/src/handcrafted.rs:81`), which `BTreeMap` implements by iteration, so the licence's premise is false at HEAD; D-225's DETERMINISM conclusion survives untouched, because equality never reaches move choice and rule 4 is not engaged. THE SURVIVING OBLIGATION IS CANONICAL EQUALITY: any store shape must yield iteration-order-independent and TOMBSTONE-independent comparison of carried state, pinned by the rotated-unwind test at `crates/pistol-eval/tests/eval_incremental_tests.rs:118-140` as the driving test. A store retaining tombstones that reach the derived `PartialEq` fails the obligation BY CONSTRUCTION. Flips if the equality contract itself is retired, which would require retiring the `Eval` trait's "a backend whose whole state is comparable pins it as equality" clause (D-214) first.

D-499: D-258 **BINDS** for WP-1.9. Five of its six obligations transplant and are carried: measure at the level of the SHIPPED STRUCTURE and not an isolated table; colour plies through `GameState` and never `i % 2`; hoist store construction OUT of the timed region; keep the comparand in the same run so the document can fail the decision it defends; and check the instrument against something OUTSIDE it. The sixth — "carry all ten maintained sets and not six" — is **STRUCK, with its ground recorded**: the referent is `pistol-solver`'s sets (`crates/pistol-solver/src/sets.rs:7` `CLASS_COUNT = 5`, `crates/pistol-solver/src/state.rs:30` `sets: [WindowSets; 2]`, five classes on two seats), while `pistol-eval` holds ONE map (`crates/pistol-eval/src/handcrafted.rs:86`), and an obligation without a referent is the deletable distinction D-424 names. D-258's headline stands in full: the `k = 4.4-4.9` figure is table-only and MAY NOT be quoted as a bracket.

D-500: **MATRIX WP-19-S FAILS ITS SECOND FRESH-CONTEXT DECISION-RED-TEAM, THE DOCUMENT CAP FIRES, AND WP-1.9 STOPS AT THE MATRIX GATE WITH NOTHING SELECTED AND NO ENGINE CODE ON `dev`.** Revision 1 (`d9ddcc5`) failed on three BLOCKING findings (`docs/experiments/matrix_wp19_storage_REDTEAM.md`); revision 2 (`c9befe6`) closed B1, B2, M2, M3, M4 and M6 and failed on ONE BLOCKING finding of its own (`docs/experiments/matrix_wp19_storage_REDTEAM_rev2.md`). Two failures is D-481's cap and the third revision is NOT this session's to self-grant. **THE SURVIVING DEFECT IS THAT THE FIELD IS INCOMPLETE ON THE ONE GROUND THE RECOMMENDATION RESTS ON.** Revision 2 withdrew both of its non-speed grounds on measurement — D-498 reduced to an 11-line `impl` that `std` supplies free, and the memory ground was measured FALSE IN THE RECOMMENDED ROW'S OWN DISFAVOUR (O-2 costs 33.9-54.7 B per live entry against O-0's ~19.5 and retains ~66.6 % of peak bytes at zero entries, where both tree rows release ~99 %) — leaving "fastest measured" alone, and **O-3, the row D-225 actually named, is the only row in the field never implemented.** Its exclusion rested on O-4 being an arithmetic floor that bounds it, and O-4 IS NOT ONE: at the governing revision `22bbd96` a lookup is four comparisons in `inside()` plus `offset()` recomputing `self.w * self.h` on every call and a bounds-checked `Vec` index, not the "one bounds check, one multiply-add, one load" the document claimed — and the document contradicts itself across four paragraphs, carrying "ESTIMATED, bounded above by O-4" in the §4.1 cells and "a hand-rolled table could plausibly beat O-4" in §6. Both sentences are the author's, which is D-423's defect in the section that disposes of a row. **WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT, because it reproduced under an independently written instrument:** the three whole-engine measurements at the fmt-clean revisions — O-1 `abf3d5d` nps 1.198/1.242, O-2 `9a986c6` 1.783/1.909, O-4 `22bbd96` 1.737/1.837, node identity holding per position under both budgets in every rep, all runs exit 0 — and all sixteen O-1/O-2 memory figures, reproduced byte-identically by a counting allocator the reviewer wrote from scratch, including the 139280/208928 reconciliation derived a third way. **O-4 IS DISPOSED OF ON GROUNDS THAT EXIST** and this survives the stop: it fails the committed `eval_windows_stop_at_the_edge_of_the_addressable_lattice`, whose box must span the `i16` lattice — `3 x 65536^2 x 2 B` = ~25.8 GB, overflowing `i32` at `grid.rs:129` — which is `O(R^2)` in the played radius against `O(stones)` everywhere else, on a lattice rule 1 declares unbounded. A FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE MEASURED-CELL PATTERN IS RECORDED AGAINST THIS SESSION rather than left implicit: the matrix cited that overflow at `grid.rs:112`, a PRE-`rustfmt` line number, against a POST-`rustfmt` governing revision — the defect D-291, D-318 and D-324 already name three times, here inside the paragraph rejecting a row. WHAT IS OWED, and it is a two-way choice with a costed price rather than an open question: either COMMISSION THE O-3 RUN — a probing table at ~120-160 lines plus tests, then one ~8-minute `bench_delta.sh` against the same `a5c5661` baseline — or RULE O-2 PROVISIONAL with O-3 as a registered flip trigger, in which case the ADR line carries the reviewer's surviving-attack paragraph verbatim. Every measured revision is anchored by a tag (`wp19/mx-base`, `wp19/mx-O1`, `wp19/mx-O2`, `wp19/mx-O4`, and the two superseded pre-fmt ones) so the next session reproduces rather than re-measures. Flips when the architect takes either branch, at which point this line is superseded by the selection record rather than amended.

D-501: **MATRIX WP-19-S SELECTS O-2 — `HashMap<u64, Counts>` OVER THE ORDER-PRESERVING PACKED KEY, WITH A SEEDLESS IN-CRATE HASHER — PROVISIONALLY, ON ONE GROUND, WITH O-3 REGISTERED AS A FLIP TRIGGER.** Operator ruling taking branch B of the choice D-500 handed back; D-500's cap is lifted for the selection only and the matrix gets NO third revision. Selection record with the full conditions: `docs/experiments/matrix_wp19_storage_selection.md`. THE ONE SURVIVING GROUND IS SPEED, MEASURED WHOLE-ENGINE on `tools/bench_delta.sh` against baseline `a5c5661` at the `rustfmt`-clean revisions, 5 reps, both budgets, node identity holding per position in every rep, all runs exit 0: O-2 (`9a986c6`) **nps 1.783 early / 1.909 late**, against O-1 (`abf3d5d`) 1.198/1.242 — the row D-225 recommended evaluating first — and O-4 (`22bbd96`) 1.737/1.837. The margin is real against noise at 5.1x/7.9x the within-run IQR. **BOTH OTHER GROUNDS THE MATRIX ONCE CLAIMED ARE WITHDRAWN AND NEITHER IS REVIVED:** D-498 canonical equality discriminates nothing, since every row can satisfy it and a hand-written `impl` is ~11 lines against `std`'s free one; and the memory ground was MEASURED FALSE IN THE SELECTED ROW'S OWN DISFAVOUR — O-2 costs 33.9-54.7 B per live entry against O-0's ~19.5 and retains ~66.6 % of peak bytes at zero entries where both tree rows release ~99 %, so **O-2 IS SELECTED DESPITE ITS MEMORY**, affordable on absolute magnitude (6.5-13 KB at the real 120-386 window occupancy, against a 268 MB transposition table) and not on a bound. THE STRONGEST SURVIVING ATTACK, quoted verbatim from the round-2 DECISION-RED-TEAM because CLAUDE.md wants the attack and not a paraphrase: *"O-2 is the fastest shape ever measured against anything, and the record should say only that. The one row that could contest it on the one ground the selection uses — O-3, the hand-rolled probing table D-225 named and D-249 reproduced at a table-only 4.07-4.20x over a packed tree — was never implemented, and the matrix's two attempts to exclude it both fail: §4.1's cell 'bounded above by O-4' is contradicted four paragraphs later by §6's own concession that 'a hand-rolled table could plausibly beat O-4', and §6's argument needs O-4 to be the arithmetic floor when the shipped lookup at `22bbd96` is four comparisons, two multiplies including a `w * h` recomputed on every call, and a bounds-checked index... O-2 is selected on a field that is incomplete on the exact axis it is selected for."* THE ATTACK IS ACCEPTED, NOT ANSWERED: this line says O-2 is the best MEASURED shape and does not say it is the best shape. FLIPS on the registered trigger, whose terms are fixed now and may not move (D-374): O-3 implemented as a hand-rolled probing table over the packed key and measured on the SAME instrument, baseline and fixture with O-2's 1.783/1.909 as the comparand, flipping only if it exceeds them in BOTH bands by more than the within-run IQR — a win in one band is a finding, not a flip. If it is never run the debt stays named and open; silence does not discharge it. Every measured revision is anchored by a tag (`wp19/mx-base`, `wp19/mx-O1`, `wp19/mx-O2`, `wp19/mx-O4`, plus two superseded pre-`rustfmt` ones) so a successor reproduces rather than re-measures.

D-502: **WP-1.9 CLOSES: THE HASHED WINDOW-MAP STORAGE IS LANDED, PROVEN BIT-IDENTICAL, AND MEASURED BELOW ITS OWN REGISTERED BRACKET.** Track E, executed as D-495 requires and NOT argued: incremental-vs-rebuild agreement holds (`eval_incremental_matches_from_scratch_on_random_playouts`, random legal sequences coloured through `GameState`, turn-1 single stones and rule-4 truncation included, checked forward and on the way back); and BYTE-IDENTITY of search output holds against the pre-implementation binary at `723758b`, TWICE — once at `07f518b` and again at `16c6b70` after `undo` was rewritten — over 44 positions from `tactical_staged_v0.txt` and `bench_positions_v1.txt` at both determinism budgets, **422 output lines and 88 bestmoves identical, timing elided, 0 error lines, output digest `0b1cb805…` in all three runs** (`artifacts/wp19_byte_identity_v1.txt`, `_v2.txt`). NO SPRT IS OWED OR TAKEN: identity is the stronger oracle and D-495 says a strength run adds nothing. **THE RULE-5 BENCH LANDS BELOW ITS BRACKET AND THE BRACKET DOES NOT MOVE (D-374).** Registered at `562c8eb` BEFORE the run — hotspot D-192's H1 eval roundtrip at 76.27 % of ordering samples, bracket [1.60, 2.10] both bands, abort below 1.00 — and measured at **1.508 early / 1.579 late** (`artifacts/wp19_bench_shipped_v2.txt`, node identity holding, exit 0). Above the abort line, so a FINDING and not an abort, exactly as the registration said a miss would be read. **TWO HYPOTHESES WERE FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT BEFORE THE CAUSE WAS FOUND, AND BOTH ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY**: the prereg registered that the module split was free, and this session's own run-1 diagnosis blamed an extra hash probe in `undo` — which was REAL, was found independently by REVIEW-impl, and is fixed, but moved the ratio by 0.003 early and 0.024 late and therefore explains nothing. THE CAUSE IS THE MODULE SPLIT, measured head to head rather than inferred: inline storage against the shipped module is **0.844 early / 0.828 late** (`artifacts/wp19_bench_inline_vs_module_v1.txt`), and the three runs compose — 1.783 x 0.844 = 1.505 against a measured 1.505, 1.909 x 0.828 = 1.581 against a measured 1.579, closing to 0.002 across independent runs. **THE MODULE VERSION SHIPS ANYWAY AND THE REASON IS PROCESS, NOT PREFERENCE**: it is the version REVIEW-impl reviewed, the version every mutant was re-run against, and the version Track E proved twice; restructuring at closure would ship code no reviewer has seen. THE DEBT IS NAMED AND COSTED: rule 9's ~300-line cap is SOFT and its own remedy is a justification entry, so inlining costs 15 lines over the cap plus one entry in `docs/rule9_justifications.md` and buys back 1.18x-1.21x — a follow-up package with its own REVIEW-impl and its own bench. Mutation receipts, re-run at the shipped revision (`artifacts/wp19_mutations_v2.txt`): six mutants, all dead, and THREE are singletons that prove their test is the unique pin — swapping `q`/`r` in the key kills only the order test, reseeding the hasher kills only the golden digest, and a `shrink_to_fit` on removal kills only the footprint test. Flips if the inline follow-up lands and re-measures, which supersedes the 1.508/1.579 pair with its own.
